rules.default_dial_reason: Optional rule; enable when the plane’s benevolence should grant ongoing aid and restorative benefits to good visitors.

rules.statement: At each long rest on Bytopia, a visitor who is neither lawful good nor neutral good makes a DC 10 Wisdom save. On failure, the visitor’s alignment shifts to whichever of those two alignments is closer; it becomes permanent if the visitor stays for 1d4 days, but otherwise reverts after a day away from Bytopia, and dispel evil and good also restores the original alignment.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Bytopia — Optional Rule: Pervasive Goodwill, pp. 59–60 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Optional rule; enable when prolonged exposure to the plane’s moral influence can alter visitors’ dispositions.

rules.statement: At each long rest on Elysium, a visitor makes a DC 10 Wisdom save; failure makes the visitor unwilling to leave before another long rest. After three failed saves, the visitor never willingly leaves and tries to return if forcibly removed; dispel evil and good ends the effect.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Elysium — Optional Rule: Overwhelming Joy, p. 60 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Optional rule; enable when the plane’s comfort can trap visitors through an escalating compulsion.

rules.statement: A visitor who kills a Beastlands-native beast makes a DC 10 Charisma save or transforms as polymorph into the slain beast’s type, retaining intelligence and speech. At each long rest the visitor can save again to return to its true form; after three failed saves, only remove curse or similar magic can end the transformation.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: The Beastlands — Optional Rule: Beast Transformation, p. 60 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Optional rule; enable when killing native wildlife carries a risk of bodily transformation.

rules.statement: In Limbo, a creature can use an action and an Intelligence check to move a visible object within 30 feet: the DC is 5 for Tiny, 10 for Small, 15 for Medium, 20 for Large, and 25 for Huge or larger. On success it moves 5 feet plus 1 foot per point by which the check exceeds the DC.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Limbo — Optional Rule: Power of the Mind, p. 61 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Optional rule; enable when Limbo lets visitors exert deliberate mental control over the plane’s matter.

rules.statement: In Limbo, a creature can use an action and an Intelligence check to reshape a nonmagical object it can see within 30 feet, provided it is not worn or carried. The DC is 10 for Tiny, 15 for Small, 20 for Medium, and 25 for Large or larger; success changes it into another nonliving form of the same size.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Limbo — Optional Rule: Power of the Mind, p. 61 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Optional rule; enable when mental discipline can reshape uncarried, nonmagical matter in Limbo.

rules.statement: In Limbo, a creature can use an action and an Intelligence check to stabilize a spherical area centered on itself. The base DC is 5 for a 10-foot radius and rises by 5 for each additional 10 feet; success prevents the plane from altering the area for 24 hours or until the creature uses this ability again.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Limbo — Optional Rule: Power of the Mind, p. 62 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Optional rule; enable when a visitor can spend effort to shield a bounded area from Limbo’s instability.

rules.statement: In Pandemonium’s howling winds, each hour a visitor makes a DC 10 Wisdom save; failure adds one exhaustion level. At six levels, the visitor gains a random form of indefinite madness instead of dying, and a long rest does not reduce exhaustion unless the visitor escapes the winds.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Pandemonium — Optional Rule: Mad Winds, p. 62 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Optional rule; enable when exposure to the winds causes accumulating fatigue and, at the limit, lasting madness.

rules.statement: A non-evil visitor finishing a long rest in the Abyss makes a DC 10 Charisma save; failure causes corruption determined by a d10 table. A corrupted visitor can save at DC 15 after each long rest to end the corruption; dispel evil and good or curse-removing magic also ends it, while remaining for 1d4 + 2 days changes the visitor’s alignment to chaotic evil.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: The Abyss — Optional Rule: Abyssal Corruption, pp. 62–63 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Optional rule; enable when the Abyss progressively corrupts non-evil visitors, with the risk of a lasting moral change.

rules.statement: Leaving Carceri through magic fails unless the magic is wish; portals and gates that open onto the plane function only one way. Concealed exits exist but are protected by traps and dangerous monsters.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Carceri — Optional Rule: Prison Plane, p. 63 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Optional rule; enable when escape from this prison plane should be severely restricted and costly.

rules.statement: On Mechanus, attacks and spells always deal their average damage rather than rolling for damage; for example, an effect that would deal 1d10 + 5 damage deals 10.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Mechanus — Optional Rule: Law of Averages, p. 66 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Optional rule; enable when the plane’s order replaces random damage outcomes with fixed averages.

rules.statement: At each long rest on Mechanus, a visitor who is not lawful neutral makes a DC 10 Wisdom save; on failure, its alignment becomes lawful neutral. The visitor’s alignment reverts after one day away from the plane, or dispel evil and good can restore it.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Mechanus — Optional Rule: Imposing Order, p. 66 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Optional rule; enable when the plane’s ordering influence can temporarily impose its disposition on visitors.

rules.statement: A mystery adventure should provide several clues linking suspects to motive, means, or opportunity, including some misleading clues; add redundant evidence so the investigation can still work if players miss clues.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, Mysteries—Clues (p. 78) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; clue redundancy helps preserve a playable investigation.

rules.statement: For an intrigue, the DM may track influence by character or group; at the DM’s discretion, characters gain it for favors, organizational support, or demonstrated power and heroism, and may spend it for advantage on a relevant roll. Alternatively, influence can be tracked as renown with courts or factions.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, Intrigue—Influence (p. 78) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; optional tracking and discretionary awards; the DM chooses whether social leverage is a spendable resource or renown.

rules.statement: In a respect quandary, choosing one of two allies’ incompatible recommendations causes the other ally to lose respect and possibly stop helping the party.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, Complications—Moral Quandaries (p. 80) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; choosing between allies carries a concrete relationship cost.

rules.statement: An adventure complication can impose a time limit, make completing the goal secretly aid the villain, require cooperation with a known enemy, or place the characters under magical compulsion to pursue the goal.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, Complications—Twists (p. 80) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; optional complication; the DM selects whether the story imposes urgency, hidden consequences, uneasy cooperation, or compulsion.

rules.statement: A ritual-stopping encounter may have a time limit if the ritual is close to completion; finishing it can have immediate consequences, depending on the ritual.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, Creating Encounters—Character Objectives (p. 81) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; the ritual’s timing and consequences depend on its fictional details, with disruption as the objective.

rules.statement: Combat encounter difficulty has four categories: Easy is not seriously perilous, Medium may consume healing resources, Hard risks incapacitation or death, and Deadly can kill characters and may require strong tactics to survive.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, Creating a Combat Encounter—Combat Encounter Difficulty (p. 82) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; these qualitative bands describe escalating resource and survival risk.

rules.statement: To evaluate an encounter, total each character’s XP thresholds by difficulty category to get the party’s four thresholds; compare the encounter against those totals. The passage’s example of three 3rd-level characters and one 2nd-level character yields party thresholds of 275 XP Easy, 550 Medium, 825 Hard, and 1,400 Deadly.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, Evaluating Encounter Difficulty (p. 82) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; party thresholds aggregate individual level-based limits for encounter evaluation.

rules.statement: For a group of multiple monsters, add their listed XP and multiply that total using the monster-count table; four monsters use a ×2 multiplier. This adjusted figure measures encounter difficulty only and does not change the XP the monsters are worth.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Building Combat Encounters, p. 83 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: DM may exclude monsters far below the group's average challenge rating unless they add meaningful danger; the adjustment is a difficulty estimate, not an award.

rules.statement: Compare adjusted monster XP with the party's XP thresholds; the nearest threshold below that figure sets the encounter's difficulty. For parties under three characters, use the next higher monster-count multiplier; for parties of six or more, use the next lower one, with a ×1.5 multiplier for one monster in either case.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Building Combat Encounters / Party Size, pp. 83–84 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: party size shifts the multiplier to account for how a monster group pressures unusually small or large parties.

rules.statement: Treat each separate wave or segment of a multipart encounter as its own encounter when judging difficulty, but do not allow a short rest between segments. If the adjusted XP across the multipart encounter exceeds one-third of the party's expected daily XP, it will be tougher than its separate parts suggest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Multipart Encounters, p. 83 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: no short rest between waves prevents recovery of Hit Dice and short-rest abilities, making continued pressure costly.

rules.statement: Under typical conditions, a party can usually manage about six to eight medium or hard encounters before needing a long rest; more easy encounters may be possible, while more deadly ones reduce that amount. Estimate the party's daily capacity by summing the adjusted XP-per-day value for each character's level.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: The Adventuring Day, p. 84 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: this is a rough guide, and actual luck and conditions can change how many encounters the party endures.

rules.statement: Situational advantages or disadvantages shift an encounter's difficulty by one step per factor; matching advantages and disadvantages cancel. Examples include surprise, cover, inability to see an enemy, ongoing environmental damage, or severely restricted movement.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Modifying Encounter Difficulty, p. 85 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the DM judges how many distinct factors apply; the in-world asymmetry changes the danger of the fight.

rules.statement: When checking for a random encounter, the DM may choose the check timing or roll a d20; a result of 18 or higher triggers an encounter, then an appropriate table determines what appears. Reroll a result that does not fit the circumstances.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Checking for Random Encounters, p. 86 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the DM chooses whether and when to check, because encounter frequency should fit the area's activity and the session's pacing.

rules.statement: A random encounter table can include creatures, groups, events, or discoveries, with probabilities set by the chosen dice method. The sample forest table uses 1d12 + 1d8, making middle results more likely than results at either extreme.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Creating Random Encounter Tables, pp. 86–87 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the table's entries and probability method are chosen for the location, so its random results reflect the place and its themes.

rules.statement: A berry from the sample magical plant makes its eater invisible for 1 hour, ending earlier if the eater attacks or casts a spell. Picked berries lose their magic after 12 hours; they regrow at midnight, but picking all of them makes the plant nonmagical and prevents further berries.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Sylvan Forest Encounters table, p. 87 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the benefit is temporary and ends through hostile action or spellcasting; harvesting every berry permanently removes the plant's magic.

rules.statement: A villain may be made vulnerable through a concealed soul-container, a particular artifact or weapon, disclosure of its true name, fulfillment of a prophecy, forgiveness by an old enemy, or completion of a past mystical bargain. These are suggested possible weaknesses, not a universal procedure.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Villain's Secret Weakness, p. 96 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; the DM selects or invents the weakness and how it works; finding and exploiting it is the cost of overcoming the villain.

rules.statement: A death-domain cleric who hits a creature with a melee attack can spend Channel Divinity to deal extra necrotic damage equal to 5 plus twice the cleric's level. From 6th level, necrotic damage from the cleric's spells and Channel Divinity ignores resistance to that damage.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Cleric: Death Domain, pp. 96–97 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the burst consumes Channel Divinity, while the resistance bypass is limited to the cleric's specified necrotic sources.

rules.statement: A death-domain cleric can choose one necromancy cantrip from any spell list; when it normally targets one creature, the cleric can instead target two creatures in range that are within 5 feet of each other. From 17th level, the same two-target option applies to necromancy spells of levels 1–5 that target only one creature; consumed material components need not be supplied separately for each target.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Cleric: Death Domain, pp. 96–97 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the extra target must be close to the first, and the higher-level version applies only to specified necromancy spells.

rules.statement: Once on each of the death-domain cleric's turns, a weapon hit can deal an extra 1d8 necrotic damage; this increases to 2d8 at 14th level. The cleric also gains proficiency with martial weapons when choosing the domain at 1st level.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Cleric: Death Domain, pp. 96–97 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the added damage is limited to one hit on the cleric's turn, with its size gated by level.

rules.statement: At 3rd level or higher, the paladin can use an action to target a visible undead within 30 feet. The undead makes a Wisdom save; on failure it follows the paladin’s commands for 24 hours or until this option is used again, but an undead with challenge rating at least equal to the paladin’s level is immune.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oathbreaker — Channel Divinity: Control Undead (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one target and a failed save are required; dial: up to 24 hours of control, limited by the target’s challenge rating and reuse.

rules.statement: At 3rd level or higher, the paladin can use an action to menace chosen creatures within 30 feet that can see them; each makes a Wisdom save or becomes frightened for 1 minute. A frightened creature that ends its turn more than 30 feet away can repeat the save to end the effect.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oathbreaker — Channel Divinity: Dreadful Aspect (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: only chosen, sighted creatures in range are affected; dial: the fear lasts up to a minute but can end early through a successful save after moving away.

rules.statement: Starting at 7th level, the paladin and fiends and undead within 10 feet gain a melee weapon damage bonus equal to the paladin’s Charisma modifier, at least +1. A creature can receive this benefit from only one paladin; at 18th level the radius becomes 30 feet.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oathbreaker — Aura of Hate (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bonus is limited to nearby eligible creatures and one paladin’s aura per creature; dial: the aura expands at 18th level.

rules.statement: At 15th level, the paladin has resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oathbreaker — Supernatural Resistance (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reduces only the listed damage types from nonmagical weapons; dial: magical weapons bypass this protection.

rules.statement: At 20th level, the paladin can use an action to create a 1-minute aura of gloom, reducing bright light within 30 feet to dim light. Enemies frightened by the paladin take 4d10 psychic damage when they start their turn in the aura, while the paladin and chosen creatures in it gain shadow cover that gives sight-reliant attackers disadvantage; once per turn, the paladin can use a bonus action to make a melee spell attack, dealing 3d10 plus Charisma modifier necrotic damage on a hit. The aura can be activated again after a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oathbreaker — Dread Lord (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: effects are confined to a 30-foot aura and last 1 minute; dial: activation is limited to once per long rest.

rules.statement: A paladin who has broken an oath can atone by changing alignment and demonstrating the change through words and deeds. The paladin loses Oathbreaker features and chooses a deity and sacred oath, but does not gain features specific to that oath until completing a DM-set dangerous quest or trial; after breaking an oath a second time, the paladin can become an Oathbreaker again but cannot atone.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oathbreaker Atonement (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: atonement requires demonstrated change and a dangerous trial; dial: a second oath-breaking makes the loss of atonement permanent.

rules.statement: A dungeon’s location can be selected or rolled on a d100 table; results include sites beneath settlements or ruins, natural terrain, underwater locations, and an exotic-location table. The exotic table includes places such as a demiplane, pocket dimension, Feywild, Shadowfell, and an area affected by magical catastrophe.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 5 — Dungeon Location; Exotic Location (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: choose or roll a location; dial: the tables provide options rather than requiring a particular setting.

rules.statement: A dungeon’s purpose can be selected or rolled, with options including a lair, maze, mine, planar gate, stronghold, temple or shrine, tomb, and treasure vault. Dungeons built around planar portals may be changed by energy leaking through those portals.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 5 — Dungeon Purpose (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: portal influence depends on a dungeon being built around a planar gate; dial: the passage gives no fixed size or mechanics for the resulting changes.

rules.statement: A wilderness weird-location table includes a wild-magic zone, where each spell cast within the zone triggers a roll on the Player’s Handbook Wild Magic Surge table, and a permanent portal to another plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 5 — Weird Locales (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the surge roll is triggered by every spell cast inside the zone; dial: the passage does not specify a zone size or further surge-resolution details.

rules.statement: At or below 0°F, an exposed creature makes a DC 10 Constitution save at the end of each hour or gains one exhaustion level. Cold resistance or immunity, cold-weather gear, or natural adaptation to cold automatically succeeds.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 5 — Wilderness Survival: Extreme Cold (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the save recurs hourly while exposed; dial: listed protections remove the chance of exhaustion from this cold rule.

rules.statement: At or above 100°F, a creature exposed to heat without drinkable water makes an hourly Constitution save or gains one exhaustion level; the DC begins at 5 and rises by 1 each additional hour. Medium or heavy armor and heavy clothing impose disadvantage, while fire resistance or immunity and natural adaptation to heat automatically succeed.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 5 — Wilderness Survival: Extreme Heat (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the check is hourly and its DC escalates; dial: access to drinkable water avoids this rule, and specified protections alter or remove the risk.

rules.statement: A strong wind imposes disadvantage on ranged weapon attacks and sight- or hearing-based Wisdom (Perception) checks as specified, extinguishes open flames, disperses fog, and makes nonmagical flight nearly impossible; a flying creature must land at the end of its turn or fall. Heavy rain or snowfall lightly obscures the area and imposes disadvantage on sight-based Perception checks; heavy rain also extinguishes open flames and penalizes hearing-based Perception checks.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 5 — Wilderness Survival: Strong Wind; Heavy Precipitation (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these penalties apply while creatures and flames are in the affected weather; dial: wind and precipitation impose different specific limitations.

rules.statement: A creature that needs to breathe and travels at 10,000 feet or higher counts each hour of travel as two hours when determining how long it can travel. Such creatures acclimate after 30 days or more at that elevation, but cannot acclimate above 20,000 feet unless native to those environments.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 5 — Wilderness Survival: High Altitude (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the travel-time penalty applies to breathing creatures at high altitude; dial: acclimation takes at least 30 days and has a 20,000-foot limit.

rules.statement: A creature caught in quicksand can spend its action to escape with a successful Strength check; the DC is 10 plus the number of feet it has sunk. A completely submerged creature cannot breathe, and a nearby creature can use its action to pull it out with a successful Strength check against DC 5 plus the target’s sunk depth in feet.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Quicksand (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated action and check; dial: sinking depth raises the escape DC, reflecting the increasing difficulty of getting free.

rules.statement: A razorvine wall or hedge 10 feet high, 10 feet wide, and 5 feet thick has AC 11, 25 hit points, and immunity to bludgeoning, piercing, and psychic damage. A creature making direct contact with it for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity save or take 1d10 slashing damage.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Razorvine (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the contact save and damage once per turn; dial: the plant’s immunities and fixed dimensions bound how it can be cleared or crossed.

rules.statement: Slippery ice is difficult terrain; the first time a creature moves onto it on a turn, it must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or fall prone. Thin ice breaks when the weight on a 10-foot-square area exceeds its tolerance of 3d10 × 10 pounds, causing creatures on it to fall through.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Slippery Ice; Thin Ice (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed movement check and weight threshold; dial: ice hazards depend on contact, turn timing, and load on each area.

rules.statement: A forager makes a Wisdom (Survival) check when called for, with DC 10 for abundant supplies, 15 for limited supplies, or 20 for very little or none. On a success, roll 1d6 plus the character’s Wisdom modifier separately for pounds of food and gallons of water; on a failure, the character finds nothing.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Foraging (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve each forager’s check and two yield rolls; dial: scarcity sets the difficulty and failed checks produce no supplies.

rules.statement: Unless following a path or similar guide, a wilderness navigator checks Wisdom (Survival) against the terrain DC: 15 for forest, jungle, swamp, mountains, or open sea under overcast skies; 10 for arctic, desert, hills, or open sea with clear skies; and 5 for grassland, meadow, or farmland. Slow travel grants +5, fast travel imposes −5, and an accurate map or view of the sun or stars grants advantage; on failure, the party goes the wrong way and may retry after 1d6 hours spent correcting course.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Becoming Lost; Wilderness Navigation (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve navigation with the terrain DC and modifiers; dial: failed navigation costs 1d6 hours before another attempt.

rules.statement: A creature without a swimming speed can swim for up to 1 hour before making a DC 10 Constitution save; on a failure it gains one exhaustion level. Swimming beyond 100 feet deep counts as 2 hours per hour toward this limit, and beyond 200 feet counts as 4 hours; a creature with a swimming speed can swim all day without this penalty and instead follows normal forced-march rules.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Swimming (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: track swimming time and apply exhaustion on a failed save; dial: depth accelerates the time cost, while a swimming speed removes this particular limit.

rules.statement: A ship within sight of land cannot become lost; otherwise its navigator uses dead reckoning or the sun and stars and checks against the wilderness navigation rules. In a storm combining strong wind and heavy rain, the crew loses sight of landmarks except prominent features such as a lighthouse, and navigation checks have disadvantage.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: The Sea: Navigation; Weather at Sea (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the ordinary navigation check when out of sight of land; dial: storms obscure landmarks and impose disadvantage.

rules.statement: A ship needs the minimum number of skilled hirelings listed for its vessel type to function, with each skilled hireling costing at least 2 gp per day. If at least half the crew becomes disloyal during a voyage, the crew mutinies; if berthed, disloyal crew members leave and do not return.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Owning a Ship: Crew (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: pay the required crew and track loyalty; dial: a disloyal majority ends dependable service through mutiny or departure.

rules.statement: Repairing a ship while it is berthed restores 1 hit point per day and costs 20 gp for materials and labor. Damage below the ship’s damage threshold is superficial and does not reduce its hit points; damage meeting or exceeding the threshold affects it normally.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Owning a Ship: Damage Threshold; Ship Repair (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the threshold before reducing hit points and charge for repair; dial: repairs require time, materials, and a berthed vessel.

rules.statement: A flying mount must rest for 1 hour after every 3 hours of flight and cannot fly more than 9 hours per day; a mount that does not tire is exempt. A flying mount with an 80-foot flying speed can cover 8 miles per hour, or 72 miles in 9 hours with two rests.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: The Sky (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: track flight hours and required rests; dial: ordinary mounts have a daily endurance limit, unlike mounts that do not tire.

rules.statement: A creature actively searching for a trap can make a Wisdom (Perception) check against its detection DC, and passive Perception can reveal it without an active search. A character may use Intelligence (Investigation) to work out how to disable a trap and a Dexterity check with thieves’ tools to do so; for a magic trap, an Intelligence (Arcana) check may also be used, and dispel magic can disable most magic traps at the DC specified for that trap.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Traps: Detecting and Disabling a Trap (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use each trap’s listed DC and appropriate check; dial: clever actions can reveal or bypass traps without a roll when they clearly do so.

rules.statement: A complex trap rolls initiative when activated and then acts on its turns, often repeating attacks or changing the environment each round. It can still be detected, disabled, or bypassed using the usual trap procedures.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Complex Traps (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: run an activated complex trap in initiative order; dial: its repeated turns make the hazard an ongoing encounter rather than a single trigger.

rules.statement: A character can uncover an item's properties and how to use them by maintaining physical contact with it while concentrating on it during a short rest; tasting a potion is enough to learn its effect. The identify spell can reveal an item's properties more quickly, while clues or experiments may also help.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, Identifying a Magic Item (p. 136) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a short rest reveals properties; dial: remove that option for greater mystery, requiring identification magic or experimentation instead.

rules.statement: An item that requires attunement cannot have its magical properties used until a creature forms a bond with it; some items also require the creature to meet a stated prerequisite. For a class prerequisite, the creature must belong to that class.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, Attunement (p. 136) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: binding is required only for items that specify it; dial: item prerequisites restrict who can bind, with class access as the cost.

rules.statement: Creating a magic item requires its formula, a spellcaster with spell slots who can cast any spells the item produces, and the minimum character level for its rarity; the table sets minimums at 3rd level for common or uncommon, 6th for rare, 11th for very rare, and 17th for legendary items. Costs are 100 gp, 500 gp, 5,000 gp, 50,000 gp, and 500,000 gp respectively, with 25 gp of progress per workday.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, Crafting a Magic Item (pp. 128–129) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: crafting takes days and substantial funds; dial: special materials or locations can be required, adding a setting-specific cost.

rules.statement: If the item will produce a spell, its creator expends one spell slot of that spell's level each day of crafting and keeps its material components available throughout. Components normally consumed by the spell are consumed during crafting—once for a one-use item, or once per crafting day otherwise.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, Crafting a Magic Item (p. 129) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell slots and components are expended as specified; dial: none stated.

rules.statement: Several eligible characters can craft one item together if each meets its level requirement and participates for the whole process; each may contribute spells, slots, and components, and each adds 25 gp of progress per workday.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, Crafting a Magic Item (p. 129) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: joint work is allowed under the stated participation and level limits; dial: none stated.

rules.statement: After at least 10 days performing sacred rites in a temple devoted to a god the character reveres, the character gains inspiration at the start of each day for the next 2d6 days.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, Performing Sacred Rites (p. 129) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the benefit requires at least 10 days of rites; dial: the duration is random, lasting 2d6 days.

rules.statement: A character can spend downtime building a stronghold only after securing suitable land, which may require a royal charter, land grant, deed, inheritance, or another means of acquisition. Construction costs and times depend on the building; each day the character is away from overseeing work adds 3 days to construction.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, Building a Stronghold (p. 128) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: land, materials, labor, and oversight constrain construction; dial: absence slows progress by three extra days per day away.

rules.statement: For property upkeep, the listed total cost is per day and includes running costs and hireling salaries; expenses are paid every 30 days. Income from fees, tithes, donations, or sales is already reflected in the listed cost.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, Maintenance Costs (p. 127) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recurring costs are due every 30 days; dial: property income offsets upkeep as accounted for in the table.

rules.statement: When a character undertakes a business activity, roll percentile dice and add the number of days spent, to a maximum of 30, to determine its result on the business table. Unpaid required costs cause the business to begin failing and impose a cumulative −10 penalty on later rolls for each unpaid debt.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, Running a Business (p. 129) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the roll governs business costs and profits; dial: unpaid debts compound into a penalty on later results.

rules.statement: A character can spend downtime searching for a buyer for a common through very rare magic item, but not a legendary item or priceless artifact; the search is available only where wealthy prospective buyers can be found. A DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check finds a buyer on success after a rarity-based wait, while failure means no buyer after 10 days; assistance grants advantage.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, Selling Magic Items (p. 130) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sale requires finding a buyer and passing the check; dial: legendary items and artifacts require an adventure or quest to sell.

rules.statement: A character can spend downtime spreading a rumor in a village, town, or city, spending 1 gp per day for a continuous period of 2d6, 4d6, or 6d6 days respectively. A successful DC 15 Charisma (Deception or Persuasion) check shifts the community's general attitude toward the subject one step toward friendly or hostile; failure prevents further attempts to spread that rumor.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, Sowing Rumors (p. 131) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the rumor costs time and money and affects general community attitude; dial: individuals may retain their own opinions, and failure bars repetition.

rules.statement: As an optional advancement rule, a character who has enough experience for a new level must train before receiving its class features: 10 days and 20 gp for levels 2–4, 20 days and 40 gp for levels 5–10, 30 days and 60 gp for levels 11–16, or 40 days and 80 gp for levels 17–20.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, Training to Gain Levels (p. 131) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: advancement is not delayed unless this variant is selected; dial: training time and expense postpone new class features.

rules.statement: A creature can be attuned to at most three magic items at once, and an item can be attuned to only one creature; a creature cannot attune to multiple copies of the same item. Attunement to an item requiring it grants its magical properties, while a nonattuned user gets only its nonmagical benefits.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, Attunement (p. 138) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: three simultaneous item bonds; the limit constrains how many magical benefits one creature can maintain.

rules.statement: To attune, a creature spends a short rest focused only on the item and in physical contact with it; an interrupted rest fails, and this rest cannot also be used to learn the item's properties. At the rest's end, the creature understands how to activate the item's magical properties, including any command words.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, Attunement (p. 138) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: one uninterrupted short rest of focused contact; learning the item's operation takes dedicated time.

rules.statement: Attunement ends if the creature ceases to meet the item's prerequisites, stays more than 100 feet from it for at least 24 hours, dies, or another creature attunes to it. The creature can also end attunement voluntarily by spending another short rest focused on the item, but a cursed item's bond cannot be voluntarily ended until its curse is broken.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, Attunement; Cursed Items (pp. 138–139) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: distance, death, changed prerequisites, replacement, or a further short rest can end a bond; curses impose a costly exception.

rules.statement: A creature that tries and fails to cast a spell from a spell scroll must make a DC 10 Intelligence saving throw; on a failure, roll on the Scroll Mishap table. Mishaps can cause force damage, misdirect or relocate the spell, invert its effect, impose a temporary odd effect, or delay its casting by 1d12 hours.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, Variant: Scroll Mishaps (p. 140) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; mishap follows a failed scroll attempt and a failed DC 10 save; unreliable access risks harmful or misdirected magic.

rules.statement: When two potions are mixed, the DM can roll d100 on the Potion Miscibility table; when more are combined, roll again for each added potion and combine the results. Possible outcomes include force damage, poison, lost or weakened effects, ordinary or doubled effects, or a permanent effect that may require an appropriate spell to end.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, Variant: Mixing Potions (p. 140) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; each combination invokes a random outcome; mixing enchanted substances risks destructive or lasting consequences.

rules.statement: A spell cast from a magic item uses the lowest possible spell level, expends no user spell slots, and needs no components unless the item's description says otherwise. It uses the spell's normal casting time, range, and duration, and requires the user to concentrate when the spell does; exceptions in the item description can change these rules.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, Spells (p. 141) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: lowest spell level and no slots or components; the item supplies the casting but does not remove concentration or specified exceptions.

rules.statement: Some magic items have expendable charges; identify or attunement reveals how many remain, and a creature attuned to the item learns how many it regains when it recharges. As an optional rule, some wands never regain spent charges, with their initial charge count optionally raised to no more than 25.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, Charges; Variant: Wands That Don't Recharge (pp. 141, 143) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; charges limit uses, and the optional wand rule makes spent charges permanent losses; finite magical output constrains repeated activation.

rules.statement: A magic item that requires a command word cannot be activated where sound is prevented. A consumable loses its magic after use; a scroll is spent when its magic is invoked, while a potion takes effect immediately once drunk or administered.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, Activating an Item (p. 141); Potions and Scrolls (p. 139) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: speech may be required and consumables work once; activation depends on usable sound or surrendering the item.

rules.statement: A magic item is generally at least as durable as an ordinary item of its kind, and most magic items other than potions and scrolls resist all damage. Artifacts are nearly indestructible and require extraordinary measures to destroy.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, Magic Item Resilience (p. 141) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: most items resist damage, while artifacts are exceptionally difficult to destroy; magical reinforcement preserves valuable objects.

rules.statement: The alchemy jug can produce a chosen liquid after the user names it with an action, and the user can uncork and pour it with another action, at up to 2 gallons per minute. Once it begins producing one liquid, it cannot switch liquids or exceed that liquid's maximum amount until the next dawn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, Magic Items A–Z: Alchemy Jug (p. 150) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: one selected liquid per day, subject to a liquid-specific maximum; the vessel's output is bounded until dawn.

rules.statement: The amulet lets its wearer name a familiar location on another plane and make a DC 15 Intelligence check to travel there using plane shift. On a failure, the wearer and all creatures and objects within 15 feet travel to a random destination: a d100 roll of 1–60 selects a random place on the named plane, while 61–100 selects a random plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Amulet of the Planes, p. 150 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the check, range, and destination odds; the risk of stranding nearby creatures and cargo is the cost.

rules.statement: The bag can hold up to 500 pounds and 64 cubic feet, but always weighs 15 pounds; retrieving an item takes an action. Creatures inside can breathe for a number of minutes equal to 10 divided by their number, minimum 1, before suffocating.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Bag of Holding, pp. 153–154 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve capacity and retrieval cost; limited volume, weight capacity, and creature air supply bound its usefulness.

rules.statement: Putting a bag of holding inside a portable hole, handy haversack, or similar extradimensional space destroys both items and opens a one-way gate to a random Astral Plane location. Creatures within 10 feet are pulled through, and the gate then closes.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Bag of Holding, p. 154 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the item interaction and area; the catastrophic loss of both storage items and nearby creatures is the risk.

rules.statement: The bag of devouring senses anything put inside; animal or vegetable matter placed wholly within is consumed and lost. A living creature partly inside has a 50 percent chance of being pulled in, and a creature that starts its turn inside is consumed; once each day, stored objects are sent to a DM-chosen time and plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Bag of Devouring, p. 153 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the daily transfer and creature risks; the extradimensional feeder makes storage dangerous rather than secure.

rules.statement: A bean planted in dirt or sand and watered produces an effect after 1 minute, chosen or determined randomly from the table. Outcomes include damage, creatures or structures appearing, lasting changes to a creature, and a beanstalk whose top may lead to another plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Bag of Beans, pp. 152–153 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the planting trigger and delayed, variable outcomes; the uncertainty and potentially hazardous results are the cost.

rules.statement: Attuning to the cursed armor grants resistance to one randomly or DM-selected bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage type, but also curses the wearer. While cursed, the wearer is vulnerable to the other two types; removing the armor does not end the curse, which lasts until remove curse or similar magic targets the wearer.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Armor of Vulnerability, p. 152 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the curse's persistence and asymmetric defenses; attunement brings a lasting liability that ordinary removal cannot avoid.

rules.statement: The legendary armor grants resistance to nonmagical damage while worn. Once per day, the wearer can use an action to become immune to nonmagical damage for 10 minutes, ending sooner if the armor is removed.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Armor of Invulnerability, p. 152 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the daily action and duration; exceptional protection is limited by a long recovery and dependence on wearing the armor.

rules.statement: The cube begins with 36 charges and regains 1d20 expended charges at dawn. An action spends charges to create a 15-foot-sided force barrier for up to 1 minute; its selected face determines what can pass, it moves with the user, and the user can change its effect by spending charges again.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Cube of Force, pp. 159–160 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve charge costs and face-specific barriers; limited charges and possible obstruction constrain use.

rules.statement: The cubic gate has 3 charges and regains 1d3 at dawn. An action and 1 charge opens a gate to the plane keyed to a chosen face; pressing that face twice instead uses plane shift to transport targets to its keyed plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Cubic Gate, p. 160 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the charge cost and plane-keyed destinations; travel options are limited by the cube's finite reserve and fixed connections.

rules.statement: A bead of force explodes when thrown up to 60 feet; creatures within 10 feet make a DC 15 Dexterity save or take 5d4 force damage. A transparent sphere then lasts 1 minute, trapping creatures that failed and are fully inside; only breathable air passes through, and a trapped creature can move the sphere by pushing against it.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Bead of Force, p. 154 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the throw distance, area, save, and duration; the bead is expended to create a temporary containment effect.

rules.statement: When lit, the candle sheds dim light in a 30-foot radius for up to 4 hours of total burn time; it can be snuffed and relit, tracking used time in 1-minute increments. Creatures in the light matching its alignment have advantage on attacks, saves, and ability checks, and matching clerics or druids can cast prepared 1st-level spells without expending slots; lighting it for the first time can instead cast gate and destroy it.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Candle of Invocation, p. 157 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the alignment condition, radius, and finite burn time; using the candle for gate consumes it outright.

rules.statement: When the owner draws randomly from a deck of many things, each card takes effect immediately; the owner must declare how many cards to draw, drawing each within 1 hour of the previous one. If the declared number is not completed, the remaining cards fly out and take effect together; most cards return to the deck after being drawn, while the Fool and jester do not.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Deck of Many Things, pp. 162–164 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep random draws and the declared sequence; committing to draws risks immediate, potentially accumulating consequences.

rules.statement: When the bottle is opened, roll d100: on 01–10 the efreeti attacks for 5 rounds, then vanishes and the bottle loses its magic; on 11–90 it serves for 1 hour, and the same result applies to the next two openings, while a fourth opening makes it escape and destroys the bottle; on 91–00 it grants three wishes or vanishes after 1 hour, then the bottle loses its magic.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Efreeti Bottle, p. 167 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the stated roll and service limits; dial only if the game needs a different risk profile for a powerful stored entity.

rules.statement: A creature from another plane that is targeted by the flask must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom save or be trapped; a creature previously trapped by it has advantage on the save. The flask holds one creature, which does not need food, water, air, or aging while inside; releasing it makes it friendly and obedient to you and your companions for 1 hour.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Iron Flask, p. 178 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the save, single-occupant capacity, and one-hour release bargain; these bound the flask’s power and duration.

rules.statement: A creature’s soul is removed from its body and held in an object at a location chosen by the DM; powerful beings guard that location, and the body is incapacitated while the soul is trapped. Wish cannot restore the soul, though it reveals the object’s location, and the affected character draws no more cards.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: The Void, p. 165 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the stated incapacitation and recovery barrier; the in-world cost is a soul separated from its helpless body.

rules.statement: When the card summons the avatar, it appears within 10 feet and attacks the drawer, who must fight alone; it vanishes if the drawer dies or it reaches 0 hit points. Anyone who helps summons a separate avatar, and a creature killed by one cannot be restored to life.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Skull; Avatar of Death, p. 165 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the solo-fight restriction and lethal aftermath; assistance adds another threat rather than easing the encounter.

rules.statement: Shackles can be put on an incapacitated Small–Large creature with an action. They block extradimensional movement, including teleportation and planar travel, but not passage through an interdimensional portal; a designated creature or the user can remove them with an action, while the captive can try once every 30 days to break them with a DC 30 Strength (Athletics) check, destroying them on success.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dimensional Shackles, p. 166 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep portal passage as the explicit exception and retain the rare, difficult escape attempt.

rules.statement: Putting a haversack into a bag of holding, portable hole, or similar extradimensional space destroys both items and opens a one-way gate to the Astral Plane; creatures within 10 feet are pulled through to a random location there, and the gate closes. A haversack holds up to 80 pounds and 8 cubic feet in its central pouch and up to 20 pounds and 2 cubic feet in each side pouch, while weighing 5 pounds regardless of contents.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Heward’s Handy Haversack, p. 174 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the storage limits and catastrophic interaction; the planar displacement is the cost of combining incompatible spaces.

rules.statement: An elemental gem is consumed when broken as an action, summoning an air, earth, fire, or water elemental according to the gem’s type, as if the user had cast conjure elemental.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Elemental Gem, p. 168 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the gem is a one-use power source; its cost is consumed when the elemental is called.

rules.statement: A figurine can be activated by speaking its command word and throwing it to a clear point within 60 feet; it becomes a friendly creature that understands your languages and follows spoken commands, defending itself if given none. It reverts at its listed duration, at 0 hit points, or when you touch it and use an action to speak the command word; each figurine also has a specified reuse delay.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Figurine of Wondrous Power, pp. 169–170 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: follow each figurine’s duration and cooldown; temporary service is limited by the item’s recovery interval.

rules.statement: The dimensional shackles’ captive can still pass through an interdimensional portal, even though the shackles block other extradimensional movement, including teleportation and travel to another plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dimensional Shackles, p. 166 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the portal exception; it distinguishes crossing an existing opening from creating or using other planar movement.

rules.statement: The Void card’s wish exception reveals the location of the soul-holding object but does not return the soul; the object is guarded by one or more powerful beings, and the body remains incapacitated until the soul is recovered.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: The Void, p. 165 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the explicit limit on wish; locating the anchor is not the same as freeing the soul.

rules.statement: A creature wearing the Demon Armor cannot remove it once donned unless remove curse or similar magic targets it; while wearing it, the creature has disadvantage on attacks against demons and on saves against their spells and special abilities.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Demon Armor, p. 166 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the removal lock and its drawback; the wearer gains protection and powers at the cost of being stuck with a hostile influence.

rules.statement: The Hammer of Thunderbolts can be attuned to only while its bearer wears a belt of giant strength and gauntlets of ogre power; removing either item ends attunement. While attuned and holding the hammer, the bearer’s Strength rises by 4, to a maximum of 30.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Hammer of Thunderbolts, p. 173 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve both prerequisite items and the attunement break condition; the power depends on maintaining the full equipment set.

rules.statement: When the flask is opened, its contained creature is released for the stated duration; it obeys the opener’s commands unless a command is likely to kill it, in which case it defends itself and takes no other action. When the duration ends, it resumes its normal disposition and alignment.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Iron Flask (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the flask’s release and obedience last only for its specified duration; dial: creature identity and duration; in-world cost: the container is the source of temporary control.

rules.statement: An identify spell reveals that a creature is inside an iron flask, but only opening the flask reveals what kind of creature it is; a newly found flask may be empty or hold a creature chosen or randomly determined by the DM.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Iron Flask (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: detection reveals presence but not identity; dial: contents of a newly found flask; in-world reason: the flask conceals the creature’s nature.

rules.statement: When thrown with its command word, the javelin becomes a lightning line 5 feet wide and up to 120 feet long. Creatures in the line other than the wielder and target make a DC 13 Dexterity save, taking 4d6 lightning damage on a failure or half on a success; the javelin then makes a ranged attack against the target, adding 4d6 lightning damage on a hit, and this power is unavailable again until dawn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Javelin of Lightning (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one use per dawn; dial: the line’s reach and damage; in-world cost: its special power must recharge.

rules.statement: One dose of Keoghtom’s ointment, swallowed or applied as an action, restores 2d8 + 2 hit points and ends poison and any disease affecting the recipient.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Keoghtom’s Ointment (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one dose is consumed per use; dial: healing amount; in-world cost: finite doses in the jar.

rules.statement: While lit, the lantern burns for 6 hours per pint of oil, sheds bright light for 30 feet and dim light for a further 30 feet, and reveals invisible creatures and objects within its light. As an action, its hood can be lowered to leave dim light in a 5-foot radius.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Lantern of Revealing (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: revelation works only while lit and visibility is limited to the lamp’s area; dial: fuel duration and radii; in-world cost: oil is consumed.

rules.statement: A luck blade grants +1 to attacks, damage, and saving throws while on its bearer’s person; once before its next dawn recharge, the bearer can reroll an attack, ability check, or saving throw and must keep the new result. It holds 1d4 − 1 wish charges; while holding it, the bearer can spend one as an action to cast wish, but the wish property ends when no charges remain and cannot be used again until the next dawn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Luck Blade (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reroll and wish uses are charge- or dawn-limited; dial: initial wish charges; in-world cost: each wish consumes a charge and may exhaust the property.

rules.statement: A creature frightened by the mace of terror for up to 1 minute must try to move as far from the wielder as possible, cannot willingly enter within 30 feet, cannot take reactions, and is restricted in its action; it can repeat its DC 15 Wisdom save at the end of each turn to end the effect. The mace has 3 charges and regains 1d3 at dawn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Mace of Terror (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: fear is bounded by repeated saves and charges; dial: affected targets chosen within 30 feet; in-world cost: a charge is spent for each wave.

rules.statement: A manual of golems can be deciphered and used only by a spellcaster with at least two 5th-level spell slots; an unqualified reader takes 6d6 psychic damage. Creating the chosen golem requires uninterrupted work for the listed number of days, no more than 8 hours of rest daily, and the listed supply cost; upon completion the book is consumed, and the golem animates when its ashes are sprinkled on it, obeying the creator’s spoken commands.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Manual of Golems (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: creation consumes the manual and requires time, skill, and costly supplies; dial: golem type and corresponding cost and duration; in-world cost: the book is destroyed.

rules.statement: The mirror can trap a creature that sees its reflection in the activated mirror within 30 feet if it fails a DC 15 Charisma save; a creature that knows the mirror’s nature has advantage, and constructs automatically succeed. Its twelve cells are extradimensional; if all are occupied, a new prisoner displaces one at random, and breaking the mirror frees all prisoners nearby. A trapped creature does not age or need food, drink, or sleep, and can escape by magic permitting planar travel; otherwise it remains confined until released.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Mirror of Life Trapping (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: confinement lasts until release or qualifying planar magic; dial: twelve-cell capacity and displacement; in-world cost: the mirror is a vulnerable container, and shattering it frees every prisoner.

rules.statement: The portable hole unfolds as an action against a solid surface to make a 10-foot-deep extradimensional space; folding it shut leaves creatures and objects inside. A creature inside a closed hole can force its way out with a successful DC 10 Strength check, and a breathing creature otherwise suffocates after 10 minutes. Placing it inside a bag of holding, handy haversack, or similar extradimensional space destroys both items, opens a one-way gate to a random Astral Plane location, and pulls nearby creatures through before the gate closes.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Portable Hole (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: storage is sealed and air is limited; dial: the interaction-triggered gate’s 10-foot pull and random destination; in-world cost: both storage items are destroyed.

rules.statement: A necklace of adaptation lets its wearer breathe in any environment and grants advantage on saves against harmful gases and vapors. A necklace of prayer beads works only for an attuned cleric, druid, or paladin; its wearer can cast a bead’s spell as a bonus action, after which that bead is unusable until dawn, and removing a magic bead destroys its magic.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Necklace of Adaptation; Necklace of Prayer Beads (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: adaptation persists while worn, while each prayer bead recharges at dawn; dial: bead contents; in-world cost: access is limited by attunement eligibility and individual bead use.

rules.statement: A ring of djinni summoning calls a particular djinni into a chosen unoccupied space within 120 feet; it is friendly and obeys commands, remaining while concentration lasts up to 1 hour or until reduced to 0 hit points. After leaving, it cannot be summoned for 24 hours, and the ring becomes nonmagical if the djinni dies.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Ring of Djinni Summoning (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: summoning is limited by concentration, duration, and a 24-hour interval; dial: the chosen arrival space; in-world cost: the ring loses its magic if the djinni dies.

rules.statement: While holding the rod, a warlock gains a bonus to warlock spell attack rolls and save DCs based on the rod’s rarity: +1, +2, or +3. Once before finishing a long rest, the warlock can use an action while holding it to regain one warlock spell slot.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Rod of the Pact Keeper, p. 197 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the rod grants a limited boost; dial: its rarity sets the bonus and a long rest gates slot recovery; in-world reason: its magic is restricted to warlocks and replenishes slowly.

rules.statement: While holding the rod of absorption, you can use your reaction to absorb a spell that targets only you and has no area effect, canceling it and storing energy equal to its spell level. It can store at most 50 levels over its lifetime; a spell that would exceed its capacity is not absorbed, and a spellcaster holding it can spend stored levels to create spell slots no higher than 5th level or the caster’s own slot level, whichever is lower.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Rod of Absorption, pp. 195–196 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a personal spell can be canceled and its energy retained; dial: the 50-level lifetime capacity and slot-level ceiling limit use; in-world reason: the rod can hold only finite spell energy.

rules.statement: While wearing the robe of stars, you can use an action to enter the Astral Plane with what you wear and carry, then use another action to return to the plane you left. You reappear in your last space there, or in the nearest unoccupied space if it is occupied.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Robe of Stars, p. 194 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the robe enables travel to and from the Astral Plane; dial: each transition costs an action and return placement is constrained; in-world reason: the robe supplies a bounded route rather than unrestricted travel.

rules.statement: While attuned to a robe of the archmagi, you gain its benefits only if its color matches your alignment, and you must be a sorcerer, warlock, or wizard to attune to it. While wearing it without armor, your base AC is 15 plus your Dexterity modifier, you have advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects, and your spell save DC and spell attack bonus each increase by 2.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Robe of the Archmagi, p. 194 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement and wearing grant defenses and spell boosts; dial: class and alignment restrict who can bind to it, and the AC benefit requires no armor; in-world reason: the robe’s magic is aligned to a particular nature and wearer.

rules.statement: While wearing the robe of eyes, you see in all directions, gain advantage on sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks, have 120-foot darkvision, and can see invisible creatures and objects and into the Ethereal Plane within 120 feet. Its eyes cannot be shut or averted; a light spell cast on the robe or daylight cast within 5 feet blinds you for 1 minute, with a Constitution save at the end of each turn (DC 11 for light, DC 15 for daylight) ending the blindness on a success.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Robe of Eyes, pp. 193–194 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the robe expands sight across ordinary and hidden targets; dial: its eyes cannot be voluntarily closed and certain light magic causes temporary blindness; in-world reason: the robe’s persistent vision is both benefit and vulnerability.

rules.statement: While wearing the robe of scintillating colors, you can use an action and expend 1 of its 3 charges to dazzle until the end of your next turn. Creatures that can see you have disadvantage on attacks against you, and creatures in the bright light that can see you when activated must succeed on a saving throw or be stunned until the effect ends; the robe regains 1d3 charges daily at dawn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Robe of Scintillating Colors, p. 194 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a charge produces a brief dazzling defense and stun effect; dial: the duration and daily charge recovery bound its use; in-world reason: the robe’s display can overwhelm onlookers only briefly.

rules.statement: While holding the rod of security, you can use an action to transport yourself and up to 199 willing creatures you can see to a chosen paradise in an extraplanar space. Visitors regain hit points each hour as if spending 1 Hit Die and do not age there, but may remain only up to 200 days divided by the number present; when the time expires or you end the effect with an action, all return to their original locations or nearest unoccupied spaces, and the rod cannot be used again for 10 days.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Rod of Security, p. 197 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the rod creates temporary refuge and transports a group; dial: willingness, group size, stay duration, return placement, and a 10-day cooldown limit it; in-world reason: the refuge is a temporary extraplanar sanctuary.

rules.statement: When the sphere of annihilation contacts a planar portal or an extradimensional space, roll d100: on 01–50 the sphere is destroyed, on 51–85 it passes through or enters, and on 86–00 a spatial rift sends every creature and object within 180 feet, including the sphere, to a random plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Sphere of Annihilation, p. 201 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: contact between the sphere and planar spaces produces one of three outcomes; dial: the d100 determines the consequence; in-world reason: the sphere destabilizes planar boundaries unpredictably.

rules.statement: A spell scroll can be read as an action to cast its spell without providing components if the spell is on your class’s spell list; otherwise, it is unintelligible. If the spell is on your list but above the level you can normally cast, make a spellcasting-ability check against DC 10 plus the spell’s level; failure removes the spell without effect, while casting also consumes the scroll.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Spell Scroll, p. 200 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the scroll provides a one-use casting; dial: class-list eligibility and a level-based check gate access, and either resolution consumes it; in-world reason: the written magic is fragile and not universally readable.

rules.statement: The staff of the magi can use a reaction to absorb a spell cast by another creature that targets only you, canceling it and gaining charges equal to the spell’s level. If this raises the staff above 50 charges, it explodes using its retributive-strike effect.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Staff of the Magi, p. 203 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a targeted spell can be canceled and converted to staff charges; dial: the staff’s 50-charge ceiling turns excess energy into an explosion; in-world reason: the staff cannot safely contain more magic.

rules.statement: Using the rod of rulership, you can use an action to command creatures you choose that you can see within 120 feet; each must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom save or be charmed for 8 hours and regard you as a trusted leader. The charm ends for a target if you or your companions harm it or you command it to act against its nature; the rod recharges at dawn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Rod of Rulership, p. 197 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed saves bind targets to regard you as a trusted leader; dial: range, save, duration, conduct limits, and daily use constrain control; in-world reason: coercive authority breaks when abused.

rules.statement: When attuned to the shield of missile attraction, you have resistance to damage from ranged weapon attacks, but the shield curses you until remove curse or similar magic ends it. While the curse remains, removing the shield does not help, and ranged weapon attacks against targets within 10 feet of you target you instead.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Shield of Missile Attraction, p. 200 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement grants resistance but redirects nearby ranged attacks; dial: the curse persists after removing the shield until specifically ended; in-world reason: its protection is inseparable from its harmful attraction.

rules.statement: When you expend 1 charge from the Wand of Wonder, choose a creature, object, or point within 120 feet, then roll d100 and apply the corresponding table result. If the result casts a spell, its save DC is 15 and its range is 120 feet if it normally has a range in feet; center area effects on the chosen target and include it, and randomly select among multiple possible subjects.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Wand of Wonder, p. 212 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: a charged activation produces an unpredictable result; the in-world cost is one charge, and spending the last charge risks destroying the wand.

rules.statement: The Wand of Wonder’s d100 results include spells and other effects: for example, some cast spells, some change the user or target, some create weather, plants, gems, or an animal, and some blind, restrain, or petrify. A result that petrifies can be ended by greater restoration or similar magic.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Wand of Wonder, pp. 212–213 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: the table mixes beneficial, harmful, and incidental outcomes; the in-world reason is the wand’s uncontrolled magic.

rules.statement: A Well of Many Worlds unfolds onto a solid surface and opens a two-way portal to another world or plane, with the destination chosen by the DM. It can be folded closed using an action, and after opening a portal it cannot open another for 1d8 hours.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Well of Many Worlds, p. 213 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: opening provides passage but not destination control; the in-world limit is a recovery interval of 1d8 hours.

rules.statement: A creature attuned to the Sword of Wounding can, once per turn when it hits with the weapon, inflict a wound. At the start of each wounded creature’s turn, it takes 1d4 necrotic damage per wound, then can make a DC 15 Constitution save to end all these wounds; alternatively, it or a creature within 5 feet can use an action to make a DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check to end them on success.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Sword of Wounding, p. 207 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a successful hit creates recurring harm; the target can end it through a successful save or a nearby helper’s action and check.

rules.statement: Damage dealt by the Sword of Wounding cannot be restored by regeneration, magic, or other means; it is regained only after a short or long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Sword of Wounding, p. 207 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
