rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recovery is delayed until rest, imposing a lasting cost on victims.

rules.statement: A sentient magic item acts as an NPC under the DM’s control, and the item—not its wielder—controls its activated properties. A cooperative relationship permits normal access; if the relationship is strained, it can suppress those properties or turn them against the wielder.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Sentient Magic Items, p. 214 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: access depends on the relationship with the item; the in-world cost of conflict is lost or hostile use of its powers.

rules.statement: When a wielder acts against a sentient item’s alignment or purpose, the item can contest the wielder with a Charisma check. If the item wins, it can demand compliance; refusal lets it prevent attunement, suppress activated properties, or attempt to control the wielder.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Conflict, p. 216 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: a contested check gives the item leverage; the in-world cost of defying it is impaired access or loss of agency.

rules.statement: If a sentient item tries to control its wielder, the wielder makes a Charisma save against DC 12 + the item’s Charisma modifier. On a failure, the wielder is charmed for 1d12 hours and must try to obey the item; taking damage allows another save to end the effect, and the item cannot try this again until the next dawn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Conflict, p. 216 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: failed resistance imposes a long-lasting charm; damage offers another chance to break it, while the item’s attempt is limited to once per day.

rules.statement: A sentient item can communicate through emotion, thoughts, speech, or telepathy, and can perceive nearby surroundings within a range determined for the item. Its characteristics and any special purpose shape its behavior and willingness to cooperate.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Communication; Senses; Special Purpose, pp. 214, 216 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the item’s awareness and communication are bounded by its chosen senses and communication mode.

rules.statement: The Wand of Enemy Detection can spend 1 charge and an action to reveal the direction, but not distance, of the nearest hostile creature within 60 feet for 1 minute. It can detect hostile creatures even if they are ethereal, invisible, disguised, or hidden; the effect ends if the holder stops holding the wand.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Wand of Enemy Detection, p. 210 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sensing costs a charge and requires holding the wand; it gives direction but withholds distance.

rules.statement: The Tome of the Stilled Tongue lets an attuned wizard holding it cast a spell written in it as a bonus action without using a spell slot or verbal or somatic components. This can be used once until the next dawn; removing the tongue from the cover permanently erases every spell in the tome.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Tome of the Stilled Tongue, pp. 208–209 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: the book grants a spell without the usual slot or components, but only once per day; removing its tongue destroys its stored spell contents.

rules.statement: A spell attack made while holding the attuned Wand of the War Mage ignores half cover and gains an attack-roll bonus set by the wand’s rarity: +1, +2, or +3.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Wand of the War Mage, p. 212 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the benefit requires attunement and holding the wand; its magnitude is limited by the item’s rarity.

rules.statement: An artifact normally cannot be damaged; it can be destroyed only by its individually specified weakness, which may require research or completing a quest to discover.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Destroying Artifacts, p. 221 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: an artifact resists ordinary destruction; dial: set its unique weakness and the effort to learn it, since destruction requires a rare circumstance.

rules.statement: While attuned, a minor detrimental property can impose a continuing penalty or nearby effect, such as disadvantage on spell saves, blindness when more than 10 feet from the artifact, or preventing creatures within 300 feet from resting.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Minor Detrimental Properties, p. 220 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the selected detriment persists during attunement; dial: choose or roll its scope and severity, with the bearer paying the ongoing cost.

rules.statement: A major detrimental property can impose lasting bodily, mental, or behavioral consequences; examples include losing speech, gaining vulnerability to all damage, or being compelled to complete a quest as if under geas until it is completed.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Major Detrimental Properties, pp. 220–221 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the detriment applies on attunement or for as long as attunement lasts, as specified; dial: select its severity and duration, with significant risks to the bearer.

rules.statement: Attuning to the Eye requires removing your own eye and pressing the artifact into the socket; it grafts in place and remains until death, and removing it kills you. Attuning to the Hand similarly requires cutting off your left hand and grafting the artifact to the stump; removing it also kills you.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Eye and Hand of Vecna, p. 224 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: gaining either artifact requires permanent bodily sacrifice and makes removal fatal; dial: none—the bodily cost is fixed by the rule.

rules.statement: After studying the Book of Exalted Deeds for 80 hours, you gain its benefits, but lose them if you do no kindness or generosity for 10 days or willingly do evil; the book then leaves you. An evil creature attempting to read it takes 24d6 radiant damage, which cannot be reduced or avoided.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Book of Exalted Deeds, p. 222 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the benefits require sustained good conduct and can be lost; dial: none—the required study time, conduct, and harm to evil readers are specified.

rules.statement: After 80 hours of study, the Book of Vile Darkness grants benefits and lets its attuned reader alter its contents in ways that advance evil. A non-evil creature attuning to it must make a DC 17 Charisma save or become neutral evil; the book disappears if its bearer does no evil within 10 days or willingly does good, and death while attuned imprisons the bearer’s soul so it cannot be restored to life.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Book of Vile Darkness, p. 223 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: power is conditional on serving evil, with alignment and post-death costs; dial: none—the passage supplies the study, conduct, and save thresholds.

rules.statement: To control an Orb of Dragonkind while attuned, you use an action to look into it and speak its command word, then make a DC 15 Charisma check. Success gives you control while you remain attuned; failure charms you for that duration, prevents you from ending attunement voluntarily, and lets the orb cast suggestion on you at will.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Orb of Dragonkind, p. 225 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control depends on a Charisma check, and failure gives the orb influence; dial: none—the DC and consequences are explicit.

rules.statement: A charm can grant an effect or spell use without attunement; spell use from a charm needs no spell slot or components. Charges or uses may be limited, and the charm vanishes when its stated use limit or duration ends.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Charms, p. 228 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the gift is temporary or use-limited and requires no attunement; dial: specify the uses or duration, which is the gift’s finite cost.

rules.statement: A charm cannot function in an antimagic field, and its effects can be dispelled, but the charm itself cannot be removed from its bearer except by wish.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Charms, p. 228 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: antimagic and dispelling suppress or end effects, but ordinary removal is blocked; dial: none—the exceptions are stated.

rules.statement: A blessing lasts forever unless its granting god takes it away, is not suppressed by an antimagic field, and cannot benefit a creature more than once from the same blessing. There is no absolute limit on how many different blessings a creature may receive, though having more than one at once should be rare.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Blessings, p. 228 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: blessings persist but remain subject to the giver’s revocation; dial: keep simultaneous blessings rare, reflecting the exceptional nature of divine favor.

rules.statement: When you wield the Axe of the Dwarvish Lords while attuned, it grants listed benefits only if you are a dwarf; a non-dwarf attuned to it is cursed, gradually taking on dwarf-like appearance over seven days without gaining dwarf traits. Removing the curse undoes the physical change, but ending attunement alone does not remove the curse.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Axe of the Dwarvish Lords, p. 222 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ancestry gates the benefits and non-dwarves incur a persistent curse; dial: none—the seven-day transformation and curse-ending condition are specified.

rules.statement: If the Book of Exalted Deeds is opened, only an attuned creature can release its clasp; after 80 hours of study, that creature gains its benefits, while other readers gain no benefits from viewing its pages.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Book of Exalted Deeds, p. 222 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement gates access and study gates benefits; dial: none—the access condition and 80-hour cost are explicit.

rules.statement: A character can gain either a 2-point increase to one ability score or 1 point to two scores, with a score capped at 30; alternatively, the character can gain a new feat subject to the DM’s approval. These options can be awarded repeatedly instead of an epic boon.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Alternatives to Epic Boons (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: award one advancement reward; dial: the DM chooses whether to use these options instead of a boon, to fit campaign progression.

rules.statement: A character who accepts special training must spend downtime with a skilled trainer and is guaranteed a benefit: inspiration at dawn for 1d4 + 6 days, proficiency in a skill, or a feat.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Training (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: training costs downtime; dial: choose the benefit and availability, reflecting the trainer’s time and access.

rules.statement: Epic boons are optional rewards for 20th-level characters, usually bestowed after a major achievement. As an advancement option, the DM may grant one boon for each 30,000 XP earned beyond 355,000 XP; a boon generally cannot be gained more than once unless it says otherwise.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Epic Boons (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: no boon unless the DM awards one; dial: tie exceptional power to major deeds or excess XP.

rules.statement: After a melee weapon attack misses, the character may choose to make it hit instead; this can be used once, refreshing after a short rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Boon of Combat Prowess (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one converted miss per short rest; dial: availability of the boon sets how often combat certainty is possible.

rules.statement: As an action, the character can cast misty step without a spell slot or components, then cannot do so again until finishing a short rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Boon of Dimensional Travel (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one action-powered use per short rest; dial: the boon’s rarity determines access to short-range magical movement.

rules.statement: The character’s hit point maximum increases by 40.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Boon of Fortitude (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a permanent 40-point increase; dial: granting the boon raises the character’s capacity to survive harm.

rules.statement: The character gains a 9th-level spell slot if they do not already have one.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Boon of High Magic (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant only if the character lacks such a slot; dial: the boon expands top-tier spell capacity.

rules.statement: The character no longer ages, is immune to effects that age them, and cannot die of old age.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Boon of Immortality (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: aging and death from old age are removed; dial: this boon changes the character’s lifespan and vulnerability.

rules.statement: When taking damage from any source, the character may reduce that damage to 0; this can be done once per short rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Boon of Invincibility (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: negate one instance of damage per short rest; dial: the boon determines how often harm can be wholly prevented.

rules.statement: The character can ignore any creature’s damage resistances.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Boon of Irresistible Offense (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resistance does not reduce the character’s damage; dial: this boon bypasses a defensive rule.

rules.statement: The character can add 1d10 to an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw they make; the use refreshes after a short rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Boon of Luck (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one self-directed roll boost per short rest; dial: the boon grants limited control over uncertain outcomes.

rules.statement: When a check or saving throw misses its target by only 1 or 2, the DM may turn the failure into success but attach a complication or hindrance. A DM may also complicate a success that meets the target exactly.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Resolution and Consequences — Success at a Cost (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: off; dial: optional; the character gets the intended result but pays through a new obstacle or setback.

rules.statement: The DM may give different consequences for failures of different sizes; for example, failing a trap-disarm check by 5 or more can trigger the trap, while a smaller failure does not. A natural 20 or 1 on an ability check or saving throw has no automatic special effect, though the DM may choose to make its outcome more consequential.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Resolution and Consequences — Degrees of Failure; Critical Success or Failure (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: off; dial: optional; larger margins or exceptional rolls can change consequences at the DM’s discretion.

rules.statement: On a map, foot travelers cover 20/30/40 feet per minute in a dungeon at slow/normal/fast pace, and 2/3/4 city squares per minute when each square is 100 feet. At province scale, with one-mile hexes, they cover 2/3/4 hexes per hour or 18/24/30 per day; at kingdom scale, with six-mile hexes, they cover 1 hex per 3/2/1.5 hours, or 3/4/5 per day.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Exploration — Using a Map; Map Travel Pace (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: on; dial: travel pace; faster progress trades off against the caution or endurance associated with slower travel.

rules.statement: For travel driven by flight, magic, an engine, wind, or a current, convert speed to distance by multiplying speed by 10 for feet per minute, or dividing speed by 10 for miles per hour. For daily distance, multiply the hourly rate by the hours traveled (typically 8); fast pace adds one-third and slow pace reduces it by one-third.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Exploration — Special Travel Pace (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: on; dial: special movement; powered or naturally driven travel avoids ordinary walking limits, while pace still adjusts the distance.

rules.statement: On a clear day, outdoor visibility is about 2 miles, limited by obstructions; rain reduces it to 1 mile, and fog to 100–300 feet. From a high vantage point on a clear day, visibility can reach 40 miles.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Exploration — Visibility Outdoors (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: on; dial: weather and vantage; conditions and obstructions constrain what travelers can see.

rules.statement: If neither side is stealthy, creatures notice one another once within sight or hearing range. Otherwise, compare the hiding group’s Dexterity (Stealth) checks with the other group’s passive Wisdom (Perception).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Exploration — Noticing Other Creatures (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: on; dial: stealth; concealment can delay detection, but only against observers who fail to notice it.

rules.statement: Tracking requires a Wisdom (Survival) check, with no roll needed for obvious tracks. Suggested DCs include 10 for dirt or grass, 15 for bare stone, +5 for each day since passage, and −5 when the creature left a trail such as blood; a failed check loses the trail, but a careful search can find it again in 10 minutes in a confined area or 1 hour outdoors.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Exploration — Tracking; Tracking DCs (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: on; dial: tracking difficulty; terrain, elapsed time, and signs left behind determine the effort needed to follow a trail.

rules.statement: An interacting creature begins friendly, indifferent, or hostile. Friendly creatures usually help when there is no risk, indifferent creatures need a successful Charisma check to be persuaded, and hostile creatures require one or more challenging checks and may be impossible to sway; conversation can shift attitude by at most one step in a single interaction.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Social Interaction — Starting Attitude; Conversation (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: on; dial: attitude; willingness depends on the creature’s disposition and the risks or costs of helping.

rules.statement: At the request point, an active participant can make a Charisma check, with Persuasion, Deception, or Intimidation potentially applying. The creature’s attitude sets reaction thresholds: friendly creatures accept no-risk requests at DC 0, minor risk at 10, and significant risk at 20; indifferent creatures give no help at 0, accept no-risk requests at 10, and minor risk at 20; hostile creatures oppose at 0, give no help at 10, and accept no-risk requests at 20.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Social Interaction — Charisma Check; Conversation Reaction (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: on; dial: social outcome; greater risk or sacrifice requires a higher check, and disposition changes the response.

rules.statement: A substantial, helpful contribution from another participant gives the Charisma check advantage; a counterproductive or offensive contribution gives it disadvantage. Repeated attempts may achieve nothing or risk angering the creature and making it hostile.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Social Interaction — Aiding the Check; Multiple Checks; Repeat? (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: on; dial: group support and retry risk; allies can help or hinder, and pressing the request can worsen the relationship.

rules.statement: A destructible object can be assigned AC and hit points; suggested AC ranges from 11 for cloth, paper, or rope to 23 for adamantine. Objects are immune to poison and psychic damage, and a damage threshold blocks all damage from an attack or effect below the threshold; sufficiently large objects can be divided into sections with separate hit points.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Objects — Statistics for Objects; Object Armor Class; Damage Threshold (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: on; dial: object resilience; material, size, damage type, and any threshold limit what can damage an object.

rules.statement: Optional flanking rules grant advantage on melee attacks against an enemy when allies occupy qualifying opposite positions adjacent to it; a creature that cannot see the enemy or is incapacitated cannot flank. Optional facing rules restrict normal targeting to a creature’s front and side arcs, make attacks from its rear have advantage, and allow the creature to change facing at the end of its move or as a reaction when another creature moves.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Combat — Optional Rule: Flanking; Optional Rule: Facing (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: off; dial: tactical positioning; flanking rewards encirclement, while facing exposes a creature’s rear and constrains its awareness.

rules.statement: A chase uses initiative; each participant can move and take one action on its turn. A participant may Dash without a check a number of times equal to 3 + its Constitution modifier; each additional Dash requires a DC 10 Constitution check at turn’s end or adds one exhaustion level, and exhaustion level 5 removes the participant from the chase.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 8, Chases—Beginning a Chase; Dashing (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow repeated sprinting; dial: extra effort risks exhaustion and level 5 stops the runner.

rules.statement: At the end of each chase round, if the quarry has not escaped or been caught, it makes a Dexterity (Stealth) check against pursuers’ passive Wisdom (Perception); it escapes if its result exceeds the highest score. The check fails automatically if the lead pursuer never loses sight of it, and circumstances can grant advantage or disadvantage.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 8, Chases—Ending a Chase (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use visibility and passive detection; dial: escape depends on losing sight and situational advantages.

rules.statement: At the end of each participant’s turn in a chase, that participant rolls a d20 for a complication; if one occurs, it affects the next participant in initiative order. Either the roller or the affected participant can spend Inspiration to negate it.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 8, Chases—Chase Complications (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: complications can interrupt a pursuit; dial: a random roll creates risk, while Inspiration can cancel it.

rules.statement: Urban and wilderness chase complication tables use a d20: results 11–20 cause no complication, while results 1–10 specify obstacles or hazards. Those hazards can require checks or saves, slow movement, or inflict effects such as damage, prone, restrained, blinded, or an opportunity attack.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 8, Urban Chase Complications; Wilderness Chase Complications (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use a random complication table; dial: terrain hazards impose checks, lost movement, or harm.

rules.statement: A disease can have any chosen transmission, eligible targets, symptoms, and cure; the passage does not impose a shared disease procedure. Some diseases can affect only particular creature types or origins, or spare specified groups.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 8, Diseases (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: disease rules are individually defined; dial: the DM chooses who is susceptible and how infection works.

rules.statement: A creature exposed to sewer plague must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution save or become infected; symptoms begin after 1d4 days. It gains one exhaustion level, regains only half the usual hit points from spent Hit Dice, and regains none from a long rest; after each long rest it saves against DC 11, gaining exhaustion on failure or losing one on success, and recovers if a success lowers exhaustion below 1.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 8, Diseases—Sewer Plague (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed infection and recovery cycle; dial: failed daily saves worsen exhaustion, while success reduces it.

rules.statement: A creature that drinks water tainted by sight rot must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution save or be infected. One day later, sight-based attacks and ability checks take a −1 penalty that worsens by 1 after each long rest; at −5 the creature is blinded until magic restores its sight, while three doses of Eyebright ointment cure the disease.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 8, Diseases—Sight Rot (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the impairment worsens over time; dial: treatment can prevent one step per dose and three doses cure it.

rules.statement: A creature exposed to a poison uses the poison’s listed Constitution save and effect. Exposure depends on type: contact affects exposed skin, ingested poison requires swallowing a dose, inhaled poison is breathed in, and injury poison applies when slashing or piercing damage comes from a coated weapon or ammunition.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 8, Poisons (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the poison’s stated save and effect; dial: the delivery type limits how exposure occurs.

rules.statement: A character can harvest poison from a dead or incapacitated poisonous creature in 1d6 minutes by succeeding on a DC 20 Intelligence (Nature) check; poisoner’s-kit proficiency can substitute if the character lacks Nature proficiency. Success yields one dose, failure yields none, and failure by 5 or more exposes the character to the creature’s poison.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 8, Crafting and Harvesting Poison (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require time and a difficult check; dial: failure can waste the opportunity or expose the harvester.

rules.statement: Short-term madness lasts 1d10 minutes and uses the short-term table; long-term madness lasts 1d10 × 10 hours and uses the long-term table. Indefinite madness instead gives a flaw that lasts until cured; calm emotions suppresses madness, lesser restoration ends short- or long-term madness, and greater restoration or stronger magic is needed for indefinite madness.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 8, Madness—Madness Effects; Curing Madness (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: determine a mental effect and duration from its category; dial: stronger, indefinite effects require stronger treatment.

rules.statement: When proficiency dice are used instead of a fixed proficiency bonus, a character rolls the die listed for its level in place of adding the bonus to an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw; a feature that doubles proficiency allows two proficiency-die rolls instead of one.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 9, Proficiency Dice (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: use variable dice instead of a fixed bonus; this makes training less predictable.

rules.statement: For a noncombat challenge with meaningful failure risk, the DM may award XP as if it were a combat encounter of comparable difficulty. A major milestone is worth the XP of a hard encounter and a minor milestone the XP of an easy encounter; alternatively, the DM can award levels by sessions or story goals instead of tracking XP.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 8, Noncombat Challenges; Milestones; Level Advancement Without XP (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: award advancement for risky challenges or milestones; session- or story-based leveling removes XP tracking.

rules.statement: A character begins at 1st level with 5 hero points; at each level gained, discard any unspent points and reset the total to 5 plus half the character’s level. After making an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw but before its result takes effect, the player may spend 1 point to roll a d6 and add it to the d20; a point can also turn a failed death save into a success, and only 1 point can be spent per roll.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Hero Points (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: hero points make outcomes more forgiving; the limited, level-reset pool constrains how often luck can intervene.

rules.statement: When a failed Sanity saving throw causes long-term or indefinite madness, reduce the character’s Sanity by 1. Greater restoration can restore Sanity lost this way, and Sanity can also increase through level advancement.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Sanity Score (p. 266) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: alien horrors can leave lasting mental damage; restoration magic or advancement can repair the loss.

rules.statement: When a character confronts a threat they have no hope of overcoming, the DM can call for a Wisdom save at a circumstance-based DC; failure frightens the character for 1 minute. At the end of each of the character’s turns, a successful repeat save ends the effect.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Fear (p. 266) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: fear temporarily restricts a character’s choices; repeated saves provide a route to recovery.

rules.statement: After a short rest, a character cannot spend Hit Dice until someone uses one charge of a healer’s kit to treat them.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Healer’s Kit Dependency (p. 266) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: recovery requires medical supplies; the kit charge limits access to healing.

rules.statement: As an action, a character can use a healing surge and spend up to half their Hit Dice, rolling each die and adding their Constitution modifier to regain that many hit points. They may choose to spend another die after each roll, but cannot use another surge until finishing a short or long rest; a short rest restores Hit Dice equal to one quarter of character level, minimum 1, and a long rest restores all spent Hit Dice.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Healing Surges (pp. 266–267) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: a surge converts a limited Hit Die reserve into combat healing; rest gates its reuse and replenishes the reserve.

rules.statement: Under the gritty-realism rest variant, a short rest takes 8 hours and a long rest takes 7 days. Under epic heroism, those durations are 5 minutes and 1 hour; the DM may limit long-rest spell recovery to half of maximum slots, rounded down, and to slots of 5th level or lower, requiring a full 8-hour rest for complete recovery and for slots of 6th level or higher.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Rest Variants (p. 267) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: rest schedules alter recovery pace; longer rests slow adventuring, while restricted spell recovery moderates rapid-rest play.

rules.statement: A character who has not learned to use firearms can gain proficiency through the Player’s Handbook downtime training rules, provided enough ammunition is available for practice. Firearm ammunition is destroyed on use; a burst-fire weapon can instead attack every creature in a 10-foot cube within normal range, each making a DC 15 Dexterity save or taking normal weapon damage, and this uses 10 pieces of ammunition.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Firearms: Proficiency and Properties (pp. 267–268) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: firearm use consumes ammunition and may require training; burst fire trades ten shots for an area attack.

rules.statement: To work out unfamiliar technology, a character makes Intelligence checks until they achieve 2 successes for a simple device or 4 for a complex one. A total of 9 or lower on a check counts as a failure and wastes one charge or use if applicable; 10–14 is a failure, 15–19 is a success, and 20 or higher is a success that grants advantage on the next check; the device might break after 4 failures before a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Alien Technology (pp. 268–269) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: device operation is learned through risky investigation; failed attempts can waste charges or break the technology.

rules.statement: Each player starts with 1 plot point and may spend it during a session for one of the group’s chosen effects: establish a setting or situation detail everyone accepts, require the player to their right to add a complication, or take over as DM. Under the shared-pool rule, once every player has spent a point, each gains 1 point.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Plot Points (pp. 269–270) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: players can alter the story or its authorship; the limited point supply and group agreement constrain changes.

rules.statement: With initiative score, each creature’s initiative is 10 plus its Dexterity modifier instead of a roll. With side initiative, each side rolls an unmodified d20, higher goes first, ties are rerolled, and members of a side choose their own turn order; with speed factor, participants choose actions first, then roll initiative each round with applicable action and size modifiers.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Initiative Variants (pp. 270–271) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: these variants exchange random ordering or speed for predictability, teamwork, or action-dependent timing.

rules.statement: When a creature takes damage from one source equal to at least half its hit point maximum, it makes a DC 15 Constitution save; on failure, roll a d10: 1 drops it to 0 hit points, 2–3 drops it to 0 but stable, 4–5 stuns it until its next turn ends, 6–7 prevents reactions and imposes disadvantage on attacks and ability checks until then, and 8–10 prevents reactions until then.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Massive Damage (p. 273) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: a single severe blow can cause shock beyond ordinary damage; the saving throw and random table make the added danger uncertain.

rules.statement: When an injury-triggering event occurs—such as a critical hit, dropping to 0 hit points without being killed outright, or failing a death save by 5 or more—roll on the Lingering Injuries table. Results can impose lasting limits or penalties, and some injuries heal through specified magical healing or, for certain wounds, extended rest or successful daily treatment.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Injuries (pp. 272–273) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: serious trauma can persist after combat; injury-specific magic, rest, or treatment imposes different recovery costs.

rules.statement: When a creature or group meets a listed morale trigger, the creature or group’s leader makes a DC 10 Wisdom save; overwhelming opposition gives disadvantage, and a failed save makes them flee by the quickest route or surrender if escape is impossible. If the leader cannot save, the group’s next-highest-Charisma creature rolls instead.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Morale (p. 273) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: fear of defeat can redirect combatants; triggers and a saving throw make flight or surrender conditional.

rules.statement: To estimate a monster’s final challenge rating, calculate defensive and offensive ratings, average them, and round to the nearest rating; use that rating to set proficiency bonus and XP. A rating 0 monster is worth 0 XP if harmless, otherwise 10 XP.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 275, Average Challenge Rating (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated averaging and rounding procedure; dial: playtest-based adjustment; reason: observed play may show the estimate is inaccurate.

rules.statement: When adding class levels to a monster, give it the class features for each level, but not the class’s starting equipment; add one Hit Die of its normal size per level and keep proficiency bonus tied to challenge rating rather than class level. Recalculate challenge rating after any further adjustments.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 283, Monsters with Classes (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply class features with these exceptions; dial: adjust abilities and other statistics; reason: added levels may change threat unpredictably.

rules.statement: A monster’s saving throw DC can use the challenge-rating table or be calculated as 8 + proficiency bonus + the relevant ability modifier. Choose the ability that best fits the effect.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 278, Step 12. Save DCs (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: table or formula; dial: choose the relevant ability; reason: effects arise from different capabilities.

rules.statement: For a monster’s spell that deals damage, use the spell-damage table as a guide; it assumes half damage on a successful save or missed attack. If it deals no damage on a successful save, its damage may be increased by 25 percent.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 283, Spell Damage (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: follow the damage benchmark; dial: raise damage by up to the stated amount; reason: a successful defense otherwise prevents all damage.

rules.statement: A healing spell can use the spell-damage table to set the amount restored, but a cantrip should not restore hit points.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 284, Healing Spells (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the table as a benchmark; dial: none for cantrip healing; reason: minor magic is not intended to provide repeatable healing.

rules.statement: A magic item’s rarity can guide its maximum spell level and static bonus: suggested spell-effect ceilings range from 1st level for common items to 9th for legendary ones, while suggested bonuses range from +1 for uncommon items to +4 for legendary items.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 285, Power Level (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use rarity as a power ceiling; dial: tune the item within that guide; reason: stronger benefits make the item more valuable and disruptive.

rules.statement: Require attunement when passing an item among party members to share lasting benefits would disrupt play, or when its bonus could stack with benefits from other items and encourage excessive collection.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 285, Attunement (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require binding when sharing or stacking is disruptive; dial: decide item by item; reason: limits circumvention of intended access and bonus caps.

rules.statement: A monster can be given immunity to one or more debilitating conditions; the choice should fit its nature. Such immunity does not affect its challenge rating.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 279, Step 18. Condition Immunities (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use only fitting immunities; dial: select applicable conditions; reason: physiology or construction can make some states impossible.

rules.statement: An NPC built from a monster’s stat block can receive race ability modifiers and listed racial features, after which its challenge rating is recalculated if its statistics change.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 282–283, Creating NPCs from Scratch (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the listed racial adjustments; dial: recalculate when combat statistics shift; reason: inherited traits can alter capability and danger.

rules.statement: An eladrin can cast misty step once through its subrace trait, regaining that use after a short or long rest; the example pairs this with a +1 Intelligence increase and elf weapon proficiency.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 286, Example Subrace: Eladrin (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one use per rest interval; dial: retain or change the trait’s scope when designing a subrace; reason: planar-boundary magic is potent and limited.

rules.statement: An aasimar has resistance to necrotic and radiant damage, can see in dim light as if it were bright light within 60 feet and in darkness as if it were dim light there, and cannot distinguish color in darkness. Its walking speed is 30 feet, and it speaks, reads, and writes Common and Celestial.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Aasimar, p. 287 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial heritage and sensory details; celestial ancestry explains the resistances and vision.

rules.statement: An aasimar knows the light cantrip; at level 3 it can cast lesser restoration once, and at level 5 it can cast daylight once as a 3rd-level spell. Each spell use returns after a long rest, and Charisma is the spellcasting ability for these spells.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Aasimar — Celestial Legacy, p. 287 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial access by level and daily uses; the heritage grants limited celestial magic.

rules.statement: A class’s skill or tool proficiency can be exchanged for another without changing the class’s intended power; armor and weapon proficiencies can also be changed to suit a culture or faith. If an exchange removes a substantial benefit, the designer may add a compensating feature.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Changing Proficiencies, p. 287 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial proficiency selections; cultural institutions and religious rules determine training and restrictions.

rules.statement: A class’s spell list can be changed to alter its theme, but changing a warlock list requires care because warlocks recover spell slots on a short rest and may cast some spells more often per day than other spellcasters.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Changing Spell Lists, p. 287 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial spell access; short-rest recovery increases the practical supply of some spells.

rules.statement: A campaign may limit classes or subclasses to particular races or cultures, but the DM decides whether characters may break those limits and is encouraged to use such choices to develop the character’s story rather than simply refuse them.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Restricting Class Access, p. 287 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial eligibility; local traditions shape who is normally trained or able to enter a class.

rules.statement: A class feature may be replaced for a specific campaign need, but the replacement should contribute about as much to social interaction, exploration, or combat as the removed feature. Compare resource use and recovery timing, and playtest changes because replacing one kind of strength with another can unbalance the class.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Substituting Class Features, pp. 287–288 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial feature design; replacement costs and recovery should preserve the class’s overall usefulness.

rules.statement: A new class option should remain distinct in theme while being no more or less powerful than existing options, and its features should be compared with features of similar level and tested in play.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Creating New Class Options, p. 288 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial new options; comparison and testing limit unintended advantages.

rules.statement: Under the spell-point variant, a spellcaster spends points to create a spell slot and then casts a spell using that slot; cantrips cost no points. The caster cannot spend below 0 points and regains all spent points after a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Variant: Spell Points, pp. 288–289 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial flexible spell-slot creation; the caster’s finite point pool is the daily cost.

rules.statement: Spell-slot creation costs 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, and 13 points for spell levels 1 through 9, respectively. A character can create only one slot of each level 6 or higher between long rests.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Spell Point Cost, p. 288 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial high-level access; expensive slots and the one-per-level limit constrain burst casting.

rules.statement: The spell-point pool and maximum slot level depend on spellcaster level; paladin and ranger levels count as half, while Eldritch Knight fighter and Arcane Trickster rogue levels count as one-third. A character cannot create a slot above the table’s maximum even if it has enough points.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Spell Points by Level, p. 289 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial pool and ceiling by caster level; class progression limits the strongest slot available.

rules.statement: To generate a dungeon, roll a starting area, then extend each passage by rolling its next feature until it reaches a door or chamber; use the door, chamber, exit, and stairs tables when indicated. The DM can limit growth at the map edge, treat off-map passages as entrances, or use rerolls or substitutions when a result does not fit the intended dungeon.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Appendix A: Random Dungeons, pp. 290–292 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial dungeon size and rerolls; map boundaries or planned scope constrain procedural growth.

rules.statement: Dungeon hazards and obstacles can affect a room or a wider area; examples include an aura that prevents living creatures from regaining hit points, winds that halve speed and hinder ranged attacks, poisonous gas that deals 1d6 poison damage per minute, and barriers that block passage. Random traps are generated by choosing a trigger, a severity, and an effect.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Random Dungeon Hazards, Random Obstacles, and Random Traps, pp. 296–297 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial area and severity; environmental dangers obstruct movement or impose ongoing costs on those exposed.

rules.statement: To generate random dungeon dressing, roll once on each of the Noises, Air, and Odors tables; roll on the other dressing tables as often as desired, or select furnishings that fit the area.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dungeon Dressing (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; this is an optional procedure for adding environmental details.

rules.statement: When a touched object triggers a trick, it can age the first creature to touch it (01–03), animate itself or nearby objects (04–06), or ask three skill-testing questions and produce a reward if all are answered correctly (07–10).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Tricks table (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the severity of aging and the reward; the object’s effect supplies the cost or benefit.

rules.statement: A trick can grant resistance or vulnerability (11–13), or change a touched character’s alignment, personality, size, appearance, or sex (14–16).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Tricks table (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial which trait changes and for how long; the table gives no duration.

rules.statement: A trick can convert one substance into another (17–19), create a force field (20–22), or create an illusion (23–26).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Tricks table (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the materials, field, or illusion; the table specifies no limits or duration.

rules.statement: A trick can suppress magic items temporarily (27–29), enlarge or reduce characters (30–32), or speak a riddle through a magical mouth (33–35).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Tricks table (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the duration and affected items or characters; only temporary item suppression is specified.

rules.statement: A trick can cause confusion among creatures within 10 feet (36–38), give directions that may be true or false (39–41), or grant a wish (42–44).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Tricks table (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the confusion’s resolution and the wish’s limits; the table leaves these unspecified.

rules.statement: A trick can fly away to avoid being touched (45–47), cast a binding command on the characters (48–50), or increase, reduce, negate, or reverse gravity (51–53).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Tricks table (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the duration and scope; the table does not specify how characters resist or end the effects.

rules.statement: A trick can induce greed (54–56), hold an imprisoned creature (57–59), lock or unlock exits (60–62), or offer a chance game for a promised reward or valuable information (63–65).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Tricks table (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the stakes and release conditions; the table gives no resolution details for the game or imprisonment.

rules.statement: A trick can help or harm certain creature types (66–68), transform characters into other forms for 1 hour (69–71), or present a puzzle or riddle (72–75).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Tricks table (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the affected creature types and puzzle reward; the transformation lasts 1 hour.

rules.statement: A trick can prevent movement (76–78), release coins, gems, a magic item, or a map (79–81), or release, summon, or become a monster (82–84).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Tricks table (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the duration and the exact reward or monster; the table supplies possible outcomes but no further limits.

rules.statement: A trick can cast a persuasive suggestion on the characters (85–87), wail loudly when touched (88–90), or speak in ordinary speech, nonsense, poetry, song, spellcasting, or screams (91–93).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Tricks table (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the suggestion and its duration; the table does not specify how it resolves.

rules.statement: A trick can teleport characters elsewhere (94–97) or exchange the minds of two or more characters (98–00).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Tricks table (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the destination and the exchange’s duration; the table specifies neither.

rules.statement: A character who honors a chosen deity’s commands and taboos gains piety; opposing that deity, dishonoring it, damaging its temples, or obstructing its aims reduces piety. Piety cannot be converted into a fixed number here; the passage leaves how much is gained or lost to the DM.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 23, Piety (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; the DM sets piety changes, so the deity’s expectations and the character’s conduct determine the cost.

rules.statement: For each piety rank gained, the character can pray once per day for divine favor, usually a cleric spell such as bless; the favor may include a sign from the deity. High piety can also earn a lasting blessing or charm.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 23, Piety (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; the DM chooses persistent rewards, and continued devotion is the in-world price of divine favor.

rules.statement: A dead creature’s soul leaves its body, travels through the Astral Plane, and goes to the plane where its deity resides; without a deity, it goes to a plane matching its alignment.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 25, Bringing Back the Dead (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; death sends the soul along a route determined by its deity or alignment.

rules.statement: Returning a dead creature to life requires retrieving its soul from its destination plane and returning it to its body. A soul that does not wish to return cannot be restored; it knows the identity, alignment, and deity of the creature trying to revive it and can refuse based on that knowledge.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 25, Bringing Back the Dead (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; revival depends on retrieving the soul and obtaining its willingness, not merely having access to a spell.

rules.statement: Permanent teleportation circles in major cities can connect with teleport, plane shift, and teleportation circle spells. Because a circle can provide entry into a city, the city may protect it with military and magical guards.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 23, Teleportation Circles (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; the city’s defenses impose a security cost on using a circle as an entrance.

rules.statement: Greater deities cannot be summoned and generally stay out of mortal affairs; when one manifests an avatar, destroying that avatar does not harm the deity. Lesser deities have bodies somewhere in the planes and can be encountered by mortals.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 11, Divine Rank (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; divine rank limits whether mortals can summon, encounter, or harm a deity directly.

rules.statement: Quasi-deities do not hear or answer prayers, grant spells, or control aspects of mortal life, though they could theoretically become gods by gathering enough worshipers. They include demigods born of a deity and mortal, titans created by deities, and vestiges who have lost nearly all their worshipers.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 11, Divine Rank (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; quasi-divine status withholds ordinary divine services, while accumulated worship offers a possible route to godhood.

rules.statement: A planar portal is a stationary connection between a particular place on one plane and a particular place on another. It might be a passable opening, a structure or site present on multiple planes, or a vortex joining an elemental realm to a similar location.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 2, “Planar Portals,” p. 45 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial portal form; its endpoints and physical presentation depend on the setting.

rules.statement: A portal can require a time, situation, spoken command, or held key before it works. A randomly operating portal typically admits 1d6 + 6 travelers, then closes for 1d6 days.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 2, “Planar Portals,” p. 45 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial its trigger and capacity; access is limited by the portal’s local operating conditions.

rules.statement: Plane shift requires a forked metal rod attuned to the destination plane; making one costs at least 250 gp. Without specialized location information, the spell reaches the general vicinity of the intended place rather than a precise destination.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 2, “Spells,” pp. 46–47 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial destination precision; travel requires a costly, destination-specific component and may still leave a journey to complete.

rules.statement: Gate opens a portal to a specific point on another plane, bypassing much of the journey there, but it is a 9th-level spell and does not remove obstacles at the destination. A deity, demon lord, or similarly powerful being can prevent it from opening within its domain.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 2, “Spells,” p. 47 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the blocking entity; precise passage is powerful but can be denied within a powerful being’s territory.

rules.statement: The Astral Plane is a route to the Outer Planes, and travelers there do not age or need food or water. Astral-dwelling humanoids establish outposts elsewhere so their children can mature.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 2, “Astral Plane,” p. 47 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the plane’s other environmental traits; its stated protections do not provide for children’s growth.

rules.statement: On the Astral Plane, a creature moves by willing itself to move; in combat its speed in feet equals three times its Intelligence score.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 2, “Astral Plane,” p. 47 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial movement outside combat; combat movement is limited by the traveler’s Intelligence.

rules.statement: Astral projection sends a traveler’s consciousness through the Astral Plane and allows it to manifest on an Outer Plane as if physically present, but in a dreamlike state. Death in either plane does not itself cause actual harm; severing the silver cord in the Astral Plane, or killing the traveler’s helpless physical body on the Material Plane, causes true death.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 2, “Astral Projection,” p. 47 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial which threats can sever the cord; the projected traveler is protected except against specific failures.

rules.statement: Astral gateways to other planes appear as colored pools 1d6 × 10 feet in diameter. Finding the pool leading to a desired plane takes 1d4 × 10 hours of travel by chance.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 2, “Color Pools,” p. 47 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial pool destinations and colors; finding the desired exit costs uncertain travel time.

rules.statement: A psychic wind gives the whole traveling group one shared location result, then each affected traveler makes a DC 15 Intelligence save; only a failed save also suffers an individually rolled mental result. The location roll can add 1d6 or 3d10 hours, misdirect arrival, or send travelers through a color pool to a random plane; mental results include stun with repeat saves, madness, 11 or 22 psychic damage, or brief unconsciousness that ends if the creature takes damage or someone uses an action to wake it.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Psychic Wind Effects, p. 48 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the table when psychic wind strikes; dial: DM controls exposure and destination consequences; reason: the storm disrupts both route and mind.

rules.statement: The Border Ethereal overlaps the Material and Inner Planes; a traveler there can see the adjacent plane, but with limited range, and is ordinarily invisible and silent to its inhabitants. Ordinary attacks do not cross the boundary, solid objects do not impede Ethereal movement, and gravity does not constrain up-or-down movement; certain magical effects and living beings are exceptions.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Border Ethereal, p. 48 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use these boundary effects while in the Border Ethereal; dial: magical and living exceptions remain; reason: the overlap permits observation and passage without ordinary contact.

rules.statement: A curtain in the Deep Ethereal leads to a corresponding Border Ethereal region: its color identifies the Material Plane, Shadowfell, Feywild, or an Inner Plane. Travel between planes through the Deep Ethereal takes 1d10 × 10 hours regardless of endpoints; distance and measurable speed do not govern the journey, although combat movement uses normal speeds.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Deep Ethereal / Ethereal Curtains, p. 49 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the fixed travel-time roll and curtain destinations; dial: navigation and passage of time are hard to judge; reason: Deep Ethereal travel follows planar connections rather than distance.

rules.statement: An ether cyclone gives travelers warning when their passive Wisdom (Perception) is at least 15, for 1d4 rounds. If they cannot reach an exit, roll its effect: most often travel is extended, requiring each traveler to make a DC 15 Charisma save; if at least half succeed, delay the group 1d10 hours, otherwise double travel time. Other results send the group to a random plane’s Border Ethereal or, on a 20, into the Astral Plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Ether Cyclones / Ether Cyclone, p. 49 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve the cyclone table and group save; dial: travelers may seek an exit before impact; reason: the storm can delay or displace those caught in it.

rules.statement: A Fey crossing links a Material Plane place to its near-perfect Feywild counterpart; passage can be as simple as entering the site. Crossings usually open only under particular conditions, such as a full moon, a specified date, or carrying a particular item, and permanently changing the land on either side can close one.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Fey Crossings, p. 50 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: crossings obey their local opening conditions; dial: the DM sets those conditions and whether land alteration closes the route; reason: portals are tied to particular places and circumstances.

rules.statement: On leaving the Feywild, a creature makes a DC 10 Wisdom save; Fey creatures and creatures with Fey Ancestry automatically succeed. Failure erases memories of the time spent there, while success preserves them; magic that ends a curse can restore erased memories.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Optional Rules: Feywild Magic — Memory Loss, p. 50 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: this is an optional rule; reason: Feywild departure can cost memories, with a saving throw and restorative magic as limits.

rules.statement: After at least a day in the Feywild, the DM can choose a time shift or roll the Feywild Time Warp table when a creature or group leaves. A wish can remove the resulting effect; powerful fey might grant such a wish in exchange for the recipients accepting geas and completing a quest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Optional Rules: Feywild Magic — Time Warp, p. 50 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: time warp is optional and the DM may choose the shift; reason: correcting the temporal cost can involve a wish and a binding quest.

rules.statement: A nonnative visitor to the Shadowfell can be required, usually no more than once per day, to make a DC 10 Wisdom save; failure causes a randomly determined despair effect. If a despairing character fails again, the new effect replaces the old one; after a long rest the character can attempt a DC 15 Wisdom save to end it, and calm emotions or magic that removes a curse also ends it.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Optional Rule: Shadowfell Despair, p. 50 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: this is an optional rule and the DM chooses when to call for the save; reason: prolonged exposure can impose despair, removable by rest, spell, or curse-ending magic.

rules.statement: An incompatible visitor who spends a long rest on an Outer Plane must make a DC 10 Constitution save against psychic dissonance; failure adds one level of exhaustion. Good-versus-evil incompatibility applies, but lawful-versus-chaotic incompatibility does not apply on Mechanus or Limbo.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Optional Rule: Psychic Dissonance, p. 59 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: this is optional; reason: a plane’s moral nature wears down visitors out of tune with it.

rules.statement: The River Styx crosses the top layers of several Lower Planes, with tributaries reaching lower layers and allowing passage between layers; skilled ferrymen carry passengers between planes for a price. A non-fiend that tastes or touches its water is affected by feeblemind, resisted with a DC 15 Intelligence save.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Traveling the Outer Planes — The River Styx, p. 58 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the contact save and require payment for ferries; reason: the river provides routes but its water threatens minds and passage is not free.

rules.statement: On Mechanus, attacks and spells use their average damage instead of rolling damage dice; for example, 1d10 + 5 damage becomes 10. A non-lawful-neutral visitor who finishes a long rest there must make a DC 10 Wisdom save or become lawful neutral; the change ends after a day elsewhere, or can be ended by dispel evil and good.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Mechanus / Optional Rule: Imposing Order, p. 60 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: the alignment effect is optional; reason: Mechanus imposes regularity on damage and can press visitors toward its order.

rules.statement: The Outlands is a disk between the Outer Planes, with sixteen gate-towns around its edge; each town is built around a portal to one Outer Plane. Travel across the Outlands can take a traveler between areas themed after different planes without leaving that plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 67, The Outlands and Sigil (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the Outlands permits overland movement between planar-themed regions without requiring a planar crossing.

rules.statement: Sigil contains many portals to other planes and worlds. Portal keys, including command words or objects needed to operate particular portals, can be traded there.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 68, Sigil, City of Doors (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; portal access depends on locating and using the appropriate key.

rules.statement: Demiplanes are separate extradimensional spaces with their own physical laws; they can be created by magic or arise as isolated folds of reality, and can range from one room to an entire realm. When connected to another plane, entry can be as simple as stepping through a portal or passing through a mist wall.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 68, Demiplanes (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; entry is simple only where a connection exists.

rules.statement: Plane shift can theoretically take travelers to a demiplane, but obtaining the precisely tuned fork needed for that destination is extremely difficult; gate is a more dependable option if the caster knows the demiplane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 68, Demiplanes (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; travel is constrained by rare tuning and destination knowledge.

rules.statement: The Far Realm lies outside the known multiverse and may have distinct physical and magical laws. Its influence can warp matter into forms that defy ordinary geometry and biology.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 68, The Far Realm (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; exposure to alien planar influence can alter matter.

rules.statement: No well-known Far Realm portals are currently viable; ancient elves once opened a vast portal, but its location and even its home world are forgotten. Other lost portals might remain, marked by alien magic that mutates the surrounding area.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 68, The Far Realm (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; passage is rare and dangerous, with mutating effects around possible portals.

rules.statement: In a wild magic zone, whenever a spell is cast, roll on the Wild Magic Surge table in the Player’s Handbook to determine the result.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 109, Weird Locales (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the zone makes spellcasting trigger an unpredictable surge.

rules.statement: On a plane with planar vitality, creatures cannot be frightened or poisoned, and they are immune to disease and poison.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 67, Optional Rule: Planar Vitality (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; optional planar rule; the plane’s vitality suppresses these states and hazards.

rules.statement: If two potions are mixed, roll percentile dice to determine their combined result. Outcomes can make both potions ineffective, make one ineffective, halve both potions’ numerical effects and durations, let both work normally, double one potion’s numerical effects and duration, or make one potion’s simplest effect permanent; an effect that cannot be halved or doubled is unaffected by that adjustment.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Potion Miscibility (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial: the DM determines the permanent effect; in-world, mixing potions creates unpredictable magical interactions.

rules.statement: A creature that fails to cast a spell from a scroll must make a DC 10 Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, roll on the Scroll Mishap table: possible outcomes include force damage based on the spell’s level, misdirected or delayed effects, a harmless reversal, or a temporary strange effect.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Variant: Scroll Mishaps (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial: the DM rolls the mishap result; in-world, failed scroll magic can misfire unpredictably.

rules.statement: A magic item intended to be worn must be worn in the appropriate way; most adjust to the wearer’s size, though the DM can rule that an item only fits a particular size or shape. Whether an item works when worn by a nonhumanoid is also left to the DM’s judgment.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Wearing and Wielding Items (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial: the DM decides exceptions; in-world, an item’s physical design and magic determine who can use it.

rules.statement: A character normally can’t wear multiple items of certain kinds at once, including two pairs of footwear, two pairs of gloves, multiple bracers, multiple suits of armor, multiple headwear items, or multiple cloaks; the DM can allow exceptions. Paired items grant their benefits only when both parts are worn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Multiple Items of the Same Kind; Paired Items (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial: the DM may permit exceptions; in-world, the body and paired item design limit simultaneous use.

rules.statement: An item’s description specifies how it is activated. If activation requires an action, that action is not the Use an Item action, so features that alter that action cannot activate it; an item requiring a spoken command cannot be activated where sound is prevented.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Activating an Item; Command Word (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial: activation details are item-specific; in-world, the item requires its prescribed action or audible command.

rules.statement: The Amulet of the Planes lets its wearer spend an action to name a familiar location on another plane and make a DC 15 Intelligence check. Success casts plane shift; failure transports the wearer and creatures and objects within 15 feet to a random destination, determined by percentile roll: 1–60 is a random place on the named plane, while 61–100 is a random plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Amulet of the Planes (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial: the failed check’s destination is random; in-world, the amulet can misdirect planar travel.

rules.statement: A bag of holding can contain up to 500 pounds and 64 cubic feet, and weighs 15 pounds regardless of contents; retrieving an object takes an action. A breathing creature inside can survive for up to 10 minutes, then begins suffocating; overloading, piercing, or tearing the bag destroys it and scatters its contents in the Astral Plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Bag of Holding (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial: capacity and survival time are fixed; in-world, the bag’s extradimensional space has limited storage and air.

rules.statement: Putting a bag of holding, handy haversack, or portable hole inside another similar extradimensional space destroys both items and opens a one-way gate to the Astral Plane. Creatures within 10 feet are pulled through to a random Astral location, after which the gate closes.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Bag of Holding; Heward’s Handy Haversack; Portable Hole (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial: the destination is random; in-world, incompatible extradimensional spaces rupture into an Astral passage.

rules.statement: The Cubic Gate has six faces keyed to different planes, including the Material Plane. As an action, pressing a face once casts gate to its linked plane, or pressing it twice casts plane shift to transport targets there; each use costs one of its three charges, and it regains 1d3 charges daily at dawn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Cubic Gate (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial: the DM assigns the linked planes; in-world, each keyed face provides a limited planar route.

rules.statement: Dimensional shackles placed on an incapacitated Small, Medium, or Large creature prevent extradimensional movement, including teleportation and planar travel, but do not stop passage through an interdimensional portal. The wearer or a designated creature can remove them as an action; once every 30 days the bound creature can attempt a DC 30 Strength (Athletics) check to break free and destroy them.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dimensional Shackles (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial: escape is a very difficult, infrequent check; in-world, the shackles suppress dimensional movement but do not close portals.

rules.statement: A bag of tricks lets a user spend an action to pull out and throw a fuzzy object up to 20 feet; it becomes a creature determined by the bag’s color-specific d8 table.
