The creature is friendly and acts on the user’s turn; a bonus action can direct its next movement and action, and the bag stops working after three objects until the next dawn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Bag of Tricks (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial: creature identity is determined by the table; in-world, each stored object produces a temporary companion.

rules.statement: A potion of flying grants a flying speed equal to the drinker’s walking speed and the ability to hover for 1 hour. When the effect ends, a drinker still aloft falls unless another effect keeps them there.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Potion of Flying (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial: duration is fixed; in-world, the potion’s temporary mobility ends after an hour.

rules.statement: A portable hole unfolds against a solid surface to create a 10-foot-deep extradimensional space; it does not create a passage through to another location. Folding it closes the space while leaving contents inside, and an occupant can force an exit with an action and a successful DC 10 Strength check; a breathing occupant can survive 10 minutes before suffocating.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Portable Hole (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial: occupants have a limited escape route and air supply; in-world, the hole is storage rather than a portal.

rules.statement: A robe of the archmagi can be attuned to only by a creature whose alignment matches the robe’s good, neutral, or evil designation. While wearing it without armor, the wearer’s base AC is 15 plus Dexterity, has advantage on saves against spells and other magic, and gains +2 to spell save DCs and spell attack rolls.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 195, Robe of the Archmagi (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial only if alignment categories differ; access is restricted by the robe’s originating moral alignment.

rules.statement: A wearer can use an action to remove one patch from a robe of useful items, producing the object or creature it depicts. The robe has two patches each for a lantern, mirror, pole, rope, and sack, plus 4d4 additional patches; after the last patch is removed, it becomes an ordinary garment.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 195, Robe of Useful Items (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the patch contents; using the robe consumes its finite supply of stored objects.

rules.statement: A wizard copying a spell from a scroll must make an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 plus the spell’s level. The spell is copied only on a success, but the scroll is destroyed whether the check succeeds or fails.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 195, spell scroll copying (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the check difficulty; learning from a scroll risks consuming the source without gaining the spell.

rules.statement: A sphere of annihilation destroys matter it passes through or that passes through it, except for artifacts; an object or creature that merely touches it without being wholly engulfed takes 4d10 force damage. An uncontrolled sphere can be moved by a creature within 60 feet that uses an action and succeeds on a DC 25 Intelligence (Arcana) check; on failure, it moves 10 feet toward that creature.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 201, Sphere of Annihilation (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial control access; manipulating a dangerously destructive object can make it move toward the would-be controller.

rules.statement: When a sphere of annihilation contacts a planar portal or an extradimensional space, roll d100: on 01–50 the sphere is destroyed, on 51–85 it passes through or enters the space, and on 86–00 a spatial rift sends the sphere and every creature and object within 180 feet to a random plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 201, Sphere of Annihilation (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the destination only if the world’s planar map is fixed; contact can destroy the sphere or displace a broad area of beings and objects.

rules.statement: A creature holding the attuned staff of charming can spend an action and one of its 10 charges to cast charm person, command, or comprehend languages using its own spell save DC. The staff regains 1d8 + 2 charges at dawn; after its last charge is spent, a d20 roll of 1 makes it a nonmagical quarterstaff.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 201, Staff of Charming (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the charge recovery; borrowed spellcasting draws on a limited reserve and may ruin the staff.

rules.statement: A holder of the attuned staff of charming who fails a save against an enchantment spell targeting only them can turn that failure into a success, once per dawn. If they succeed against such a spell, they may use a reaction and spend one charge to reflect it at its caster as though they had cast it.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 201, Staff of Charming (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the daily defense; resisting or returning enchantment is limited by the dawn reset or the staff’s charges.

rules.statement: The wand of wonder’s listed random effects include spells and other outcomes such as weather, an uncontrolled animal appearing, an object shifting to the Ethereal Plane, or a creature being blinded or turned blue. Its table assigns each outcome a d100 range; the excerpt does not state the wand’s activation procedure.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: pp. 202–213, Wand of Wonder effect table (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial whether to supply omitted activation rules; random outcomes can produce uncontrolled effects rather than the intended result.

rules.statement: Using an action to spread the well of many worlds on a solid surface opens a two-way portal to a world or plane chosen by the DM. An action to fold the cloth closes the portal, and after opening one, the item cannot open another for 1d8 hours.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 213, Well of Many Worlds (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the destination; travel depends on an externally chosen endpoint and the cloth’s recovery interval.

rules.statement: A creature attuned to and wearing winged boots can fly at its walking speed for up to 4 hours, in one flight or several flights of at least 1 minute each. If airborne when the duration runs out, it descends 30 feet per round until landing; the boots recover 2 hours of flight for every 12 hours unused.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 214, Winged Boots (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial recharge timing; flight is a limited reserve, and exhaustion of it forces a gradual descent.

rules.statement: A sentient magic item acts as an NPC controlled by the DM, and the item—not its wielder—controls its activated properties. A wielder in good standing with the item can use those properties normally; if the relationship is strained, the item can suppress them.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 214, Sentient Magic Items (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial what constitutes a strained relationship; access to an item’s power depends on its independent will.

rules.statement: A character who gains the boon of planar travel chooses one plane other than the Material Plane. As an action, they can cast plane shift without a spell slot or components, targeting only themselves, to travel to that plane or return from it to the Material Plane; use recharges after a short rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 232, Boon of Planar Travel (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the chosen plane; travel is limited to the selected route and a short-rest recharge.

rules.statement: When a character faces a threat they have no hope of overcoming, the GM may call for a Wisdom save at a circumstance-based DC. On a failure, the character is frightened for 1 minute and can repeat the save at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 266, Fear (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f06)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use when the threat warrants it; dial: the GM sets the DC; in-world, the character’s fear fades as they regain composure.

rules.statement: After a horrific experience, the GM may call for a Charisma save at a DC based on its severity. On a failure, the character gains a short-term or long-term madness chosen by the GM or determined randomly.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 266, Horror (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f06)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply only when the experience merits horror; dial: the GM sets severity and the resulting madness; the cost is a potentially lasting mental consequence.

rules.statement: A character cannot spend Hit Dice after a short rest until someone uses one use of a healer’s kit to treat and bandage their wounds.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 266, Healer’s Kit Dependency (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f06)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: this optional healing constraint; the in-world cost is requiring supplies and treatment before recovery.

rules.statement: With this healing option, a long rest restores all spent Hit Dice. A short rest restores Hit Dice equal to one-quarter of the character’s level, with a minimum of one die.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 267, Healing Surges (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f06)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: pair this recovery rule with healing surges; the in-world limit is that short rests restore fewer dice than long rests.

rules.statement: Under slow natural healing, a character regains no hit points at the end of a long rest; instead, they can spend Hit Dice to recover hit points, as they do during a short rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 267, Slow Natural Healing (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f06)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: use for a grittier campaign; the in-world cost is prolonged recovery without magical healing.

rules.statement: Under epic heroism, a short rest lasts 5 minutes and a long rest lasts 1 hour. As an optional additional limit, spellcasters regain only half their maximum spell slots, rounded down, and only slots of 5th level or lower; a full rest restores all slots, including slots of 6th level or higher.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 267, Epic Heroism (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f06)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: use the shortened rests, and optionally the slot limit; the in-world tradeoff is faster recovery that may enable more frequent combat and spell use.

rules.statement: Under gritty realism, a short rest lasts 8 hours and a long rest lasts 7 days.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 267, Gritty Realism (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f06)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: use for a slower, less combat-focused campaign; the in-world cost is needing substantial time between full recoveries.

rules.statement: A GM can change a class’s skill or tool proficiencies without generally changing its power, or alter its armor and weapon proficiencies to reflect the setting; if the change weakens the class, the GM can compensate with a benefit.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Pages 287–288, Changing Proficiencies (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f06)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: customize classes to fit the world; the in-world restriction or benefit reflects the character’s culture or order.

rules.statement: A GM can replace a class’s spell list to change its flavor, but should be cautious with the warlock list because warlocks regain spell slots after a short rest and may use some spells more often per day than other spellcasters.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 288, Changing Spell Lists (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f06)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: customize spell access carefully; the in-world and balance cost is that short-rest slot recovery can increase repeated spell use.

rules.statement: A GM can restrict access to classes, subclasses, or other class options by associating them with particular races or cultures, and decides whether exceptions are allowed.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 288, Restricting Class Access (dnd5e-dmg-2014#f06)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: use setting-based access limits; the in-world reason is a tradition or culture’s control of training, while exceptions remain the GM’s choice.

rules.statement: A dragon’s hoard worth at least 15,000 gp can bind the dragon, its lair, and its territory in a magical connection that empowers legendary actions and spreads the dragon’s regional influence. Dragons commonly establish additional lairs as their hoards grow, with a new lair often tied to each additional 15,000 gp of hoard value.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragon Hoards, p. 69 (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: hoard value determines the connection; dial: scale regional reach and empowerment to the dragon’s treasure.

rules.statement: If a dragon’s lair contains less than 10,000 gp in treasure, it no longer counts as a lair: the dragon cannot take lair actions there, and the area’s regional effects end as if the dragon had died.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragon Hoards, p. 70 (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: below the stated treasure threshold, both lair actions and regional effects cease; the cost is loss or removal of the hoard.

rules.statement: Some linked hoard pieces preserve the dragon’s ownership claim across separated caches, helping make them function as one hoard. A dragon can be weakened by plundering its treasure and breaking its connection to the lair and surrounding territory.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragon Hoards, pp. 69–70 (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: linked treasure maintains the dragon’s claim; dial: severing or stealing pieces can disrupt the connection.

rules.statement: A dragon’s lair can produce local supernatural effects, such as purifying water within 6 miles or causing persistent rain; effects vary by dragon and may extend beyond the lair itself.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects, pp. 67–68 (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: effects are localized around a lair; dial: choose the area and effect to express the dragon’s influence.

rules.statement: A lair can open a passageway to another world on the Material Plane, and some dragon lairs are connected to portals leading to other planes. Such a portal or passage can enable travel between worlds.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects, p. 67; Crystal Dragon Adventure Hooks, p. 105; Dragon Turtle, p. 115 (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: travel requires access to a particular lair passage or portal; dial: set its destination and availability.

rules.statement: A dragon in its lair can use additional lair actions described for its kind; examples include recharging its breath weapon on a d6 roll of 6, regaining hit points by drawing on the lair’s magic, or gaining resistance to physical damage until its next turn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Additional Lair Actions, pp. 67–68 (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the dragon must be in its lair and some effects depend on a die roll; dial: select or adapt actions for the dragon and its setting.

rules.statement: A dragon’s regional effects manifest only when it reaches the specified age or challenge threshold for its kind; younger dragons can manifest them using lower DCs. The passage suggests adjusting a younger dragon’s challenge rating upward if it also receives additional lair actions.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects, p. 68 (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: age or challenge limits access to effects; dial: lower DCs or adjust challenge rating to represent a younger dragon’s power.

rules.statement: Dragons presented as spellcasters can cast the listed spells a specified number of times per day without material components, using the spellcasting ability and save DC given for that dragon.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragon Spellcasting, p. 77 (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: casting is limited by the listed daily uses and save DC; the dragon needs no material components.

rules.statement: A magical curse placed on a dragon’s hoard can impose different effects on affected creatures, including automatic failure against the dragon’s Frightful Presence, restricted movement, reduced healing during rests, or a soul remaining on the hoard after death until the victim finishes a long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Hoard Curses, pp. 70–71 (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the curse targets creatures affected by the hoard and may persist through death; dial: choose a curse effect and its release condition.

rules.statement: A dragon may be aware of its other incarnations on different Material Plane worlds. With development, that awareness can become active communication, allowing ancient dragons to coordinate plans across worlds.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragonsight, p. 7 (dnd5e-fizban#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: awareness is passive; dial: active contact and coordinated plans; the cost is time and development of the ability.

rules.statement: Moonstone dragons can link their lairs with portals that allow travel in either direction. A portal can be closed immediately.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Moonstone Dragons, p. 213–214 (dnd5e-fizban#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the passage describes linked lairs, not unrestricted travel; dial: opening portals permits travel between those sites, and closing one ends access.

rules.statement: Within an emerald dragon’s lair, it can attempt to alter the perceptions of a creature it can sense; the target makes a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw. A creature made to obey by the dragon’s lair effect follows its directions as well as it can, except for directions that would directly harm it.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Emerald Dragons, p. 200 (dnd5e-fizban#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect is confined to the lair and subject to a saving throw; dial: its reach and the extent of obedience determine how strongly the lair controls intruders.

rules.statement: Natural stone within 6 miles of a sapphire dragon’s lair can serve as a conduit for its psionic presence; the dragon can target such stone formations with its psionic energy. Its telepathic communication range doubles while it is within 1 mile of its lair.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Sapphire Dragons, p. 219 (dnd5e-fizban#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the conduit is limited to natural stone in the lair’s region; dial: the wider the conduit network, the more places can carry the dragon’s presence.

rules.statement: A dragon’s hoard can retain traces of the dragon’s inherent magic after the treasure is taken. Exposure to another dragon’s hoard can reawaken that magic, with unpredictable results.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Disclaimer, p. 4 (dnd5e-fizban#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: taken treasure may retain a magical trace; dial: exposure to another hoard can reactivate it, at the cost of unpredictable effects.

rules.statement: Your ancestry determines the damage type for your breath and resistance. When you take the Attack action, you can replace one attack with a breath in the listed area; targets make a Dexterity save against DC 8 + Constitution modifier + proficiency bonus, taking 1d10 damage on a failure or half on a success. Damage becomes 2d10 at level 5, 3d10 at 11, and 4d10 at 17; uses equal proficiency bonus return after a long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chromatic Dragonborn Traits; Gem Dragonborn Traits; Metallic Dragonborn Traits, pp. 12–14 (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ancestry sets the damage type; dial: proficiency-bonus uses and scaling dice; in-world cost: breath uses recover only after a long rest.

rules.statement: From level 5, chromatic dragonborn can use an action to gain immunity to their ancestry damage type for 1 minute, once per long rest. Gem dragonborn can manifest wings as a bonus action for 1 minute, gaining a flying speed equal to walking speed and the ability to hover, once per long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chromatic Warding; Gem Flight, pp. 12–13 (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ancestry unlocks a temporary defense or flight; dial: one use per long rest; in-world reason: the draconic energy is limited.

rules.statement: At level 5, metallic dragonborn gain a second breath option: a 15-foot cone. Each target makes a saving throw, becoming incapacitated until the start of your next turn on a failed Constitution save, or being pushed 20 feet and knocked prone on a failed Strength save. The breath can be used once per long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Metallic Dragonborn Traits, p. 14 (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the heritage grants a choice of control effect; dial: one use per long rest; in-world cost: the burst exhausts the breath.

rules.statement: A Way of the Ascendant Dragon monk can change the damage of an unarmed strike to acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison. When taking the Attack action, the monk can replace one attack with a 20-foot cone or 30-foot line of chosen energy; targets make Dexterity saves against the monk's ki save DC, taking two Martial Arts dice on a failure or half on success, rising to three dice at level 11. Uses equal proficiency bonus return after a long rest; with no uses left, spend 2 ki points to use it again.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Draconic Strike; Breath of the Dragon, p. 15 (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the monk channels draconic energy through strikes or breath; dial: proficiency-bonus uses, with ki as an extra cost; in-world reason: the technique draws on limited inner reserve.

rules.statement: At level 6, using Step of the Wind can create spectral wings until the end of the turn, granting flying speed equal to walking speed. This can be done a number of times equal to proficiency bonus per long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Wings Unfurled, p. 15 (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: movement technique briefly grants flight; dial: proficiency-bonus uses per long rest; in-world cost: the wings fade at turn's end.

rules.statement: At level 11, a monk can create a 10-foot aura for 1 minute, once per long rest, or spend 3 ki points to use it again. The aura either lets the monk impose frightened on a chosen creature within it (Wisdom save, repeat save at each turn's end) or grants the monk and allies within it resistance to one chosen damage type.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Aspect of the Wyrm, p. 16 (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: choose fear or shared resistance; dial: duration and ki cost; in-world reason: sustaining the aura consumes draconic focus.

rules.statement: At level 17, a monk can spend 1 ki point to make Breath of the Dragon a 60-foot cone or 90-foot line, dealing four Martial Arts dice on a failed save or half on success. The monk also gains 10-foot blindsight, and activating the aura can deal 3d10 chosen elemental damage to any number of visible creatures in it, each allowed a Dexterity save.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ascendant Aspect, p. 16 (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: high-level draconic mastery expands sensing and attack; dial: breath enhancement costs ki; in-world reason: greater output demands focused reserve.

rules.statement: A level 3 Drakewarden can use an action to summon its bound drake into an empty space within 30 feet. It obeys commands, takes its turn after yours, and normally Dodges unless you use a bonus action to command another action; it vanishes at 0 hit points, if summoned again, or when you die. After summoning, another summon requires a long rest, unless you expend a spell slot of level 1 or higher.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Drake Companion, pp. 17–18 (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a bonded drake serves as companion; dial: action to summon and rest or spell-slot recharge; in-world cost: the bond cannot repeatedly manifest the drake without recovery.

rules.statement: A drake's chosen essence sets its damage immunity and the damage added when it infuses a visible ally's hit within 30 feet; that added damage is 1d6. At level 7 it gains flight, and its bite gains 1d6 chosen damage while its summoner gains resistance to that type; at level 15 the bite bonus becomes 2d6 and the pair can use a reaction to grant resistance to a damage instance when within 30 feet, a number of times equal to proficiency bonus per long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Drake Companion; Bond of Fang and Scale; Perfected Bond, pp. 17–18 (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bond shares the drake's elemental essence; dial: proximity and limited reaction uses; in-world reason: protection depends on the active bond.

rules.statement: At level 11, a Drakewarden can exhale or command its drake to exhale a 30-foot cone; targets make Dexterity saves against the ranger's spell save DC, taking 8d6 damage on failure or half on success. Damage rises to 10d6 at ranger level 15; use it once per long rest, or expend a spell slot of level 3 or higher to use it again.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Drake's Breath, p. 18 (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ranger and drake share a breath attack; dial: rest or high-level spell slot; in-world cost: repeating the attack consumes substantial power.

rules.statement: A 2nd-level spell fills a visible 20-foot cube within 60 feet with magical mischief for up to 1 minute, requiring concentration. Roll a d4 for the effect and roll again at the start of each of your turns; before each roll, you may move the cube up to 10 feet. Effects include charm, blindness, incapacitation with random movement, or difficult terrain, each generally lasting until the start of your next turn and allowing the specified save.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Nathair's Mischief, p. 22 (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the spell cycles unpredictable effects in a bounded cube; dial: concentration and repeated random rolls; in-world cost: the caster must maintain the spell to sustain the shifting field.

rules.statement: A 4th-level spell can target a creature seen within 120 feet, or a creature whose name is spoken; if the named target is not in range, the spell has no effect. The target makes an Intelligence save, taking 7d6 psychic damage and becoming incapacitated until your next turn on failure, or half damage without incapacitation on success; damage rises by 1d6 per slot level above 4th.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Raulothim's Psychic Lance, p. 23 (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a mental strike can target by name; dial: range and save limit the effect; in-world cost: a wrong or distant target makes the spell fail.

rules.statement: A 2nd-level spell sends cold energy through a 30-foot cone; each target makes a Constitution save, taking 3d8 cold damage and having speed reduced to 0 for 1 minute on failure. The ice can be removed by the target or another creature within reach using an action; on a successful save, the target takes half damage and is not hindered. Higher-level slots add 1d8 damage per slot level above 2nd.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Rime's Binding Ice, p. 23 (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the blast can immobilize targets in ice; dial: save, action to break free, and slot scaling; in-world cost: the restraint is temporary and can be cleared by effort.

rules.statement: A platinum scale can be removed as an action to produce one of three effects: restore 10d4 hit points to you or a touched creature, create a +1 shield that grants radiant immunity for up to 1 hour, or create a light hammer for up to 1 hour that deals an extra 2d4 radiant damage and an extra 2d4 damage against chromatic dragons. The scarf has three scales; removed scales regrow at dawn, and an unused created item vanishes after 1 minute.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Platinum Scarf (p. 26) (dnd5e-fizban#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one scale per use, with only three available until dawn; the wearer spends a scarce stored charge for healing or temporary gear.

rules.statement: Drinking the potion changes you for 1 hour into an adult dragon matching the scale in the potion. You use that dragon's game statistics but retain your languages, personality, and memories; your equipment either melds into the form or falls to the ground, and you cannot use Change Shape or legendary or lair actions.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Potion of Dragon's Majesty (p. 26) (dnd5e-fizban#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the transformation lasts only 1 hour and excludes key dragon abilities; taking dragon form trades your usual statistics and potentially your equipment.

rules.statement: While holding the attuned gem, you can use it as a spellcasting focus and spend up to 3 charges when casting a spell to ignore material components with a gold-piece cost up to 500 gp per charge. At the end of a long rest, choose a spell from any class list that you can cast; you know it and can cast it with appropriate spell slots until your next long rest, and the gem restores all charges daily at dawn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ruby Weave Gem (p. 26) (dnd5e-fizban#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: component waivers consume up to three daily charges, while access to the chosen spell lasts only until the next long rest.

rules.statement: While wielding the attuned sapphire shield, you have resistance to psychic and thunder damage, and you can use your reaction when a creature within 5 feet damages you to deal 2d6 thunder damage to it. As an action, you can locate aberrations within 1 mile until the end of your next turn; the shield indicates their direction, and this locating property recharges at dawn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Sapphire Buckler (p. 26) (dnd5e-fizban#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: protection applies while wielding the shield; retaliation costs a reaction, and locating aberrations is limited to one use per dawn.

rules.statement: The attuned firearm needs no ammunition, has ranges of 100/300 feet, and deals 2d6 necrotic damage on a hit. A target reduced to 0 hit points by it is turned to dust and can be restored only by true resurrection or wish; while it is on your person, you can cast disintegrate (save DC 18) as an action, once per dawn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Topaz Annihilator (p. 26) (dnd5e-fizban#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the dust effect sharply limits ordinary revival, while the special spell is available only once per dawn.

rules.statement: A hoard item gains one state after a year steeping in a dragon's hoard, up to the maximum state allowed by that dragon's age; the dragon knows which items are steeping and their states. If a dragon dies, an item in its lair that begins steeping within 1 hour can rise one state after 8 hours, but not beyond the dragon's age-based ceiling; an unattended, unattuned item outside a dragon's hoard falls one state every 30 days until Slumbering.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Increasing Power / Decreasing Power (pp. 25–26) (dnd5e-fizban#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: power accrues from prolonged exposure to a dragon's hoard and fades when an item is unattuned and away from one; the dragon also knows about items in its hoard.

rules.statement: A Dragon's Wrath weapon's state determines its bonuses and breath-derived effects: Slumbering adds 5 damage of that breath type to each creature of your choice within 5 feet of a target on a natural 20; Stirring grants +1 to attack and damage and adds 1d6 damage of that type on a hit; Wakened raises those bonuses to +2 and 2d6 and allows a once-per-dawn 30-foot cone for 8d6 damage, DC 16 Dexterity save for half. Ascendant raises the bonuses to +3 and 3d6 and the cone to 60 feet, 12d6, DC 18.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragon's Wrath Weapon (pp. 27–28) (dnd5e-fizban#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: stronger effects require the item's higher hoard state; the cone is limited to once per dawn.

rules.statement: A Dragon-Touched Focus gives advantage on initiative and can serve as a spellcasting focus. Its Stirring benefit depends on the dragon family: certain elemental-damage spells gain a d6 bonus to one damage roll, a gem focus allows a short teleport after casting a spell with a spell slot, or a metallic focus lets you use your reaction to grant a visible creature within 30 feet advantage on a saving throw; at higher states it grants specified spells and, at Ascendant, lets you treat one spell of 1st level or higher as cast with a 9th-level slot once per dawn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragon-Touched Focus (pp. 28–29) (dnd5e-fizban#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: benefits depend on the focus's hoard state and dragon family; the 9th-level-slot substitution is limited to once per dawn.

rules.statement: A Dragon Vessel can be commanded as a bonus action while empty to fill with a beverage or a potion determined by its hoard state, from a healing or climbing potion at Slumbering to a potion of dragon's majesty at Ascendant. Its potion loses its magic if not consumed within 24 hours, and the vessel's filling property recharges at dawn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragon Vessel (p. 29) (dnd5e-fizban#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the vessel produces one state-appropriate potion per dawn, and the potion expires if not consumed within 24 hours.

rules.statement: A Scaled Ornament grants advantage on saves to avoid or end being charmed or frightened while Slumbering; when Stirring, it also grants +1 AC, prevents those conditions, and lets chosen creatures within 30 feet have advantage on saves against them. When Wakened, it can use a reaction once per dawn to prevent damage of its dragon's breath type and restore hit points equal to the prevented damage; when Ascendant, it grants a flying speed equal to your walking speed and the ability to hover while worn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Scaled Ornament (p. 29) (dnd5e-fizban#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: defenses depend on the ornament's state; damage negation costs a reaction and recharges at dawn.

rules.statement: A draconic familiar gift lets you cast find familiar as a ritual without material components, and the familiar always takes the form of a pseudodragon. When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can forgo one of your attacks so the familiar can use its reaction to make one attack.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Draconic Familiar (p. 30) (dnd5e-fizban#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the familiar's attack uses your reaction opportunity by requiring you to give up one of your own attacks.

rules.statement: A draconic gift can grant blindsight to 10 feet, letting you perceive nearby things despite blindness or darkness and see creatures there unless they successfully hide; it also grants advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks. Another gift lets you contact a dragon echo on another Material Plane world by casting contact other plane as a ritual, but the echo's knowledge may be limited and its attitude may reflect the source dragon.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Draconic Senses / Echo of Dragonsight (p. 30) (dnd5e-fizban#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sensory reach is limited to 10 feet and hidden creatures can evade it; contact reaches an echo whose knowledge and disposition may be constrained.

rules.statement: A draconic gift lets you use a bonus action to frighten chosen creatures within 120 feet that can see and are aware of you; each makes a Wisdom save against DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier or becomes frightened for 1 minute. Affected creatures repeat the save at the end of each turn, ending the effect on a success; uses equal your proficiency bonus return after a long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Frightful Presence (p. 30) (dnd5e-fizban#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: targets can repeat the save each turn, and the number of uses is limited by proficiency bonus per long rest.

rules.statement: A dragon's magical influence can produce half-dragons through several distinct routes: exposure to its lair region, magical fruit, a loving bond, blood contact or consumption, a gift to a child, or prolonged exposure to its hoard. Some routes are deliberate gifts; others can occur by accident.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Half-Dragon Origin table (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow each listed origin; dial: make the transformation rare or require deliberate dragon action, since several routes are described as occasional or magical accidents.

rules.statement: When a dragon dies, roll 1d6 on the Dragon Death Throes table: it may trigger a lair action centered on itself, use its breath weapon, change or vanish leaving an organ, create a Wild Magic Surge, release energy that grants creatures within 120 feet the benefit of a long rest, or send its body through a portal to an echo's lair on another world, empowering that echo.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Death of a Dragon; Dragon Death Throes table (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: roll 1d6 when a dragon dies; dial: reroll results likely to kill a character, because the passage explicitly recommends avoiding an overly lethal outcome.

rules.statement: After a dragon dies, its regional effects usually end immediately or change; some effects instead persist for 1d10 days. Examples include fouled water or nightmares within 6 miles, a tremor within 6 miles, dramatic weather changes within 6 miles, and vegetation withering within 1 mile.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Reversal (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: end regional effects at death; dial: let selected effects linger for 1d10 days, with the region suffering the dragon's magical aftermath.

rules.statement: A dying dragon's power can be transferred to another creature by methods such as inhaling its last breath, receiving a gemstone or treasure, or claiming power from its corpse; blood, organs, or muscle can carry the power, but lingering energies can seriously injure someone who uses the corpse this way. Power can also transfer automatically to participants or creatures present at death, potentially affecting creatures within 300 feet, or to creatures that damaged the dragon during its life.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Passing the Mantle (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transfer is possible but not guaranteed; dial: choose the recipients and method, balancing the reward against dangerous residual energy or the difficulty of obtaining it.

rules.statement: When a dragon becomes undead, its echoes on other Material Plane worlds can suffer a wasting affliction that spreads outward from it. Affected dragons become more violent and cruel, age more rapidly, and may be driven to seek undeath themselves.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Undeath (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: let undeath affect echoes; dial: determine how far and quickly the wasting spreads, since the text describes cross-world consequences but gives no distance or timing.

rules.statement: Each chromatic, metallic, and gem dragon that has lived has a unique echo on every Material Plane world; echoes may be very similar or radically different. A table roll can determine how much they differ, including a result that makes an echo undead or a shadow dragon.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Echoes Across the Worlds; Dragon Echo Characteristics table (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: give each such dragon an echo on every Material Plane world; dial: roll or choose the degree of difference, with fate across worlds remaining a defining connection.

rules.statement: Most metallic and gem dragons can change into a Humanoid or Beast form by adulthood or ancient age, respectively. A dragon can use its Change Shape action without changing its challenge rating; a dragon made an innate spellcaster can instead use the polymorph spell to assume another form.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Shape-Shifting (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the ability to the dragon kinds and ages described; dial: extend it to other dragons only by using the passage's suggested variants, since the ability is not universal.

rules.statement: A dragon can pass power to a follower or other creature as a blessing, supernatural gift, or similar benefit, potentially with drawbacks if a Dark Gift is used. A dragon may also support artists, adventurers, or causes as a patron, but this passage gives no fixed mechanical cost or grant for that support.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Passing the Mantle; Followers—Patron (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: make the benefit a chosen supernatural gift; dial: attach a drawback or a service expectation only if desired, because the passage leaves the specific terms to the DM.

rules.statement: A dragon's magical scale markings grant protective wards: it usually has one ward, plus one additional ward for each age category above wyrmling. Possible wards include immunity to form-altering effects; immunity to emotion-sensing and thought-reading, with disadvantage on checks to judge its intentions or sincerity; advantage on saves against spells and magical effects; or resistance to nonmagical weapon damage or one damage type.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Hidecarved Dragons; Engraved Wards and Hidecarved Wards table (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: assign one ward plus one per age category above wyrmling; dial: choose or roll the ward, as the passage allows either method.

rules.statement: A hidecarved dragon with the death ward protection can cast death ward on itself once, regaining the ability after a long rest. Its magical scale markings can also affect its echoes across the Material Plane, giving them some measure of the same protection.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Hidecarved Wards; Mystic Markings (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit one self-cast between long rests; dial: decide how strongly the markings affect echoes, since the passage specifies only that they gain a measure of the protection.

rules.statement: A dragon with dragonsight revelation adds half its proficiency bonus, rounded down, to ability checks using skills in which it lacks proficiency. Initiation into the Inheritors of the First World can awaken awareness of echoes and communication with them through a lucid-dream-like process.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Inheritors of the First World; Awakening Dragonsight (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the stated bonus to unproficient skill checks; dial: reserve the echo-awareness and communication for dragons that develop dragonsight or undergo initiation.

rules.statement: The Chamber studies the Draconic Prophecy as a map of possible futures and cause-and-effect relationships, rather than a fixed prediction. Its agents may observe, interpret marks as signs, or manipulate events to push outcomes toward futures they want.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: The Chamber (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: treat prophecy as branching possibilities, not certainty; dial: allow intervention to change outcomes, at the cost of long-term consequences that may unfold over centuries.

rules.statement: When a creature casts a spell of 1st level or higher in a wild-magic area, it rolls a d10; on a 1, it rolls on the Wild Magic Surge table.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 4, “Lair Location” (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: trigger only on the stated roll; dial: the area’s exact size and spell frequency; the surge is a local magical hazard.

rules.statement: A minion can be given a trait that makes it impossible to compel it to act against its master’s instructions.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 3, “Dragons’ Minions” (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the restriction applies only to actions contrary to the master’s instructions; dial: whether it applies to every form of compulsion; loyalty constrains the minion’s agency.

rules.statement: A minion can telepathically communicate with its master while both are on the same plane of existence.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 3, “Dragons’ Minions” (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: communication requires the same plane; dial: the communication’s range and detail; planar separation breaks the link.

rules.statement: When a minion dies, it can release energy in a 5-foot-radius sphere, damaging each creature there with the damage type of its master’s breath weapon; the passage does not specify the damage amount.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 3, “Dragons’ Minions” (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated radius and damage type; dial: damage amount, which the passage leaves unspecified; the minion’s death triggers the burst.

rules.statement: While its master is within 60 feet, a dying minion can let the master regain hit points equal to up to four times the minion’s challenge rating.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 3, “Dragons’ Minions” (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: cap the recovery at four times the minion’s challenge rating and require the 60-foot proximity; the minion’s death fuels the master’s recovery.

rules.statement: When an attack hits its master, a minion within 5 feet can use its reaction to make the attack hit itself instead.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 3, “Dragons’ Minions” (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require the minion to be within 5 feet and spend its reaction; the minion takes the hit meant for its master.

rules.statement: A creature that drinks from water within 1 mile of a dragon’s lair makes a Wisdom saving throw against a DC of 8 + the dragon’s proficiency bonus + its Charisma modifier. On a failure, it is charmed by the dragon for 24 hours; on a success, it is immune to this effect for the next 24 hours.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 4, “Regional Effects—Water Changes” (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the stated save, duration, and immunity; dial: which water sources are affected; drinking the water exposes the creature to the lair’s influence.

rules.statement: Magic portals can form as fissures, archways, or tunnels within 1 mile of a dragon’s lair, connecting to an appropriate Elemental Plane. Pools or passageways can also permit communication or travel between different worlds on the Material Plane.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 4, “Regional Effects—Planar Connections” (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated portal locations and destinations; dial: access and stability, which the passage does not define; passage depends on a lair’s planar connections.

rules.statement: If a dragon dies or leaves its area, the personality traits its presence induced in nearby residents fade over 1d10 days.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 4, “Regional Effects—Changes to Creatures” (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: fade the influence over 1d10 days after the dragon’s death or departure; dial: how quickly it fades within that range; the effect wanes with its source.

rules.statement: At initiative count 20, a dragon can use a lair action that lets it roll a d6 and recharge its breath weapon on a 6, regain hit points equal to the number of Hit Dice it has, or cause creatures damaged by its breath weapon on its previous turn to take another 10 (3d6) damage of that type.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 4, “Lair Actions” (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed outcomes and timing; dial: which lair actions the dragon has; the lair’s magic supports the dragon and extends its breath’s impact.

rules.statement: A dragon can use a lair action to gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage until initiative count 20 on the next round.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 4, “Lair Actions” (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the three stated resistances for the stated duration; dial: whether this action is available to a particular dragon; the lair’s energy hardens its scales.

rules.statement: An ancient dragon can have 8–10 treasure caches, each worth 200,000 gp; separate caches can anchor the dragon’s power at different locations.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 4, “Dragon Hoards—Linking Hoards” (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use 8–10 caches at 200,000 gp each; dial: how far apart they are and how their power works; dividing the hoard extends the dragon’s magical reach.

rules.statement: A dragon’s hoard worth about 15,000 gp or more links the dragon, its lair, and its territory through magic, empowering its legendary actions and regional effects. A dragon can divide its treasure among caches while linking them with designated items that help preserve its claim over the scattered hoard.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Plundering a Hoard, p. 67 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the link follows the dragon’s treasure; dial: choose whether linked caches remain a single claim after division.

rules.statement: If a dragon’s lair holds less than 10,000 gp in treasure, it ceases to count as a lair there: the dragon loses access to lair actions at that site, and its regional effects end as if it had died. Disturbing the hoard alerts the dragon to intruders, prompting it or its minions to investigate.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Plundering a Hoard, p. 67 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the stated treasure threshold and alert; dial: decide how quickly the dragon or its minions can respond.

rules.statement: Moving valuable treasure from a legendary dragon’s hoard can leave supernatural effects attached to individual items or coins, such as altering water or weather, attracting small animals, influencing dreams or personality, drawing bearers toward the lair, or encouraging plant growth. An item from a legendary dragon’s hoard can purify water it touches.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Hoard Quirks—Regional Effects, p. 68 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: effects can persist after treasure moves; dial: choose which effect follows which treasure and its reach.

rules.statement: A spirit bound to an important hoard item may manifest as a ghostlike creature or make the item sentient. Completing the spirit’s unfinished business—such as returning or destroying the item, or reuniting it with a set—can let the spirit rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Haunted Hoards, p. 68 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the spirit remains bound until its unfinished business is resolved; dial: determine the task and what counts as completion.

rules.statement: A dragon’s violent death can curse its hoard and affect both thieves and others who contact the treasure. Gathering the entire hoard together again is generally required to break the curse; removing even one coin from the assembled hoard can reactivate it.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: A Dragon’s Curse, pp. 68–69 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the curse reaches treasure-contacting creatures and requires the whole hoard; dial: set how widely contact spreads the curse.

rules.statement: A remove curse spell suppresses the hoard curse on one affected character for 1 hour, and greater restoration also suppresses it temporarily. Returning the entire hoard to the dragon’s lair ends the curse; the passage does not provide a fixed duration for greater restoration’s suppression.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: A Dragon’s Curse, p. 69 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: treat these spells as temporary relief and full return as the lasting cure; dial: specify the unspecified suppression duration for greater restoration.

rules.statement: A curse-breaking rite can involve casting hallow, making an offering, bathing the treasure in blood, or making a sacrifice; a curse may also be bypassed if another dragon’s hoard takes ownership of the treasure, or if the treasure is freely given. The passage presents these as possible approaches rather than a universal fixed procedure.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Breaking a Hoard Curse, p. 71 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use a rite, transfer of ownership, or gift to end or bypass the curse; dial: choose which elements the specific curse demands.

rules.statement: An amethyst dragon’s lair can warp space in its chimneys: moving upward from the upper level returns a creature to the lower level, and moving downward from the lower level returns it to the upper level. A creature or object dropped through a chimney falls endlessly unless it or an outside force can stop it; this property disappears 1d10 days after the dragon dies.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Amethyst Dragon Lairs, p. 79 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the chimney’s spatial rule persists while the dragon lives and fades after death; dial: define what can stop the fall.

rules.statement: A black dragon of young, adult, or ancient age can know the listed spells for its age: young dragons know blindness/deafness and create or destroy water; adults also know plant growth; ancients also know insect plague. It can cast each listed spell once per day without material components, using Charisma as its spellcasting ability; the listed save DCs are 13, 16, and 19, respectively.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Black Dragon Spellcasting, p. 82 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the age-based spell list, daily use limit, and stated save DC; dial: apply this optional spellcasting package only to dragons designated as spellcasters.

rules.statement: A legendary black dragon in its lair can cause a visible point within 120 feet to erupt in a 20-foot-high cylinder of filthy water. Creatures in the cylinder when it appears or ending their turn there make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) poison damage on a failure or half on a success; the area is difficult terrain.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Black Dragon Lairs—Additional Lair Actions, p. 82 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated range, dimensions, save, damage, and terrain; dial: select whether this optional lair action is available.

rules.statement: A legendary black dragon in its lair can target up to three creatures it can see in the lair with grasping muck. Each target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or become restrained until initiative count 20 on the next round.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Black Dragon Lairs—Additional Lair Actions, p. 82 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect targets at most three visible creatures and ends at the stated initiative count; dial: choose whether the optional action is in the lair’s repertoire.

rules.statement: A legendary black dragon in its lair can make swamp gas erupt as a sphere centered on a point it can see there. Each creature in the area must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect early.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Black Dragon Lairs—Additional Lair Actions, p. 82 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: poison lasts up to 1 minute with a save at each turn’s end; dial: choose whether this optional lair action is available and set the sphere’s area as needed.

rules.statement: An adult or ancient bronze dragon in its lair can choose creatures in water within 120 feet that it can see; each must succeed on a DC 15 Strength save or be moved by a forceful current.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Bronze Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Actions (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the current affects chosen visible creatures in the lair’s water within 120 feet; dial: narrow or broaden the reachable water area; in-world reason: the dragon’s control is tied to its lair.

rules.statement: An adult or ancient bronze dragon in its lair can create a 20-foot-radius sphere of abrasive salt crystals at a point it can see; creatures there make a DC 15 Dexterity save or take 10 (3d6) slashing damage.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Bronze Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Actions (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the burst is limited to a visible point in the lair and a 20-foot radius; dial: change the radius or save difficulty; in-world reason: the effect is a localized lair defense.

rules.statement: An adult or ancient bronze dragon in its lair can conjure spectral dolphins; each creature in water within 120 feet must succeed on a saving throw or take 5 (1d10) slashing damage, after which the swarm vanishes.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Bronze Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Actions (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the swarm is temporary and threatens creatures in water within 120 feet; dial: adjust its reach or damage; in-world reason: the apparition is a brief lair effect.

rules.statement: Within 10 miles of a bronze dragon’s lair, sapient creatures that spend a year find it nearly impossible to break a promise.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Bronze Dragon Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the promise effect requires a year within 10 miles and makes breaking promises nearly impossible; dial: change duration or range; in-world reason: the lair gradually influences nearby inhabitants.

rules.statement: A bronze dragon’s hidden-cove sentinel statue has magically warded eyes that alert the dragon to intruders.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Bronze Dragon Lair Features — Sentinel Statue (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ward detects intruders at the statue; dial: set what counts as an intruder or its detection range; in-world reason: it serves as an early-warning defense.

rules.statement: A blue dragon’s lair can produce a misleading mirage: until initiative count 20 on the next round, creatures other than the dragon have a 50 percent chance at each junction to go in a direction other than the one they intended.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Blue Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Actions (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the misdirection lasts until initiative count 20 next round and applies at each junction with a 50 percent chance; dial: vary duration or probability; in-world reason: the lair confuses navigation.

rules.statement: A blue dragon in its lair can create a 5-foot-radius, 20-foot-deep pit at a visible ground point within 120 feet; a creature above it makes a DC 15 Dexterity save, falling prone at the bottom and taking 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage on a failure, while on a success it moves to the nearest unoccupied space instead.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Blue Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Actions (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the pit’s dimensions, range, save, and damage are specified; dial: change the pit size or placement range; in-world reason: the dragon reshapes ground within its lair.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of a blue dragon’s lair, the area can appear to be a lush oasis; a creature that examines the illusion can make a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check to disbelieve it, after which it sees the real terrain with the image superimposed.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Blue Dragon Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the illusion extends through the immediate surroundings and can be disbelieved with the stated check; dial: adjust its footprint or check difficulty; in-world reason: the lair’s mirage masks the desert landscape.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of a blue dragon’s lair, a constant sandstorm can blow.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Blue Dragon Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the storm is a persistent regional effect within 1 mile; dial: change its area or persistence; in-world reason: the lair alters nearby weather.

rules.statement: Creatures that spend a year within 1 mile of a blue dragon’s lair find blue objects fascinating and feel compelled to acquire them whenever possible.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Blue Dragon Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the compulsion develops after a year within 1 mile and focuses on acquiring blue objects; dial: vary the duration or strength; in-world reason: prolonged proximity changes local preferences.

rules.statement: Within 6 miles of a brass dragon’s lair, a small wispy cloud follows non-evil creatures as they travel, shielding them from direct sun and granting advantage on saving throws against extreme heat.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Brass Dragon Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the cloud follows non-evil creatures within 6 miles and grants advantage against extreme heat; dial: change eligibility or range; in-world reason: the lair provides a protective regional benefit.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of a brass dragon’s lair, creatures find pleasure in hearing their own voices; the air fills with a deafening chorus of birds and small animals, while sapient creatures talk extensively.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Brass Dragon Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect applies within 1 mile and encourages vocal behavior; dial: adjust the area or intensity; in-world reason: the lair influences the sounds and behavior of nearby creatures.

rules.statement: An adult or ancient dragon turtle may receive lair actions while in its lair at the DM’s option; doing so increases its challenge rating by 1. At initiative count 20, losing ties, it chooses one listed action, and cannot choose the same one in consecutive rounds.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragon Turtle Lair Actions, p. 114–115 (dnd5e-fizban#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: no lair actions; dial: grant them to adult or ancient turtles for +1 challenge rating, reflecting greater lair-based danger.

rules.statement: The turtle can send a current through its lair: creatures within 30 feet make a DC 15 Strength save or move 30 feet in a direction it chooses; on a success, they move 10 feet instead.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragon Turtle Lair Actions—Blasting Current, p. 115 (dnd5e-fizban#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: applies in the lair within 30 feet; dial: use the forced movement and save as written, representing currents under the turtle’s influence.

rules.statement: The turtle can target a point it can see in its lair with kelp in a 20-foot-radius sphere; creatures there that fail a DC 15 Strength save are restrained until the end of their next turn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragon Turtle Lair Actions—Entangling Kelp, p. 115 (dnd5e-fizban#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one visible point in the lair and a DC 15 save; dial: restraint lasts only until the target’s next turn ends.

rules.statement: The turtle can cause steam to erupt in a 15-foot cone from a point on the ground it can see within 120 feet; creatures in the area make a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage on a failure or half on a success. Being underwater does not grant resistance to this damage.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragon Turtle Lair Actions—Steam Eruption, p. 115 (dnd5e-fizban#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the stated cone, range, save, and damage apply; dial: underwater conditions do not reduce this fire damage through resistance.

rules.statement: A dragon turtle’s lair can produce diverting currents within the region: each foot of swimming costs 1 extra foot, or 2 extra feet in difficult terrain, even for creatures with a swimming speed.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects—Diverting Currents, p. 115 (dnd5e-fizban#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: affects swimming movement in the lair’s currents; dial: apply the extra movement cost, making unwanted approach more difficult.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of the lair, ocean-floor crevasses form two-way portals to the Elemental Plane of Water, allowing creatures from that plane to dwell nearby.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects—Elemental Portals, p. 115 (dnd5e-fizban#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: portals occur within 1 mile and connect both ways; dial: passage permits nearby elemental-water creatures to enter the region.

rules.statement: Geothermal vents heat water within 6 miles of the lair to 100 degrees Fahrenheit. If the dragon turtle dies, its regional effects fade over 1d10 days.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects—Hot Water, p. 115 (dnd5e-fizban#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the listed temperature extends 6 miles; dial: the effects persist after death but fade over 1d10 days.

rules.statement: Older green or faerie dragons may receive lair actions at the DM’s option; at initiative count 20, losing ties, they choose one listed action. The same action cannot be used in consecutive rounds.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Faerie Dragon Lair Actions, p. 121 (dnd5e-fizban#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: no lair actions; dial: grant them to an older faerie dragon or green dragon in its lair, as an optional increase in lair capability.

rules.statement: A faerie dragon can bend air and magic around itself; until initiative count 20 on the next round, a ranged attack that misses it is rerolled against a random creature within 30 feet of it that lacks total cover against the attack.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Faerie Dragon Lair Actions—Chaotic Aura, p. 121 (dnd5e-fizban#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: lasts until initiative count 20 next round and redirects only missed ranged attacks; dial: a random eligible nearby creature becomes the new target.

rules.statement: A faerie dragon can make roots and vines grow around it, making the ground within 20 feet difficult terrain until initiative count 20 on the next round.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Faerie Dragon Lair Actions—Grasping Plants, p. 121 (dnd5e-fizban#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the difficult terrain covers 20 feet around the dragon and lasts until initiative count 20 next round.

rules.statement: The first time a creature comes within 1 mile of a faerie dragon’s lair, it must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom save or feel compelled to leave an offering worth at least 5 gp in a secluded spot; the dragon immediately senses where it is. A creature can be affected only once.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects—Compulsory Offering, p. 122 (dnd5e-fizban#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one attempt per creature, DC 15, and an offering worth at least 5 gp; dial: failure compels the gift and reveals its location to the dragon.

rules.statement: Time within 1 mile of a faerie dragon’s lair flows at a rate between half and twice normal speed. Sapient creatures that spend a year within 5 miles feel a persistent urge to play pranks; if the dragon dies, these regional effects fade over 1d10 days.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects—Malleable Time and Mischief Afoot, p. 122 (dnd5e-fizban#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: time varies from one-half to twice its usual rate within 1 mile; the prank urge follows a year’s exposure within 5 miles and fades after death over 1d10 days.

rules.statement: Gold dragons know different spells by age: young dragons have bless, cure wounds, slow, suggestion, and zone of truth; adults also know commune and geas; ancients additionally know plane shift, word of recall, and the listed adult spells. Save DCs are 17, 21, and 24 for young, adult, and ancient dragons respectively; plane shift has +16 to hit, and marked spells take longer than 1 action to cast.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Gold Dragon Spellcasting table, p. 123 (dnd5e-fizban#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell access and save DC depend on age category; dial: higher age grants more spells and stronger save DC, reflecting accumulated capability.

rules.statement: A sapphire dragon can use a lair action to open or close passages through the lair’s thin walls, changing which routes connect its chambers.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Sapphire Dragon Lair Features — Disguised Entrances (p. 142) (dnd5e-fizban#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow the lair’s resident dragon to alter routes; dial: restrict this to lair actions, since it is a site-bound defense.

rules.statement: Some gloomy caves and other dark places within 1 mile of a shadow dragon’s lair on the Material Plane become portals to the Shadowfell, allowing creatures from that plane to settle nearby.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Shadow Dragon Lairs — Regional Effects (p. 144) (dnd5e-fizban#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: portals form in qualifying gloomy places; dial: limit them to within 1 mile of the lair, with Shadowfell access as the consequence.

rules.statement: Within 6 miles of a shadow dragon’s lair, light is diminished and the land lies in lightly obscuring gloom.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Shadow Dragon Lairs — Regional Effects (p. 144) (dnd5e-fizban#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the regional gloom around the lair; dial: keep it within 6 miles, as an environmental cost of the dragon’s presence.

rules.statement: A legendary adult or ancient shadow dragon in its lair can use a lair action to extinguish nonmagical light within 60 feet and dispel light-creating spells in that area.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Shadow Dragon Lairs — Additional Lair Action (p. 144) (dnd5e-fizban#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit the light-removing action in the lair; dial: restrict it to legendary dragons and a 60-foot radius.

rules.statement: A legendary adult or ancient silver dragon in its lair can force visible creatures of its choice within 120 feet to make a DC 15 Constitution save; on a failure they are restrained until initiative count 20 of the next round. Cold resistance grants advantage, while cold immunity means automatic success.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Silver Dragon Lairs — Additional Lair Action (p. 148) (dnd5e-fizban#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated save and brief restraint; dial: limit the effect to the lair, visible targets, and legendary dragons.

rules.statement: A shadow dragon’s existence can cause creatures with Intelligence 5 or higher within 1 mile of its lair to feel forlorn and hopeless.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Shadow Dragon Lairs — Regional Effects (p. 144) (dnd5e-fizban#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the emotional effect to qualifying creatures; dial: keep its reach to 1 mile and its cause tied to the lair.

rules.statement: A legendary adult or ancient white dragon in its lair can cause sleet to fall in a 20-foot-radius, 40-foot-high cylinder centered on a point it can see within 120 feet. Creatures in the area must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution save or be blinded until initiative count 20 on the next round.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: White Dragon Lairs — Additional Lair Actions, p. 157 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect is confined to a selected area; dial: the save DC and duration; reason: the lair’s storm hinders intruders.

rules.statement: A legendary adult or ancient white dragon in its lair can create strong wind in a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on itself. The wind lasts until the dragon uses a lair action again or dies, and does not impede the dragon’s flight.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: White Dragon Lairs — Additional Lair Actions, p. 157 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the wind affects a bounded sphere; dial: its duration; reason: the dragon’s own movement remains unhindered.

rules.statement: Within 6 miles of a white dragon’s lair, extreme cold prevails. If the climate is already extremely cold, creatures without cold resistance or immunity have disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects, p. 159 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect is regional; dial: whether it intensifies existing extreme cold; reason: unprotected creatures struggle in the cold.

rules.statement: Within 6 miles of a white dragon’s lair, icy surfaces reflect light like mirrors, giving creatures other than the dragon disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. At each passage intersection or branch, such a creature has a 50 percent chance of heading in a direction other than the one it intended.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects, p. 159 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the regional effect hinders intruders; dial: the 50 percent chance of misdirection; reason: reflective ice disrupts concealment and navigation.

rules.statement: A legendary amethyst dragon in its lair can telepathically target one creature with a whisper. On a failed DC 15 Wisdom save, the creature is charmed until initiative count 20 on the next round and obeys the dragon’s commands unless they would directly harm it.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Amethyst Dragon Lair — Lair Actions, p. 161 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the charm lasts only briefly; dial: the target’s save and the harm restriction; reason: the dragon’s psychic influence cannot compel self-harm.

rules.statement: A legendary amethyst dragon in its lair can cast forcecage without components, using its spell save DC. The spell ends early if the dragon uses this lair action again or dies.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Amethyst Dragon Lair — Lair Actions, p. 162 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect follows forcecage’s rules; dial: it ends early on the specified event; reason: the dragon’s continuing control sustains the prison.

rules.statement: A legendary amethyst dragon in its lair can occupy its own space and a chosen space in the lair that it can fit into until initiative count 20 on the next round. When it moves or acts, it chooses which version does so; an effect that targets both spaces affects it only once.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Amethyst Dragon Lair — Lair Actions, p. 162 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
