rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the second presence lasts until the next round’s initiative count 20; dial: the dragon chooses which location acts; reason: the projection does not duplicate the dragon’s vulnerability.

rules.statement: Within 6 miles of a legendary amethyst dragon’s lair, crystals and geodes form along muddy shores and lake beds, and aquatic wildlife thrives; foraging in those waters yields twice the usual food. If the dragon dies, aquatic populations return to normal over 1d10 days, while existing crystals remain and new ones form at the normal rate.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Amethyst Dragon Lair — Regional Effects, p. 162 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effects extend 6 miles and wildlife recovers after death; dial: the 1d10-day recovery; reason: the dragon’s magic alters local abundance.

rules.statement: A legendary amethyst dragon can use an action to cast clairvoyance without components, targeting any body of water within 6 miles of its lair. It can also cast legend lore once per day without components, naming a person, place, or object within 1 mile of the lair as the subject.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Amethyst Dragon Lair — Regional Effects, p. 162 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: both spells retain their stated limits; dial: the water, distance, and daily-use restrictions; reason: the lair channels the dragon’s remote awareness.

rules.statement: An ancient amethyst dragon can teleport as a bonus action to an unoccupied space it can see within 60 feet. It can also cast plane shift once per day without components as part of its psionic spellcasting.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Amethyst Dragon — Bonus Actions and Spellcasting, p. 162 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: teleportation is limited to 60 feet and plane shift to once daily; dial: those uses and destinations; reason: powerful mobility is constrained by range and frequency.

rules.statement: An ancient amethyst dragon can magically become any Medium or Small creature while keeping its game statistics except size. The change ends if it reaches 0 hit points or uses a bonus action to end it.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Amethyst Dragon — Bonus Actions, p. 162 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the transformation preserves the dragon’s statistics; dial: size and the two ending conditions; reason: the disguise changes appearance, not underlying capability.

rules.statement: A chromatic dragon can shape its breath energy into an animated creature of a matching acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison form. Each form determines the creature’s armor class, resistance, traits, and attacks; the created creature can serve as a guardian or be sent to gather treasure.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Animated Breath, p. 165 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the creation’s abilities depend on its chosen matching form; dial: the form and its listed traits; reason: the animated creature embodies the creator’s breath energy.

rules.statement: If the aspect of Bahamut would reach 0 hit points, it instead returns to 500 hit points, recharges its breath weapon, and regains expended uses of Legendary Resistance. For the next hour it can use mythic actions; defeating it after this change awards an additional 155,000 XP.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Aspect of Bahamut — Platinum Brilliance, p. 167 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the second phase lasts one hour; dial: the recovery, restored resources, and additional reward; reason: the aspect’s divine force sustains it through a decisive defeat.

rules.statement: The aspect of Tiamat can, while grappling a creature, force it to make a DC 25 Charisma save. On a failure it takes 44 (8d10) psychic damage and is banished to Avernus, returning at the start of Tiamat’s next turn to an unoccupied space within 10 feet of her.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Aspect of Tiamat — Mythic Actions, p. 168 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: banishment lasts only until Tiamat’s next turn; dial: the save, damage, and return point; reason: the planar displacement is a temporary attack, not permanent exile.

rules.statement: When the chromatic greatwyrm is reduced to 0 hit points, its awakening restores it to 425 hit points, recharges its breath, and restores its expended Legendary Resistance uses; for 1 hour afterward it can use mythic actions. Defeating it after this happens awards an additional 105,000 XP.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chromatic Greatwyrm, Chromatic Awakening (page 168) (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: awakening is a fixed second phase; dial: its exceptional recovery and extra reward are limited to this greatwyrm.

rules.statement: The greatwyrm’s breath recharges on a roll of 5–6; it blasts a 300-foot cone, forcing a DC 26 Dexterity save for 78 damage of the greatwyrm’s kind, or half damage on a success.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chromatic Greatwyrm, Breath Weapon (page 168) (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the cone and save resolve normally; dial: damage type depends on the dragon’s kind.

rules.statement: While the greatwyrm’s awakening has activated within the last hour, it can spend legendary-action opportunities on mythic options; its flare costs 2 actions and forces creatures within 60 feet to make a DC 26 Dexterity save or take 22 damage of its kind.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chromatic Greatwyrm, Mythic Actions (page 168) (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the option is available only during the one-hour awakened period and consumes two legendary actions.

rules.statement: An ancient crystal dragon’s radiant breath recharges on 5–6, affects a 90-foot cone, and deals 49 radiant damage on a failed DC 22 Constitution save or half on a success; afterward it gains 25 temporary hit points.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Crystal Dragon, Scintillating Breath (page 170) (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve the cone and save; dial: temporary hit points scale with the dragon’s age.

rules.statement: The ancient crystal dragon can magically become any Medium or Small creature while retaining its statistics except size; the change ends at 0 hit points or when it spends a bonus action to end it.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Crystal Dragon, Change Shape (page 170) (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation preserves nearly all statistics; dial: the permitted size and form are restricted.

rules.statement: A crystal dragon can teleport to a visible unoccupied space within 60 feet as a bonus action; it can also use this option through its legendary-action feature for 2 actions.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Crystal Dragon, Psychic Step and Legendary Actions (page 170) (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: destination must be visible, empty, and within range; dial: legendary use costs two actions.

rules.statement: A deep dragon’s nightmare breath recharges on 5–6 and fills a cone; a creature failing the specified Wisdom save takes psychic damage and is frightened for 1 minute, but can repeat the save at each turn’s end to end the fear. A successful save halves the damage and avoids the condition.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Deep Dragon, Nightmare Breath (page 175) (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed save causes fear with repeat saves; dial: cone size, save DC, and damage vary by age.

rules.statement: A legendary deep dragon can use its lair action to fill a visible 20-foot cube within 120 feet with toxic spores; creatures failing a DC 15 Constitution save take 14 poison damage and are poisoned until the end of their next turn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Deep Dragon, Lair Actions (page 176) (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the cube, save, and brief poisoned duration are fixed; the effect is restricted to the lair action.

rules.statement: If a dracohydra takes at least 30 damage in one turn, one head dies; at the end of its turn it regrows two heads for each head lost since its previous turn, unless it took radiant damage since then, and gains 10 hit points per head regrown.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dracohydra, Multiple Heads (page 178) (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: head loss and regrowth follow the stated damage and turn conditions; radiant damage prevents that regrowth.

rules.statement: When a draconian dreadnought reaches 0 hit points, it bursts into flame and becomes ash; creatures within 10 feet must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity save or take 10 fire damage.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Draconian Dreadnought, Death Throes (page 179) (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the death-triggered blast resolves once; its fire damage and radius are fixed.

rules.statement: A draconian infiltrator that kills a Medium or smaller Humanoid can use its reaction to assume that creature’s appearance, retaining its statistics except size; the disguise ends at its death or when it uses an action to end it.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Draconian Dreadnought, Shape Theft (page 179) (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the change requires a qualifying kill and reaction; it copies appearance, not the victim’s abilities.

rules.statement: A draconic shard can inhabit an object infused with a gem dragon’s psionic power; destroying its spectral form or inhabited object forces it into a cracked gemstone, and only destroying that stone can finally put it to rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Draconic Shard (page 182) (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: destruction of the first form or vessel only changes the shard’s state; final destruction requires breaking its gemstone anchor.

rules.statement: A shard can use an action to vanish into a visible nonsentient object of Medium size or smaller within 30 feet, possessing it. The object uses the shard’s AC, and damage to the object reduces the shard’s hit points.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Inhabit Object, p. 181 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: possession is limited to a nearby nonsentient object and damage still harms the shard; the shard risks being destroyed.

rules.statement: While possessing an object, the shard can leave by using an action; possession also ends if it is turned, reduced to 0 hit points, or affected by an effect that ends possession. On leaving, it appears in the nearest unoccupied space.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Inhabit Object, p. 181 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: several specific ways end the bond; possession is not permanent.

rules.statement: While possessed, the object becomes magical if it was not already and displays a tiny cracked gemstone. The shard can make it fly at its own flying speed, use its senses, speak aloud or telepathically, cast spells, and use its legendary actions.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Inhabit Object, p. 181 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the object’s added capabilities depend on the shard inhabiting it.

rules.statement: A creature wearing or carrying the inhabited object gains an extra 1d8 force damage on each attack and resistance to psychic damage.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Inhabit Object, p. 181 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: these benefits require the creature to wear or carry the possessed object.

rules.statement: When the shard reaches 0 hit points, it disappears and leaves a Tiny cracked gemstone with AC 20, 15 hit points, and immunity to all damage except force. If the gemstone survives, it dissipates after 1d20 days and the shard reforms there, or in the nearest unoccupied space, with all its hit points.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Rejuvenation, p. 181 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: revival is delayed and can be prevented by destroying the gemstone.

rules.statement: The shard can unleash a psychic pulse in a 60-foot-radius sphere. Chosen creatures there make a DC 20 Intelligence save; on a failure they take 55 (10d10) psychic damage and are stunned until the end of their next turn, while on a success they take half damage and are not stunned.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Psychic Crush, p. 181 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the pulse affects a large area, but the shard chooses its targets and a successful save avoids the stun.

rules.statement: A dragonbone golem’s chosen creatures that start their turns within 20 feet must make a DC 15 Wisdom save while it is not incapacitated. A failure frightens the creature until its next turn starts; a success grants immunity to this aura for 24 hours.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Fear Aura, p. 183 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the fear is brief, and a successful save prevents repeated exposure for 24 hours.

rules.statement: An egg hunter adult can release spores in a 30-foot-radius sphere; creatures must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution save or be poisoned for 1 minute. While poisoned this way, a creature can take an action or a bonus action on its turn, but not both, and cannot take reactions; it repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the effect on a success and gaining 24-hour immunity if it succeeds or the effect ends.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Torpor Spores, p. 193 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the impaired state can end on a repeated save, and successful targets gain temporary immunity.

rules.statement: When the adult egg hunter takes damage, it gives itself resistance to that damage.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Rapid Adaptation, p. 193 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the resistance applies to the damage that triggered this reaction, not as a general stated immunity.

rules.statement: A creature that fails its save against the elder brain dragon’s breath, or succeeds but is not a Construct or Undead, becomes infested with tadpoles. It takes 16 (3d10) psychic damage at the start of each turn and repeats the save at each turn’s end, ending the infestation after three successes; magic that ends a curse or restores at least 40 hit points kills the tadpoles immediately.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Tadpole Brine Breath, p. 194 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the infestation causes recurring damage and needs three successful saves to end, though specified magic removes it immediately.

rules.statement: If an infested Humanoid reaches 0 hit points, it remains stable and unconscious for 6d12 hours; when that time ends, it transforms into a mind flayer with all its hit points. Casting wish on the unconscious creature prevents the transformation and removes the infestation.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Tadpole Brine Breath, p. 194 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: transformation follows unconsciousness after a 6d12-hour delay, with a specific powerful spell as an escape.

rules.statement: When an ancient dragon turtle would be reduced to 0 hit points, its hit points instead reset to 350, and its steam breath recharges; for 1 hour it can use mythic actions. Defeating it after this occurs awards an additional 62,000 XP.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Blessing of the Sea, p. 191 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the one-time defeat threshold restores the turtle to a fixed pool and escalates the encounter.

rules.statement: An adult emerald dragon can replace a failed saving throw with a success up to three times per day. Its once-per-day perception shift also lets it cast hallucinatory terrain without components, using Intelligence and a save DC of 17.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Adult Emerald Dragon (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: three saves per day and one illusion per day; dial: none; these limits bound the dragon’s defensive and deceptive output.

rules.statement: An emerald dragon’s disorienting breath recharges on a 5–6 and fills a cone whose length depends on its age: 15 feet for a wyrmling, 30 feet for a young dragon, and 60 feet for an adult. Creatures in the cone make an Intelligence save (DC 12, 15, or 18, respectively); failure deals 5d6, 9d6, or 12d6 psychic damage and imposes a d4, d6, or d6 penalty on their next attack roll or ability check through the end of their next turn, while success halves damage and avoids the penalty.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Emerald Dragon stat blocks (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recharge and age-based area, save, damage, and penalty; dial: none; the effect is limited by its recharge and short duration.

rules.statement: Emerald dragons can cast the listed spells as psionics without spell components, using Intelligence; the adult’s save DC is 17 and its listed at-will spells are mage hand and minor illusion, with detect thoughts, dispel magic, invisibility, and major image each available once per day. The young dragon has a save DC of 14, at-will mage hand and minor illusion, and detect thoughts, invisibility, and silent image each once per day.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Emerald Dragon stat blocks—Spellcasting (Psionics) (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: only the listed spells and daily uses; dial: none; restricted spell selection and frequency cap the dragon’s magical output.

rules.statement: An emerald dragon can magically take the form of any Medium or Small creature while keeping its statistics except for size; the change ends if it reaches 0 hit points or uses a bonus action to end it. It can also teleport as a bonus action to a visible unoccupied space within 60 feet.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Adult Emerald Dragon—Bonus Actions (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: forms are limited to Medium or Small and teleportation to a visible space within 60 feet; dial: none; the conditions and range limit escape and disguise.

rules.statement: An emerald dragon’s lair can create crystal formations and emerald veins within 6 miles, make nearby fire and lava usable as targets for the dragon’s clairvoyance, attract giant lizards, and cause rocks to shift and obstruct paths. When the dragon dies, the rocks stop moving immediately, the lizard population returns to normal over 1d10 days, and existing crystals and emeralds remain while new ones form at the ordinary rate.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Emerald Dragon—Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: regional effects extend 6 miles and mostly end or subside after death; dial: none; the lair’s influence is place-bound and its effects have distinct persistence.

rules.statement: If a gem greatwyrm would be reduced to 0 hit points, its hit points instead reset to 400, its breath weapon and expended legendary resistances are restored, and it can use Mass Telekinesis for the next hour. Defeating it after this awakening is worth an additional 90,000 XP, for 180,000 XP total.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Gem Greatwyrm—Gem Awakening (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one awakening after a short or long rest, with a fixed 400-hit-point reset and one-hour benefit; dial: none; the second phase makes defeat require overcoming a distinct recovery.

rules.statement: A ghost dragon’s attachment to one priceless hoard object anchors its spirit after death. Its terrifying breath recharges on a 6, deals 9d8 cold damage on a failed DC 21 Constitution save (half on success), and frightens failed-save creatures for 1 minute; frightened creatures are paralyzed and can repeat the save at each turn’s end, with immunity to this dragon’s breath for 24 hours after a success or when the effect ends.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ghost Dragon; Ghost Dragon—Terrifying Breath (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one named hoard object anchors the spirit; breath recharges on 6 and successful targets gain 24-hour immunity; dial: none; the anchor and immunity constrain persistence and repeated exposure.

rules.statement: A hollow dragon reduced to 0 hit points breaks into nine pieces, each with AC 19, 27 hit points, and immunity to psychic and poison damage. If all pieces are within 6 miles of the head after 1d6 days, they teleport to it and merge, restoring the dragon to full hit points and activity.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Hollow Dragon—Reconstruction (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reconstruction requires all nine pieces within 6 miles and takes 1d6 days; dial: none; separating or damaging the pieces can delay or prevent the return.

rules.statement: A hoard scarab’s once-per-day dust makes creatures within 5 feet, or 10 feet for a swarm, save against DC 13 Dexterity or glow for 10 minutes, shed dim light in a 10-foot radius, and lose the benefit of invisibility. Every dragon within 1 mile becomes aware of and can unerringly track an affected creature; dispel magic ends the effect.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Hoard Scarabs—Scale Dust (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one use per day, short-radius burst, 10-minute duration, and dispel magic termination; dial: none; exposure makes stealth costly by alerting nearby dragons.

rules.statement: A metallic greatwyrm reduced to 0 hit points instead resets to 450 hit points, recharges its breath weapon, regains expended legendary resistances, and gains mythic actions for 1 hour. Defeating it after this awakening is worth an additional 120,000 XP, for 240,000 XP total.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Metallic Greatwyrm—Metallic Awakening (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one awakening after a short or long rest, with a fixed 450-hit-point reset and one-hour mythic phase; dial: none; the encounter’s second phase is a limited revival rather than ordinary healing.

rules.statement: A metallic peacekeeper can telepathically share what it senses with its master and communicate with that master while both are on the same plane. Its calming mist recharges on a 5–6, fills a 30-foot-radius sphere, and on a failed DC 14 Charisma save charms a creature for 1 minute, leaving it incapacitated with speed 0.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Metallic Peacekeeper—Telepathic Bond; Calming Mist (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sensing and communication require the same plane; the mist has a recharge, save, and one-minute duration; dial: none; the construct’s link and control effect are bounded by distance, plane, and resistance.

rules.statement: A creature struck by the dragon’s tail must make a Strength save or be knocked prone; the save DC is 21 for an ancient moonstone dragon and 18 for an adult.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Moonstone Dragon / Adult Moonstone Dragon, pp. 213–214 (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the listed save and prone result; dial: use the age-specific DC; reason: stronger dragons resist being avoided.

rules.statement: Dream breath affects creatures in its cone: a failed Constitution save causes unconsciousness for 10 minutes, ending early if the creature takes damage or someone uses an action to wake it. The cone is 90 feet for ancient, adult, and young dragons; the wyrmling’s cone size is not legible in this passage.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Moonstone Dragon, Breath Weapon, pp. 213–215 (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the printed save and duration; dial: cone size varies by age; reason: the breath creates a temporary sleep state.

rules.statement: A moonstone dragon’s lair has portals within 6 miles connecting the Material Plane, Feywild, and Border Ethereal. A creature can cross a portal in either direction by spending 5 feet of movement; if the dragon dies, nearby portals close immediately.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Adult Moonstone Dragon, Regional Effects, p. 214 (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: crossings cost 5 feet of movement and are limited to portals in the regional area; dial: portals end when the dragon dies; reason: the dragon’s presence sustains the planar passage.

rules.statement: A moonstone dragon can send a visible creature within 120 feet to a harmless dream demiplane on a failed DC 15 Charisma save. The target is stunned there until initiative count 20 on the next round, then returns to its former space or the nearest unoccupied space.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Moonstone Dragon, Lair Actions, p. 214 (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve on the lair’s initiative-count-20 action; dial: one-round banishment and a save cap the effect; reason: the destination is a brief, harmless dream-space.

rules.statement: A sapphire dragon can transform into any Medium or Small creature while retaining its game statistics except size. The transformation ends if it reaches 0 hit points or uses a bonus action to end it.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Sapphire Dragon, Bonus Actions, p. 216; Adult Sapphire Dragon, p. 217 (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the dragon’s statistics except size; dial: only Medium or Small forms are allowed and the dragon can end it with a bonus action; reason: the change is constrained and reversible.

rules.statement: A sapphire dragon can teleport to an unoccupied space it can see within 60 feet. The same movement can be used as a legendary option by spending 2 legendary actions.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Sapphire Dragon, Bonus Actions and Legendary Actions, p. 216 (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require a visible unoccupied destination within 60 feet; dial: the legendary-action use costs 2 actions; reason: rapid repositioning consumes the dragon’s limited turn resources.

rules.statement: A topaz dragon’s regional influence makes a creature finishing a long rest within 6 miles of its lair make a DC 15 Constitution save or be unable to reduce exhaustion or regain spent Hit Dice. Resistance or immunity to necrotic damage prevents this effect.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Adult Topaz Dragon, Regional Effects, p. 224 (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: check at the end of a long rest; dial: the effect is limited to the lair’s 6-mile region and excludes necrotic-resistant or immune creatures; reason: the dragon’s negative energy impedes recovery.

rules.statement: A topaz dragon can end an active spell of 5th level or lower that it knows is present in its lair.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Adult Topaz Dragon, Lair Actions, p. 224 (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: only an active spell in the lair that the dragon is aware of can be ended; dial: the spell-level ceiling is 5th; reason: the lair’s cancellation effect is bounded.

rules.statement: A topaz dragon’s lair can infuse negative energy: up to two visible creatures in the lair each make a DC 15 Constitution save or take 14 (4d6) necrotic damage. Until initiative count 20 on the next round, creatures in the lair other than the dragon cannot regain hit points.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Adult Topaz Dragon, Lair Actions, p. 224 (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply damage to failed saves and block healing for the stated interval; dial: at most two creatures are directly targeted; reason: the lair’s temporary field suppresses recovery.

rules.statement: A topaz dragon can use its action to cast clairvoyance without components, targeting a body of water within 6 miles of its lair; a sapphire dragon can similarly target a natural stone formation in its 6-mile region. In each case, the lair region carries the dragon’s psionic presence through the named material.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Adult Topaz Dragon, Regional Effects, p. 224; Sapphire Dragon, Regional Effects, p. 219 (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sensing requires an action and a suitable target material in the lair region; dial: water and natural stone are separate target domains; reason: each dragon senses through a material linked to its regional influence.

rules.statement: A gem dragon wyrmling has AC 16, 33 hit points, a 30-foot walking speed, and 60-foot flying and 30-foot swimming speeds; it has resistance to cold and necrotic damage.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Gem dragon wyrmling stat block, p. 223 (dnd5e-fizban#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: fixed creature statistics; dial: none; its defenses and movement are set by its stat block.

rules.statement: The dragon can breathe air and water, and can communicate telepathically with creatures within 120 feet; it also has blindsight to 10 feet and darkvision to 120 feet.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Gem dragon wyrmling stat block, p. 223 (dnd5e-fizban#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these senses and communication ranges are always available; dial: none; they come from the creature’s nature.

rules.statement: Its bite is a melee attack with +4 to hit and 5-foot reach against one target, dealing 7 piercing damage plus 2 additional damage on a hit.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Actions—Bite, p. 223 (dnd5e-fizban#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the attack uses the listed accuracy, reach, and damage; dial: none; it is a standard bodily attack.

rules.statement: When its desiccating breath is available, the dragon exhales energy in a 15-foot cone; each creature in the area makes a DC 11 Constitution save, taking 21 necrotic damage and becoming weakened on a failure, or half damage without weakening on a success. The effect recharges on a roll of 5 or 6, and the weakening lasts until the end of the affected creature’s next turn, imposing disadvantage on Strength checks and halving damage from Strength-based weapon attacks.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Actions—Desiccating Breath, p. 223 (dnd5e-fizban#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed cone, save, damage, recharge, and duration; dial: none; the breath is a limited-use attack with a brief physical weakening effect.

rules.statement: The dragon can cast bane once per day without spell components, using Intelligence as its spellcasting ability; its spell save DC is 12.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Spellcasting (Psionics), p. 223 (dnd5e-fizban#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one component-free casting per day at the listed save DC; dial: none; the stat block supplies the dragon’s limited spell output.

rules.statement: A dragon’s magical power can remain in the world after its death and cause a surge; if the first result would likely kill a character, roll again. Possible results include a final breath attack, the body changing into stone or metal, or the body fading over several days.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 42, dragon death and magical surges (dnd5e-fizban#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a dragon’s death can leave a dangerous magical aftermath; dial: the passage gives examples, not a complete roll table.

rules.statement: A dragon’s death can cause harmful changes within 6 miles of its lair for a time; one example is ordinary vegetation within 1 mile blackening and dying. The dragon’s power can also persist and, over time, contribute to a new generation of dragons.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 42, dragon death and its aftermath (dnd5e-fizban#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the deceased dragon’s power affects nearby life and may endure; dial: the kinds and duration of effects vary.

rules.statement: Dragonsight can give a dragon awareness of its other incarnations on different Material Plane worlds; with further development, a dragon can explore possibilities involving those worlds and potential futures.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 9, Dragonsight; page 48, Prophecy (dnd5e-fizban#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: this is cross-world awareness, not ordinary travel; dial: access to possible futures depends on the dragon’s development.

rules.statement: Portals can connect different worlds of the Material Plane. Moonstone dragons may link multiple lairs with magic portals, and a portal in their lair can be opened in either direction and then closed immediately.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 51, World Adventure Hooks; pages 213–214, moonstone dragon lairs (dnd5e-fizban#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a portal provides passage between linked places; dial: the passage supplies no general travel cost or universal portal rules.

rules.statement: A dragon may serve as a patron by using some of its wealth to support artists, adventurers, or causes; the dragon may expect work, creations, or other service in return. Dragons can also share accumulated knowledge or teach disciples.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 53, dragons as patrons and teachers (dnd5e-fizban#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: support or instruction comes from a patron’s resources and knowledge; dial: what the patron expects in exchange is left to the relationship.

rules.statement: Within 6 miles of a dragon’s lair, a creature may have to make a Wisdom saving throw against a DC based on the dragon’s proficiency bonus and Charisma modifier; on a failure, the dragon charms it for 24 hours. A creature that succeeds is immune to that effect for the next 24 hours.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 66, regional effects related to water (dnd5e-fizban#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lair imposes a bounded charm effect; dial: it affects only creatures subject to the lair’s regional influence.

rules.statement: Nathair’s Mischief fills a visible 20-foot cube within 60 feet with magical effects for up to 1 minute while the caster concentrates. Roll a d4 for the effect when the spell is cast and again at the start of each of the caster’s turns; the caster can move the cube up to 10 feet before each roll.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 22, Nathair’s Mischief (dnd5e-fizban#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the spell repeatedly randomizes a bounded area; dial: concentration and the 1-minute duration limit the effect.

rules.statement: Nathair’s Mischief can charm, blind, or incapacitate creatures that fail the relevant saving throw, or make the cube difficult terrain; each result lasts until the start of the caster’s next turn. The d4 results determine which of these effects occurs.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 22, Mischievous Surge table (dnd5e-fizban#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed saves impose brief conditions or movement restrictions; dial: the effect changes with each random result.

rules.statement: Fizban’s Platinum Shield creates a field around one creature within 60 feet for up to 1 minute, requiring concentration and a dragon scale worth at least 500 gp. The target gains half cover and resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning, and poison damage.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 22, Fizban’s Platinum Shield (dnd5e-fizban#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the spell protects one chosen creature; dial: concentration, duration, range, and the costly material component constrain its use.

rules.statement: The Platinum Shield’s caster can use a bonus action on a later turn to move the field to another creature within 60 feet. While protected, a creature that succeeds on a saving throw against an effect that normally deals half damage instead takes none.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 22, Fizban’s Platinum Shield (dnd5e-fizban#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: protection can be reassigned and improve successful saves; dial: moving it costs a bonus action and requires a valid target within range.

rules.statement: A character with the Draconic Healing gift learns Cure Wounds and can cast it once without a spell slot, regaining that free use after a long rest; the character can also cast it with available spell slots. The character chooses Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as the spellcasting ability for casts granted by the gift.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 17, Gift of the Metallic Dragon (dnd5e-fizban#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the gift grants a spell and one free cast; dial: the free cast refreshes only after a long rest.

rules.statement: The Gift of the Gem Dragon lets its bearer use a reaction when damaged by a creature within 10 feet to force that creature to make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, it takes 2d8 force damage and is pushed; on a success, it takes half damage and is not pushed, and the gift’s uses return after a long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 17, Gift of the Gem Dragon (dnd5e-fizban#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the gift turns a nearby attacker’s harm into a reactive push and damage; dial: it costs a reaction and has limited uses that refresh on a long rest.

rules.statement: When a dragon dies, roll a d6 for its death effect: 1, it immediately uses a lair action centered on itself; 2, it uses its breath weapon; 3, its body becomes stone or metal, or dissipates leaving a transformed organ; 4, roll on the Player’s Handbook Wild Magic Surge table, rerolling an inappropriate result; 5, creatures within 120 feet gain the benefit of finishing a long rest; 6, its body is drawn through a portal to an echo’s lair on another world, strengthening that echo.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Death of a Dragon; Dragon Death Throes table (dnd5e-fizban#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the d6 table; dial: reroll a result likely to kill a character; a dying dragon releases unpredictable magical force.

rules.statement: When a dragon dies, regional effects usually end immediately or shortly afterward; some lingering effects last 1d10 days. Examples include fouled water and nightmares within 6 miles, a tremor within 6 miles, dramatic weather within 6 miles, or vegetation blackening and dying within 1 mile.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Reversal (dnd5e-fizban#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: end effects at death; dial: let selected lingering effects persist for 1d10 days; the dragon’s passing disrupts its influence on the surrounding region.

rules.statement: A dragon’s power can pass to another creature around its death, through means such as inhaling its breath, absorbing power from its corpse, or a burst affecting creatures within 300 feet. The corpse may retain dangerous energy that can seriously injure someone trying to claim its power; the transferred benefit is chosen from the book’s draconic gifts, charms, or other supernatural gifts.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Passing the Mantle (dnd5e-fizban#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow a chosen transfer method and benefit; dial: make claiming corpse power dangerous; the dragon’s power persists briefly and may injure claimants.

rules.statement: Most metallic and gem dragons can change into a Humanoid or Beast form by adult or ancient age; some other dragons have this ability as well. The passage also permits using an adult or ancient dragon’s Change Shape action, or the Monster Manual variant, without changing other traits.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Shape-Shifting (dnd5e-fizban#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the stated age and kind limits; dial: extend the ability to other dragons; shape-changing supports gathering information and moving among other peoples.

rules.statement: A hidecarved dragon has one protective ward, plus one additional ward for each age category above wyrmling. Ward options include immunity to form-altering effects; immunity to effects that sense emotions or read thoughts, with disadvantage on Insight checks to judge it; advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects; resistance to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing; resistance to one additional damage type; or the ability to cast Death Ward on itself, regained after a long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Hidecarved Dragons; Hidecarved Wards table (dnd5e-fizban#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant one ward plus one per age category above wyrmling; dial: choose or roll ward effects; carved sigils protect dragons carrying out a shared purpose.

rules.statement: A dragon’s minion can gain one or more listed traits: on death, it deals 1d8 damage in a 5-foot-radius burst of the type of its master’s breath weapon; it cannot be compelled to disobey its master; when it dies within 60 feet, its master regains hit points equal to four times its challenge rating; it can use its reaction to make an attack that hits its master hit the minion instead if within 5 feet; or it can communicate telepathically with its master while both are on the same plane.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragons’ Minions (dnd5e-fizban#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: add chosen traits to a minion’s statistics; dial: give one or more traits; the dragon’s magic can extend to creatures serving it.

rules.statement: When a dragon joins a hidecarved lauth, its echoes on other worlds gain a measure of the magical protection from its engraved markings; some accept the boon, while others investigate it and may awaken dragonsight.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Hidecarved Dragons; Mystic Markings (dnd5e-fizban#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the protection to the dragon’s echoes; dial: determine whether an echo investigates or develops dragonsight; the sigils’ influence crosses worlds.

rules.statement: In a wild-magic zone, whenever a creature casts a spell of 1st level or higher, roll a d10; on a 1, roll on the Wild Magic Surge table in the Player’s Handbook.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 4, Lair Location table (dnd5e-fizban#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the zone triggers the surge check; dial: use the book’s surge table; in-world reason: the site is a wild-magic area.

rules.statement: A moonstone dragon’s lair can consist of locations on multiple planes linked by portals the dragon controls. The dragon opens portals to travel between them, but may sometimes leave them open, allowing inhabitants of one location to enter another.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 5, Moonstone Dragon Lairs (dnd5e-fizban#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: portals connect the dragon’s lair sites; dial: the dragon may leave a portal open; in-world reason: it forgets to close one.

rules.statement: A dragon given spellcasting can cast each listed spell once per day, requires no material components, and uses Charisma as its spellcasting ability.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 5, Using the Entries (dnd5e-fizban#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one use per listed spell each day, without material components; dial: spell selection is optional; in-world reason: the dragon’s magic expresses its innate power.

rules.statement: A bronze dragon’s regional effect can make sapient creatures that spend a year within 10 miles of its lair find it nearly impossible to break a promise.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 5, Bronze Dragon Lairs; Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect applies after a year within range; dial: use it as a regional effect; in-world reason: the dragon’s lair influences the surrounding area.

rules.statement: A dragon’s curse can cause affected creatures to automatically fail saving throws against that dragon’s Frightful Presence, prevent them from regaining hit points during a short rest, or keep a dead affected creature’s soul on the hoard until the victim finishes a long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 4, Hoard Curse Effects table (dnd5e-fizban#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use one of the listed curse effects; dial: choose which effect applies; in-world reason: the dragon’s death or treasure carries its curse.

rules.statement: In dire circumstances, a follower’s sacrifice of a vast hoard or even their own life might persuade Bahamut to send aid as a divine aspect. The passage gives no guaranteed outcome or fixed exchange rate.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Aspect of Bahamut, p. 164 (dnd5e-fizban#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: aid is exceptional and conditional; dial: what sacrifice is sufficient and whether Bahamut responds, since the passage leaves both to judgment.

rules.statement: Within 6 miles of a legendary moonstone dragon’s lair, portals link the Material Plane, Feywild, and Border Ethereal. A creature can pass through a portal in either direction by spending 5 feet of movement; if the dragon dies, the nearby portals close immediately.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects, pp. 212–214 (dnd5e-fizban#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: crossing costs 5 feet of movement; dial: portal locations and destinations within the stated planes, since the passage does not specify their exact layout.

rules.statement: Within 6 miles of a moonstone dragon’s lair, when a creature that understands a language sleeps or enters a trance, the dragon can make telepathic contact and converse with it in a dream. The creature remembers the conversation when it wakes.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects, pp. 212–214 (dnd5e-fizban#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: the effect requires sleep or trance and language comprehension; dial: whether the dragon initiates contact in a particular instance.

rules.statement: An amethyst dragon can use an action to cast clairvoyance without spell components, targeting any body of water within 6 miles of its lair. If the dragon dies, nearby aquatic populations return to normal over 1d10 days; existing amethyst crystals remain, but new ones form at a normal rate.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects, p. 160 (dnd5e-fizban#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: sensing is limited to regional water and the recovery period is 1d10 days; dial: what the dragon observes through the spell, using the spell’s rules.

rules.statement: A moonstone dragon’s dream breath fills a cone (90 feet for the adult and ancient dragons; 90 feet for the young dragon in the shown stat block). Each creature in the area that fails the listed Constitution save falls unconscious for 10 minutes; damage or another creature using an action to wake it ends the effect.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Moonstone Dragon stat blocks, pp. 211–215 (dnd5e-fizban#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: the stated save, duration, and two ways to end the unconsciousness apply; dial: which creatures lie within the cone.

rules.statement: The amethyst dragon’s singularity breath affects a 90-foot cone: creatures make a DC 23 Strength save, taking 14d8 force damage on a failure or half on a success. A failed save also reduces a creature’s speed to 0 until the start of the dragon’s next turn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Amethyst Dragon, p. 160 (dnd5e-fizban#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: use the listed cone, save DC, damage, and speed duration; dial: which creatures are in the area.

rules.statement: The ancient amethyst dragon can cast each listed spell once per day without spell components, using Intelligence as its spellcasting ability; the listed spells include plane shift. A legendary action costing 2 actions can be used to cast one of its spells or use Psychic Step.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Amethyst Dragon, p. 160 (dnd5e-fizban#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: each listed spell is limited to once per day and the special legendary option costs 2 actions; dial: spell choice, within the listed options.

rules.statement: A legendary moonstone dragon’s spellcasting requires no material components and uses Charisma; the adult and ancient versions can cast faerie fire at will and each of their other listed spells once per day. The adult’s legendary spellcasting option costs 2 actions.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Moonstone Dragon stat blocks, pp. 211–214 (dnd5e-fizban#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: use the listed frequency, ability, and action cost; dial: spell selection within the options given for that dragon.

rules.statement: An adult or ancient amethyst dragon can magically take the form of a Medium or Small creature while retaining its game statistics except for size. The transformation ends if it reaches 0 hit points or uses a bonus action to end it.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Amethyst Dragon, p. 160 (dnd5e-fizban#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: the dragon retains its statistics and has the two stated ways to end the change; dial: the chosen eligible form.

rules.statement: The amethyst dragon can teleport as a bonus action to an unoccupied space it can see within 60 feet. Its legendary Psionics option costs 2 actions and can use that teleport or its spellcasting.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Amethyst Dragon, p. 160 (dnd5e-fizban#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: the teleport is limited to a visible unoccupied space within 60 feet; dial: destination selection within that limit.

rules.statement: A creature that dies on the Abyss dissolves into foul matter, and its spirit returns to the Abyss to form again after a period of time. If it is killed outside the Abyss, its body is destroyed but it reforms in the Abyss; the passage gives no fixed return time.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Demons (dnd5e-mm-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death returns the demon to its home plane; dial: recovery time and whether the return can be prevented, at the cost of a lasting threat.

rules.statement: Devils advance or fall in rank through infernal promotion and demotion, which can alter their physical form; promotion may involve a painful transformation. A devil that dies outside the Nine Hells is destroyed permanently, while one killed there dissolves and later reforms.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Devils (dnd5e-mm-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: rank governs form and survival; dial: how often promotion or demotion changes a devil, with status and bodily stability at stake.

rules.statement: A genie can grant a wish, but after doing so it cannot grant another for a period that is usually one year. It may twist careless wording to undermine the wisher’s intent.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Genies (dnd5e-mm-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a wish is powerful but scarce; dial: the waiting period and how strictly wording is interpreted, with the wisher risking unintended results.

rules.statement: A ghost can leave the Material Plane for the Ethereal Plane, or return from the Ethereal Plane to the Material Plane. It can also attempt to possess a creature nearby; a successful Charisma save resists the attempt, and the possession ends if the ghost is turned or forced out.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ghost (dnd5e-mm-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ghost crosses between two planes and possession is resistible; dial: how often crossing or possession is available, at the cost of exposure to turning or expulsion.

rules.statement: A doppelganger can read a creature’s thoughts at close range, continuing each day while the target remains within range. Barriers block this sense when they include more than 3 feet of wood or dirt, 2 feet of stone, or a thin sheet of lead.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Doppelgangers (dnd5e-mm-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: thoughts are sensed through limited barriers; dial: range and persistence, with lead or sufficiently thick material providing protection.

rules.statement: A dryad can magically charm a creature it can see, with the effect lasting up to 24 hours or until the dryad dies. The target can resist the charm with a saving throw.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Dryads (dnd5e-mm-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the charm ends at its time limit or the dryad’s death; dial: its reach and duration, at the cost of a saving throw and dependence on the dryad.

rules.statement: A ghost’s possession lets it control a target’s body while the target is displaced; the target makes a Charisma save to resist. The ghost retains its own game statistics, and the possession ends if the ghost is turned or forced out.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ghost (dnd5e-mm-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control requires overcoming a save and can be expelled; dial: control duration and what actions the possessor can take, with the host’s body at risk.

rules.statement: A troll regains hit points at the start of its turn, but this recovery stops until the start of its next turn if it takes acid or fire damage. The troll dies only if it starts its turn at 0 hit points and does not regenerate.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Trolls (dnd5e-mm-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: regeneration restores the troll unless acid or fire interrupts it; dial: healing rate and interruption window, with the need to exploit its weakness.

rules.statement: A revenant knows the direction to its chosen foe while both are on the same plane of existence. If the foe is too powerful to defeat before the revenant’s time runs out, the revenant may choose a new target.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Revenants (dnd5e-mm-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the revenant senses direction only on the same plane; dial: whether the pursuit can be redirected, at the cost of its limited time.

rules.statement: Monster categories establish what kind of being a creature is; other game effects can refer to its type or parenthetical tag, but those labels have no rules of their own. A monster’s listed alignment is a default that the DM may change, and creatures that do not make moral choices can be unaligned.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Introduction — Monster Types; Tags; Alignment (pp. 7–8) (dnd5e-mm-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed type, tags, and alignment; dial: change them to suit the setting, since these entries are guidance rather than binding rules.

rules.statement: A monster’s challenge rating estimates the threat it poses to a rested, appropriately equipped party of four characters of the same level. Monsters with a rating of 0 are generally negligible alone; those with no effective attacks award no XP, while those with attacks are worth 10 XP each.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Introduction — Challenge; Experience Points (p. 10) (dnd5e-mm-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the printed rating and XP; dial: the DM can award XP for otherwise neutralizing the threat, because success need not mean killing it.

rules.statement: Innate spells of 1st level or higher are cast at their lowest level unless stated otherwise, cannot be heightened, and cannot be replaced with other spells. A monster with the Spellcasting feature uses its spell slots and can cast a listed spell at a higher level when it has a suitable slot; the DM may replace listed spells with spells of the same level from the same class list.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Introduction — Innate Spellcasting; Spellcasting (p. 11) (dnd5e-mm-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the stat block’s spells and casting limits; dial: replace prepared or known spells when needed, recognizing that this may alter the monster’s threat.

rules.statement: A monster’s psionics tag marks spellcasting done through mental power; such casting typically needs no components, and the tag may be referenced by other rules.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Introduction — Psionics (p. 11) (dnd5e-mm-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed tag and omit components when typical; dial: follow any specific exception, since the passage says component-free casting is usual rather than absolute.

rules.statement: A monster may use the actions in its stat block or a generally available creature action. It cannot use Multiattack for an opportunity attack, which must be a single melee attack.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Introduction — Actions; Multiattack (pp. 11–12) (dnd5e-mm-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the stat-block options and single-attack opportunity limit; no additional cost is stated.

rules.statement: A monster with an ability marked X/Day regains its expended uses after a long rest. For a Recharge X–Y ability, roll a d6 at the start of each of the monster’s turns after use; the ability returns on a listed result, and it also returns after a short or long rest.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Introduction — Limited Usage (p. 12) (dnd5e-mm-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: follow the listed frequency or recharge range; the limiting cost is waiting for a qualifying roll or rest.

rules.statement: A monster’s special hit can establish a grapple without a further check unless the attack says otherwise. A grappled target can use its action to escape with a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against the listed DC, or against 10 plus the monster’s Strength (Athletics) modifier if no DC is given.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Introduction — Grapple Rules for Monsters (p. 12) (dnd5e-mm-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the attack’s grapple and escape DC; the target pays an action and risks failing the check.

rules.statement: A legendary creature can take one legendary action option at a time, only at the end of another creature’s turn; it refreshes its spent legendary actions at the start of its own turn. It cannot use them while incapacitated.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Introduction — Legendary Actions (p. 12) (dnd5e-mm-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the creature’s listed number and options; incapacitation blocks use, and each turn boundary restores spent capacity.

rules.statement: A legendary creature with lair actions can use one option, or none, on initiative count 20, losing ties. Its presence may also cause regional effects; those effects end immediately or fade over time when it dies.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Introduction — A Legendary Creature’s Lair; Lair Actions; Regional Effects (p. 12) (dnd5e-mm-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed lair options and regional effects; dial: regional effects may fade rather than vanish at once, depending on the entry.

rules.statement: An aarakocra deals an extra 1d6 damage when, while flying, it dives at least 30 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a melee weapon attack.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Aarakocra — Dive Attack (p. 12) (dnd5e-mm-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require the stated flight, distance, direction, and hit; the bonus is limited to a qualifying melee strike.

rules.statement: Five aarakocra within 30 feet of one another can summon an air elemental by each spending their action and movement on an aerial dance for three consecutive turns and maintaining concentration throughout. When the dance is complete, it appears in an unoccupied space within 60 feet, is friendly and follows spoken commands, and remains for up to 1 hour, until it or all its summoners die, or until any summoner dismisses it as a bonus action; a summoner must finish a short rest before dancing again. When it returns to the Elemental Plane of Air, aarakocra within 5 feet can travel with it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Summoning Air Elementals, p. 13 (dnd5e-mm-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the five participants, concentration, duration, and rest limit; the in-world cost is coordinated effort and sustained focus.

rules.statement: While underwater, an aboleth’s mucus can infect a creature that touches it or hits it with a melee attack from within 5 feet; a failed DC 14 Constitution save makes the creature diseased for 1d4 hours and able to breathe only underwater. After 1 minute, the disease also prevents regaining hit points except underwater and causes 1d12 acid damage every 10 minutes outside water unless the skin is moistened; at that stage, only heal or another disease-curing spell of 6th level or higher removes it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Aboleth, Mucous Cloud, p. 14 (dnd5e-mm-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the save, staged onset, and specified cures; the cost is a progressively severe disease.

rules.statement: An aboleth can, three times per day, target a creature it sees within 30 feet; a failed DC 14 Wisdom save makes the target charmed and controlled until the aboleth dies or the two are on different planes. The target cannot take reactions, and the pair can communicate telepathically at any distance; damage lets the target repeat the save, and being at least 1 mile away permits another save once per 24 hours.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Aboleth, Enslave, p. 14 (dnd5e-mm-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the uses, range, save, and stated escape checks; control risks ending if the aboleth dies or the target reaches another plane.

rules.statement: When an aboleth’s body is destroyed, its spirit returns to the Elemental Plane of Water, where a new body forms over days or months. It retains its memories and can continue its plans.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Aboleth, Enemies of the Gods, p. 15 (dnd5e-mm-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow return and eventual re-embodiment as described; the cost is loss of the current body and a potentially long delay.

rules.statement: In its lair, an aboleth acts on initiative count 20, losing ties, to use one listed lair effect. It can cast phantasmal force without components on any number of creatures it sees within 60 feet, but while concentrating on that effect cannot use another lair action; alternatively, it can pull creatures within 20 feet of a water pool up to 20 feet into it and knock them prone on failed DC 14 Strength saves, or deal 2d6 psychic damage to chosen creatures it sees in water within 90 feet that fail DC 14 Wisdom saves. The latter two options cannot be repeated until a different lair action has been used.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Aboleth Lair Actions, p. 15 (dnd5e-mm-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: confine these effects to the lair and their stated ranges and saves; the in-world source is the lair’s ambient magic.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of an aboleth’s lair, underground surfaces become wet and difficult terrain and water sources become supernaturally fouled, causing the aboleth’s enemies to vomit after drinking. The aboleth can also use an action to create a concentrated image of itself within that radius, at a place it has seen or a charmed creature can currently see; the image lasts while concentration is maintained, is intangible, and lets the aboleth sense, speak, and use telepathy from its position, but vanishes if damaged. When the aboleth dies, the first two regional effects fade over 3d10 days.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Aboleth Regional Effects, p. 15 (dnd5e-mm-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the 1-mile boundary, concentration, and death fade; the effects are tied to the creature’s lair and presence.

rules.statement: An animated object follows its creator’s commands, or, without a current command, carries out its last order as best it can and may act independently on simple instructions. Its animating magic ends when it reaches 0 hit points, leaving it inanimate and badly damaged; it does not need air, food, drink, or sleep.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Animated Objects, p. 19 (dnd5e-mm-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep command-following and destruction at 0 hit points; the construct’s operating cost excludes ordinary sustenance.

rules.statement: A banshee is bound to the place where it died and cannot travel more than 5 miles from it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Banshee, Sorrow Bound, p. 23 (dnd5e-mm-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enforce the 5-mile boundary; the in-world cost is permanent attachment to the death site.

rules.statement: A basilisk can force a creature that starts its turn within 30 feet and can see it to make a DC 12 Constitution save, unless the basilisk is incapacitated. On a failure the creature becomes restrained and must save again at the end of its next turn; a success ends the effect, while a second failure petrifies it until greater restoration or other magic frees it. A creature can avert its eyes to avoid the initial save, but looking at the basilisk before its next turn immediately triggers a save.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Basilisk, Petrifying Gaze, p. 25 (dnd5e-mm-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the two-stage saves, sight requirement, and specified remedy; avoiding the gaze prevents the initial exposure.

rules.statement: In its lair, a beholder can act on initiative count 20, losing ties, to create one of three effects: a 50-foot-square area within 120 feet becomes difficult terrain until the next round’s initiative count 20; walls within 120 feet grow grasping limbs until the following round’s count 20, potentially grappling creatures that start within 10 feet and fail a DC 15 Dexterity save, with escape by a DC 15 Athletics or Acrobatics check; or an eye appears on a solid surface within 60 feet and fires one random eye ray at a target the beholder can see. It cannot repeat an effect until it has used all three and cannot use the same effect in consecutive rounds.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Beholder Lair Actions, p. 28 (dnd5e-mm-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain initiative timing, ranges, save DCs, and rotation limits; the effects are confined to the lair’s ambient magic.

rules.statement: At the start of each turn, a beholder chooses whether its 150-foot antimagic cone is active and which direction it faces; while active, it suppresses magic in the area, including the beholder’s own eye rays.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Beholder — Antimagic Cone, p. 29 (dnd5e-mm-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial its area or duration; the beholder’s control over the cone limits when its own rays can function.

rules.statement: A beholder fires three randomly selected eye rays, rerolling duplicates, at one to three visible targets within 120 feet; each ray has its own saving throw and effect, including charm, paralysis, fear, slowing, damage, forced movement, sleep, petrification, disintegration, or death.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Beholder — Eye Rays, p. 29 (dnd5e-mm-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the ray list, number, or range; random selection and limited targets constrain the beholder’s output.

rules.statement: A death tyrant’s active 150-foot negative-energy cone prevents creatures in it from regaining hit points; a humanoid that dies there rises as a commanded zombie at the start of its next turn if its body remains intact, keeping its initiative place.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Death Tyrant — Negative Energy Cone, p. 30 (dnd5e-mm-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the cone or animation condition; healing is blocked and only intact humanoid bodies become servants.

rules.statement: Inside its lair, a death tyrant can take one action at initiative count 20, losing ties: it makes a 50-foot cube within 120 feet lightly obscured and difficult terrain until the next count 20; makes hostile creatures starting within 10 feet of a wall save DC 17 Dexterity or become grappled; or opens a spectral eye within 50 feet to fire one random eye ray at a chosen target. It cannot repeat an option until it has used all three, or use the same option on consecutive rounds.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Death Tyrant’s Lair — Lair Actions, pp. 28–29 (dnd5e-mm-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the available effects or cadence; the lair’s ambient magic is limited to a rotating set of effects.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of a death tyrant’s lair, creatures sometimes feel watched; when a creature hostile to the tyrant and aware of it finishes a long rest there, a d20 roll of 10 or less exposes it to one random tyrant eye ray. These effects fade over 1d10 days after the tyrant dies.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Death Tyrant’s Lair — Regional Effects, p. 29 (dnd5e-mm-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the radius, trigger, or fade time; the threat is localized to the lair and diminishes after its source dies.

rules.statement: A spectator summoned by a magical ritual guards its summoner’s chosen place or treasure for 101 years, barring everyone except the summoner unless given other instructions; if the guarded item is stolen or destroyed before the term ends, the spectator vanishes. When its service ends, it may leave or remain where it was posted.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Spectator — Magical Guardians / Freed from Service, p. 32 (dnd5e-mm-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the term or release trigger; service is tied to a specific post and can end early if its protected item is lost.

rules.statement: A spectator may fire up to two eye rays per turn at visible creatures within 90 feet, using each ray at most once that turn; its rays can confuse, paralyze, frighten, or deal necrotic damage. If it succeeds on a save against a spell or a spell attack misses it, it can redirect that spell to a creature it can see within 30 feet, which makes its own save or is targeted by a rerolled attack.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Spectator — Eye Rays and Spell Reflection, p. 32 (dnd5e-mm-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the number or range of rays and redirection; limited uses and nearby alternate targets constrain its defenses.

rules.statement: A vine blight can entangle creatures of its choice in a 15-foot-radius area; the area becomes difficult terrain for nonplants for 1 minute, and affected creatures must pass a DC 12 Strength save or be restrained. A creature can use its action to free itself or another within reach with a successful DC 12 Strength check.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Vine Blight — Entangling Plants, p. 33 (dnd5e-mm-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the area, duration, or escape check; the restraint is temporary and can be actively broken.

rules.statement: A motionless twig blight or vine blight is indistinguishable from a dead shrub or a tangle of vines, respectively.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Twig Blight / Vine Blight — False Appearance, p. 33 (dnd5e-mm-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the disguising forms or detection rules; remaining motionless is the condition for concealment.

rules.statement: A cambion can innately cast alter self, command, and detect magic three times per day each, and plane shift on itself once per day; these spells require no material components. Its spellcasting ability is Charisma, with save DC 14.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Cambion — Innate Spellcasting, p. 37 (dnd5e-mm-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the spell list or daily uses; the fixed innate allotment limits repeated casting.

rules.statement: A cambion can magically charm one visible humanoid within 30 feet for 1 day on a failed DC 14 Wisdom save, causing it to obey spoken commands. If the target takes harm from the cambion or another creature, or receives a suicidal command, it can repeat the save; a successful initial save or an ended effect makes it immune to this charm for 24 hours.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Cambion — Fiendish Charm, p. 37 (dnd5e-mm-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial duration, range, or escape trigger; harm and suicidal orders give the target a chance to break free.

rules.statement: A carrion crawler’s tentacles deal 1d4+2 poison damage and require a DC 13 Constitution save; on failure, the target is poisoned and paralyzed for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each turn to end the effect on a success.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Carrion Crawler — Tentacles, p. 38 (dnd5e-mm-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the save DC or duration; the target receives repeated chances to end the paralysis.

rules.statement: A chuul can sense magic within 120 feet at will; this sense functions like the stated detection spell but is not itself magical.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Chuul — Sense Magic (dnd5e-mm-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: at-will range and detection are fixed; the reason is the chuul’s innate magic-sensing trait.

rules.statement: A creature grappled by a chuul’s tentacles must make a DC 13 Constitution save or be poisoned and paralyzed for up to 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending both effects on a success.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Chuul — Tentacles (dnd5e-mm-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect is limited by a failed save and recurring chances to end it; the cost is the target’s lost actions while paralyzed.

rules.statement: A cloaker attached to a creature takes half the damage dealt to it, rounded down, and the attached creature takes the other half. A Large or smaller target can be detached by using an action to succeed on a DC 16 Strength check; the cloaker can also detach itself by spending 5 feet of movement.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Cloaker — Damage Transfer; Bite (dnd5e-mm-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: damage is divided while the attachment lasts; separation costs an action and a successful check, or movement by the cloaker.

rules.statement: A cloaker’s audible moan forces creatures within 60 feet that can hear it, other than aberrations, to succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom save or become frightened until the end of the cloaker’s next turn. A creature that succeeds is immune to that cloaker’s moan for 24 hours.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Cloaker — Moan (dnd5e-mm-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the fear is brief and requires hearing plus a failed save; successful resistance blocks repeat exposure for 24 hours.

rules.statement: Once per short or long rest, a cloaker outside bright light can create three illusory duplicates. While any remain, visible attackers targeting it with an attack or harmful spell randomly target it or a duplicate; entering an area of light removes all duplicates, and a duplicate disappears when hit or when it fails a damage-effect save.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Cloaker — Phantasms (dnd5e-mm-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the defense is limited to one use per rest and ends in light or when duplicates take the specified hits; its cost is the rest-based use.

rules.statement: After a cockatrice bite, the target must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution save or begin turning to stone and become restrained. It repeats the save at the end of its next turn; success ends the effect, while failure leaves it petrified for 24 hours.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Cockatrice — Bite (dnd5e-mm-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: petrification follows two failed saves, with a second-turn chance to end the threat; the bite initiates the process.

rules.statement: A couatl can magically take the form of a humanoid or beast of its own challenge rating or lower, or return to its true form; it returns to its true form on death. In the alternate form, its statistics and speech remain, but its Armor Class, movement, Strength, Dexterity, and actions are replaced as specified, and it gains eligible capabilities of the new form while retaining its listed exceptions.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Couatl — Change Shape (dnd5e-mm-2014#004)
