rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the shape is limited to humanoid or beast forms at or below its challenge rating; death ends the transformation.

rules.statement: A couatl is immune to scrying and to effects that sense its emotions, read its thoughts, or detect its location.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Couatl — Shielded Mind (dnd5e-mm-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the specified mental and location-sensing effects do not work; the protection is an inherent trait.

rules.statement: A crawling claw is bound to its creator’s will. The creator can mentally command it while it is in sight; without a new command it follows its last one, and commands must be simple enough for its limited senses and intellect.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Crawling Claw — Creator’s Control (dnd5e-mm-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control requires the creator’s sight for new commands and is limited by the claw’s comprehension; otherwise it repeats its last command.

rules.statement: If a demilich’s phylactery remains intact, destroying the demilich is not permanent: its skull reforms after 1d10 days. If it can feed one soul to its phylactery, it regains its lich form.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Demilich — Enduring Existence (dnd5e-mm-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: return is delayed 1d10 days and depends on an intact phylactery; restoring lich form additionally costs one soul.

rules.statement: A demilich’s tomb can prevent unauthorized creatures from teleporting into or out of its area or using planar travel to enter or leave it; such travel still works within the tomb if it is not used to cross its boundary. If the demilich is destroyed, the tomb’s listed traits fade over 10 days.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Demilich’s Lair — Lair Traits (dnd5e-mm-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: unauthorized boundary-crossing travel is blocked while the tomb’s ward persists; destroying the demilich ends the ward gradually over 10 days.

rules.statement: A demon killed outside the Abyss dissolves and reforms there with its mind and essence intact; killing it in the Abyss is the stated way to destroy it permanently. A demon with an essence amulet can reform at a time and place of its choosing after its abyssal form is destroyed.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Demons — Eternal Evil; Protected Essence (dnd5e-mm-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death outside the Abyss returns the demon there rather than ending it; an amulet further lets it choose when and where to reform.

rules.statement: A mortal who breaks a contract with even a low-ranking devil immediately forfeits their soul, which is taken to the Nine Hells; a devil may instead claim the soul before death if the contract permits. Once claimed, only divine intervention can free the soul.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Devils — Dark Dealers and Soul Mongers, p. 67 (dnd5e-mm-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a bargain grants fiendish power or another boon; the dial is the contract’s terms, and the cost can be ownership of the mortal’s soul.

rules.statement: Devils can travel beyond the Lower Planes through portals or powerful summoning magic. A devil that dies outside the Nine Hells disappears and reforms at full strength on its home layer; one that dies in the Nine Hells is destroyed forever.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Devils — Dark Dealers and Soul Mongers; The Infernal Hierarchy, pp. 67–68 (dnd5e-mm-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: travel beyond the Lower Planes requires a portal or powerful summoning; the dial is the route, and death in the Nine Hells carries permanent destruction.

rules.statement: The Nine Hells consists of nine layers. Reaching the deepest layer requires descending through the eight above it in order; the River Styx is described as a direct route that runs from layer to layer, while its journey brings torment and horror.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: The Nine Hells, p. 68 (dnd5e-mm-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: passage to the ninth layer is sequential; the dial is the hazardous route, with the Styx offering speed at the cost of torment and horror.

rules.statement: Every devil above lemure rank has a secret true name. A mortal who learns one can use powerful summoning magic to call that devil and exert some measure of control over it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Devil True Names and Talismans, p. 68 (dnd5e-mm-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a true name enables summoning and limited control; the dial is access to the name and the strength of control the magic permits.

rules.statement: When an evil mortal’s soul reaches the Nine Hells, it becomes a lemure. Archdevils and greater devils can promote lemures to lesser devils; archdevils can promote lesser devils to greater devils; only Asmodeus can promote a greater devil. Promotion carries the devil’s memories into its new form.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: The Infernal Hierarchy — Promotion and Demotion, p. 68 (dnd5e-mm-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: infernal authorities can raise a devil’s rank and change its form; the dial is the authority’s station, and memories persist through promotion.

rules.statement: Archdevils or greater devils can demote a lesser devil to lemure, erasing its memories; an archdevil can demote a greater devil to lesser status, but that devil keeps its memories. Devils cannot promote or demote a devil that has not sworn fealty to them, while Asmodeus can act on any devil because all swear fealty to him.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: The Infernal Hierarchy — Promotion and Demotion, p. 68 (dnd5e-mm-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: demotion is punishment for failure or disobedience; the dial is fealty and rank, with the lowest demotion erasing memory.

rules.statement: A demon using the variant summoning action chooses a listed result and succeeds on the stated chance, which varies by demon and result. The summoned demon appears in an unoccupied space within 60 feet, allies with its summoner, cannot summon other demons, and remains for 1 minute, until it or the summoner dies, or until dismissed by the summoner as an action.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Variant: Demon Summoning, p. 55 (dnd5e-mm-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a demon can call specified reinforcements with a listed chance; the dial is the demon’s own summoning options, and the ally is temporary.

rules.statement: A quasit may become a familiar to a willing master, forming a telepathic bond. While they are within 1 mile, the master can sense through the quasit’s senses; within 10 feet, the master also gains the quasit’s Magic Resistance. The quasit can end its service and bond at any time, for any reason.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Variant: Quasit Familiar, p. 64 (dnd5e-mm-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: willing service creates a sensing bond and nearby protection; the dial is distance, and the quasit can end the arrangement at will.

rules.statement: A quasit can use its action to change between its true form and bat, centipede, or toad form; only its movement modes change, and carried equipment is not transformed. It returns to its true form if it dies.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Quasit, p. 64 (dnd5e-mm-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one action changes the quasit’s form among three animal-like options; the dial is limited to the listed forms and movement changes.

rules.statement: A chasme’s drone affects non-demons that start their turn within 30 feet: they must make a DC 12 Constitution save or fall unconscious for 10 minutes. Creatures unable to hear it automatically succeed; damage or an action splashing the creature with holy water ends the effect, and a successful save or ended effect grants 24-hour immunity.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Chasme — Drone, p. 58 (dnd5e-mm-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: proximity to an audible drone risks unconsciousness; the dial is hearing and the saving throw, with damage or holy water ending the state.

rules.statement: A balor’s whip hit deals its listed damage and forces a DC 20 Strength save; on failure, the target is pulled up to 25 feet toward it. When the balor dies, each creature within 30 feet makes a DC 20 Dexterity save or takes 70 fire damage, taking half on a success; the blast also ignites unattended flammable objects and destroys the balor’s weapons.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Balor — Whip; Death Throes, p. 56 (dnd5e-mm-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a successful whip hit can pull a target, while the balor’s death creates a damaging blast; the dial is distance and saving throws.

rules.statement: A yochlol can use its action to become toxic mist or return to its true form. In mist form it is incapacitated and cannot speak, can fly and pass through any non-airtight space, and is immune to nonmagical damage; a creature sharing its space at the start of its turn must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution save or be poisoned and incapacitated until that turn ends.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Yochlol — Mist Form, p. 66 (dnd5e-mm-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: mist form grants passage and protection but prevents action and speech; the dial is its restricted movement and the nearby creature’s save.

rules.statement: A devil can be called from the Nine Hells and compelled to serve; a talisman bearing its true name can assist with binding, and making such a relic requires the blood of a worthy sacrifice, typically someone loved by its maker. A summoned devil generally resents service and tries to corrupt its summoner so the summoner’s soul goes to the Nine Hells; imps readily serve as familiars but also seek to corrupt their masters.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Devils; Variant: Imp Familiar, pp. 68–69 (dnd5e-mm-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: service carries a corruption risk; dial: the true-name talisman and sacrifice make binding more accessible, at the cost of a loved one’s blood.

rules.statement: Some devils can attempt a magical summoning once per day, with the chance and available reinforcements depending on the devil; listed chances range from 30% to 60%, while a pit fiend succeeds automatically. A summoned devil appears in an unoccupied space within 60 feet, is an ally, cannot summon other devils, and remains for 1 minute, until it or its summoner dies, or until dismissed by the summoner as an action.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Summon Devil, p. 68 (dnd5e-mm-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reinforcements are temporary and usually uncertain; dial: the pit fiend’s summoning is reliable, reflecting its greater power.

rules.statement: An imp familiar can contract to serve a willing master and form a telepathic bond; within 1 mile, the master senses what the imp senses, and within 10 feet the master shares the imp’s Magic Resistance trait. If the master breaks the contract’s terms, the imp may end its service and the bond.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Variant: Imp Familiar, p. 69 (dnd5e-mm-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bond grants remote perception and nearby magical defense; dial: the imp can withdraw both benefits if the master violates the bargain.

rules.statement: A lemure that dies in the Nine Hells returns with all its hit points after 1d10 days, unless a good-aligned creature killed it while under a bless spell, or holy water is sprinkled on its remains.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Lemure, p. 77 (dnd5e-mm-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death is temporary for this devil in its home plane; dial: specified holy intervention prevents its return.

rules.statement: An imp can use an action to change into a rat, raven, or spider, or back to its true shape; only its movement speeds change, its equipment stays as it is, and death restores its true shape. It can also turn invisible until it attacks or loses concentration, and its carried or worn equipment becomes invisible with it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Imp, p. 77 (dnd5e-mm-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation and invisibility enable disguise or concealment; dial: invisibility ends on an attack or lost concentration.

rules.statement: A bearded devil’s beard hit can poison a creature for 1 minute on a failed DC 12 Constitution save; while poisoned this way, the target cannot regain hit points, and it repeats the save at the end of each turn to end the effect. Its glaive can also inflict a wound on an undead or construct: the wound deals 1d10 hit points at the start of each turn, increasing by 1d10 per further glaive hit; a DC 12 Wisdom (Medicine) action or magical healing closes it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Bearded Devil, p. 71 (dnd5e-mm-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: poison and wounds impede recovery or worsen over time; dial: a repeated save, treatment, or magical healing ends the relevant effect.

rules.statement: An erinyes’s longbow hit can poison a target that fails a DC 14 Constitution save; the poison lasts until lesser restoration or similar magic removes it. The erinyes can also use a reaction to gain +4 AC against one melee attack, provided it sees the attacker and is wielding a melee weapon.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Erinyes, p. 73 (dnd5e-mm-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: poison persists without ordinary timed recovery; dial: restorative magic is required, while the defensive reaction has sight and weapon limits.

rules.statement: A horned devil’s tail can cause an infernal wound in a non-undead, non-construct target that fails a DC 17 Constitution save; it loses 3d6 hit points at the start of each turn, with the loss increasing by 3d6 each time the devil hits it with the tail. A creature can use an action and succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom (Medicine) check to stop the wound, and magical healing also closes it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Horned Devil, p. 74 (dnd5e-mm-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the wound escalates with further hits; dial: medical intervention or magical healing can end it.

rules.statement: An ice devil’s spear can impose a 1-minute effect after a failed DC 15 Constitution save: speed falls by 10 feet, the target cannot take both an action and bonus action on a turn, and it cannot take reactions. The target repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the effect on a success.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ice Devil, p. 76 (dnd5e-mm-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect restricts movement and actions; dial: repeated saves provide an escape before its 1-minute limit.

rules.statement: A pit fiend’s hostile creature starting its turn within 20 feet must make a DC 21 Wisdom save or become frightened until the start of its next turn; on a successful save, that creature is immune to this aura for 24 hours. The pit fiend can also cast detect magic and fireball at will, and hold monster and wall of fire three times per day each, without material components; its spell save DC is 21 and Charisma is its spellcasting ability.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Pit Fiend, p. 78 (dnd5e-mm-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: proximity can induce brief fear and innate spells have stated usage limits; dial: a successful save grants a full-day reprieve from the aura.

rules.statement: An ice devil can create an opaque ice wall on a visible solid surface within 60 feet, up to 30 feet long and 10 feet high or a dome up to 20 feet across; creatures in its space are pushed out and may choose a side unless incapacitated, then save DC 17 Dexterity against 10d6 cold damage, half on success. The wall lasts 1 minute or until the devil is incapacitated or dies; it can be breached, and each destroyed section leaves damaging frigid air that affects creatures moving through it until the wall vanishes.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ice Devil, Wall of Ice, p. 76 (dnd5e-mm-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the wall blocks and damages while creating hazardous gaps; dial: it is temporary, rechargeable only as specified by its action, and vulnerable to damage and fire.

rules.statement: If a dracolich’s body is destroyed, its spirit returns to its gem if both are on the same plane; if the gem touches another dragon’s corpse, the spirit can possess it and form a new dracolich. If the gem is on another plane when the body is destroyed, the spirit has nowhere to return and passes into the afterlife.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Dracolich Phylacteries, p. 84 (dnd5e-mm-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the gem preserves the spirit and permits a new body; dial: return depends on the gem’s location and access to a dragon corpse.

rules.statement: Only an ancient or adult true dragon can become a dracolich; a younger dragon or a non-true dragon with the dragon type dies in the attempt, and a shadow dragon cannot undergo the change. A successful transformation changes its type to undead, removes traits dependent on living physiology, and means it no longer needs air, food, or sleep; it gains necrotic resistance, poison immunity, and immunity to being charmed, exhausted, frightened, paralyzed, or poisoned, while retaining prior immunities and gaining advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Dracolich template, p. 85 (dnd5e-mm-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation requires an eligible true dragon; dial: the transformation is fatal to younger or ineligible creatures, and undead existence removes living needs.

rules.statement: A dragon can become a shadow dragon only if it is a true dragon born in the Shadowfell or resident there for several years; a dracolich cannot become one. The change grants necrotic resistance, doubled proficiency on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and in dim light or darkness resistance to damage except force, psychic, or radiant, plus the ability to Hide as a bonus action; sunlight imposes disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Wisdom checks.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Shadow Dragon template, pp. 86–87 (dnd5e-mm-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: only true dragons can transform; dial: years in the Shadowfell or birth there are the exposure cost, while sunlight weakens the result.

rules.statement: A shadow dragon changes acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison damage dealt by its bite to necrotic damage, and its damaging breath weapon likewise deals necrotic damage. A humanoid reduced to 0 hit points by that breath dies, and an undead shadow rises from the corpse immediately after the dragon's initiative and obeys it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Shadow Dragon template, p. 87 (dnd5e-mm-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: damage types change as part of the transformation; dial: breath-created servants require a humanoid victim to die.

rules.statement: A dragon that becomes a dracolich or shadow dragon might keep, lose, or gain any of its lair actions, at the DM's discretion.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Dracolich template, p. 85; Shadow Dragon template, p. 86 (dnd5e-mm-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: lair actions are not fixed by the transformation; dial: their availability is set for the individual lair.

rules.statement: A young or older dragon may innately cast a number of spells each day equal to its Charisma modifier, each spell once per day without material components. Spell level is capped at one-third its challenge rating, rounded down; its spell-attack bonus is proficiency bonus plus Charisma modifier, and its save DC is 8 plus proficiency bonus plus Charisma modifier.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Variant: Dragons as Innate Spellcasters, p. 87 (dnd5e-mm-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: this is an optional variant; dial: spell count, daily reuse, and maximum level limit the dragon's innate magic.

rules.statement: A shadowfell portal can form in a desolate place or deeply shadowed cavern and transport a nearby lairing dragon into the Shadowfell without its awareness; a dragon sleeping for months or years may be carried through while it sleeps. Years spent there can transform a true dragon, and returning to the Material Plane does not reverse that change.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Dragon, Shadow, pp. 85–86 (dnd5e-mm-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: portals occur in specified gloomy places; dial: involuntary transport and years of exposure impose the travel and transformation cost.

rules.statement: A legendary dragon's lair can warp its surrounding region: a black dragon's territory within 6 miles takes twice as long to cross, its nearby water is fouled, and fog lightly obscures the land; a blue dragon's territory within 6 miles has thunderstorms and dust devils, and concealed sinkholes may form. On the dragon's death, some effects end immediately or fade over 1d10 days, while persistent terrain changes such as sinkholes remain.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Black Dragon Regional Effects, p. 90; Blue Dragon Regional Effects, p. 93 (dnd5e-mm-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: effects are tied to a legendary dragon's lair and listed region; dial: travel hazards and lingering terrain are the local cost, with some effects ending after death.

rules.statement: A dragon's breath weapon recharges on a roll of 5 or 6 at the start of its turn; when available, it affects the specified line or cone, and each creature in the area makes the listed saving throw, taking the listed damage on a failure or half on a success. For example, an adult blue dragon's lightning breath is a 90-foot line 5 feet wide, with a DC 19 Dexterity save and 12d10 lightning damage.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Adult Blue Dragon stat block, p. 92 (dnd5e-mm-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recharge and area determine when and whom the breath can affect; dial: the saving throw can reduce damage but does not eliminate the threat.

rules.statement: A dragon's Frightful Presence targets creatures of its choice within 120 feet that are aware of it; each must succeed on the listed Wisdom save or be frightened for 1 minute, and may repeat the save at the end of each turn to end the effect. A creature that succeeds or ends the effect becomes immune to that dragon's presence for 24 hours.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Adult Blue Dragon stat block, p. 92 (dnd5e-mm-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: awareness, range, and a saving throw govern who is affected; dial: the condition can be ended by repeated saves and grants a day of immunity.

rules.statement: A legendary dragon has 3 legendary actions, used one at a time only at the end of another creature's turn, and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. A wing attack costs 2 actions, damages and can knock prone nearby creatures that fail a Dexterity save, then lets the dragon fly up to half its flying speed.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Adult Blue Dragon stat block, p. 92 (dnd5e-mm-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: actions are capped at 3 per round and gated by other creatures' turns; dial: the wing attack spends 2 actions and allows movement only after its save-based effect.

rules.statement: A black dragon's lair can pull a grounded creature up to 20 feet into a visible water pool within 120 feet unless it succeeds on a DC 15 Strength save; it can also create a persistent insect cloud that damages creatures on entry and at turn-end, or magical darkness that blocks darkvision and nonmagical light. The dragon cannot use the same lair effect in consecutive rounds, and the darkness dispels overlapping light created by a spell of 2nd level or higher.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Black Dragon Lair Actions, p. 90 (dnd5e-mm-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: lair actions occur on initiative count 20 and cannot repeat in consecutive rounds; dial: the effects are geographically limited and impose saving throws or spell interaction.

rules.statement: A blue dragon's lair can bury one visible creature under falling ceiling debris unless it succeeds on a DC 15 Dexterity save; a DC 10 Strength check as an action frees a buried target, which is restrained and unable to breathe or stand. It can instead blind creatures in a sand cloud for up to 1 minute, with end-of-turn saves, or arc lightning between two visible solid surfaces within the stated 120-foot limits.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Blue Dragon Lair Actions, p. 93 (dnd5e-mm-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: lair effects trigger on initiative count 20 and cannot repeat consecutively; dial: burial costs an action and a check to escape, while blindness allows repeated saves.

rules.statement: A green dragon can breathe both air and water. Its poison breath recharges on a roll of 5 or 6; it fills a 15-foot cone, and each creature there makes a DC 11 Constitution save, taking 21 (6d6) poison damage on a failure or half on a success.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Green Dragon Wyrmling, p. 95 (dnd5e-mm-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; no dial; this is a fixed creature capability with a stated recharge and save.

rules.statement: On initiative count 20, a green dragon in its lair can make grasping roots and vines fill a 20-foot-radius area within 120 feet; creatures there that fail a DC 15 Strength save are restrained. A creature can use an action to free itself or another creature with a successful DC 15 Strength check; the roots wilt when this effect is used again or the dragon dies.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Green Dragon’s Lair—Lair Actions, p. 96 (dnd5e-mm-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial; the effect is limited to a visible ground area and a recurring lair action; restraint and an action-based escape are its costs.

rules.statement: A green dragon can create a thorny wall on a solid surface it can see within 120 feet, up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high, and 5 feet thick. Creatures in its space make a DC 15 Dexterity save or take 18 (4d8) piercing damage and are pushed out; crossing costs 4 feet of movement per foot, and creatures in contact risk the same damage each round, while the wall ends when the dragon repeats this lair action or dies.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Green Dragon’s Lair—Lair Actions, p. 96 (dnd5e-mm-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial; the wall is a temporary, bounded obstruction with traversal and damage costs, rather than a permanent structure.

rules.statement: A green dragon can surround a creature it can see within 120 feet with magical fog; on a failed DC 15 Wisdom save, the creature is charmed until initiative count 20 of the next round.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Green Dragon’s Lair—Lair Actions, p. 96 (dnd5e-mm-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; the save can prevent the effect and its duration is limited to the next round.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of a legendary green dragon’s lair, magical thickets form maze-like, line-of-sight-blocking passages; moving through them costs 4 feet per foot, and a creature in them risks 1d6 piercing damage each round on a failed DC 15 Dexterity save. If the dragon dies, the thickets become mundane within 1d10 days and lose their thorns.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Green Dragon’s Lair—Regional Effects, p. 96 (dnd5e-mm-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial; the effect is confined to the lair’s surrounding mile and weakens after the dragon’s death.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of a legendary green dragon’s lair, it leaves no physical tracks unless it chooses otherwise, and can ignore impediments and damage from ordinary plants as those plants part before it. Magical means can still track it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Green Dragon’s Lair—Regional Effects, p. 96 (dnd5e-mm-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial; concealment is local and does not defeat magical tracking.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of a legendary green dragon’s lair, nearby rodents and birds act as its eyes and ears; when it dies, this supernatural link ends.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Green Dragon’s Lair—Regional Effects, p. 96 (dnd5e-mm-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial; surveillance depends on local animals and ends with the dragon’s death.

rules.statement: An ancient red dragon can turn a failed saving throw into a success up to three times per day.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ancient Red Dragon, p. 98 (dnd5e-mm-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; the benefit is capped at three uses per day.

rules.statement: An ancient red dragon’s breath recharges on a roll of 5 or 6 and fills a 90-foot cone; each creature there makes a DC 24 Dexterity save, taking 91 (26d6) fire damage on a failure or half on a success.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ancient Red Dragon—Actions, p. 98 (dnd5e-mm-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; a successful save halves the damage and the breath has a recharge limit.

rules.statement: A creature that fails an ancient red dragon’s DC 21 Wisdom save while within 120 feet and aware of it becomes frightened for 1 minute; it may repeat the save at the end of each turn, ending the effect on a success. A successful save, or ending the effect, grants immunity to that dragon’s frightful presence for 24 hours.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ancient Red Dragon—Actions, p. 98 (dnd5e-mm-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; repeat saves allow escape, and success gives temporary immunity.

rules.statement: A legendary red dragon’s lair can open rocky fissures within 1 mile as portals to the Elemental Plane of Fire, allowing fire elementals to enter and dwell nearby; these portals and the region’s other supernatural effects fade over 1d10 days after the dragon dies.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Red Dragon’s Lair—Regional Effects, p. 99 (dnd5e-mm-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial; access is limited to fissures near the lair and the portals fade after the dragon’s death.

rules.statement: An ancient brass dragon can magically become a humanoid or beast whose challenge rating is no higher than its own, or return to its true form; it resumes its true form if it dies. It keeps its alignment, hit points, Hit Dice, speech, proficiencies, Legendary Resistance, lair actions, mental ability scores, and this ability, while other statistics are replaced except for class features and legendary actions; it chooses whether its equipment is absorbed or carried.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ancient Brass Dragon—Actions, p. 105 (dnd5e-mm-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial; the form is challenge-rating limited and most statistics are replaced, while death ends the disguise.

rules.statement: When the dragon’s breath is available again on a roll of 5–6, it uses one of its listed breath effects. A target in the stated line or cone makes the specified saving throw; the effect gives its listed damage or other result, with damage halved on a successful save where specified.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Dragon stat blocks — Breath Weapons (dnd5e-mm-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recharge and area are fixed by the stat block; the save and listed effect determine each target’s outcome.

rules.statement: A brass wyrmling exhales sleep gas in a 15-foot cone; each creature there must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution save or be unconscious for 1 minute. Damage to the creature or another creature using an action to wake it ends the effect early.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Brass Dragon Wyrmling — Sleep Breath (dnd5e-mm-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the cone, save DC, and duration are fixed; the effect ends through harm or an ally’s action.

rules.statement: A dragon can frighten chosen creatures within 120 feet that are aware of it; each must succeed on the stat block’s Wisdom save or be frightened for 1 minute. Affected creatures can repeat the save at the end of each turn, and a creature that succeeds or ends the effect becomes immune to that dragon’s fright for 24 hours.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Dragon stat blocks — Frightful Presence (dnd5e-mm-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: awareness, range, save, and repeated chances constrain the effect; success grants temporary immunity.

rules.statement: A copper dragon’s slowing gas makes creatures that fail a Constitution save unable to take reactions, halves their speed, limits them to one attack per turn, and lets them take an action or bonus action but not both, for up to 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the effects on a success.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Copper Dragon — Slowing Breath (dnd5e-mm-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the listed movement and action limits apply only after a failed save and can end early on a later save.

rules.statement: An older bronze, copper, or gold dragon can magically take the form of a humanoid or beast whose challenge rating is no greater than its own, or return to its true form; death also restores its true form. It chooses whether carried equipment is absorbed or borne, retains specified traits including hit points, speech, proficiencies, key mental scores, and this ability, while most other statistics are replaced by the new form’s; the new form’s class features and legendary actions are excluded.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Adult and Ancient Dragon stat blocks — Change Shape (dnd5e-mm-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation is limited by form type and challenge rating; only the specified traits persist.

rules.statement: A dragon with legendary actions has 3 uses, spent one option at a time only at the end of another creature’s turn, and regains spent uses at the start of its turn. Detect and Tail Attack cost one use each; Wing Attack costs two, forces creatures within the listed radius to save or take damage and fall prone, then lets the dragon fly up to half its flying speed.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Dragon stat blocks — Legendary Actions (dnd5e-mm-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the per-turn pool, timing window, and two-use cost bound extra actions.

rules.statement: A copper dragon can turn a visible 10-foot-square ground area within 120 feet into 3-foot-deep mud; creatures there must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity save or become restrained. A creature can use an action to make a DC 15 Strength check to free itself or another within reach; crossing the mud costs 2 feet of movement per foot, and on the next round it hardens, raising the escape DC to 20.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Copper Dragon’s Lair — Lair Actions (dnd5e-mm-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect is restricted to a small chosen area and has a timed hardening and a costly escape action.

rules.statement: A brass dragon’s lair can produce helpful or misleading tracks in sand within 6 miles, illusory monsters within 1 mile that cannot harm creatures and are revealed by physical contact or a successful DC 20 Investigation check, and awareness of creatures with Intelligence 3 or higher that come within 30 feet of a water source within 1 mile. When the dragon dies, the tracks fade over 1d10 days and the other effects end immediately.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Brass Dragon’s Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-mm-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each effect has a stated radius and its persistence depends on the dragon’s survival.

rules.statement: Within 6 miles of a bronze dragon’s lair, the dragon can alter weather once per day as the weather-control spell; underwater plants become vividly colored, and the dragon can create illusory sounds in different parts of its lair. If the dragon dies, the weather eventually returns to normal and the other changes fade over 1d10 days.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Bronze Dragon’s Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-mm-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the weather change is limited to once daily and a defined region; effects fade after the dragon’s death.

rules.statement: On initiative count 20 in its lair, a gold dragon can glimpse the future, gaining advantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws until initiative count 20 on the next round.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Gold Dragon’s Lair — Lair Actions (dnd5e-mm-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the benefit lasts only until the next round’s initiative count 20.

rules.statement: On initiative count 20 in its lair, a gold dragon can force one creature it sees within 120 feet to make a DC 15 Charisma save or be sent to a dream plane the dragon imagines. The creature can use its action to contest the dragon with a Charisma check to escape; otherwise the effect ends at the next initiative count 20, returning it to its prior space or the nearest unoccupied space.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Gold Dragon’s Lair — Lair Actions (dnd5e-mm-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the displacement is a brief, bounded lair effect with an action-based escape attempt and automatic return.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of a copper dragon’s lair, normally non-speaking tiny beasts can speak and understand Draconic, but cannot speak with other creatures; intelligent creatures in the same region tend to giggle, making even serious matters seem amusing. The effects end immediately when the dragon dies.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Copper Dragon’s Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-mm-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: speech is restricted to one language and one-mile region; both changes depend on the dragon’s presence.

rules.statement: A silver dragon’s lair creates magical regional effects: within 6 miles, it can telepathically contact and converse in dreams with language-capable creatures when they sleep or enter trance or reverie; nearby opalescent mist warns of nearby evil by taking haunting forms; and gems and pearls within 1 mile shed dim light in a 5-foot radius. All these effects end immediately if the dragon dies.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Regional Effects, gold dragon (p. 116); Regional Effects, silver dragon (p. 119) (dnd5e-mm-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the radii and warning behavior; the dragon’s presence sustains the lair’s effects.

rules.statement: A silver dragon can alter weather once per day in a radius centered on its lair, using the effect of Control Weather. When it dies, the changed weather returns to normal as that spell describes, while its other regional effects fade after 1d10 days.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Regional Effects, silver dragon (p. 119) (dnd5e-mm-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the duration and scope; weather changes are tied to the dragon’s lair and death.

rules.statement: A silver dragon’s lair winds buoy non-evil creatures falling within 1 mile, unless the fall was caused by the dragon or its allies: they descend at 60 feet per round and take no falling damage. Given days or longer, the dragon can make clouds and fog in its lair as solid as stone and shape them into structures or other objects.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Regional Effects, silver dragon (p. 119) (dnd5e-mm-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the protected creatures and construction time; both effects depend on the dragon’s lair.

rules.statement: A silver dragon can magically become a humanoid or beast whose challenge rating does not exceed its own, or return to its true form; death also restores its true form. It chooses whether carried or worn equipment is absorbed or carried in the new shape, and retains its alignment, hit points, Hit Dice, speech, proficiencies, Legendary Resistance, lair actions, mental ability scores, and this shape-changing action, while other statistics are replaced except for class features or legendary actions of the adopted form.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Change Shape, adult and ancient silver dragon (pp. 117–118) (dnd5e-mm-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the allowed forms and retained traits; the dragon’s power limits transformation and preserves specified abilities.

rules.statement: A silver dragon’s Frightful Presence affects creatures it chooses that are within 120 feet and aware of it: each must make a Wisdom save (DC 18 for adult, DC 21 for ancient) or become frightened for 1 minute. An affected creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on success; a successful save or ended effect grants immunity to that dragon’s presence for 24 hours.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Frightful Presence, adult and ancient silver dragon (pp. 117–118) (dnd5e-mm-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the save DC and range by dragon age; awareness and a repeat save constrain the effect.

rules.statement: A silver dragon’s paralyzing breath recharges on a roll of 5–6 and fills a cone (15 feet for a wyrmling, 30 feet for a young dragon, 60 feet for an adult, or 90 feet for an ancient dragon). Creatures in it make a Constitution save (DC 13, 17, 20, or 24 respectively) or become paralyzed for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each turn to end the effect on success.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Breath Weapons, silver dragon (pp. 117–119) (dnd5e-mm-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial cone, save DC, and recharge by age; use is limited by the recharge roll and repeat saves.

rules.statement: The dryad can magically charm a visible humanoid or beast within 30 feet that fails a DC 14 Wisdom save, making it regard her as a trusted friend and favor her requests without giving her control. The creature can repeat its save if the dryad or her allies harm it; otherwise the effect lasts 24 hours or until the dryad dies, leaves the target’s plane, or ends it as a bonus action; a successful save grants 24-hour immunity, and she can maintain the charm on at most one humanoid and three beasts.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Fey Charm, dryad (p. 122) (dnd5e-mm-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial targets and maximum simultaneous bonds; harm, separation, death, and the dryad’s choice end the effect.

rules.statement: A dryad can spend 10 feet of movement, once on her turn, to enter a living tree within reach and emerge in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of a second living tree she can see, up to 60 feet away; both trees must be at least Large.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Tree Stride, dryad (p. 122) (dnd5e-mm-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the distance and tree-size requirement; travel costs movement and requires two suitable trees.

rules.statement: A duergar can enlarge itself and its carried or worn equipment for 1 minute, becoming Large and doubling the damage dice of Strength-based weapon attacks; it has advantage on Strength checks and saves. It reaches the largest size that fits if the space available prevents it from becoming Large, and the ability recharges after a short or long rest.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Enlarge, duergar (p. 123) (dnd5e-mm-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial duration and size by available space; the ability is limited by its rest-based recharge.

rules.statement: A duergar can turn itself and its equipment invisible until it attacks, casts a spell, enlarges itself, or loses concentration, for up to 1 hour. It can use this ability again after a short or long rest.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Invisibility, duergar (p. 123) (dnd5e-mm-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the duration and break conditions; maintaining the effect requires concentration and it recharges on a rest.

rules.statement: A drider can innately cast Dancing Lights at will, and can cast Darkness and Faerie Fire once each per day, without material components; its spellcasting ability is Wisdom and its save DC is 13. A dryad instead uses Charisma (save DC 14): Druidcraft at will, Entangle and Goodberry three times each per day, and Barkskin, Pass without Trace, and Shillelagh once each per day, all without material components.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Innate Spellcasting, drider (p. 120) and dryad (p. 122) (dnd5e-mm-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial spell access and daily uses; innate casting provides specific spells without material components but limits repeated use.

rules.statement: Elementals are bodiless life forces on their home planes; magic can call them to the Material Plane, where they instinctively resent being summoned and require force of will to control. Powerful magic can bind an elemental spirit into a material form, and the binding’s strength and the materials used determine how securely and effectively it holds the spirit.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Elementals: Conjured by Magic; Bound and Shaped (p. 124) (dnd5e-mm-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the binding strength and material; summoning and confinement impose control and material requirements.

rules.statement: A creature struck by the drow’s hand crossbow must make a DC 13 Constitution save or be poisoned for 1 hour; on a failure by 5 or more, it is also unconscious until it takes damage or another creature uses an action to wake it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Drow — Hand Crossbow (pp. 129–130) (dnd5e-mm-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: poison and unconsciousness follow a failed save; dial: duration and severity; the target can be awakened or harmed to end unconsciousness.

rules.statement: Drow can innately cast dancing lights at will and darkness and faerie fire once each per day; elite warriors and mages also have levitate once per day, usable on themselves only. These castings require no material components and use Charisma for the save DC.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Drow — Innate Spellcasting (pp. 129–130) (dnd5e-mm-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: abilities are available without study or material components; dial: daily uses and self-only levitation limit output.

rules.statement: A drow mage is a 10th-level wizard with Intelligence-based spellcasting, DC 14 saves, +6 spell attacks, and the listed prepared spells and spell slots: four 1st-level, three each 2nd–4th-level, and two 5th-level slots.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Drow Mage — Spellcasting (p. 130) (dnd5e-mm-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: learned spellcasting uses prepared spells and finite slots; dial: preparation and slot counts constrain use.

rules.statement: Once per day, a drow mage can summon a quasit, or attempt to summon a shadow demon with a 50 percent chance of success. The demon appears within 60 feet, acts as an ally, cannot summon other demons, and remains for 10 minutes or until it or the summoner dies, or the summoner dismisses it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Drow Mage — Summon Demon (p. 130) (dnd5e-mm-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a successful call produces a temporary allied demon; dial: once daily, uncertain shadow-demon outcome, and fixed duration.

rules.statement: A drow priestess can attempt once per day to summon a yochlol within 60 feet; it is an ally, cannot summon other demons, and remains for 10 minutes or until it or the priestess dies, or she dismisses it. A failed attempt deals 1d10 psychic damage to the priestess.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Drow Priestess of Lolth — Summon Demon (p. 130) (dnd5e-mm-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the call can create a temporary ally; dial: a 30 percent success chance and psychic harm on failure impose risk.

rules.statement: An empyrean’s mood can alter nearby surroundings: unhappiness may bring environmental signs of desolation, while jubilation brings sunlight, frolicking animals, and birdsong. When an empyrean dies, its spirit returns to its home plane, where a parent resurrects it unless there is a reason not to.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Empyrean — Manifest Emotion; Immortal Titans (p. 131) (dnd5e-mm-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: mood affects the surroundings and death returns the spirit home; dial: environmental changes and resurrection depend on disposition and a parent’s choice.

rules.statement: An ettercap’s web attack recharges on a roll of 5–6 and can restrain one Large or smaller creature it hits; the target can use an action to escape with a DC 11 Strength check, or the restraint ends if the webbing is destroyed (AC 10, 5 hit points, resistance to bludgeoning, immunity to poison and psychic damage).
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ettercap — Web (p. 132) (dnd5e-mm-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a successful web hit restrains; dial: recharge, escape action, and breakable webbing limit the hold.

rules.statement: An ettin has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and on saves against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, or knocked unconscious. When one head sleeps, the other remains awake.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ettin — Two Heads; Wakeful (p. 133) (dnd5e-mm-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the two-headed body resists listed states and maintains watch; dial: advantages apply only to specified checks, saves, and sleep circumstance.

rules.statement: A faerie dragon’s euphoria breath recharges on a 5–6; one creature within 5 feet that fails a DC 11 Wisdom save is affected for 1 minute, cannot take reactions, and rolls a d6 at the start of each turn to determine its behavior. On a 5–6 result it can spend its turn making a DC 11 Wisdom save to end the effect.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Faerie Dragon — Euphoria Breath (p. 134) (dnd5e-mm-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save imposes a timed behavior effect; dial: the target’s turn-by-turn options are random and a successful save ends it.

rules.statement: A flameskull destroyed at 0 hit points regains all its hit points after 1 hour unless holy water is sprinkled on its remains or dispel magic or remove curse is used on them. If it can no longer fulfill its original purpose, a re-formed flameskull is no longer bound to its creator.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Flameskull — Rejuvenation; Eldritch Rejuvenation (p. 135) (dnd5e-mm-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: destruction leads to re-formation; dial: specific countermeasures prevent it, and loss of purpose ends its service.

rules.statement: A flumph can perceive the content of telepathic communication within 60 feet and cannot be surprised by creatures using telepathy; it is immune to effects that sense its emotions or read its thoughts, and to all divination spells.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Flumph — Advanced Telepathy; Telepathic Shroud (p. 136) (dnd5e-mm-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: telepathic traffic is perceptible nearby while the flumph’s own mind is shielded; dial: the perception and immunity have defined targets and range.

rules.statement: A galeb duhr can animate up to two visible boulders within 60 feet once per day; each uses its statistics except it has Intelligence 1 and Charisma 1, cannot be charmed or frightened, and lacks the animation action. The boulders remain animated while the galeb duhr concentrates, for up to 1 minute.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Galeb Duhr — Animate Boulders (p. 140) (dnd5e-mm-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: nearby boulders become temporary animated guardians; dial: two-object limit, daily use, concentration, and a one-minute maximum bound the effect.

rules.statement: A creature within 60 feet of a wish-granting genie can state a desired effect; the genie may fulfill it by casting wish on that creature’s behalf. A genie can grant one to three wishes to a non-genie, usually cannot grant wishes again for some time (typically a year), and can use its full allotment on the same creature only once in that creature’s existence; it may twist poorly worded requests to its own advantage.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Variant: Genie Powers—Wishes, p. 144 (dnd5e-mm-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: the described wish limits apply; dial: the genie can interpret vague wording adversely; in-world cost: the requester risks an outcome shaped by the genie’s interests.

rules.statement: A djinni can create a whirlwind at a visible point within 120 feet: it is a 5-foot-radius, 30-foot-tall cylinder, and creatures other than the djinni entering it must succeed on a DC 18 Strength save or be restrained. The djinni can move it up to 60 feet as an action while concentrating; it ends if the djinni loses sight of it, and a restrained creature can use an action and succeed on a DC 18 Strength check to escape to the nearest space outside.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Djinni—Create Whirlwind, p. 144 (dnd5e-mm-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: use the stated area, checks, movement, and concentration; dial: the field ends when sight is lost; in-world cost: maintaining control occupies the djinni’s concentration.

rules.statement: A ghost can enter the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or return from the Ethereal Plane to the Material Plane. While on one plane it is visible on the other, but cannot affect or be affected by anything there.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ghost—Etherealness, p. 148 (dnd5e-mm-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: the ghost changes between these two planes; dial: interaction across the boundary is blocked; in-world cost: it cannot affect or be affected by creatures and objects on the other plane.

rules.statement: A ghost can move through creatures and objects as though they were difficult terrain. If it ends its turn inside an object, it takes 5 (1d10) force damage.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ghost—Incorporeal Movement, p. 148 (dnd5e-mm-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: passage through solid barriers is allowed; dial: ending a turn inside an object causes damage; in-world cost: remaining embedded is dangerous.

rules.statement: Each non-undead creature within 60 feet of a ghost that can see it must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom save or become frightened for 1 minute; on a failure by 5 or more, it also ages 1d4 × 10 years. A frightened target can repeat the save at the end of each turn to end the condition; a target that succeeds or ends the effect is immune to that ghost’s visage for 24 hours, and the aging can be reversed by a spell only within 24 hours.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ghost—Horrifying Visage, p. 148 (dnd5e-mm-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: apply the save, duration, repeat saves, and immunity as stated; dial: aging requires a failure by 5 or more and has a 24-hour reversal window; in-world cost: exposure can leave lasting bodily age.

rules.statement: A ghost can attempt to possess a humanoid it can see within 5 feet; the target must succeed on a DC 13 Charisma save or the ghost takes control of its body. The possession ends if the body reaches 0 hit points, the ghost ends it as a bonus action, or an effect such as dispel evil and good forces it out; the ghost then reappears within 5 feet, and the target is immune to that ghost’s possession for 24 hours after succeeding on the save or after the possession ends.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ghost—Possession, p. 148 (dnd5e-mm-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: the saving throw, exit conditions, and immunity period govern possession; dial: the possessed creature retains awareness but loses control; in-world cost: control is limited to the borrowed body and its statistics, without the target’s knowledge or class features.

rules.statement: A ghoul’s claws can paralyze a non-elf, non-undead target for up to 1 minute if it fails a DC 10 Constitution save; the target repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the effect on a success. A ghast’s claws use the same rule against any non-undead creature, without the ghoul’s elf exception.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ghoul and Ghast—Claws, pp. 149–150 (dnd5e-mm-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: apply the creature-specific target restriction, DC, duration, and repeat saves; dial: success on a later save ends the paralysis early; in-world cost: the effect cannot paralyze undead, and ordinary ghouls also cannot affect elves this way.

rules.statement: A creature that starts its turn within 5 feet of a ghast must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution save or be poisoned until the start of its next turn. On a success, it is immune to that ghast’s stench for 24 hours.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ghast—Stench, p. 149 (dnd5e-mm-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: check creatures in range at the start of their turns; dial: a successful save grants 24-hour immunity; in-world cost: the effect is brief unless the creature keeps failing.

rules.statement: Giants use a caste order that assigns each giant a relative social rank, with rank determined by different qualities for each race; the listed order among giant kinds places storm above cloud, stone, hill, and frost, with giant kin below them. A giant of a higher-ranked kind outranks any giant of a lower-ranked kind, regardless of their individual positions within their own kinds.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: The Ordning, p. 150 (dnd5e-mm-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: use the stated cross-kind hierarchy; dial: individual standing within a kind depends on that kind’s chosen qualities; in-world cost: defying a superior is socially rude, though not inherently evil.

rules.statement: A githyanki knight’s silver greatsword deals slashing and psychic damage; on a critical hit against a creature whose body is astrally projected, the knight can cut the silver tether to its physical body instead of dealing damage.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Githyanki Knight (dnd5e-mm-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the severing option is limited to a critical hit against an astral body; dial: allow similar tether-cutting attacks only when those conditions hold, because the connection to the physical body is exposed.

rules.statement: A githzerai zerth can innately cast plane shift once per day, using Wisdom as its spellcasting ability and requiring no components.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Githzerai Zerth — Innate Spellcasting (Psionics) (dnd5e-mm-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one use daily; dial: keep the travel capability scarce, since it comes from disciplined mental power.

rules.statement: Githzerai use mental power to settle Limbo’s chaotic forces into stable, survivable forms and create sanctuaries within the plane.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Githzerai — Order amid Chaos (dnd5e-mm-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: this stabilizing effect is associated with githzerai minds and their strongholds; dial: require focused thought or a prepared sanctuary, because Limbo’s chaos otherwise remains unstable.

rules.statement: A githzerai zerth can shift its body between planes through mental power; its stat block grants plane shift once per day.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Githzerai — Disciples of Zerthimon; Githzerai Zerth (dnd5e-mm-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the specific stat block limits the shift to once daily; dial: preserve that limit, because this is an advanced discipline rather than routine movement.

rules.statement: A storm giant’s innate spellcasting uses Charisma, requires no material components, and permits detect magic, feather fall, levitate, and light at will; control weather and water breathing are each available three times per day.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Storm Giant — Innate Spellcasting (dnd5e-mm-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: at-will and daily casting limits are explicit; dial: retain the listed frequencies, since the giant’s innate magic is bounded by them.

rules.statement: A gibbering mouther’s babbling affects creatures that start their turn within 20 feet and can hear it: on a failed DC 10 Wisdom save, a creature loses reactions until its next turn and rolls a d8 to determine its turn’s behavior.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Gibbering Mouther — Gibbering (dnd5e-mm-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: requires hearing, proximity, and a failed save; dial: keep those gates, because the disruption is caused by audible gibbering.

rules.statement: On that failed save, a d8 result of 1–4 makes the creature do nothing; 5–6 denies its action and bonus action and sends it moving randomly; 7 has no stated outcome; and 8 makes it attack a randomly chosen creature in reach if possible, otherwise do nothing.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Gibbering Mouther — Gibbering (dnd5e-mm-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve the stated d8 results as given; dial: the passage leaves result 7 unspecified, so treat it as no additional effect unless a setting rule supplies one.

rules.statement: A gibbering mouther’s ground effect makes the area within 10 feet difficult terrain; a creature starting its turn there must pass a DC 10 Strength save or have its speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Gibbering Mouther — Aberrant Ground (dnd5e-mm-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a 10-foot radius and a saving throw gate the movement restriction; dial: retain the short duration, because the creature’s presence temporarily deforms nearby ground.

rules.statement: A goblin can take the Hide or Disengage action as a bonus action on each of its turns.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Goblin — Nimble Escape (dnd5e-mm-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited to these two actions and once as a bonus action per turn; dial: preserve the action-economy limit, reflecting the goblin’s quick escape tactics.

rules.statement: When a golem’s creator or the possessor of its control item gives it an order, the golem follows it; without a new instruction it continues its last order as best it can, and it cannot be reasoned with or tricked by words.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Golems — Blind Obedience (dnd5e-mm-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: command authority belongs to the creator or control-item possessor, and the golem follows its last order if instructions lapse; dial: keep its inability to act independently, since its animating spirit is bound to obedience.

rules.statement: A golem’s creator binds an elemental spirit from the Plane of Earth into its artificial body, making it obey the creator’s will; the spirit has no memory, personality, or history.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Golems — Elemental Spirit in Material Form (dnd5e-mm-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the spirit is bound into a constructed body and made obedient; dial: limit the model to a simple animating force, because the spirit has no independent identity described.

rules.statement: A clay golem subjected to acid takes no damage and instead regains hit points equal to the acid damage it would have taken.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Clay Golem — Acid Absorption (dnd5e-mm-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the incoming acid damage as healing; dial: none; the golem’s material turns a harmful energy into repair.

rules.statement: When a clay golem starts its turn at 60 hit points or fewer, roll a d6; on a 6 it becomes berserk and attacks the nearest creature it can see on each turn. If it cannot reach and attack a nearby creature, it attacks an object, preferring one smaller than itself; this continues until it is destroyed or restored to all its hit points.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Clay Golem — Berserk (dnd5e-mm-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: check once at the start of each qualifying turn; dial: none; severe damage risks loss of control until destruction or full repair.

rules.statement: A clay golem cannot have its form changed by spells or other effects, has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magic, and its weapon attacks count as magical.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Clay Golem — Immutable Form, Magic Resistance, Magic Weapons (dnd5e-mm-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: block form alteration and grant advantage on saves against magic; dial: none; its constructed body resists external magic.

rules.statement: A clay golem’s slam deals 16 (2d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage; a creature hit must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution save or have its hit point maximum reduced by the damage taken. The reduction lasts until greater restoration or other magic removes it, and the creature dies if the reduction brings its maximum to 0.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Clay Golem — Slam (dnd5e-mm-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the damage and save-based maximum reduction; dial: none; the impact degrades the victim’s capacity to survive.

rules.statement: A clay golem can use Haste when the feature recharges on a 5–6; until the end of its next turn, it gains +2 AC, advantage on Dexterity saves, and may make a slam as a bonus action.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Clay Golem — Haste (dnd5e-mm-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: roll recharge as stated and apply the benefits for one turn; dial: none; the construct temporarily accelerates and hardens.

rules.statement: A flesh golem that takes lightning damage takes no damage and instead regains hit points equal to that damage; fire damage gives it disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Flesh Golem — Lightning Absorption; Aversion of Fire (dnd5e-mm-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: lightning repairs the golem and fire impairs its next turn; dial: none; its unusual body reacts differently to opposing energies.

rules.statement: A flesh golem starting its turn at 40 hit points or fewer rolls a d6; on a 6 it becomes berserk and attacks the nearest visible creature, or an object if no creature can be reached and attacked. Its creator within 60 feet can use an action to make a DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check while speaking firmly and being heard; success ends the berserk state, though damage while still at 40 hit points or fewer can trigger it again.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Flesh Golem — Berserk (dnd5e-mm-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: check at the start of qualifying turns and let the creator attempt to calm it; dial: none; damage can overwhelm control, while its maker’s voice can restore it temporarily.

rules.statement: A gorgon that moves at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and hits it with gore that turn forces a DC 16 Strength save or knocks it prone; if the target is prone, the gorgon may make a hoof attack against it as a bonus action.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Gorgon — Trampling Charge (dnd5e-mm-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require the movement, hit, and failed save in sequence; dial: none; momentum converts a charge into a knockdown and follow-up.

rules.statement: A creature caught in a gorgon’s 30-foot cone of petrifying breath makes a DC 13 Constitution save; on a failure it becomes restrained and must save again at the end of its next turn. A success ends the effect, while another failure petrifies it until greater restoration or other magic frees it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Gorgon — Petrifying Breath (dnd5e-mm-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve the initial save and the next-turn repeat; dial: none; failing both stages turns restraint into stone-like immobility.

rules.statement: A grell’s tentacle hit deals 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage and forces a DC 11 Constitution save; failure poisons the target for 1 minute, during which it is paralyzed, and it can repeat the save at the end of each turn to end the effect. The target is also grappled (escape DC 15), and if Medium or smaller is restrained until the grapple ends; the grell has advantage on attacks against it, cannot use the tentacle attack on another target while holding it, and carries it when moving.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Grell — Tentacles (dnd5e-mm-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the failed-save condition and grapple rules; dial: none; venom incapacitates prey while the tentacles hold and transport it.

rules.statement: While all three members of a hag coven are within 30 feet of one another, each can cast the listed wizard spells using spell slots shared among the three: four 1st-level, three 2nd-level, three 3rd-level, three 4th-level, two 5th-level, and one 6th-level slot. Each hag counts as a 12th-level spellcaster, uses Intelligence, and has a spell save DC of 12 + its Intelligence modifier and spell attack bonus of 4 + that modifier.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Hag Covens — Shared Spellcasting (dnd5e-mm-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit the specified spells only while the coven is within range and spend from its common slots; dial: none; members pool limited magical resources.

rules.statement: A hag coven can make one hag eye through a one-hour ritual requiring all three members; they must do nothing else during it, and cannot perform it while blinded. A coven member can use an action to see through the eye if it is on the same plane; it has AC 10, 1 hit point, and darkvision to 60 feet, and its destruction deals 3d10 psychic damage to each coven member and blinds them for 24 hours; the coven can have only one at a time.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Hag Covens — Hag Eye (dnd5e-mm-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow one shared eye and apply its construction and destruction costs; dial: none; remote sight depends on a fragile coven-made object and risks shared injury.

rules.statement: A night hag can enter or leave the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane only while possessing a heartstone; it can use this transition as an action feature, and the stone’s touch also cures any disease. Making a heartstone takes 30 days.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Night Hag — Etherealness; Night Hag Items (dnd5e-mm-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require possession of the heartstone for planar crossing; dial: none; travel relies on a costly, slowly crafted item.

rules.statement: A harpy can sing to affect humanoids and giants that hear it within 300 feet; each must make a DC 11 Wisdom save or become charmed. The harpy must spend a bonus action on later turns to keep singing, and can stop at any time; the song also ends if it is incapacitated.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Harpy — Luring Song (dnd5e-mm-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: song radius and save difficulty; the melody draws susceptible listeners into a dangerous bond.

rules.statement: While charmed by the song, a target disregards other harpies and, if more than 5 feet from the singer, can Dash toward it by the most direct route. It does not avoid opportunity attacks, but can save again before entering damaging terrain or after taking damage from another source, and at the end of each turn; a successful save ends the effect, and a successful initial save grants immunity to that harpy’s song for 24 hours.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Harpy — Luring Song (dnd5e-mm-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: repeat-save timing and 24-hour immunity; the compulsion is forceful but offers several chances to resist.

rules.statement: A hellhound’s fire breath recharges on a roll of 5 or 6; it exhales fire in a 15-foot cone, forcing each creature there to make a DC 12 Dexterity save, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Hellhound — Fire Breath (dnd5e-mm-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: recharge threshold and cone size; the hound’s fiery attack is powerful but not always available.

rules.statement: A helmed horror has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects, and its creator chooses three spells to which it is immune; typical choices include fireball, heat metal, and lightning bolt.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Helmed Horror — Traits (dnd5e-mm-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: exactly three chosen spells; its maker tailors the construct’s defenses to anticipated threats.

rules.statement: A hobgoblin can once per turn deal extra damage with a weapon hit when the target is within 5 feet of an active ally: 7 (2d6) for a basic hobgoblin, 10 (3d6) for a captain, or 14 (4d6) for a warlord.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Hobgoblin, Hobgoblin Captain, and Hobgoblin Warlord — Martial Advantage (dnd5e-mm-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: once per turn and ally proximity; coordinated fighting rewards keeping an ally close to the target.

rules.statement: A hobgoblin captain or warlord can use a special command or warning to let a visible, nonhostile creature within 30 feet that can hear and understand it add 1d4 to an attack roll or saving throw for 1 minute. Only one such Leadership die can benefit a creature at once; the effect ends if the leader is incapacitated, and the ability recharges after a short or long rest.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Hobgoblin Captain and Hobgoblin Warlord — Leadership (dnd5e-mm-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: one-minute duration and rest-based recharge; audible leadership temporarily improves allies’ performance.

rules.statement: A homunculus shares its creator’s knowledge, languages, and senses; on the same plane, it can transmit what it senses and communicate telepathically with its master. A creator can have only one, creation attempts for another fail, and the homunculus dies when its master dies.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Homunculus — Shared Mind and Telepathic Bond (dnd5e-mm-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: one companion and same-plane link; the bond grants remote awareness but is limited and tied to the creator’s life.

rules.statement: A hydra with more than one head has advantage on saves against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, or knocked unconscious. When it takes at least 25 damage in one turn, one head dies; at the end of its turn it regrows two heads for each lost since its previous turn, unless it took fire damage, and regains 10 hit points per head regrown; it dies if all its heads die.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Hydra — Multiple Heads (dnd5e-mm-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: damage threshold, head growth, and fire interruption; severing heads triggers regenerative growth unless fire suppresses it.

rules.statement: An intellect devourer can sense the presence and location of creatures with Intelligence 3 or higher within 300 feet despite intervening barriers, unless they are protected by mind blank. Its mind attack targets a visible creature with a brain within 10 feet: a failed DC 12 Intelligence save causes 11 (2d10) psychic damage, and a 3d6 roll that meets or exceeds the target’s Intelligence reduces that score to 0, stunning it until it regains at least one Intelligence point.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Intellect Devourer — Detect Sentience and Devour Intellect (dnd5e-mm-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: detection range, save DC, and Intelligence threshold; the predator locates minds and can incapacitate them by consuming their capacity to think.

rules.statement: An intellect devourer can contest Intelligence against an incapacitated humanoid within 5 feet; if it wins, it consumes the brain, enters the skull, and controls the body. It retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, traits, telepathy, and Deep Speech, otherwise taking the host’s statistics and knowledge; protection from evil and good forces it out, as does restoration of the brain by wish, while voluntary exit costs 5 feet of movement and leaves the host dead unless its brain is restored within 1 round.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Intellect Devourer — Body Thief (dnd5e-mm-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: contest, exit methods, and one-round restoration window; taking control requires an incapacitated host and risks the host’s death.

rules.statement: An invisible stalker knows the direction and distance to its assigned quarry and its summoner’s location while they share a plane. It is bound to hunt a creature or retrieve an object until the task is complete; a task that does neither ends the binding and releases it, and it vanishes after finishing if its summoner has died.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Invisible Stalker — Faultless Tracker and Directed Hunter (dnd5e-mm-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
