rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: same-plane tracking and task limits; the summoner receives a persistent hunter, but its mandate constrains what it can be ordered to do.

rules.statement: A jackalwere can use an action to change among a specific Medium human shape, a human-jackal hybrid, and its Small jackal form; its statistics otherwise stay the same, equipment is unchanged, and death restores its true form. Its gaze forces one visible creature within 30 feet to make a DC 10 Wisdom save or fall unconscious for 10 minutes, ending early if someone uses an action to shake it awake; a successful save grants immunity to that jackalwere’s gaze for 24 hours, and undead or creatures immune to being charmed are unaffected.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Jackalwere — Shapechanger and Sleep Gaze (dnd5e-mm-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: action cost, fixed forms, save, duration, and immunity; disguise and incapacitation are useful but have clear limits.

rules.statement: A kraken’s lair can push creatures within 60 feet up to 60 feet away (DC 23 Strength save, or 10 feet on a success), make creatures in the water within that range vulnerable to lightning until the next round, or electrically charge the water so creatures within 120 feet make a DC 23 Constitution save, taking 10 (3d6) lightning damage on a failure or half on a success. On initiative count 20, the kraken chooses a lair effect and loses ties.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Kraken — Lair Actions (dnd5e-mm-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: initiative timing, ranges, and save DCs; the lair imposes local hazards around its powerful occupant.

rules.statement: If a humanoid is wounded by a lycanthrope, it must make a Constitution save with DC 8 plus the lycanthrope’s proficiency bonus and Constitution modifier or gain the curse. A humanoid may also inherit it from one or both lycanthrope parents.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Curse of Lycanthropy, p. 207–208 (dnd5e-mm-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: whether the curse is inherited or inflicted; in-world reason: bloodline or an attacking creature carries the curse.

rules.statement: A remove curse spell frees an afflicted lycanthrope, but a natural-born lycanthrope requires wish to be freed. A cursed character who embraces the curse takes the alignment associated with that lycanthrope; the DM may take control if that alignment change warrants it, until the curse is removed.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Curse of Lycanthropy; Player Characters as Lycanthropes, pp. 207–208 (dnd5e-mm-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: whether the curse is acquired or innate; in-world reason: inherited lycanthropy is harder to undo.

rules.statement: A lycanthrope resisting the curse keeps its usual alignment and personality in humanoid form, but the full moon forces a change into beast or hybrid form; when the moon wanes, it can control the beast again. A resistant lycanthrope may not remember what happened while transformed.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Curse of Lycanthropy, p. 207 (dnd5e-mm-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: whether the subject resists or embraces the curse; in-world reason: the full moon overwhelms resistance.

rules.statement: A lycanthrope that embraces the curse can learn to assume beast or hybrid form at will. The passage warns that many who embrace it succumb to bloodlust and become evil predators.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Curse of Lycanthropy, p. 207 (dnd5e-mm-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: voluntary transformation after mastery; in-world reason: accepting the curse grants control but risks violent urges.

rules.statement: A character who becomes a lycanthrope keeps its statistics except for the changes specified for its type, and gains that type’s speeds in nonhumanoid form, damage immunities, traits, and non-equipment actions. The character gains proficiency with the lycanthrope’s natural attacks and cannot speak in animal form.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Player Characters as Lycanthropes, p. 208 (dnd5e-mm-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: changes depend on the lycanthrope type and form; in-world reason: the curse grants animal capabilities and limits speech.

rules.statement: A lycanthrope’s natural attacks use the damage shown in its statistics; for the specific types listed, the character’s Strength or Dexterity may rise to a stated minimum, and certain forms grant a +1 AC bonus. Attack damage and some trait save DCs use the specified ability modifier.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Player Characters as Lycanthropes, p. 208 (dnd5e-mm-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: exact ability and defense changes vary by lycanthrope; in-world reason: the curse reshapes physical capability.

rules.statement: The lich’s ritual binds a wizard’s soul into a phylactery, keeping it in the mortal world and preventing travel to the Outer Planes. The transformation requires a potion made with poison and a sentient creature’s blood, whose soul is sacrificed to the phylactery.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Secrets of Undeath, p. 204 (dnd5e-mm-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the ritual consumes a sentient soul; in-world reason: the lich’s continued existence depends on this costly binding.

rules.statement: A lich must periodically feed souls to its phylactery using imprisonment, trapping a target’s body and soul inside it; the phylactery must be on the lich’s plane and can contain only one creature. A 9th-level dispel magic cast on it releases the prisoner, but after 24 hours the victim is consumed and only divine intervention can restore it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Soul Sacrifices, p. 204 (dnd5e-mm-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: one captive at a time and a 24-hour deadline; in-world reason: the lich sustains itself by consuming the trapped soul.

rules.statement: If a lich with a phylactery is destroyed, it regains a body in 1d10 days, with full hit points, appearing within 5 feet of the phylactery. Destroying the phylactery removes this route to restoration.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Rejuvenation; Death and Restoration, pp. 203–204 (dnd5e-mm-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: restoration takes 1d10 days and depends on an intact phylactery; in-world reason: the phylactery anchors the lich’s continued existence.

rules.statement: A lich’s phylactery can hold only one imprisoned creature; if the lich fails or neglects to sustain its body with sacrificed souls, it begins to fall apart and may eventually become a demilich.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Soul Sacrifices, p. 204 (dnd5e-mm-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: upkeep requires periodic souls and storage is limited to one; in-world reason: the lich’s body depends on the phylactery’s soul-fueled magic.

rules.statement: Kuo-toa can sense invisible creatures and creatures on the Ethereal Plane within 30 feet, and can pinpoint such a creature if it is moving. They can breathe both air and water.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Kuo-Toa, p. 200 (dnd5e-mm-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: sensing is limited to 30 feet and pinpoints only moving targets; in-world reason: this is an unusual perceptive trait.

rules.statement: If enough kuo-toa believe in a god they have invented, their collective subconscious energy can cause it to manifest physically; the god’s form reflects its inspiration and may be random or nonsensical.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: God Makers, p. 199 (dnd5e-mm-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: manifestation depends on enough shared belief; in-world reason: collective belief supplies the force that makes the god real.

rules.statement: A werewolf can use an action to change between its humanoid, wolf, and hybrid forms; its statistics stay the same except for its Armor Class, carried or worn gear does not change, and death restores its humanoid form.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 212, Shapechanger (dnd5e-mm-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation is deliberate and costs an action; dial: forms are limited to three, and death forces the true form.

rules.statement: A humanoid hit by a werewolf’s bite must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution save or be cursed with werewolf lycanthropy.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 212, Bite (dnd5e-mm-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the curse requires a failed save after a bite; dial: it affects humanoids only, with a DC 12 threshold.

rules.statement: A magmin that dies bursts with fire and magma: creatures within 10 feet make a DC 11 Dexterity save, taking 7 (2d6) fire damage on a failure or half on a success, and unattended flammable objects in the area ignite.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 213, Death Burst (dnd5e-mm-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the burst occurs on death; dial: the 10-foot area and save limit damage, while nearby unattended flammables can catch fire.

rules.statement: A magmin can use a bonus action to ignite itself or put out its flames; while ignited, it sheds bright light for 10 feet and dim light for another 10 feet.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 213, Ignited Illumination (dnd5e-mm-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ignition is controllable with a bonus action; dial: illumination is limited to the stated radii.

rules.statement: When a medusa that is able to act sees a creature within 30 feet at the start of that creature’s turn, it can force a DC 14 Constitution save. Failing by 5 or more petrifies the creature immediately; another failure restrains it and starts a turn-by-turn save, with petrification on failure and the effect ending on success; completed petrification lasts until greater restoration or other magic frees the target.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 215, Petrifying Gaze (dnd5e-mm-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: gaze requires visibility, range, and a failed save; dial: severe failure causes immediate petrification, while lesser failure allows repeated saves.

rules.statement: A creature that is not surprised can avert its eyes to avoid the medusa’s gaze save at the start of its turn, but cannot see the medusa until its next turn; looking at it then requires an immediate save. In bright light, the medusa also suffers its own gaze if it sees its reflection on a polished surface within 30 feet.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 215, Petrifying Gaze (dnd5e-mm-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: averting the eyes avoids the initial save; dial: the creature gives up sight of the medusa, and reflection creates a risk for the medusa itself.

rules.statement: A dust mephit that dies blinds creatures within 5 feet that fail a DC 10 Constitution save for 1 minute; each blinded creature can repeat the save on its turns, ending the effect on a success.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 216, Dust Mephit, Death Burst (dnd5e-mm-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death triggers the dust burst; dial: it affects only nearby creatures that fail the save, and repeated saves can end blindness.

rules.statement: A dust mephit can innately cast sleep once per day without material components, using Charisma for its innate spellcasting.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 216, Dust Mephit, Innate Spellcasting (dnd5e-mm-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: this is an innate spell, not a learned one; dial: it is limited to once per day and requires no material components.

rules.statement: A summoned mephit appears in an unoccupied space within 60 feet, acts as an ally, and remains for 1 minute, until it or its summoner dies, or until dismissed by the summoner as an action. It has a 25 percent chance to summon 1d4 of its own kind once per day, and summoned mephits cannot summon more.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 218, Variant: Mephit Summoning (dnd5e-mm-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: summoning has a daily limit and a chance of failure; dial: allies are temporary, proximity-limited, and cannot extend the chain by summoning.

rules.statement: A merfolk can breathe both air and water.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 219, Merfolk, Amphibious (dnd5e-mm-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the trait permits breathing in either environment; dial: it provides no other movement or survival benefits.

rules.statement: A mind flayer can innately cast detect thoughts and levitate at will, and dominate monster and self-only plane shift once each per day; it uses Intelligence, save DC 15, and requires no components.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 223, Mind Flayer, Innate Spellcasting (dnd5e-mm-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these are innate spells; dial: plane shift is self-only and limited to once daily, while the other daily spell is also capped.

rules.statement: A mind flayer’s tentacle hit deals 15 (2d10 + 4) psychic damage; against a Medium or smaller target it also grapples the target (escape DC 15), which must pass a DC 15 Intelligence save or be stunned until that grapple ends.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 223, Mind Flayer, Tentacles (dnd5e-mm-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the grapple follows a tentacle hit against a size-limited target; dial: stunning requires a failed save and lasts only while the grapple holds.

rules.statement: A mummy lord whose heart remains intact turns to dust when reduced to 0 hit points, then reforms at full strength after 24 hours within 5 feet of the heart. Burning the heart to ashes prevents this return; the heart has AC 5, 25 hit points, and is immune to damage other than fire.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Mummy Lord — Heart of the Mummy Lord; p. 229 (dnd5e-mm-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: return is automatic after 24 hours; dial: the heart is a vulnerable, locatable anchor that can be destroyed by fire.

rules.statement: A creature cursed by a mummy’s rotting fist cannot regain hit points, and its hit point maximum falls by 10 (3d6) every 24 hours. If that maximum reaches 0, it dies and becomes dust; the curse ends when remove curse or other magic removes it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Mummy — Rotting Fist; p. 229 (dnd5e-mm-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the curse worsens every 24 hours; dial: it can be removed by specified magic before the victim dies.

rules.statement: In a mummy lord’s lair, until initiative count 20 on the next round, a non-undead creature trying to cast a spell of 4th level or lower must make a DC 16 Constitution save. On a failure it takes 1d6 necrotic damage per spell level and the spell fails and is wasted; the caster may instead choose another action.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Mummy Lord’s Lair — Lair Actions; p. 230 (dnd5e-mm-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lair suppresses eligible spellcasting on a failed save; dial: the caster can avoid the risk by choosing another action.

rules.statement: Within the mummy lord’s lair, food becomes moldy, water evaporates, and other nonmagical drinks spoil. Divination spells cast there by others have a 25% chance to mislead; where repeated casting already risks unreliable results, increase that chance by 25 percentage points. These effects end immediately if the mummy lord is destroyed.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Regional Effects; p. 230 (dnd5e-mm-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lair’s presence warps supplies and divination; dial: destroying the mummy lord immediately ends the effects.

rules.statement: A creature that takes treasure from a mummy lord’s lair is cursed and has disadvantage on all saving throws until the treasure is returned or remove curse or other magic removes the curse. The effect ends immediately if the mummy lord is destroyed.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Regional Effects; p. 230 (dnd5e-mm-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: removing the treasure or using suitable magic ends the curse; dial: destroying the lair’s mummy lord also ends it immediately.

rules.statement: Myconid rapport spores affect eligible creatures in their stated radius, including around corners; affected creatures can communicate telepathically with one another while within 30 feet of one another, for 1 hour. The spores do not affect creatures with Intelligence below 2, undead, constructs, or elementals.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Myconids — Circles and Melds; sample myconid traits, pp. 231, 233 (dnd5e-mm-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: communication lasts 1 hour; dial: each participant must be within the spore radius to be affected and within 30 feet of another participant to communicate.

rules.statement: A myconid sovereign can use animating spores three times per day on a humanoid or Large-or-smaller beast corpse within 5 feet. After 24 hours it rises as a spore servant, which lasts 1d4 + 1 weeks or until destroyed; that corpse cannot be animated this way again.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Myconid Sovereign — Animating Spores; Spore Servant Template, pp. 231, 233 (dnd5e-mm-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the corpse becomes a temporary servant after a 24-hour delay; dial: use is limited to three times per day and each corpse only once.

rules.statement: A spore servant becomes a plant and loses its languages, most special traits and actions, and its original saving throw and skill bonuses; its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma become 2, 6, and 1. It follows myconid orders received through rapport spores, prioritizing the most powerful myconid’s orders.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Spore Servant Template; p. 231 (dnd5e-mm-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: conversion changes the creature’s capabilities and makes it responsive to myconids; dial: it retains specified physical traits and prioritizes the strongest myconid’s orders.

rules.statement: A dead spirit naga or guardian naga returns to life in 1d6 days with all hit points. Only a wish spell prevents this trait from working.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Spirit Naga and Guardian Naga — Rejuvenation; pp. 234–235 (dnd5e-mm-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: return follows death after 1d6 days; dial: a wish spell can prevent it.

rules.statement: A nightmare and up to three willing creatures within 5 feet can magically travel together between the Material Plane and Ethereal Plane. A summoned nightmare shows no special loyalty unless offered a worthy sacrifice as food when it arrives.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Nightmare — Ethereal Stride; Dread Steed; p. 236 (dnd5e-mm-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the nightmare carries willing nearby companions between the two planes; dial: a summoned steed’s loyalty depends on a worthy arrival sacrifice.

rules.statement: A nothic can target a creature it sees within 30 feet and contest its Wisdom (Insight) against the target’s Charisma (Deception). If the nothic wins, it magically learns one fact or secret about the target; a target immune to being charmed automatically wins.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Nothic — Weird Insight; p. 237 (dnd5e-mm-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: success reveals one fact; dial: a contest limits the outcome, and charm immunity prevents the nothic from learning it.

rules.statement: An oni can magically change between its true Large giant form and a Small or Medium humanoid form without changing its statistics. Its glaive changes size with it, but other equipment does not; on its death it returns to its true form and the glaive returns to normal size.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Oni — Change Shape; p. 239 (dnd5e-mm-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: shape and size change while statistics remain constant; dial: only the glaive transforms with the oni, and death ends the disguise.

rules.statement: An ooze that has not moved or attacked can be mistaken for its surroundings; a creature unaware of it that enters its space is surprised.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Gray Ooze / False Appearance, p. 244 (dnd5e-mm-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated stillness and disguise limits; dial: none; the ooze loses the disguise once it moves or attacks.

rules.statement: A gray ooze that hits a nonmagical metal weapon causes it to take a cumulative −1 penalty to damage rolls after the hit; at −5 the weapon is destroyed. Its pseudopod also gives nonmagical metal armor it hits a cumulative −1 AC penalty, destroying it when the penalty brings its AC to 10; it can eat through 2-inch-thick nonmagical metal in 1 round.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Gray Ooze / Corrode Metal and Pseudopod, p. 244 (dnd5e-mm-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: corrosion accumulates only through the described contact; dial: none; metal equipment bears the lasting cost.

rules.statement: A Medium-or-larger jelly with at least 10 hit points splits into two smaller jellies when lightning or slashing damage affects it; each has half its former hit points, rounded down.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Ochre Jelly / Split, p. 244 (dnd5e-mm-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: trigger only on the specified damage types and minimum hit points; dial: none; the original body divides into weaker bodies.

rules.statement: A pseudodragon can accept a willing creature as its familiar, forming a magical telepathic bond. While bonded, the companion can sense what the pseudodragon senses within 1 mile, gains its Magic Resistance while within 10 feet, and the pseudodragon may end the service and bond at any time.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Variant: Pseudodragon Familiar, p. 255 (dnd5e-mm-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the bond’s stated range and close-distance benefit; dial: none; the pseudodragon retains the right to leave at any time.

rules.statement: A purple worm burrows through solid rock at half its burrow speed, leaving a tunnel 10 feet in diameter.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Purple Worm / Tunneler, p. 256 (dnd5e-mm-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: tunnel creation is limited to solid-rock burrowing at half speed; dial: none; progress is slower than ordinary burrowing.

rules.statement: A creature swallowed by a purple worm is blinded and restrained, has total cover from outside effects, and takes 21 (6d6) acid damage at the start of each worm turn. If it deals the worm at least 30 damage in one turn, the worm must pass a DC 21 Constitution save at that turn’s end or regurgitate all swallowed creatures prone within 10 feet; if the worm dies, a swallowed creature can spend 20 feet of movement to escape prone.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Purple Worm / Bite, p. 256 (dnd5e-mm-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the stated ongoing damage and escape triggers; dial: none; escape depends on harming the worm, its death, or its forced regurgitation.

rules.statement: An otyugh’s bite can infect a creature: on a failed DC 15 Constitution save it is poisoned until cured, and every 24 hours its maximum hit points fall by 5 (1d10) on a failed repeat save. A successful repeat save cures the disease; it also ends if the hit-point maximum is reduced to 0.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Otyugh / Bite, p. 249 (dnd5e-mm-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the disease’s repeated daily save and stated cure conditions; dial: none; failed saves steadily reduce the victim’s maximum hit points.

rules.statement: An otyugh’s tentacle hit grapples a Medium-or-smaller target (escape DC 13) and restrains it until the grapple ends; each of its two tentacles can hold one target. Its slam forces grappled creatures to make a DC 14 Strength save, taking 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage and becoming stunned until the end of its next turn on a failure, or taking half damage without being stunned on a success.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Otyugh / Tentacle and Tentacle Slam, p. 249 (dnd5e-mm-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grapple capacity and condition durations follow the listed limits; dial: none; escape requires ending the grapple.

rules.statement: A war chief’s once-per-day battle cry grants its chosen creatures within 30 feet that can hear it advantage on attack rolls until the start of its next turn, provided they are not already affected; the chief then makes one attack as a bonus action.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Orc War Chief / Battle Cry, p. 247 (dnd5e-mm-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the range, hearing, duration, and once-daily limit; dial: none; the advantage ends at the chief’s next turn.

rules.statement: A rakshasa ignores spells of 6th level or lower unless it chooses to be affected, and has advantage on saving throws against other spells and magical effects.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Rakshasa / Limited Magic Immunity, p. 258 (dnd5e-mm-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: block only the specified spell levels and allow voluntary effects; dial: none; higher-level magic can still affect it under ordinary rules.

rules.statement: A rakshasa’s claw hit curses a creature; whenever the target finishes a short or long rest, horrible images and dreams prevent it gaining that rest’s benefits. The curse lasts until removed by remove curse or similar magic.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Rakshasa / Claw, p. 258 (dnd5e-mm-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the rest penalty until the stated removal; dial: none; the target receives no rest benefits while the curse persists.

rules.statement: When a rakshasa is killed on the Material Plane, its essence returns to the Nine Hells and remains trapped there until its body reforms, a process taking months or years; it returns with its memories and seeks revenge. If killed in the Nine Hells, it is permanently destroyed.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Rakshasa / Evil Reborn, p. 258 (dnd5e-mm-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the plane of death to determine return or permanent destruction; dial: none; Material Plane death costs months or years before bodily return.

rules.statement: A revenant always knows the direction and distance to a creature it is pursuing for vengeance, even across planes; magic cannot hide that creature from it. If it is pursuing several foes, it tracks them one at a time, beginning with the one that killed it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Revenant — Divine Justice; Vengeful Tracker (dnd5e-mm-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the revenant’s supernatural pursuit sense is always active; dial: restrict the number of simultaneous targets; in-world reason: its vengeance focuses on one foe at a time.

rules.statement: When its body is destroyed, a revenant’s soul waits 24 hours, then inhabits and animates another corpse on the same plane with all its hit points restored. A wish can prevent this return while the soul is bodiless.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Revenant — Rejuvenation (dnd5e-mm-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: return is automatic after 24 hours; dial: a wish can end the cycle; in-world cost: the revenant’s soul remains vulnerable during the interval.

rules.statement: A shadow hit by its Strength Drain attack reduces the target’s Strength by 1d4; the loss ends when the target finishes a short or long rest, but the target dies if its Strength reaches 0. A non-evil humanoid killed this way produces a new shadow 1d4 hours later.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Shadow — Strength Drain (dnd5e-mm-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the rolled reduction and death threshold; dial: only non-evil humanoid deaths spawn another shadow; in-world reason: the effect propagates through a particular kind of victim.

rules.statement: A roper can maintain up to six tendrils. A creature hit by one is grappled, restrained, and hindered on Strength checks and saves while the grapple lasts; the roper can pull each creature it has grappled up to 25 feet straight toward itself.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Roper — Grasping Tendrils; Tendril; Reel (dnd5e-mm-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: tendrils bind up to six targets; dial: each tendril can hold only one target and the pull is capped at 25 feet; in-world cost: freeing a victim requires escape or breaking the tendril.

rules.statement: A rust monster can sense the location of ferrous metal within 30 feet by scent. Its antennae can corrode a visible nonmagical ferrous object within 5 feet; carried or worn gear allows a DC 11 Dexterity save to avoid the effect, and repeated damage to armor, shields, or weapons can eventually destroy them.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Rust Monster — Iron Scent; Rust Metal; Antennae (dnd5e-mm-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: detection and corrosion follow the stated range and save; dial: limit targets to nonmagical ferrous objects; in-world cost: metal equipment can suffer cumulative, permanent damage.

rules.statement: A sahuagin can breathe air and water, but must be submerged at least once every 4 hours or it begins to suffocate. It can also magically command any shark within 120 feet through limited telepathy.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Sahuagin — Limited Amphibiousness; Shark Telepathy (dnd5e-mm-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: both traits work within their stated limits; dial: command is restricted to sharks within 120 feet; in-world cost: prolonged time out of water risks suffocation.

rules.statement: A satyr with pipes can choose a magical effect affecting creatures within 60 feet that hear it; a failed DC 13 Wisdom save can charm, frighten, or put a creature to sleep for 1 minute. Targets can repeat the save at the end of each turn, and a creature that succeeds or ends the effect becomes immune to these pipes for 24 hours.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Satyr — Variant: Satyr Pipes (dnd5e-mm-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save applies the chosen effect; dial: hearing, creature immunities, repeat saves, and 24-hour resistance limit it; in-world reason: the music’s influence is temporary and does not readily affect the same listener again.

rules.statement: A scarecrow is animated by a bound spirit whose memories from life are gone and whose purpose centers on serving its creator. If the creator dies, the spirit may continue its last commands, seek revenge, or destroy itself.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Scarecrow — Spirit-Powered Constructs (dnd5e-mm-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bound spirit animates the construct and serves its creator; dial: its response to the creator’s death varies; in-world cost: the spirit’s memories and freedom are lost.

rules.statement: A shambling mound takes no lightning damage and instead regains hit points equal to the lightning damage dealt to it. If both slam attacks hit a Medium or smaller target, the mound grapples it and can engulf it; the mound can engulf only one creature at a time.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Shambling Mound — Lightning Absorption; Multiattack; Engulf (dnd5e-mm-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: lightning damage becomes healing; dial: engulfing requires both attacks to hit and is limited to one target; in-world reason: lightning reinvigorates the plant while its bulk limits what it can hold.

rules.statement: A shield guardian is magically linked to one amulet; while both are on the same plane, the wearer can call it telepathically and the guardian knows the amulet’s direction and distance. If it is within 60 feet, half the damage the wearer takes is transferred to the guardian; the wearer can also store one spell of 4th level or lower, replacing any spell already stored.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Shield Guardian — Bound; Spell Storing (dnd5e-mm-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the amulet defines the guardian’s bond and its single stored spell; dial: the bond works only on the same plane and damage transfer only within 60 feet; in-world cost: the guardian bears transferred harm and storing a new spell erases the old one.

rules.statement: A salamander’s heated body damages a creature that touches it or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet; the adult version deals 7 (2d6) fire damage. Its metal melee weapons also deal an extra 3 (1d6) fire damage on a hit.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Salamanders — Heated Body; Heated Weapons (dnd5e-mm-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: proximity and weapon hits add the listed fire damage; dial: the body effect applies only on touch or a nearby melee hit; in-world cost: approaching or striking the salamander exposes the attacker to heat.

rules.statement: A creature that emerges from the Spawning Stone has a gem implanted in its brain; whoever obtains the gem can command it, and destroying the gem ends this control. The creature is also immune to being charmed while controlled this way.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Slaadi — Variant: Slaad Control Gems, p. 275 (dnd5e-mm-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control requires possession of the implanted gem; dial: removal or destruction changes control; in-world reason: the gem is a magical fragment of the Spawning Stone.

rules.statement: A gem can be drawn out magically, transferred to a caster’s hand by a particular outcome of imprisonment, or acquired through a wish; greater restoration destroys it without harming the slaad. A proficient practitioner can also remove it from an incapacitated slaad with one uninterrupted minute of work and a successful DC 20 Wisdom (Medicine) check; each failure deals 22 (4d10) psychic damage.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Slaadi — Variant: Slaad Control Gems, p. 275 (dnd5e-mm-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: magical or skilled removal can free the slaad; dial: failed medical attempts cause substantial harm; in-world reason: extracting the brain-embedded gem is dangerous.

rules.statement: A slaad born without a control gem gains one if it comes into contact with the Spawning Stone; slaadi on Limbo are drawn to the stone, so most acquire one.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Slaadi — Variant: Slaad Control Gems, p. 275 (dnd5e-mm-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: contact with the stone supplies the control gem; dial: this applies only to gemless slaadi that reach it; in-world reason: the stone implants a fragment of itself.

rules.statement: An egg-bearing humanoid can carry only one slaad egg to term. Over three months it develops into a tadpole; in the final 24 hours the host’s speed is halved and it has disadvantage on attacks, ability checks, and saves, then the tadpole emerges in one round and kills the host. Curing the disease before emergence disintegrates the unborn slaad.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Slaad — Red Slaad, p. 277 (dnd5e-mm-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: infection progresses to a lethal birth; dial: treatment before emergence prevents the offspring; in-world reason: the egg develops inside the host.

rules.statement: A blue slaad’s claw can infect a humanoid that fails a DC 15 Constitution save with chaos phage. While infected, the victim cannot regain hit points and loses 10 (3d6) from its hit point maximum every 24 hours; reaching 0 maximum transforms it into a red slaad, or a green slaad if it can cast spells of 3rd level or higher, and only wish reverses the change.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Blue Slaad — Claw, p. 277 (dnd5e-mm-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: infection steadily weakens and ultimately changes the victim; dial: spellcasting capacity determines the resulting form, and wish is the sole reversal; in-world reason: the disease is slaad transformation.

rules.statement: A green slaad can spend an action to change into a Small or Medium humanoid or return to its true form; its statistics stay the same except for size, carried or worn gear does not change, and death restores its true form.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Green Slaad — Shapechanger, p. 278 (dnd5e-mm-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: either form is available through an action; dial: equipment is not transformed and death ends the disguise; in-world reason: the slaad alters its appearance without changing its other capabilities.

rules.statement: A gray slaad can cast plane shift on itself once per day; a death slaad can cast plane shift once per day, without material components.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Gray Slaad and Death Slaad — Innate Spellcasting, pp. 278–279 (dnd5e-mm-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: planar departure is available through innate magic; dial: use is limited to once daily and self-only for the gray slaad; in-world reason: planar travel is one of the slaad’s innate powers.

rules.statement: A specter can pass through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain, but takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Specter — Incorporeal Movement, p. 280 (dnd5e-mm-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: solid barriers do not prevent the specter’s movement; dial: ending a turn within an object causes force damage; in-world reason: its body is incorporeal but cannot safely remain embedded.

rules.statement: A specter’s hit drains 10 (3d6) necrotic damage; on a failed DC 10 Constitution save, the victim’s hit point maximum falls by the damage taken until it finishes a long rest, and it dies if the reduction reaches 0.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Specter — Life Drain, p. 280 (dnd5e-mm-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save causes lasting maximum-hit-point loss; dial: a long rest ends the reduction, while reaching zero is fatal; in-world reason: the attack drains vitality.

rules.statement: Within its lair, a sphinx can alter time so all creatures reroll initiative, age creatures that fail a DC 15 Constitution save by 1d20 years (never reducing them below one year old), or move everything in the lair up to 10 years forward or backward. Greater restoration restores age, while wish can return the caster and up to seven others to their normal time after the time shift.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Sphinx’s Lair — Lair Actions, p. 281 (dnd5e-mm-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lair permits initiative, age, and temporal displacement effects; dial: effects are limited to the lair and recovery from age or time displacement has specified spell requirements; in-world reason: the sphinx warps time in its guarded domain.

rules.statement: A sphinx can shift itself and up to seven creatures it can see in its lair to another plane. Outside the lair it cannot use lair actions, but it can return to the lair as a bonus action and bring up to seven creatures with it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: A Sphinx’s Lair — Lair Actions, p. 281 (dnd5e-mm-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the sphinx can transport a group between planes and its lair; dial: outward travel requires being in the lair, while return requires the sphinx’s bonus action; in-world reason: its extradimensional sanctuary is under its control.

rules.statement: A sprite touching a creature learns its current emotional state; if the creature fails a DC 10 Charisma save, the sprite also learns its alignment, and celestials, fiends, and undead automatically fail. A sprite’s shortbow hit deals 1 piercing damage and can poison the target for one minute on a failed DC 10 Constitution save; a save result of 5 or lower also knocks it unconscious for that duration or until damaged or shaken awake.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Sprite — Heart Sight and Shortbow, p. 284 (dnd5e-mm-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: touch reveals emotional state and may reveal alignment, while a weak hit may poison or incapacitate; dial: alignment and unconsciousness depend on the stated saving-throw outcomes; in-world reason: sprites perceive hearts and use sleep-inducing poison.

rules.statement: Three times per day, the tarrasque can turn a failed saving throw into a success. It also has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Tarrasque, traits (p. 288) (dnd5e-mm-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain three uses and the advantage; dial: reduce either defense if the creature is too difficult to affect.

rules.statement: When a magic missile spell, line spell, or spell requiring a ranged attack roll targets the tarrasque, roll a d6: on 1–5 the effect has no effect on it; on 6 it also has no effect on the tarrasque but is reflected at the caster as though originating from the tarrasque.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Tarrasque, Reflective Carapace (p. 288) (dnd5e-mm-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated spell categories and 1-in-6 reflection chance; dial: narrow the categories or lower the reflection chance to reduce risk to spellcasters.

rules.statement: Creatures the tarrasque chooses within 120 feet that can perceive it must make a DC 17 Wisdom save or become frightened for 1 minute. A frightened creature can retry at the end of each turn, with disadvantage while the tarrasque is in its line of sight; success ends the effect and grants immunity to this presence for 24 hours.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Tarrasque, Frightful Presence (p. 288) (dnd5e-mm-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the stated range, save, duration, and immunity; dial: shorten the duration or remove the line-of-sight penalty if fear is too disabling.

rules.statement: When the tarrasque swallows a creature it is grappling, the creature becomes blinded and restrained, has total cover from effects outside the tarrasque, and takes 56 acid damage at the start of each of the tarrasque’s turns. If it takes at least 60 damage from a creature inside it during one turn, it must pass a DC 20 Constitution save at that turn’s end or regurgitate all swallowed creatures; on the tarrasque’s death, a swallowed creature can escape the corpse using 30 feet of movement and exits prone.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Tarrasque, Swallow (p. 288) (dnd5e-mm-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated damage, escape trigger, and movement cost; dial: lower the internal-damage threshold or reduce ongoing damage to make containment less lethal.

rules.statement: A creature bitten by a thri-kreen must pass a DC 11 Constitution save or be poisoned for 1 minute; if it fails by 5 or more, it is also paralyzed while poisoned this way. It can retry the save on each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Thri-Kreen, Bite (p. 289) (dnd5e-mm-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the save margin and repeated saves as given; dial: remove paralysis or shorten the poisoned duration to reduce loss of control.

rules.statement: Once per day, a treant can animate one or two trees it can see within 60 feet; each acts as its ally for up to a day, but ends early if it dies, the treant dies, the treant moves more than 120 feet away, or the treant uses a bonus action to return it to tree form. Animated trees have Intelligence and Charisma 1, cannot speak, and can only slam; after ending, a tree takes root if possible.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Treant, Animate Trees (p. 290) (dnd5e-mm-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the daily use, number, range, duration, and ending conditions; dial: reduce the number animated or shorten their duration to constrain the extra allies.

rules.statement: At the start of its turn, a troll regains 10 hit points if it has at least 1 hit point; acid or fire damage prevents this trait from functioning at the start of its next turn. It dies only if it starts a turn at 0 hit points and does not regenerate.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Troll, Regeneration (p. 292) (dnd5e-mm-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: regenerate the stated amount unless acid or fire suppresses it; dial: reduce healing or broaden the suppressing damage types if the troll is too hard to defeat.

rules.statement: A creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of an umber hulk and can see its eyes must make a DC 15 Charisma save unless the umber hulk is incapacitated. On a failure, it cannot take reactions until its next turn and rolls a d8 to determine its action and movement; it can avert its eyes to avoid the save, but cannot see the umber hulk until its next turn and must save immediately if it looks at it sooner.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Umber Hulk, Confusing Gaze (p. 293) (dnd5e-mm-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated gaze, save, and random action table; dial: reduce the radius or make the gaze less disruptive if involuntary actions are too costly.

rules.statement: Within a unicorn’s domain, nonmagical open flames go out, native creatures have advantage on checks to hide, healing magic used by a good-aligned creature on another good-aligned creature restores the maximum possible hit points, and curses on good-aligned creatures are suppressed. These regional effects end immediately if the unicorn dies.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Unicorn, Regional Effects (p. 293) (dnd5e-mm-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the effects throughout the domain and end them on the unicorn’s death; dial: limit the domain or omit effects that dominate local play.

rules.statement: A vampire’s charm targets one humanoid it can see within 30 feet that can see it; a failed DC 17 Wisdom save makes the target treat the vampire as a trusted friend and a willing target for its bite, without giving the vampire direct control. Harm by the vampire or its companions permits another save; otherwise it lasts 24 hours or until the vampire dies, moves to another plane, or ends it with a bonus action.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Vampire, Charm (p. 298) (dnd5e-mm-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the stated target limits, retry trigger, and duration; dial: shorten the duration or allow additional ways to end the influence.

rules.statement: A humanoid killed by a vampire’s bite and then buried in the ground rises the following night as a vampire spawn under that vampire’s control. If the vampire that created a spawn dies, the spawn becomes free-willed; if a true vampire lets a spawn drink its blood, the spawn becomes a true vampire and is no longer controlled by its creator.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Vampires, Born from Death (p. 296) (dnd5e-mm-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use burial, the following-night timing, and the stated control changes; dial: remove the blood-drinking route or make transformation require additional conditions.

rules.statement: A vampire that falls to 0 hit points outside its resting place turns to mist instead of falling unconscious, if it is not in sunlight or running water. At 0 hit points it must reach its resting place within 2 hours or be destroyed; there it returns to vampire form, remains paralyzed, and after 1 hour regains 1 hit point.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Vampire, Misty Escape (p. 298) (dnd5e-mm-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the environmental exclusions, two-hour deadline, and recovery sequence; dial: shorten the deadline or remove the automatic return if escape from defeat is too powerful.

rules.statement: A wight can replace one longsword attack in its two-attack routine with a Life Drain attack. On a hit, it deals 1d6 + 2 necrotic damage; the target makes a DC 13 Constitution save or its hit point maximum falls by the damage dealt until it finishes a long rest, and it dies if this reduces its maximum to 0. A humanoid killed by this attack rises as a wight-controlled zombie after 24 hours unless restored to life or its body is destroyed; the wight can control at most twelve zombies.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Wight — Life Drain (dnd5e-mm-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated save, duration, delay, and twelve-zombie limit; dial: none. The control depends on the victim dying and the body remaining available.

rules.statement: A wraith’s Life Drain hit deals 4d8 + 3 necrotic damage; a target that fails a DC 14 Constitution save also loses hit point maximum equal to the damage until a long rest, and dies if its maximum reaches 0. The wraith can turn a humanoid that died violently within the last minute into a controlled specter, appearing in the corpse’s space or the nearest empty space; it can control at most seven specters.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Wraith — Actions (dnd5e-mm-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the save DC, one-minute eligibility window, and seven-specter cap; dial: none. Creating a servant requires a recent violent death.

rules.statement: A wight or wraith in sunlight has disadvantage on attack rolls and on sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks. A wight can see in darkness to 60 feet; a wraith can do so to 60 feet and can pass through creatures and objects as difficult terrain, taking 1d10 force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Wight and Wraith — Traits (dnd5e-mm-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the sunlight penalty and movement limits as written; dial: none. Sunlight impairs these undead, and solid matter remains hazardous if they end within it.

rules.statement: A will-o’-wisp can use a bonus action to target a living creature it can see within 5 feet that has 0 hit points. The target must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution save or die; if it dies, the wisp regains 3d6 hit points.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Will-o’-Wisp — Consume Life (dnd5e-mm-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the 0-hit-point prerequisite, range, save, and healing amount; dial: none. The wisp can feed only on a nearby living creature already at the brink of death.

rules.statement: A wraith can move through creatures and objects as difficult terrain, but takes 1d10 force damage if it ends its turn inside an object. A xorn can burrow through nonmagical, unworked earth and stone without disturbing or displacing the material.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Wraith — Incorporeal Movement; Xorn — Earth Glide (dnd5e-mm-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain each creature’s distinct movement medium and the wraith’s end-of-turn damage; dial: none. The movement is not unrestricted passage through every material.

rules.statement: A xorn can pinpoint the location of precious metals and stones, including coins and gems, within 60 feet by scent. In rocky terrain, it has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Xorn — Traits (dnd5e-mm-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the 60-foot sensing radius and rocky-terrain restriction; dial: none. Its exceptional detection concerns treasure, not all objects.

rules.statement: A yeti’s gaze targets one creature it can see within 30 feet; if the creature can see the yeti, it makes a DC 13 Constitution save or takes 3d6 cold damage and is paralyzed for up to 1 minute, unless immune to cold. It can repeat the save at the end of each turn, ending the effect on a success; after a successful save or the effect ending, it is immune to that yeti’s gaze for 1 hour. The abominable yeti uses the same procedure with a DC 18 save and 6d6 cold damage.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Yeti and Abominable Yeti — Chilling Gaze (dnd5e-mm-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain visibility requirements, repeat saves, immunity exception, and one-hour protection; dial: none. The paralysis is temporary and can be resisted again each turn.

rules.statement: If a yeti takes fire damage, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn. Yetis have advantage on smell-based Wisdom (Perception) checks and on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide in snow.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Yeti — Traits (dnd5e-mm-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the short penalty and the listed circumstance-based advantages; dial: none. Fire briefly disrupts the yeti, while smell and snow assist it.

rules.statement: A yuan-ti abomination can use its action to change between its true form and a Large snake form; its statistics stay the same, carried or worn equipment does not change, and death does not trigger a form change. In its abomination form, it can cast animal friendship on snakes at will, suggestion three times per day, and fear once per day, without material components; its spell save DC is 15.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Yuan-Ti Abomination — Traits (dnd5e-mm-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the action cost, unchanged statistics, equipment exception, and spell uses; dial: none. Changing shape takes deliberate action and does not transform possessions.

rules.statement: A yuan-ti malison can use its action to change between its true form and a Medium snake form; its statistics stay the same, its equipment does not change, and death does not trigger a change. In yuan-ti form it can cast animal friendship on snakes at will and suggestion three times per day without material components; its spell save DC is 13. Its body has one of three listed human-and-serpent configurations.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Yuan-Ti Malison — Traits (dnd5e-mm-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the action cost, fixed statistics, equipment exception, and spell limit; dial: none. Its alternate shape changes appearance, not capabilities or gear.

rules.statement: A yugoloth slain away from Gehenna dissolves into ichor and reforms there at full strength; only on Gehenna can it be permanently destroyed. A summoner who uses a yugoloth’s true name as recorded in a Book of Keeping compels it to serve, though it follows instructions literally and may exploit their wording.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Yugoloths — Back to Gehenna; The Books of Keeping (dnd5e-mm-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the home-plane restriction and true-name control; dial: none. Destruction is temporary off Gehenna, while compelled service carries a risk of deliberate misinterpretation.

rules.statement: A yugoloth with the summoning option can try once per day to summon its listed allies, with a creature-specific chance of success and possible number or type of arrivals. A summoned yugoloth appears in an empty space within 60 feet, remains for up to 1 minute or until it or its summoner dies, and cannot summon others; it acts independently unless its summoner is an ultroloth, in which case it acts as an ally. The summoner can dismiss it with a bonus action.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Variant: Yugoloth Summoning (dnd5e-mm-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use each listed success chance, duration, arrival limit, and control exception; dial: none. The call is uncertain, brief, and does not guarantee obedience except for the stated ultroloth case.

rules.statement: A spider can climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check; while touching a web, it knows the exact location of every creature touching that web and ignores movement limits imposed by webbing.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Giant Spider — Spider Climb, Web Sense, Web Walker (pp. 329–330) (dnd5e-mm-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: web contact enables precise sensing, but only of creatures touching that same web.

rules.statement: A giant spider’s web attack can restrain one creature; the target can use an action to attempt a DC 12 Strength check to break free. The webbing can also be destroyed (AC 10, 5 hit points; vulnerable to fire and immune to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage).
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Giant Spider — Web (p. 329) (dnd5e-mm-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: restraint lasts until the target breaks free or the web is destroyed; escape costs an action and a successful check.

rules.statement: If a giant spider’s bite poison reduces a creature to 0 hit points, the creature is stable but remains poisoned for 1 hour, including after regaining hit points, and is paralyzed while poisoned this way.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Giant Spider — Bite (p. 329) (dnd5e-mm-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reaching 0 hit points triggers a lingering condition; recovery of hit points does not end it before the hour expires.

rules.statement: A giant toad’s bite deals 1d10 + 2 piercing damage and 1d10 poison damage, and grapples the target (escape DC 13); while grappled, the target is restrained, and the toad cannot bite another target. The toad can swallow a grappled Medium or smaller target after a hit; it is blinded and restrained, has total cover from effects outside the toad, and takes 3d6 acid damage at the start of each of the toad’s turns, with only one creature swallowed at a time.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Giant Toad — Bite and Swallow (p. 330) (dnd5e-mm-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: swallowing isolates and damages one target, but requires an existing grapple and a successful bite.

rules.statement: If a giant toad dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can leave the corpse by spending 5 feet of movement; the creature exits prone.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Giant Toad — Swallow (p. 330) (dnd5e-mm-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the host’s death releases the captive, who pays movement and emerges prone.

rules.statement: A phase spider can use a bonus action to shift from the Material Plane to the Ethereal Plane or back again.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Phase Spider — Ethereal Jaunt (p. 334) (dnd5e-mm-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: movement is between two named planes, costs a bonus action, and provides no stated distance or duration limit.

rules.statement: A swarm can occupy another creature’s space, and can pass through any opening large enough for one of its component Tiny creatures. A swarm cannot regain hit points or gain temporary hit points, and its attack damage is reduced when it has half or fewer of its hit points.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Swarm of Insects and related swarm entries (pp. 337–340) (dnd5e-mm-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the swarm’s formation permits shared space and narrow passage, but limits recovery and weakens attacks as it loses members.

rules.statement: A swarm of bats cannot use its blindsight while deafened; the killer whale likewise loses blindsight while deafened.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Swarm of Bats — Echolocation (p. 337); Killer Whale — Echolocation (p. 332) (dnd5e-mm-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: deafness blocks this sensory capability until hearing is restored.

rules.statement: An NPC spellcaster can replace a spell on its list with a different spell of the same level from that same list without changing its challenge rating. Adding racial traits also leaves an NPC’s challenge rating unchanged, while armor or weapon changes can affect it.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Appendix B — Customizing NPCs (p. 343) (dnd5e-mm-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell substitution is bounded by level and list; equipment changes can alter the NPC’s combat rating.

rules.statement: An acolyte casts with Wisdom (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit): it knows light, sacred flame, and thaumaturgy at will and has three 1st-level slots for bless, cure wounds, and sanctuary.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Acolyte — Spellcasting (p. 343) (dnd5e-mm-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: at-will cantrips and three 1st-level slots limit the acolyte’s spell output.

rules.statement: An archmage casts with Intelligence (spell save DC 17, +9 to hit), can cast disguise self and invisibility at will, and has the listed prepared wizard spells with the stated slots through 9th level; it casts stoneskin, mind blank, and time stop on itself before combat.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Archmage — Spellcasting (p. 343) (dnd5e-mm-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell use is bounded by the listed slots, while three specified spells are already active on the archmage before combat.

rules.statement: During its first turn, the assassin has advantage on attacks against creatures that have not yet acted; any hit it lands on a surprised creature is a critical hit.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Assassin, p. 343 — Assassinate (dnd5e-mm-2014#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the attack advantage only on the assassin’s first turn, and the critical-hit rule only against surprised targets; timing and surprise limit the benefit.

rules.statement: Once per turn, the assassin adds 4d6 damage to a weapon hit if it has advantage on the attack roll, or if the target is within 5 feet of an ally who is not incapacitated and the assassin does not have disadvantage.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Assassin, p. 343 — Sneak Attack (dnd5e-mm-2014#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow one qualifying damage bonus per turn; attack conditions and the once-per-turn limit constrain it.

rules.statement: When the assassin succeeds on a Dexterity save against an effect that normally deals half damage on a success, it takes no damage; on a failure, it takes half damage.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Assassin, p. 343 — Evasion (dnd5e-mm-2014#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: alter damage only for qualifying Dexterity saves; the save result determines the reduced damage.

rules.statement: A shortsword or light-crossbow hit from the assassin deals its weapon damage, then forces a DC 15 Constitution save; failure deals 7d6 poison damage and success deals half that amount. The assassin resists poison damage.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Assassin, p. 343 — Damage Resistances; Actions (dnd5e-mm-2014#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the poison save and damage on each listed weapon hit; the save and poison resistance limit the resulting harm.

rules.statement: The cultist and cult fanatic have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Cultist and Cult Fanatic, p. 345 — Dark Devotion (dnd5e-mm-2014#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant advantage only on saves against these two conditions.

rules.statement: The cult fanatic casts its listed cleric spells using Wisdom, with save DC 11 and +3 to hit with spell attacks. It has three cantrips available at will, four 1st-level slots, and three 2nd-level slots.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Cult Fanatic, p. 345 — Spellcasting (dnd5e-mm-2014#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spells use the listed ability and slots; slot counts limit leveled casting while cantrips are at will.

rules.statement: The druid casts its listed druid spells using Wisdom, with save DC 12 and +4 to hit with spell attacks. It has three cantrips available at will, four 1st-level slots, and three 2nd-level slots.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Druid, p. 346 — Spellcasting (dnd5e-mm-2014#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed spell ability and slot allotment; the available slots bound leveled casting.

rules.statement: The mage casts its listed wizard spells using Intelligence, with save DC 14 and +6 to hit with spell attacks. It has four cantrips at will, four 1st-level slots, three each of 2nd-, 3rd-, and 4th-level slots, and one 5th-level slot.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Mage, p. 347 — Spellcasting (dnd5e-mm-2014#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed spell ability and slot allotment; slot counts bound leveled casting, while cantrips are at will.

rules.statement: When the priest hits with a melee weapon after using a bonus action to expend a spell slot, its melee weapon attacks deal an extra 3d6 radiant damage until the turn ends. Spending a slot of 2nd level or higher increases the extra damage by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Priest, p. 348 — Divine Eminence (dnd5e-mm-2014#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spend a spell slot and a bonus action for a turn-long damage boost; higher-level slots cost more and scale the damage.

rules.statement: The priest casts its listed cleric spells using Wisdom, with save DC 13 and +5 to hit with spell attacks. It has three cantrips at will, four 1st-level slots, three 2nd-level slots, and two 3rd-level slots.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Priest, p. 348 — Spellcasting (dnd5e-mm-2014#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed ability and slots; finite slot counts limit leveled casting.

rules.statement: The knight can use a bonus action to issue a command or warning for 1 minute, once per short or long rest. A non-hostile creature it can see within 30 feet that hears and understands it may add a d4 to an attack roll or saving throw; a creature can benefit from only one such die at a time, and the effect ends if the knight is incapacitated.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Knight, p. 347 — Leadership (dnd5e-mm-2014#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: offer the die only within range and while the knight remains conscious; rest-based recharge, duration, and one-die limit constrain use.

rules.statement: A creature that succeeds on a DC 15 Strength save against the gladiator’s shield bash is not knocked prone; on a failure, a Medium or smaller target is knocked prone.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Gladiator, p. 346 — Shield Bash (dnd5e-mm-2014#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: impose prone only on a failed save against a qualifying target; size and save success limit the effect.

rules.statement: A spy can use a bonus action on each of its turns to Dash, Disengage, or Hide. Once per turn it can add 2d6 damage to a weapon hit if it has advantage on the attack roll, or if the target is within 5 feet of an ally who is not incapacitated and the spy has no disadvantage.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Spy, p. 349 — Cunning Action; Sneak Attack (dnd5e-mm-2014#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bonus action permits only the listed actions, and the damage bonus is limited to one qualifying hit per turn.

rules.statement: A genie with wish-granting power can grant one to three wishes to a non-genie within 60 feet, by casting wish on that creature’s behalf; it may twist the request’s wording to favor itself. The same genie can use its full allotment on a particular creature only once in that creature’s existence.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 145, Variant: Genie Powers — Wishes (dnd5e-mm-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the limited number of uses and one-per-recipient lifetime limit; dial: make wording disputes more or less consequential to fit the setting.

rules.statement: Some genies can magically disguise themselves at will; more powerful ones can use true polymorph on themselves one to three times per day, and a rare few can apply it to other creatures or objects. The effect may last longer than the spell normally allows.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 145, Variant: Genie Powers — Disguises (dnd5e-mm-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the stated limits on targets and daily uses; dial: vary access to the stronger versions by genie rank.

rules.statement: A ghost can possess a humanoid it sees within 5 feet that fails a DC 13 Charisma save; the ghost takes control while the target remains aware, and the ghost cannot be targeted except by effects that turn undead. Possession ends if the body reaches 0 hit points, the ghost ends it as a bonus action, or an effect such as dispel evil and good forces it out; the ghost then appears within 5 feet of the body.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 148, Ghost — Possession (dnd5e-mm-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed save, range, and exit conditions; dial: make possession rarer or more common by changing its recharge or resistance.

rules.statement: A ghost can shift between the Material and Ethereal Planes. While it is on one, it can see 60 feet into the other; while in the Border Ethereal, it is visible across the boundary but cannot affect or be affected by creatures on the other plane.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 148, Ghost — Ethereal Sight and Etherealness (dnd5e-mm-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the one-way interaction barrier between planes; dial: change which creatures or effects can cross that barrier.

rules.statement: A githzerai zerth can innately use plane shift once per day, with Wisdom as its spellcasting ability; the listed innate psionic spells require no components. Githyanki knights also have plane shift once per day, using Intelligence, and their listed innate spells require no components.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Pages 161–162, Githyanki Knight and Githzerai Zerth — Innate Spellcasting (dnd5e-mm-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: treat planar travel as a limited innate capability, not a freely available route; dial: change the daily allowance or destination constraints.

rules.statement: In Limbo, the plane’s chaotic matter and energy respond to sentience; githzerai use mental power to settle the surroundings into stable, survivable forms and create sanctuaries. Their fortresses remain protected from the surrounding turmoil by their will.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 160, Githzerai — Order amid Chaos (dnd5e-mm-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: make stability depend on active sentience and will; dial: set how large or durable a controlled sanctuary can be.

rules.statement: A golem’s creator binds an elemental spirit into its constructed body and subjects it to the creator’s will. A special amulet or similar item can let its holder control a golem; without instructions, it follows its last orders as best it can, and conflicting orders can make it alternate between them.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 168, Golems — Elemental Spirit in Material Form; Blind Obedience (dnd5e-mm-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep control tied to creation or a control item, with no independent reasoning; dial: vary how precisely an item can override old orders.

rules.statement: A night hag with a heartstone can enter the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane or return from it. While ethereal, it can haunt a sleeping humanoid once per day; protection from evil and good or a magic circle prevents contact.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 179, Night Hag — Etherealness and Nightmare Haunting (dnd5e-mm-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require the heartstone and preserve the stated protective counters; dial: change the frequency or duration of the haunting.

rules.statement: If a night hag’s haunting visions persist for at least 1 hour, the sleeper gains no benefit from that rest and loses 5 hit points from its maximum. The reduction lasts until removed by greater restoration or similar magic; if it lowers the maximum to 0, the target dies, and an evil target’s soul is trapped in the hag’s soul bag.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 179, Night Hag — Nightmare Haunting (dnd5e-mm-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the hour threshold, fixed reduction, and stated removal method; dial: alter the haunting’s lethality or recovery burden.

rules.statement: When an empyrean dies, its spirit returns to its home plane, where one of its divine parents resurrects it unless there is a good reason not to. Its mood can also change nearby conditions: misery can wither plants or bring salt rain, while joy can bring sunlight and lively animals.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Page 131, Empyrean — Manifest Emotion; Immortal Titans (dnd5e-mm-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the home-plane return and conditional resurrection; dial: decide how broadly emotional effects alter the surrounding environment.

rules.statement: A wizard seeking lichdom bargains with a fiends, evil gods, or similar entities for the required knowledge, and those who control that knowledge demand loyalty and service in return.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Lich — Secrets of Undeath (p. 204) (dnd5e-mm-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant the transformation knowledge; dial: require continuing fealty or service, at the price of autonomy.

rules.statement: A lich-making ritual binds the wizard’s soul into a prepared phylactery, keeping it in the mortal world rather than allowing it to travel to the Outer Planes; the wizard becomes a lich as the soul enters the vessel.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Lich — Secrets of Undeath (p. 204) (dnd5e-mm-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the soul remains anchored to the world; dial: the vessel becomes a critical vulnerability.

rules.statement: To sustain its body and consciousness, a lich must periodically imprison a creature’s body and soul in its phylactery. The phylactery must be on the lich’s plane, holds only one creature, and a 9th-level dispel magic cast on it releases the captive; after 24 hours, the captive is consumed and only divine intervention can restore it to life.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Lich — Soul Sacrifices (p. 204) (dnd5e-mm-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one captive can be held at a time; dial: the lich pays with a soul, and the victim faces irreversible death absent divine aid.

rules.statement: If a lich has a phylactery, destroying its body causes it to form a new body within 5 feet of the phylactery in 1d10 days, restored to full hit points and activity.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Lich — Rejuvenation (p. 203) (dnd5e-mm-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: body destruction is not final while the anchor exists; dial: destroying or securing the phylactery is the countermeasure.

rules.statement: A nightmare can carry itself and up to three willing creatures within 5 feet between the Material and Ethereal Planes; the passage gives no travel duration or additional cost.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Nightmare — Ethereal Stride (p. 236) (dnd5e-mm-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow travel between these two planes; dial: limit passengers to three willing nearby companions.

rules.statement: A nightmare summoned from the Lower Planes shows no special loyalty to its summoner unless a worthy sacrifice is offered as food when it arrives.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Nightmare — Dread Steed (p. 236) (dnd5e-mm-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: summoning does not ensure service; dial: a worthy sacrifice buys loyalty, at the cost of a life or other suitable offering.

rules.statement: An ancient merfolk ritual opened a gateway to the Abyss, and survivors who passed through were transformed over generations into merrow by the plane’s influence.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Merrow — Transformed Merfolk (p. 220) (dnd5e-mm-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a gateway permits passage; dial: prolonged exposure to the destination plane changes the travelers.

rules.statement: A mind flayer can innately cast plane shift once per day, but only on itself.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Mind Flayer — Innate Spellcasting (Psionics) (p. 223) (dnd5e-mm-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit planar movement; dial: restrict use to once daily and the caster alone.

rules.statement: A rakshasa can innately cast plane shift once per day, with no material components required.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Rakshasa — Innate Spellcasting (p. 237) (dnd5e-mm-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit the creature to travel between planes; dial: limit use to once per day.

rules.statement: A slaad can innately cast plane shift on itself once per day; the grayslaad’s listed daily spell uses do not require material components.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: Grayslaad — Innate Spellcasting (p. 279) (dnd5e-mm-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit self-only planar travel; dial: restrict it to one use per day.

rules.statement: A fiend can communicate telepathically with a creature it has charmed at any distance, including when they are on different planes.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: p. 286, Succubus/Incubus — Telepathic Bond (dnd5e-mm-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
