rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial; the cross-plane communication applies only to a creature the fiend has charmed.

rules.statement: The fiend can use an action to become a Small or Medium humanoid, or return to its true form. Its statistics stay the same except for size and speed, carried or worn equipment does not change, it loses flight without its wings, and death restores its true form.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: p. 286, Succubus/Incubus — Shapechanger (dnd5e-mm-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial; changing appearance does not change most capabilities or transform equipment.

rules.statement: One visible humanoid within 30 feet must pass a DC 15 Wisdom save or be charmed for 1 day and obey verbal or telepathic commands. Harm or a suicidal command permits another save; a successful save or the effect ending grants immunity to this fiend’s charm for 24 hours, and the fiend can charm only one target at a time.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: p. 286, Succubus/Incubus — Charm (dnd5e-mm-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial; control is limited to one target and ends early only under the stated conditions or a successful repeat save.

rules.statement: The fiend can kiss a charmed or willing creature, which makes a DC 15 Constitution save; failure deals 5d10 + 5 damage and success deals half. The target’s hit point maximum falls by damage dealt until it finishes a long rest, and it dies if its maximum reaches 0.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: p. 286, Succubus/Incubus — Draining Kiss (dnd5e-mm-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial; the maximum-hit-point loss lasts until a long rest, while reaching zero causes death.

rules.statement: The fiend can magically move between the Material Plane and the Ethereal Plane.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: p. 286, Succubus/Incubus — Etherealness (dnd5e-mm-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial; travel is limited to movement between these two named planes.

rules.statement: The tarrasque is immune to being charmed, frightened, paralyzed, or poisoned.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: p. 287, Tarrasque — Condition Immunities (dnd5e-mm-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial; these four conditions cannot affect this creature.

rules.statement: The tarrasque has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: p. 287, Tarrasque — Magic Resistance (dnd5e-mm-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial; the benefit applies to saves against spells and magical effects, not every kind of test.

rules.statement: When targeted by magic missile, a line spell, or a spell requiring a ranged attack roll, roll a d6: on 1–5 the tarrasque is unaffected; on 6 it is also unaffected and the effect is reflected to target the caster as though it originated from the tarrasque.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: p. 287, Tarrasque — Reflective Carapace (dnd5e-mm-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial; only the listed spell types trigger the d6, and reflection occurs on a 6.

rules.statement: The phase spider can use a bonus action to shift magically between the Material and Ethereal Planes.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: p. 334, Phase Spider — Ethereal Jaunt (dnd5e-mm-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial; the shift costs a bonus action and only connects the two specified planes.

rules.statement: A phase spider’s bite deals 1d10 + 2 piercing damage, then forces a DC 11 Constitution save against 4d8 poison damage, halved on success. If the poison reduces the target to 0 hit points, it remains stable but poisoned for 1 hour even after regaining hit points, and is paralyzed while poisoned in this way.
locators: Monster Manual 2014: p. 334, Phase Spider — Bite (dnd5e-mm-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial; the lasting poisoned state and associated paralysis apply only when the poison reduces the target to 0 hit points.

rules.statement: A character of a fantastical race can raise one ability score by 2 and another by 1, or raise three different scores by 1; no score can exceed 20. The character can speak, read, and write Common and one other language agreed with the DM.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Creating Your Character (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated score increases and language access; dial: the player and DM choose the increases and second language, within the caps.

rules.statement: Each player character has a creature-type tag, and some rules affect creatures by type; for example, cure wounds does not work on Constructs or Undead. Creature types themselves do not otherwise grant rules in this passage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Creature Type (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply type-specific restrictions when a rule names a creature type; dial: none, since the passage gives a fixed example and no cost.

rules.statement: Aarakocra can fly at their walking speed, but cannot use that flight while wearing medium or heavy armor. Starting at 3rd level, they can cast gust of wind once per long rest without material components, or use spell slots of 2nd level or higher; they choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as the spellcasting ability.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Aarakocra Traits (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the racial flight and spell access as written; dial: flight is disabled by medium or heavy armor, and the free spell use refreshes only after a long rest.

rules.statement: An aasimar can touch a creature as an action to restore hit points equal to a number of d4s equal to the aasimar’s proficiency bonus; this is usable once per long rest. At 3rd level, the aasimar can use a bonus action to adopt one chosen celestial revelation for 1 minute, once per long rest, and that revelation ends early if they use a bonus action to end it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Aasimar Traits (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the selected revelation’s specific effects and healing roll; dial: healing and revelation are each constrained by their stated action and long-rest limit.

rules.statement: A bugbear has advantage on saving throws to avoid or end being charmed, can reach 5 feet farther than usual with melee attacks on its turn, and can move through and stop in spaces large enough for a Small creature without squeezing. If it hits a creature with an attack roll before that creature has taken a turn in the current combat, the hit deals an extra 2d6 damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Bugbear Traits (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the defenses, reach, movement, and bonus damage as stated; dial: the extra damage is limited to attacks made before the target’s first turn in that combat.

rules.statement: A centaur that moves at least 30 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a melee weapon attack on the same turn can use a bonus action to make one hoof attack against that target. Its carrying and pushing, dragging, or lifting capacity counts as one size larger, but climbing that requires hands and feet costs 4 extra feet of movement for each foot climbed.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Centaur Traits (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the charge follow-up, capacity adjustment, and climbing penalty; dial: the extra hoof attack requires the stated movement, hit, and bonus action.

rules.statement: A changeling can use an action to change its appearance and voice, including coloration, hair length, sex, height, and weight, and can switch between Medium and Small. The new look cannot copy an unseen individual or alter its basic limb arrangement; clothing and equipment do not change, and the form remains until it reverts by action or dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Changeling Traits—Shapechanger (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow appearance and voice changes within the stated boundaries; dial: it costs an action and changes neither statistics, gear, nor clothing.

rules.statement: Starting at 3rd level, a deep gnome can cast disguise self once per long rest, and from 5th level can also cast nondetection once per long rest without a material component; either spell can also be cast using an appropriate spell slot. It has advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws against spells, and can make a Dexterity (Stealth) check with advantage a number of times equal to proficiency bonus per long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Deep Gnome Traits (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the spells and defenses at their listed levels; dial: spell access and enhanced Stealth checks are limited by long rests, with Stealth uses scaling by proficiency bonus.

rules.statement: A duergar can cast enlarge/reduce on itself starting at 3rd level and invisibility on itself starting at 5th level, each once per long rest without material components, and can also use appropriate spell slots. It has advantage on saves to avoid or end being poisoned, charmed, or stunned, and has resistance to poison damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Duergar Traits (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the self-only spells, condition defenses, and poison resistance; dial: each free spell use refreshes on a long rest and the spells can only target the duergar.

rules.statement: An eladrin can teleport up to 30 feet to a visible unoccupied space as a bonus action, a number of times equal to proficiency bonus per long rest. From 3rd level, that teleport gains an effect based on season: Autumn can charm up to two nearby creatures for up to 1 minute, Winter can frighten one nearby creature until the end of the eladrin’s next turn, Spring can teleport a willing nearby creature instead, and Summer deals fire damage equal to proficiency bonus to chosen creatures within 5 feet.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Eladrin Traits—Fey Step (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve the chosen season’s added effect with the listed range and duration; dial: teleports are limited by proficiency bonus per long rest, and Autumn’s charm ends if the target takes damage from the eladrin or its companions.

rules.statement: A fairy knows druidcraft and can cast faerie fire starting at 3rd level and enlarge/reduce starting at 5th level, each once per long rest through this trait; it can also cast them using appropriate spell slots. It can fly at walking speed, but cannot use that flight while wearing medium or heavy armor.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Fairy Traits (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant the cantrip, leveled spells, and flight as specified; dial: free spell uses refresh on a long rest, and armor can disable flight.

rules.statement: A firbolg can cast detect magic and disguise self once each per long rest through its racial trait, or use spell slots; its disguise can make it appear up to 3 feet shorter or taller. It can turn invisible as a bonus action until its next turn, or until it attacks, makes a damage roll, or forces a saving throw, with uses equal to proficiency bonus per long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Firbolg Traits (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the spells and brief invisibility as written; dial: each spell has one free use per long rest and invisibility ends on the listed actions or after a short duration.

rules.statement: A firbolg can communicate in a limited way with Beasts, Plants, and vegetation; they understand its words but cannot necessarily respond in kind. The firbolg has advantage on Charisma checks made to influence them.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Firbolg Traits—Speech of Beast and Leaf (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow one-way understanding and advantage on influence checks against the stated targets; dial: this grants no ability to understand their replies.

rules.statement: An air genasi can hold its breath indefinitely while not incapacitated and has resistance to lightning damage. It knows shocking grasp and, from 3rd and 5th level respectively, can cast feather fall and levitate once per long rest without material components, or use appropriate spell slots.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Air Genasi Traits (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the breath, resistance, and spell benefits; dial: the breath ability stops while incapacitated and each free leveled spell use refreshes on a long rest.

rules.statement: An earth genasi can move across difficult terrain without extra movement when walking on the ground or a floor. It knows blade ward and can cast it as a bonus action a number of times equal to proficiency bonus per long rest; from 5th level it can cast pass without trace once per long rest without a material component, or use an appropriate spell slot.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Earth Genasi Traits (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ignore difficult-terrain movement costs on ground or floors and apply the spell benefits; dial: bonus-action blade ward and the free pass without trace use are limited by long rests.

rules.statement: When you select the fire-genasi lineage, choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as the spellcasting ability for its spells. You know produce flame; from level 3 you can cast burning hands once per long rest, and from level 5 flame blade once per long rest without a material component, or cast either spell with an appropriate spell slot.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Fire Genasi Traits, pp. 16–17 (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lineage grants specified spells; dial: chosen casting ability and slot use; reason: innate elemental heritage sets the source, while rest limits bound free casting.

rules.statement: Water genasi know acid splash and can breathe air and water. From level 3 they can cast create or destroy water once per long rest, and from level 5 water walk once per long rest without a material component; either can also be cast with an appropriate spell slot, using a chosen Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma ability.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Water Genasi Traits, pp. 17–18 (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ancestry grants aquatic function and spells; dial: selected casting ability and slot option; reason: elemental lineage supplies the power, with free uses limited by rest.

rules.statement: After each long rest, a githyanki gains proficiency in one skill and one weapon or tool until its next long rest, by drawing on knowledge associated with the Astral Plane. Githyanki know mage hand, whose hand is invisible when cast through this trait; from level 3 they can cast jump and from level 5 misty step, each once per long rest or with an appropriate spell slot, without components, using a chosen Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma ability.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Githyanki Traits, p. 18 (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: shared astral experience supplies temporary proficiency and innate spells; dial: chosen ability and spell-slot use; reason: the knowledge refreshes at rest and free spell uses are limited.

rules.statement: Githzerai know mage hand, invisible when cast through the trait. From level 3 they can cast shield and from level 5 detect thoughts, each once per long rest or using a suitable spell slot, with a chosen Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma ability; the spells require no components when cast this way.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Githzerai Traits, p. 20 (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: innate psionic power grants the spells; dial: chosen casting ability and slot use; reason: free casts renew on rest, and the source removes component requirements.

rules.statement: Githzerai have advantage on saves to avoid or end the charmed or frightened condition on themselves, and resistance to psychic damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Githzerai Traits, p. 20 (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: mental discipline improves defenses and psychic resilience halves damage; dial: none; reason: innate mental conditioning protects only against these listed threats.

rules.statement: A goblin that damages a creature larger than itself with an attack or spell can add extra damage equal to its proficiency bonus. It can do so proficiency-bonus times per long rest, no more than once per turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Goblin Traits, p. 21 (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited bonus damage; dial: none; reason: the ancestry’s knack is restricted by uses per rest and once-per-turn timing.

rules.statement: A hobgoblin can take the Help action as a bonus action proficiency-bonus times per long rest. From level 3, each use also grants the helped creature and the hobgoblin temporary hit points, a brief speed increase, or an effect that imposes disadvantage on an attack roll, chosen when Help is used.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Hobgoblin Traits, p. 24 (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reciprocal fey gift enhances assistance; dial: choose one benefit per use; reason: the gift is limited by proficiency-bonus uses per long rest.

rules.statement: A hobgoblin that misses an attack or fails an ability check or save can gain a bonus equal to the number of visible allies within 30 feet, up to +3. Uses equal proficiency bonus return on a long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Hobgoblin Traits, p. 24 (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: nearby allies improve a failed roll; dial: bonus caps at +3; reason: reciprocal bonds provide leverage, but only a limited number of times per rest.

rules.statement: A githyanki’s Astral Plane-linked knowledge lets it temporarily acquire proficiencies after a long rest; the proficiencies last until the next long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Githyanki Traits, p. 18 (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: borrow experience from an astral reservoir; dial: one skill and one weapon or tool; reason: the borrowed expertise expires at the next rest.

rules.statement: A shadar-kai can teleport up to 30 feet to a visible unoccupied space as a bonus action, proficiency-bonus times per long rest. From level 3, teleporting this way also grants resistance to all damage until the start of its next turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Shadar-kai Traits, p. 32 (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a limited supernatural teleport; dial: temporary broad damage resistance from level 3; reason: the effect is tied to the Raven Queen’s blessing and restricted to uses per rest.

rules.statement: A shifter can transform into a more bestial appearance as a bonus action, gaining temporary hit points equal to twice its proficiency bonus. The state lasts 1 minute, until death, or until ended as a bonus action; it can be used proficiency-bonus times per long rest and grants one chosen additional benefit while active.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Shifter Traits, p. 33 (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: temporary bestial enhancement with temporary hit points; dial: choose one benefit and uses per rest; reason: the inherited trait is temporary and has a bounded activation count.

rules.statement: At least three mind flayer arcanists can spend three days in a ritual combining spellcasting, psionic communion, a silver-and-gemstone container, and an equal number of living victims’ souls to become free-willed undead. Their undeath lasts only as long as the life of the victim selected for each; repeating the ritual with new victims can extend it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Collaborative Undeath, pp. 42–43 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ritual requires a group, a crafted container, and several days; dial: set how often the life term can be renewed, at the cost of living victims’ souls.

rules.statement: When an alhoon is destroyed, its mind moves into the ritual container rather than restoring its body. It remains there in communion with other trapped alhoon minds and sacrificed souls; destroying the container consigns those within to oblivion.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Collaborative Undeath, pp. 42–43 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: destruction preserves a mind but not its body; dial: determine whether the container can be destroyed, risking permanent oblivion for its occupants.

rules.statement: A creature holding the alhoons’ container has advantage on attacks, saving throws, and checks against those alhoons, while they have disadvantage on those rolls against the holder. The holder can telepathically communicate with trapped souls; alhoons in the container can speak telepathically with the holder, who can silence the souls but not the alhoons.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Collaborative Undeath, p. 43 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: possession shifts the contest in the holder’s favor and grants limited communication; dial: let the holder silence trapped souls, but not the alhoons.

rules.statement: A creature swallowed by an astral dreadnought is transported to its otherwise inaccessible demiplane. A creature can leave only by magic that enables planar travel; if the dreadnought dies, the demiplane vanishes and its contents appear around the corpse.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Astral Dreadnought, Demiplanar Donjon, p. 51 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: escape requires planar-travel magic, and death releases everything stored inside; dial: decide how difficult such magic is to obtain and whether the space remains stable.

rules.statement: As a legendary action, the astral dreadnought can spend two actions to send one Huge or smaller creature it can see within 60 feet to its demiplane unless it succeeds on a DC 19 Charisma save. The target returns at the end of its next turn to its former space, or the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Astral Dreadnought, Donjon Visit, p. 51 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect lasts through the target’s next turn and allows a save; dial: the two-action cost limits its use while making the short removal tactically significant.

rules.statement: An archdruid can transform twice per day into a Beast or Elemental of challenge rating 6 or lower for up to 9 hours. The archdruid keeps its current hit points, hit point maximum, languages, ability to speak, and spellcasting; it returns to its normal form if it dies, falls unconscious, or uses a bonus action to revert.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Archdruid, Change Shape, p. 48 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the form is limited by creature type, challenge rating, uses, and duration; dial: the retained hit points and spellcasting preserve the archdruid’s capabilities through the change.

rules.statement: When a creature’s saving throw against an alkilith’s confusion-inducing effect fails by 5 or more, it is affected by the confusion spell for 1 minute without the alkilith needing to concentrate. While affected this way, it is immune to that alkilith’s confusion-inducing effect.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Alkilith, Foment Confusion, p. 44 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the stronger effect requires a failure by at least 5 and blocks repeat application while it lasts; dial: the one-minute duration sets the cost of a severe failed save.

rules.statement: An alhoon can use its reaction up to three times per day to make a visible creature within 60 feet fail a spell of 3rd level or lower that it is casting, without consuming the spell’s slots or charges.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Alhoon, Negate Spell, p. 43 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect is limited to three uses per day, a visible target, and spells of 3rd level or lower; dial: the target loses the spell’s effect but not its expenditure.

rules.statement: A creature other than a devil that begins its turn within 10 feet of Bael must make a DC 22 Wisdom save or become frightened until the start of its next turn. It automatically succeeds if it has advantage on saves against spells and magical effects; the fear ends if Bael wishes it to or becomes incapacitated.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Bael — Dread (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a short-range fear check each turn; dial: affect only creatures near Bael, with stated exceptions and an end point.

rules.statement: Bael regains 20 hit points at the start of his turn. Cold or radiant damage suspends this regeneration until the start of his next turn, and he dies only if he starts his turn at 0 hit points without regenerating.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Bael — Regeneration (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recurring recovery; dial: cold or radiant damage interrupts it, while lethal defeat depends on the turn-start checkpoint.

rules.statement: Bael can cast the listed spells without material components, using Charisma and a save DC of 21: at will, alter self, charm person, detect magic, invisibility, and major image; three times per day each, dispel magic, fly, suggestion, and wall of fire; and once per day, dominate monster.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Bael — Spellcasting (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell use is limited by the listed daily frequencies and save DC; dial: this caster needs no material components.

rules.statement: A balhannoth can use a lair action to target one creature within 500 feet; on a failed DC 16 Wisdom save, the target and its worn and carried gear teleport to an unoccupied space the balhannoth chooses within 60 feet of it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: A Balhannoth's Lair — Lair Actions (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save relocates one target; dial: the effect is limited by range, destination space, and the lair-action timing.

rules.statement: A balhannoth can use a lair action to become invisible to one creature within 500 feet that fails a DC 16 Wisdom save; this lasts 1 minute and ends if the balhannoth attacks that creature.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: A Balhannoth's Lair — Lair Actions (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: concealment affects one creature after a failed save; dial: it lasts at most 1 minute and is broken by attacking that creature.

rules.statement: A balhannoth can reshape nonliving terrain across an area up to 500 feet square to imitate a location a Humanoid desires, after 10 minutes. It cannot create moving parts or magical properties; the apparent objects are fakes on close inspection, and the change lasts until the balhannoth dies or uses this lair action again.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: A Balhannoth's Lair — Lair Actions (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: local terrain can be altered into a desire-based imitation; dial: the change takes time, excludes functioning or magical creations, and has a defined ending.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of its lair, a balhannoth senses each Humanoid's strongest desires and whether they concern a safe place to rest. Nearby creatures also feel increasingly close to their greatest desire as they approach the lair; both regional effects end immediately when the balhannoth dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: A Balhannoth's Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the creature senses desires and its lair exerts a lure; dial: effects are confined to the stated radius and cease on death.

rules.statement: A banderhobb holding even a tiny piece of a creature or object knows the most direct route to it if it is within 1 mile. It serves its creator until its existence ends, usually several days after it is created.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Banderhobb — Resonant Connection; Banderhobb description (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a physical trace supplies a route-finding link and the summoned servant follows its creator's bidding; dial: tracking requires possession of a trace, has a 1-mile limit, and the servant is short-lived.

rules.statement: When a barghest feeds for at least 1 minute on the corpse of a Fey or Humanoid it killed within the past 10 minutes, it destroys the corpse and traps the victim's soul for 24 hours. While trapped, revival magic has a 50 percent chance to fail and be wasted; once digestion is complete, the soul is digested and the victim cannot be revived, but if the barghest dies before then, the soul is released.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Barghest — Soul Feeding (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: corpse consumption temporarily binds a soul and can ultimately prevent revival; dial: feeding takes a minute, requires a recent kill, and the binding has a 24-hour interval and death escape.

rules.statement: A berbalang can create one spectral duplicate in a visible unoccupied space within 60 feet, once per short or long rest. While it exists the berbalang is unconscious; the duplicate shares its statistics and knowledge, its experiences are known to the berbalang, and it disappears if either is reduced to 0 hit points or the berbalang dismisses it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Berbalang — Spectral Duplicate (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a duplicate can scout while sharing experience; dial: use is rest-limited, only one duplicate can exist, and the original body is unconscious and vulnerable.

rules.statement: A blackguard can use its bonus action immediately after hitting with an attack to force a DC 13 Constitution save. On a failure, it chooses blindness for 1 minute, with a repeat save at the end of each affected creature's turns, or pushes the target up to 10 feet and knocks it prone.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Blackguard — Smite (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a hit can be followed by one of two effects; dial: it costs a bonus action, allows a save, and blindness has repeat saves.

rules.statement: A boggle can create an invisible rift in a visible frame or opening within 5 feet, no more than 10 feet across; it connects to a point within 30 feet that it sees or specifies by direction and distance. Only the boggle can use it, and it lasts until the end of the boggle's next turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Boggle — Dimensional Rift (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: an opening links two nearby points for passage; dial: the boggle must be adjacent to a suitable frame, only it can use the rift, and it expires next turn.

rules.statement: A creature whose soul bonds to a person with a hate-filled heart during a failed lich ritual forms a boneclaw enslaved to that master's wishes. It can be destroyed only while its master lives and remains evil; if destroyed while the master lives, it reforms with full hit points in 1d10 hours within 1 mile of the master.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Boneclaw — description; Rejuvenation (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a soul bond creates a subordinate that returns after destruction; dial: the bond depends on the master's evil and life, and reformation takes 1d10 hours.

rules.statement: When a creature other than a demon starts its turn within 30 feet of a bulezau, it makes a DC 13 Constitution save, taking 1d6 necrotic damage on a failure.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Bulezau — Rotting Presence, p. 67 (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: affects nearby non-demons; dial: set the 30-foot radius and damage; the bulezau’s presence brings ongoing decay.

rules.statement: A creature hit by a bulezau’s tail must make a DC 13 Constitution save against disease; on failure it is poisoned until the disease ends, and repeats the save every 24 hours. A success ends the disease; each failed repeat reduces its hit point maximum by 1d8, and reaching zero this way kills it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Bulezau — Barbed Tail, p. 67 (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: disease persists after the strike; dial: use the listed save interval and hit-point-maximum loss; the worsening reflects the creature’s rot.

rules.statement: A cadaver collector’s paralyzing breath fills a 30-foot cone; creatures in it that fail a DC 18 Constitution save are paralyzed for up to 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of their turns to end the effect on themselves.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Cadaver Collector — Paralyzing Breath, p. 68 (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the breath affects a cone; dial: use its save DC, duration, and repeat-save timing; the paralysis comes from the collector’s incapacitating gas.

rules.statement: After a short or long rest, a cadaver collector can summon 1d4 spirits of creatures it has slain into empty spaces within 15 feet. They act on its initiative after it, fight until destroyed, and vanish if the collector is destroyed.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Cadaver Collector — Summon Specters, p. 68 (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ability is limited by a rest and the collector’s prior kills; dial: choose the number by the stated die; the spirits are enslaved to their collector.

rules.statement: A canoloth prevents other creatures from teleporting to or from a space within 60 feet; an attempted teleport involving that area is wasted.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Canoloth — Dimensional Lock, p. 69 (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lock applies within 60 feet; dial: decide which teleport attempts enter the area; the canoloth’s guarding field denies escape or intrusion.

rules.statement: A canoloth’s tongue can hit one target within 30 feet; if the target is Medium or smaller, it is grappled (escape DC 15), pulled up to 30 feet toward the canoloth, and restrained until the grapple ends. The canoloth can hold only one target this way.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Canoloth — Tongue, p. 69 (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: only one eligible target can be held; dial: use the escape DC and pull distance; the tongue functions as a physical restraint.

rules.statement: A catoblepas’s stench forces other creatures starting their turn within 10 feet to make a DC 16 Constitution save or be poisoned until their next turn. On a success, the creature is immune to any catoblepas’s stench for 1 hour.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Catoblepas — Stench, p. 71 (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a short-range effect that repeats by turn; dial: apply the one-hour immunity after a successful save; the foul creature’s odor poisons nearby beings.

rules.statement: A catoblepas’s death ray targets one creature it can see within 30 feet, which makes a DC 16 Constitution save: it takes 8d8 necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success. If it fails by 5 or more, it takes 64 damage instead; if the ray reduces it to zero hit points, it dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Catoblepas — Death Ray, p. 71 (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one visible target and a recharge; dial: use the listed save and damage thresholds; the ray expresses the catoblepas’s lethal decay.

rules.statement: A cave fisher’s filament can adhere to a creature it touches at up to 60 feet, grappling it (escape DC 13); escape checks have disadvantage. The filament can be attacked (AC 15, 5 hit points; immune to poison and psychic damage), and breaks if the fisher uses this ability again; the fisher cannot use it while the grapple continues.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Cave Fisher — Adhesive Filament, p. 73 (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one filament grapple at a time; dial: set its range, escape disadvantage, and breakability as stated; sticky thread restrains prey but can be cut or replaced.

rules.statement: A clockwork can be assigned one malfunction; its listed d6 checks can cause a skipped turn, disadvantage on attacks, vulnerability to lightning, mistaken recognition of a creature, restricted movement, retreat, or incapacitation, depending on the malfunction.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Clockworks — Clockwork Malfunctions, p. 78 (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the malfunction’s stated trigger and die roll; dial: choose or roll a malfunction; imperfect mechanisms introduce unpredictable failures.

rules.statement: When an iron cobra’s bite hits a creature, it makes a DC 13 Constitution save; on a failure, roll a d6 for the result: confusion, paralysis until the end of its next turn, or 3d8 poison damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Clockwork Iron Cobra — Bite, p. 79 (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bite triggers one random effect only on a failed save; dial: resolve the d6 result; the cobra’s alchemical venom has variable effects.

rules.statement: A cloud giant smiling one can magically take the appearance and feel of a Beast or Humanoid it has seen, or return to its true form; its statistics other than size stay the same, its equipment is absorbed or borne by the new form, and death restores its true form.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Cloud Giant Smiling One — Change Shape, p. 82 (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: only a previously seen Beast or Humanoid can be copied; dial: select an eligible form; the transformation disguises the giant without changing most capabilities.

rules.statement: A smiling one can cast detect magic, fog cloud, light, and minor illusion at will; it can cast invisibility, silent image, suggestion, and tongues three times each per day, and gaseous form and major image once each per day. It uses Charisma for these spells, has save DC 15, and needs no material components.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Cloud Giant Smiling One — Spellcasting, p. 82 (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell uses are capped at the listed daily counts; dial: track each spell’s separate allowance; spellcasting is a bounded resource.

rules.statement: A corpse flower can contain up to nine Humanoid corpses; while inside, they have total cover from attacks and other effects originating outside. If the flower dies, the corpses can be removed.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Corpse Flower — Corpses (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: corpses remain protected inside the living plant; dial: capacity is capped at nine, reflecting its limited interior.

rules.statement: A creature that begins its turn within 10 feet of a corpse flower or one of its zombies must make a DC 14 Constitution save, unless it is a Construct or Undead. Failure poisons it until its next turn begins; success grants immunity to that flower’s stench for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Corpse Flower — Stench of Death (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: nearby creatures risk a temporary poison state; dial: one successful save suppresses repeat exposure for a day.

rules.statement: As a bonus action, the corpse flower can digest one corpse stored inside it to regain 2d10 hit points; the corpse is destroyed, while its equipment is expelled into the flower’s space.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Corpse Flower — Bonus Actions: Digest (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: stored remains can be converted into healing; dial: each use consumes a whole corpse and returns its gear.

rules.statement: As a bonus action, the corpse flower can animate one stored corpse as a zombie, appearing in an unoccupied space within 5 feet and acting immediately after the flower. The zombie is its ally but not under its control, and it carries the flower’s stench.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Corpse Flower — Bonus Actions: Reanimate (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: remains can become an allied undead creature; dial: the flower does not control the zombie, limiting command.

rules.statement: A swarm of cranium rats combines the minds and memories of its members, becoming more intelligent and gaining psionic abilities while the swarm persists. While above half its hit points, it can cast at will command, comprehend languages, and detect thoughts, plus confusion and dominate monster once each per day, without components (Intelligence; save DC 13).
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Swarm of Cranium Rats — Spellcasting (Psionics) (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the collective gains shared cognition and spells; dial: the spell suite is limited by the swarm’s health and daily uses.

rules.statement: Cranium rats and their swarms are immune to effects that would sense their emotions or read their thoughts, and to divination spells.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Cranium Rat; Swarm of Cranium Rats — Telepathic Shroud (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: mental and divinatory detection fails; dial: the protection applies to these creatures rather than granting general concealment.

rules.statement: A darkling that dies releases a flash of nonmagical light within 10 feet as its body and nonmetal, nonmagical possessions burn to ash; creatures there must make a DC 10 Constitution save or be blinded until the end of their next turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Darkling — Death Flash (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death produces a brief area hazard; dial: the light is nonmagical and destroys most carried possessions, reflecting the curse.

rules.statement: A darkling elder that dies releases magical light in a 10-foot radius; creatures in the area make a DC 11 Constitution save, taking 2d6 radiant damage and becoming blinded until the end of their next turn on a failure, or taking half damage without blindness on a success. Its body and nonmetal, nonmagical possessions burn to ash.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Darkling Elder — Death Burn (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death causes a damaging flash and brief blindness; dial: a save halves damage and avoids blindness.

rules.statement: A deep scion can change shape as a bonus action between a humanlike true form and a hybrid aquatic form; its other statistics remain the same except for speed, and its equipment does not change. Death forces it back to its true form.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Deep Scion — Bonus Actions: Change Shape (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the creature can switch forms quickly; dial: equipment is unchanged and death ends the transformation.

rules.statement: In hybrid form, a deep scion can emit a psychic screech once per short or long rest. Creatures within 30 feet must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom save or be stunned until the end of the scion’s next turn; while in water, the screech also sends its memories of the prior 24 hours to its master at any distance if both are in the same body of water.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Deep Scion — Psychic Screech (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a limited-use cry can stun nearby creatures and report memories; dial: the report requires water shared with the master and covers only the last day.

rules.statement: A warlock who breaks an evil patron’s bargain risks returning from death as a deathlock, an undead servant consumed by the urge to serve that patron. Its former ambitions give way to goals aligned with the patron’s interests.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Deathlocks — introductory text (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: breach of an evil bargain can impose posthumous service; dial: this is a risk, not an inevitable result, and the patron’s interests dictate the new purpose.

rules.statement: A derro savant can cast mage hand, message, and prestidigitation at will, and can cast invisibility, sleep, and spider climb once each per day, using Charisma (save DC 12).
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Derro Savant — Spellcasting (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the savant has a fixed spell repertoire; dial: three spells are daily-limited while the minor spells are unlimited.

rules.statement: A creature adjacent to a shield-bearing ally gains advantage on attack rolls and Dexterity saves while it remains within 5 feet of that ally.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Duergar Stone Guard — Phalanx Formation, p. 111 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply only while the spacing and shield condition hold; dial: none; the benefit depends on maintaining formation.

rules.statement: A drow arachnomancer can change into a Large spider for up to 1 hour, or return to its normal shape; it can still speak and cast spells, but worn and carried gear melds and provides no benefit. It returns to its normal form if it dies, and can use this change again after a short or long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Drow Arachnomancer — Change Shape, p. 99 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit the alternate body for the stated duration; dial: one use per short or long rest; the form limits equipment benefits.

rules.statement: A duergar can enlarge itself and its carried gear for 1 minute, becoming Large and gaining advantage on Strength checks and saves while doubling damage dice for Strength-based weapon attacks. If space prevents full size, it grows only as much as the available space permits; use recharges after a short or long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Duergar Soulblade — Enlarge, p. 110 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the specified size and strength changes; dial: one use per short or long rest; available space caps growth.

rules.statement: A duergar can become Tiny for 1 minute, shrinking its carried gear too; its weapon damage becomes 1 and it has disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saves that use Strength. It gains +5 to Dexterity (Stealth) checks and AC, and can take a bonus action to Hide on each of its turns; it can do this again after a short or long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Duergar Mind Master — Reduce, p. 109 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the full listed tradeoff; dial: one use per short or long rest; reduced size exchanges combat strength for concealment and defense.

rules.statement: A creature hit by webbing is restrained; it can use an action to make a DC 15 Strength check to break free. The web can instead be attacked (AC 10, 5 hit points), is vulnerable to fire, and is immune to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Drow Arachnomancer — Web, p. 99 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: restraint persists until escaped or the web is destroyed; dial: DC 15 and the web’s stated durability; escape costs an action.

rules.statement: A drow inquisitor’s death lance reduces a target’s hit point maximum by the necrotic damage it takes; this reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest, and the target dies if its maximum reaches 0.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Drow Inquisitor — Death Lance, p. 103 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reduce maximum hit points by damage actually taken; dial: ends after a long rest; the lasting injury can be fatal if it reaches zero.

rules.statement: A duergar’s invisibility lasts up to 1 hour, but ends if it attacks, forces a creature to save, or loses concentration; its worn and carried equipment is invisible with it. A mount sharing the effect also becomes visible immediately after it attacks.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Duergar Kavalrachni — Shared Invisibility, p. 107 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: conceal the duergar and its gear under the stated conditions; dial: up to 1 hour with interruption triggers; attacking reveals the mount.

rules.statement: A duergar mind master can force a visible creature within 60 feet to use its reaction, if available, either to make a weapon attack against another creature the duergar can see or to move up to 10 feet in a direction the duergar chooses. A creature that cannot be charmed is unaffected.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Duergar Mind Master — Mind Mastery, p. 109 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow only the specified reaction options; dial: DC 12 Intelligence save; the effect cannot compel creatures immune to charm.

rules.statement: A duergar warlord can have up to three allies within 120 feet who can hear it spend their reactions to make one weapon attack each. When a visible ally rolls an attack, the warlord can also add 1d6 to its d20 roll, but the ally takes 1d6 psychic damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Duergar Warlord — Call to Attack and Scouring Instruction, p. 112 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant the attack or roll bonus only under the stated triggers; dial: allies spend reactions, and the roll boost costs the ally 1d6 psychic damage.

rules.statement: A matron mother can give a visible ally within 30 feet a blessing that deals 2d6 psychic damage to that ally but grants advantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Drow Matron Mother — Lolth’s Fickle Favor, p. 105 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant advantage on the next attack roll within the deadline; dial: the recipient pays 2d6 psychic damage for the favor.

rules.statement: A matron mother can summon a glabrezu or yochlol into an unoccupied space within 60 feet once per day; it allies with her and cannot summon other demons. It stays for 10 minutes, until it or she dies, or until she dismisses it using an action.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Drow Matron Mother — Summon Servant, p. 105 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: create one allied demon under the stated limits; dial: once daily and at most 10 minutes; death or dismissal ends the service.

rules.statement: Within her lair, a matron mother can use a lair action on initiative count 20, losing ties, but cannot repeat the same option in consecutive rounds. One option reveals hostile creatures in the lair to her and prevents them from hiding from her or gaining the invisible condition until the next count 20.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: A Matron Mother’s Lair — Lair Actions, p. 103 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reveal threats throughout the lair for the stated interval; dial: initiative count 20 and no consecutive repeat; the effect requires the mother to be in her lair.

rules.statement: A matron mother can create a spectral web at a point she sees within 120 feet; creatures within 60 feet of that point make a DC 19 Dexterity save or become restrained for 1 minute. Each affected creature repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the restraint on a success.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: A Matron Mother’s Lair — Spectral Web, p. 103 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: restrain failed-save targets within the area; dial: DC 19, 1-minute maximum, repeat saves each turn; success ends the effect.

rules.statement: A duergar fused with a machine can leave it during a short rest, completing the escape when the rest ends, unless incapacitated.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Duergar Constructs, p. 113 (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: escape is possible after a short rest; dial: incapacitation prevents it; the cost is time spent resting.

rules.statement: A dybbuk can enter an intact corpse of a Large or smaller Beast or Humanoid within 5 feet, gaining 20 temporary hit points and taking on the corpse’s size. The possession ends when those temporary hit points are lost or the dybbuk ends it as a bonus action; it then appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the corpse.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Dybbuk, p. 114 (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: possession requires a nearby eligible corpse; dial: it lasts only while temporary hit points remain; the corpse is the vehicle and its loss ends the form.

rules.statement: While possessing a corpse, the dybbuk can use a bonus action to make it behave unnaturally; watching Beasts and Humanoids make a DC 12 Wisdom save or become frightened for 1 minute. Affected creatures can retry at each turn’s end, and a creature that succeeds is immune to this ability for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Dybbuk, Control Corpse, p. 114 (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: frightening behavior can impose fear; dial: a save, repeated recovery checks, and 24-hour immunity limit repeated exposure.

rules.statement: An eidolon that enters a sacred statue can animate it and use the statue’s statistics. The eidolon leaves if the statue reaches 0 hit points, it exits as a bonus action, or an effect turns it or forces it out; it reappears within 5 feet, and without an eidolon the statue is an object.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Eidolon, Sacred Animation and Sacred Statue, p. 115 (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a prepared statue can serve as the eidolon’s body; dial: damage, voluntary exit, or banishment ends the union.

rules.statement: After a long rest, an eladrin that is not incapacitated can choose a different seasonal aspect and use that aspect’s statistics. Damage, conditions, and other ongoing effects carry over to the new form.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Eladrin, Changeable Natures, p. 116 (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: seasonal change is available after a long rest; dial: incapacitation blocks the change, while injuries and ongoing effects persist.

rules.statement: A creature that starts its turn within 60 feet of an autumn or spring eladrin must make a DC 16 Wisdom save or be charmed for 1 minute. A successful save grants immunity to that eladrin presence for 24 hours; damage from the eladrin lets the charmed creature retry its save.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Autumn Eladrin, Enchanting Presence; Spring Eladrin, Joyful Presence, pp. 116–117 (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: proximity can charm; dial: a saving throw, duration, immunity, and a damage-triggered retry constrain the effect.

rules.statement: An elder brain detects creatures with Intelligence 4 or higher within 5 miles, learning their distance, direction, and Intelligence score but no other information. Certain protective magic prevents this detection.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Elder Brain, Creature Sense, p. 121 (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: detection covers a broad radius; dial: it reveals only limited facts and can be blocked by specified protections.

rules.statement: An elder brain can link psychically to an incapacitated creature it senses; while linked, it perceives what the creature senses. The target can try to break the link with an action and a successful DC 18 Charisma save, taking 3d6 psychic damage on success; distance beyond 5 miles also ends the link, and the brain can maintain up to ten links.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Elder Brain, Psychic Link, p. 120 (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the link grants remote perception; dial: incapacitation is required to establish it, and distance, a costly escape attempt, or the ten-link limit constrain it.

rules.statement: An elder brain’s influence alters the region within 5 miles: creatures feel watched, linked creatures hear intrusive whispers, and the brain can overhear telepathic conversations there. A conversation’s initiator can detect eavesdropping with a successful DC 18 Wisdom save, and the effects end if the brain dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Elder Brain, Regional Effects, p. 120 (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the brain’s influence reaches across its territory; dial: some effects require a psychic link or telepathic contact, and the entire field ends when the brain dies.

rules.statement: Elemental myrmidons are elementals bound by magic into ritually made plate armor; they have no memory of their former free existence and exist to follow their creators’ commands.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Elemental Myrmidons, p. 123 (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ritual armor binds an elemental to service; dial: the passage gives no release procedure, and loss of former memory is part of the binding’s cost.

rules.statement: For one month, each of three shields made from a flail snail’s intact shell can grant its wielder the snail’s Antimagic Shell trait. When that magic fades, the shield remains an exotic shield suitable for making a spellguard shield.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Using the Shell of a Flail Snail, p. 126 (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one shell yields up to three temporary magic shields; dial: the granted trait lasts only one month, after which the shields lose that magic.

rules.statement: When Fraz-Urb'luu is alive, the area around his lair warps: within 6 miles, Persuasion and Insight checks are disadvantaged while Deception and Performance checks are advantaged; thinking creatures see brief visions of dead companions, and paths within 6 miles twist and make navigation exceptionally difficult. If he dies, these regional effects fade over 1d10 days.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Fraz-Urb'luu — Regional Effects, p. 130 (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: effects extend over a fixed region; dial: a dangerous territory-wide distortion that ends gradually after its source dies.

rules.statement: Fraz-Urb'luu's cultists gain an improved ability to read others; as a bonus action, a cultist can locate illusions and hidden creatures within 15 feet. The quick detection is limited to that range.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Cultists of Fraz-Urb'luu, p. 130 (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the patron grants a bounded perceptual benefit; dial: supernatural awareness is restricted to nearby targets.

rules.statement: A gazer can serve a willing master as a familiar if the master is at least a 3rd-level spellcaster, forming a telepathic bond that lets the master sense through the gazer while they are within 1 mile. If the master physically harms it, the gazer ends the service and breaks the bond.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Variant: Gazer Familiar, p. 135 (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a willing familiar bond grants shared perception; dial: eligibility, a 1-mile limit, and harm-triggered termination constrain it.

rules.statement: Geryon's lair can make one creature he sees within 60 feet restrained for up to 1 minute on a failed DC 21 Wisdom save. The creature can end the restraint early by damaging one or more of its allies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Geryon's Lair Actions, pp. 136–137 (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a bounded lair effect imposes restraint; dial: the target can escape by paying a moral and tactical cost.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of Geryon's lair, freezing winds persist and howls can disrupt a rest: a creature finishing a short or long rest there must pass a DC 21 Wisdom save or gain no benefit from that rest. Sapient creatures also see portals to places they regard as safe, but passing through one always deposits the traveler somewhere in Stygia; the effects fade over 1d10 days after Geryon dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Geryon — Regional Effects, p. 137 (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lair creates a persistent regional hazard and false refuge; dial: apparent safe passage has an involuntary destination, and the effects linger after the lair's master dies.

rules.statement: A frost salamander native to the Frostfell can reach the Material Plane by wandering through planar gates; the passage gives no specific toll or operating limit for those gates.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Frost Salamander, p. 133 (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: planar gates connect the Frostfell to the Material Plane; dial: the passage specifies no cost or gate restrictions.

rules.statement: A gauth's random eye-ray attack selects three distinct rays by rolling three d6s and rerolling duplicates, then targets one to three creatures it can see within 120 feet. Its magic-draining ray can suppress one randomly selected magic item's properties until the start of the gauth's next turn and removes 1d4 charges from a charged item; single-use items are excluded.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Gauth — Eye Rays, p. 134 (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: random selection chooses distinct effects and a target set; dial: item suppression is brief, and charge loss makes it costly.

rules.statement: A gauth's paralysis ray can paralyze a target for 1 minute on a failed DC 14 Constitution save; the target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Gauth — Eye Rays, p. 134 (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed resistance imposes paralysis; dial: repeated saves provide an ongoing chance to end it.

rules.statement: A gauth's sleep ray can render a target unconscious for 1 minute on a failed DC 14 Wisdom save, but has no effect on Constructs or Undead. Damage or another creature spending an action to wake the target ends the sleep.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Gauth — Eye Rays, p. 134 (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed resistance imposes sleep on eligible targets; dial: damage or an ally's action ends it early.

rules.statement: A gazer's random eye-ray attack selects two distinct rays by rolling two d4s and rerolling duplicates, choosing one or two visible targets within 60 feet. Its telekinetic ray can push a Medium or smaller creature up to 30 feet directly away on a failed DC 12 Strength save, or move an unattended Tiny object up to 30 feet in any direction and finely manipulate it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Gazer — Eye Rays, p. 135 (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: random selection picks distinct rays; dial: telekinetic movement is limited by range, target size, and a saving throw for creatures.

rules.statement: If the gauth dies, its stored magical energy erupts: creatures within 10 feet make a DC 14 Dexterity save, taking 3d8 force damage on a failure or half damage on a success.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Gauth — Death Throes, p. 134 (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death releases a damaging burst; dial: the blast is confined to 10 feet and allows a saving throw for reduced damage.

rules.statement: A githyanki can cast listed psionic spells without components, using Intelligence and the stated save DC; each spell is limited by its at-will or per-day frequency. A githyanki can also teleport itself and carried equipment up to 30 feet to a visible, unoccupied space, with some versions recharging on a 4–6.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Githyanki Kith’rak; Githyanki Supreme Commander, pp. 140–142 (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell uses and teleport are limited by listed frequency or recharge; dial their availability because psionic exertion is the cost.

rules.statement: A supreme commander can cut the tether between an astrally projected target’s body and astral form instead of dealing damage on a critical hit. Its spellcasting is component-free and uses Intelligence, while its three legendary actions refresh at the start of its turn and can be spent only one at a time at the end of another creature’s turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Githyanki Supreme Commander, p. 142 (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the severing requires a critical hit against an astral body; dial its lethality because it ends the target’s tether rather than merely harming it.

rules.statement: In its Limbo lair, a githzerai anarch can create a lasting object from Limbo’s unformed substance with a 9th-level creation effect; it lasts until concentration ends, and moving more than 120 feet away breaks concentration. It can also try to move a visible object within 150 feet, with a Wisdom check and a size-based DC from 5 for Tiny to 25 for Huge or larger.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: An Anarch’s Lair, p. 143 (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: created objects persist only while concentration holds and within the stated range; dial their stability because Limbo’s substance is being shaped.

rules.statement: In Limbo, an anarch can spend 10 minutes shaping the unformed substance throughout a centered 5-mile area into chosen inanimate forms. It can stabilize objects created in Limbo and brought to the Material Plane while it remains alive; after its death, these effects end in 1d6 rounds and the forms unravel, then dissipate 1d6 rounds later.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: An Anarch’s Lair, p. 143 (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: shaping takes 10 minutes and stabilization depends on the anarch’s continued life; dial persistence because the place’s ordered form is sustained by its presence.

rules.statement: An enlightened githzerai’s temporal strike can, on a failed DC 16 Wisdom save, send a creature one round forward in time; it vanishes for that interval and returns to its former space, or the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied. The strike recharges on a 6.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Githzerai Enlightened, p. 144 (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect requires a failed save and has a one-round interval; dial its use by the recharge because temporal displacement removes the target briefly.

rules.statement: A gray render instinctively bonds to an intelligent creature, protects its master, and does not willingly harm that creature; when hurt, it may make a claw attack against a random creature within reach other than its master. Its bond can make it disruptive outside combat, since it may follow, dig, destroy property, or attack things unpredictably.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Gray Render, pp. 146–147 (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bond is to one master and the retaliatory target is random; dial the costs as persistent protection paired with poor control.

rules.statement: A grung’s direct skin contact can poison a grappler or other creature touching it for 1 minute after a failed DC 12 Constitution save. Once contact ends, the affected creature can repeat the save at the end of each turn to end the poison; grungs themselves are immune to poison and the poisoned condition.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Grung, p. 149 (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: poisoning requires failed resistance and ends on a successful repeat save; dial risk by the need for direct contact.

rules.statement: A grung that is not immersed in water for at least 1 hour during a day gains one exhaustion level at that day’s end; it can recover only through magic or by immersing itself for at least 1 hour. Grungs can breathe both air and water.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Grung, p. 149 (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the daily water requirement and recovery methods are fixed; dial its burden through the creature’s access to water.

rules.statement: A creature poisoned by a grung can also suffer a color-specific effect that lasts as long as that grung’s poison does: effects include forced noise or eating, charm and speaking Grung, restricted movement, fear of allies, or a compulsion to reach liquid or mud. The green effect restricts movement to climbing or standing jumps, and a flying target cannot act or react until it lands.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Variant: Grung Poison, pp. 150–151 (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the extra effect lasts only while the poison lasts; dial its form by the grung’s color and the target’s resulting compulsion or restriction.

rules.statement: A guard drake is produced through a several-day ritual requiring a chromatic dragon’s aid, 10 pounds of fresh scales from that dragon, fresh meat, and an iron cauldron; an egg emerges and hatches within hours. It imprints on the first creature to feed it, can be trained in two to three weeks, and cannot reproduce or supply scales for making more drakes.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Guard Drake, p. 151 (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: creation requires specific donor, ingredients, time, and feeding; dial access because the dragon’s scales and assistance are necessary costs.

rules.statement: When a hellfire engine’s weapon kills a creature, that creature’s soul rises from the River Styx as a lemure in Avernus in 1d4 hours. Revival before that happens prevents the outcome; afterward restoration requires a wish or killing the lemure and casting true resurrection on the original body, while constructs and devils are unaffected.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Hellfire Engine, p. 153 (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the change follows a killing blow and has a 1d4-hour window for ordinary revival; dial the severe recovery cost because death redirects the soul.

rules.statement: A hobgoblin devastator casting a damaging spell or one that forces saves can choose itself and any number of allies to be immune to that spell’s damage and automatically succeed on its required saves. Its listed spells use Intelligence, have DC 13, and have limited daily uses where stated.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Hobgoblin Devastator, p. 153 (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the protection applies only to allies the caster chooses and only to its qualifying spell; dial its scope by the spell and chosen group.

rules.statement: A dragon can invest a chosen kobold with a damage resistance tied to the dragon’s color; alternatively, the same abilities can appear innately in a kobold at hatching. The resistance is acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison, selected by the listed d10 ranges.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Kobold Dragonshield — Dragon’s Resistance (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the resistance follows the investing dragon’s color; dial: allow an innate version, with the reason that rare kobolds hatch with the gift.

rules.statement: A frightened or paralyzed dragonshield that failed a saving throw against the effect can retry that save at the start of its turn; on success, the effect ends for it and nearby kobolds within 30 feet. Kobolds helped this way gain advantage on their next attack roll.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Kobold Dragonshield — Heart of the Dragon (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: this recovery and rallying benefit applies only to the specified conditions and nearby kobolds; its cost is limited to a successful repeat save.

rules.statement: An inventor chooses or rolls a d8 to use one improvised weapon effect, and can use each option repeatedly. Effects include damage, persistent fire or acid, releasing insect swarms, or a skunk spray that can incapacitate a target for up to 1 minute with repeat saves to end it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Kobold Inventor — Weapon Invention (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use one listed improvised effect at a time; dial: require physical consumables and fragile devices, since these are makeshift weapons.

rules.statement: A dragonshield’s resistance type is determined by the dragon color that empowered it, while a scale sorcerer has innate arcane talent and uses Charisma to cast its listed spells (DC 12). The sorcerer can cast mage hand and prestidigitation at will, and charm person, fog cloud, and levitate twice per day each.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Kobold Scale Sorcerer — Spellcasting (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell access and frequency are fixed by the creature’s innate talent; the limited daily uses constrain stronger spells.

rules.statement: A kraken grants some of its worshippers power in return for service as priests. The kraken can speak through a priest after a short or long rest, frightening chosen listeners within 300 feet who fail a DC 14 Wisdom save for up to 1 minute; affected creatures can repeat the save at each turn’s end.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Kraken Priest — Voice of the Kraken (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the priest serves the kraken, which may possess the priest to speak; dial: the passage does not specify a precise bargain or additional price.

rules.statement: A korred’s head hair changes into the material used to cut it, and it can weave that hair into a rope it controls. As a bonus action, it can send a rope within 30 feet up to 20 feet to grapple a visible Large or smaller creature; a failed DC 13 Dexterity save leaves the target grappled and restrained, until freed by release, incapacitation or death of the korred, or escape with a DC 13 check.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Korred — Magical Hair; Command Hair (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the rope must be made from the korred’s hair and remains dependent on the korred; a destroyed rope has AC 20 and 20 hit points.

rules.statement: A rope of korred hair within its living maker’s control regains 1 hit point at the start of each of the maker’s turns while it has at least 1 hit point. At 0 hit points, the rope is destroyed.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Korred — Command Hair (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the living korred maintains the rope; its continued function is limited by the maker’s survival and the rope’s hit points.

rules.statement: Juiblex’s lair can create a slippery patch up to 10 feet square; creatures there or entering it must make a DC 21 Dexterity save or fall prone and slide 10 feet in a random direction. It can instead create sticky slime in a similarly sized area, requiring a DC 21 Strength save or restraining creatures; a restrained creature can use an action to escape with a DC 21 Strength check.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Juiblex’s Lair — Lair Actions (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the slime affects an area in Juiblex’s lair and persists for 1 hour or until burned away; dial: fire removes it after 1 round but deals 22 (4d10) fire damage to creatures starting their turn in burning slime.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of Juiblex’s lair, small bodies of water become highly acidic and corrode objects that touch them. Within 6 miles, Medicine and Survival checks have disadvantage and surfaces are often slick with clinging slime; these effects fade over 1d10 days after Juiblex dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Juiblex — Regional Effects (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effects are tied to proximity to Juiblex’s lair and fade after its death; their reach is limited to the stated radii.

rules.statement: A ki-rin’s lair can cause nearby creatures and plants to grow more vigorous, keep water pure, suppress curses, diseases, and poisons, and slow certain creatures’ falls so they take no falling damage, all within 3 miles. The regional effects end immediately when the ki-rin dies, except the invigorating effect on flora and fauna lasts 3 years.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Ki-Rin — Regional Effects (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each benefit is limited by the stated radius and creature exclusions; most effects end with the ki-rin’s death.
