rules.statement: A ki-rin can create permanent soft plant-based objects filling at most a 20-foot cube, temporary stone or metal objects filling at most a 2-foot cube, or permanent wood and similar hard plant-based objects filling at most a 10-foot cube. Objects appear in unoccupied spaces in the lair after 1 minute; the stone and metal objects vanish after 1 hour.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Ki-Rin — Lair Actions (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: creation is confined to the ki-rin’s lair and capped by volume; stone and metal creations are temporary.

rules.statement: A hobgoblin can teleport itself and carried or worn equipment up to 30 feet to a visible unoccupied space, but both its starting space and destination must be in dim light or darkness. It can also cast minor illusion and prestidigitation at will, and charm person, disguise self, and silent image once per day each using Intelligence (DC 12).
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Hobgoblin — Shadow Jaunt; Spellcasting (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: teleportation is restricted by visibility, distance, and dim-light or darkness at both ends; listed spell uses are limited as stated.

rules.statement: A kruthik gains advantage on an attack against a creature when a non-incapacitated ally is within 5 feet of that target. It can tunnel through solid rock at half its burrowing speed, leaving a tunnel whose diameter depends on its growth stage: 2½ feet when young, 5 feet as an adult, and 10 feet as a hive lord.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Kruthik; Adult Kruthik; Kruthik Hive Lord, pp. 169–170 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the listed proximity and digging limits; dial: tunnel size by growth stage; the cost is slower movement through rock.

rules.statement: A hive lord’s acid spray recharges on a roll of 5–6 and fills a 15-foot cone; creatures there make a DC 14 Dexterity save, taking 22 (4d10) acid damage on a failure or half on a success.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Kruthik Hive Lord, p. 169 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated recharge and save; dial: cone size or damage; the cost is an intermittent attack with a limited area.

rules.statement: A leucrotta can imitate Beast sounds and Humanoid voices it has heard; a listener identifies the imitation with a successful DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) check. At the start of a non-leucrotta, non-gnoll creature’s turn within 5 feet, it must make a DC 12 Constitution save or be poisoned until that turn ends; success grants immunity to all leucrotta stench for 1 hour.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Leucrotta, p. 170 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the check, radius, and short condition duration; dial: detection difficulty or immunity duration; the in-world hazard is close proximity to a foul creature.

rules.statement: A leviathan partially freezes after taking at least 50 cold damage during one turn; until the end of its next turn its speeds become 20 feet and its attack rolls have disadvantage. It can pass through spaces as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing and can enter and stop in a hostile creature’s space.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Leviathan, p. 171 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the damage threshold and one-turn impairment; dial: threshold or duration; cold damage is the cost that slows the creature.

rules.statement: A meazel can teleport itself, its gear, and a creature it is grappling up to 500 feet, but both endpoints must be in dim light or darkness and the destination must be a place it has seen. Any other creature transported is cursed for 1 hour or until ended by remove curse or greater restoration; while cursed, Undead and Shadowfell-native creatures within 300 feet can sense it, preventing it from hiding from them.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Meazel, p. 177 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated range, shadow requirement, and curse; dial: range or curse duration; darkness and exposure to predators constrain the escape.

rules.statement: If terror overwhelms a creature in the Feywild or where its influence is strong, one or more meenlocks may appear in nearby shadows; when multiple arise, a lair forms with one entrance and a central chamber. Up to four meenlocks can torment one incapacitated creature telepathically for an hour; if it remains incapacitated, it saves against DC 10 plus participating meenlocks, taking 10 (3d6) psychic damage on a failure or half on a success, and a Humanoid reduced to 0 hit points by this damage transforms into a meenlock under the DM’s control.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Meenlock; Telepathic Torment, p. 178 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the four-participant cap and hour-long torment; dial: save DC or transformation threshold; fear and prolonged helplessness are the in-world costs.

rules.statement: A merregon can redirect an attack-roll hit meant for another Fiend within 5 feet onto itself. It has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Merregon, p. 179 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the 5-foot protection range and Fiend-only target; dial: range or eligible allies; the bodyguard absorbs the hit.

rules.statement: A merrenoloth’s vessel can be magically kept on course to a named destination and prevented from sinking even with a breached hull; these effects fade 1d6 hours after the merrenoloth dies. While captaining a vessel, it can use one lair action at initiative count 20, choosing gale, propulsion that adds 30 feet of speed, or repairs restoring 22 (4d10) hit points; it cannot repeat the same option in consecutive rounds.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Merrenoloth, p. 180 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the vessel-bound benefits and their death-triggered decay; dial: duration or repair amount; the magic depends on the captain’s continued presence.

rules.statement: A mindwitness that receives a telepathic message can share it with up to seven other creatures it can see within 600 feet. Its telekinetic ray can move a creature that fails a DC 13 Strength save up to 30 feet and restrain it until the mindwitness’s next turn or until it is incapacitated; the ray can also move an unattended object of up to 300 pounds and finely manipulate it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Mindwitness, p. 181 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the seven-recipient and weight limits; dial: distance or capacity; line of sight and resistance checks constrain the effect.

rules.statement: A marut enforces a contract recorded on gold and placed in its chest until the terms are fulfilled, punishing any party that breaks the written terms; it follows the text rather than presumed intent, and lethal force is limited to what the contract requires, a complete breach, or an attack on the marut. It can also force a seen creature within 60 feet to make a DC 20 Charisma save or be banished to a teleportation circle in Sigil.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Marut; Plane Shift, p. 173 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enforce clear written terms and the stated banishment save; dial: penalties or destination; parties pay for the recorded agreement and risk literal enforcement.

rules.statement: A maurezhi that consumes a slain Humanoid’s corpse over about 10 minutes takes its appearance as it was in life; the disguise lasts 1d6 days and gradually decays, then falls away. Its bite reduces a Humanoid’s Charisma by 1d4 until a short or long rest; if this reduces Charisma to 0, the victim dies and rises as a ghoul after 24 hours unless revived or destroyed.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Maurezhi, p. 175 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the corpse-eating requirement and listed durations; dial: disguise duration or ability loss; acquiring the form requires consuming a body.

rules.statement: A meazel or meenlock can teleport only between unoccupied spaces in dim light or darkness: the meazel’s range is 500 feet to a previously seen place, while the meenlock’s is 30 feet and need not be in sight. A meenlock’s shadow teleport recharges on 5–6.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Meazel, p. 177; Meenlock, p. 178 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the shadow-only endpoints and different ranges; dial: distance or recharge; suitable darkness and, for the meazel, prior knowledge limit travel.

rules.statement: When the molydeus fails a saving throw, it may choose to succeed instead, up to three times per day; it also has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Molydeus — Legendary Resistance; Magic Resistance (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the listed three uses and magical-save advantage; dial: reduce either defense for a less resilient monster.

rules.statement: On a weapon attack roll of 20, the molydeus decapitates a target with a head that cannot survive without it, unless the target took no damage, has legendary actions, or is Huge or larger; those exempt larger or legendary targets instead take 6d8 extra force damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Molydeus — Demonic Weapon (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the specified critical-hit result and exclusions; dial: remove instant death because the weapon is bestowed by a demon lord.

rules.statement: Once per day, a molydeus can try to summon its choice of 1d6 babaus, 1d4 chasmes, or one marilith, with a 50 percent chance of success. The demon appears in an empty space within 60 feet of a molydeus ally, cannot summon other demons, and remains for 1 minute, until it or the molydeus dies, or until dismissed by the molydeus as an action.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Variant: Demon Summoning — Summon Demon (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the once-daily 50-percent chance and short duration; dial: alter the summoned demon or frequency to reflect the summoner's threat.

rules.statement: A morkoth can make its lair water breathable and clear, or restore it to ordinary water; the change takes effect after 1 minute and requires no action.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Regional Effects — Alter Water (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the delayed change only within the lair; dial: broaden the area if the island's influence is stronger.

rules.statement: A morkoth knows when any creature or object newly arrives on its island or in its sanctum, and as an action can locate one creature or object anywhere on the island.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Regional Effects — Locate Creatures and Objects (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: arrival awareness and one active location per action; dial: restrict detection when visitors have suitable protective magic.

rules.statement: A visitor who has been on the island for less than a year must make a DC 10 Intelligence save whenever it finishes a short or long rest; on a failure, one possession it chooses is misplaced nearby and concealed. A DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check can find it for a short time, but if it remains unrecovered for 1 hour it ends up in the morkoth's lair, where it is easy for the owner to notice and recover.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Regional Effects — Lost Possessions (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the save at each rest and retain the one-year limit; dial: reduce the frequency or duration for a milder island effect.

rules.statement: A visible entrance to a morkoth's lair can exert an enchantment, which the morkoth can switch on or off while in its lair and not incapacitated. A creature within 30 feet that can see the entrance must make a DC 15 Wisdom save or use its movement on each turn to approach the morkoth by the most direct route; the effect ends if the creature sees the morkoth and succeeds on a repeat save, or succeeds on a repeat save at a turn's end or after taking damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Regional Effects — Supernatural Lure (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the 30-foot trigger and repeated escape saves; dial: widen the trigger only if the lair's enchantment is meant to dominate its surroundings.

rules.statement: A creature killed by a nabassu can have its soul devoured if it is neither a Construct nor Undead and died within the last hour; the nabassu must remain within 5 feet of the corpse for 10 minutes. It gains hit dice and stronger attacks for 6 days, while the devoured creature can be restored only by a wish spell.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Nabassu — Devour Soul (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require a recent eligible corpse and the full 10-minute process; dial: adjust the temporary gains to reflect the victim's strength.

rules.statement: A creature slain by a narzugon's hellfire lance has its soul sent to the River Styx and, 1d4 hours later, it rises in Avernus as a lemure. If it is not revived before that change, only a wish spell or killing the lemure and casting true resurrection on the original body restores it; Constructs and devils are unaffected.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Narzugon — Hellfire Lance (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the delay and narrow restoration routes; dial: change the soul's destination or recovery cost to suit the setting's afterlife.

rules.statement: Infernal tack binds a nightmare to the creature wearing its spurs until that wearer dies or the tack is removed. As an action, the wearer can summon the nightmare, which appears within 20 feet at the start of the wearer's next turn, acts as an ally on the wearer's initiative, and remains for 1 day, until either dies, or until dismissed as an action; a slain nightmare reforms in the Nine Hells within 24 hours and can then be summoned again.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Magic Item: Infernal Tack (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require evil alignment and retain the forced service and removal/death endpoints; dial: make the nightmare more cooperative only if it develops loyalty.

rules.statement: A neogi can force one visible creature within 30 feet to make a DC 14 Wisdom save; failure charms it for 1 day, or until the neogi dies or is more than 1 mile away. The target obeys the neogi, cannot take reactions, and can communicate telepathically with it at up to 1 mile; whenever damaged, it may repeat the save to end the effect.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Neogi / Neogi Master — Enslave (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the daily duration, range break, and damage-triggered escape save; dial: shorten the control period to reduce the cost of failed resistance.

rules.statement: On each turn, a mouth of Grolantor moves all its movement toward the nearest creature or other thing it perceives as food, then rolls 1d10 to determine its action: results 1–3 make three attacks against one random nearby creature, 4–5 attack each creature in reach or itself if none are there, 6–7 bite one random nearby creature or become stunned until its next turn if none are there, and 8–10 bite and make two attacks against one random nearby creature; when the specified attacks have no target, it instead gains advantage on attack rolls until its next turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Mouth of Grolantor — Mouth of Chaos (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: roll the d10 each turn and preserve the random targeting; dial: change outcome weights to tune how dangerous the loss of control is.

rules.statement: When a goblin-hosting nilbog is targeted by an attempt to damage it, the attacker must first succeed on a DC 12 Charisma save or become charmed until the end of its next turn and spend its action praising the nilbog; that charm prevents the attacker from dealing damage, except through the nilbog's damage-negating reaction. Separately, the free nilbog spirit can attempt to possess a goblin on initiative count 20: the goblin makes a DC 15 Charisma save, and on failure uses the nilbog statistics; on success, it cannot be targeted by that spirit for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Nilbog — Nilbogism (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the separate save DCs and 24-hour failed-possession immunity; dial: change the host eligibility or defense if possession should be rarer.

rules.statement: A creature other than a devil that starts its turn within 20 feet of one or more nupperibos must make a DC 11 Constitution save or take 5 (2d4) acid damage; when affected by two or more such clouds, it makes the save with disadvantage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Nupperibo — Cloud of Vermin (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the aura each turn; dial: the 20-foot reach and save keep it bounded; in-world, vermin torment nearby non-devils.

rules.statement: In the Nine Hells, a nupperibo can track without error any creature damaged by a nupperibo’s vermin cloud during the previous 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Nupperibo — Driven Tracker (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the trace lasts 24 hours; dial: only cloud-damaged prey qualifies; in-world, the vermin mark a meal.

rules.statement: When an adult or elder oblex’s memory-draining attack succeeds, the target takes psychic damage and is memory drained until it completes a short or long rest, or receives heal or greater restoration. While drained, it subtracts a d4 from attack rolls and ability checks; repeated drain increases the die size stepwise, and reaching a d20 instead makes the target unconscious for 1 hour, ending the effect.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Adult Oblex and Elder Oblex — Eat Memories (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: impose the stated penalty and duration; dial: escalation stops at unconsciousness and specified remedies end it; in-world, stolen memories leave the victim impaired.

rules.statement: An oblex that drains a target learns its languages and gains all its skill proficiencies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Adult Oblex and Elder Oblex — Eat Memories (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: copy capabilities from a drained target; dial: only languages and skill proficiencies transfer; in-world, the oblex consumes memories.

rules.statement: An adult oblex can cast charm person, detect thoughts, and hypnotic pattern three times each per day, using Intelligence and requiring no spell components; charm person is cast as a 5th-level spell.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Adult Oblex — Spellcasting (Psionics) (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow the listed casts; dial: each is limited to three uses daily; in-world, psionic power expresses the oblex’s mind-hunting nature.

rules.statement: An elder oblex can cast charm person and detect thoughts at will, and can cast dimension door, dominate person, hypnotic pattern, and telekinesis three times each per day, using Intelligence without spell components; charm person is cast as a 5th-level spell.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Elder Oblex — Spellcasting (Psionics) (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enable the listed spells; dial: stronger effects have daily limits; in-world, accumulated memories empower the elder.

rules.statement: An adult oblex can extrude up to 1d4 + 1 replicas of creatures whose memories it has stolen. Each replica looks, feels, and sounds like its model, but has a faint sulfur smell; it shares the oblex’s space occupancy, remains tethered by damage-immune slime out to 120 feet, and vanishes if no passage at least 1 inch wide connects it to the oblex.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Adult Oblex — Sulfurous Impersonation (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: create memory-based replicas; dial: number, range, passage, and tether bound them; in-world, the slime body remains physically connected.

rules.statement: An elder oblex can extrude 2d6 + 1 such replicas, with the same sensory resemblance and tether rules as an adult oblex.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Elder Oblex — Sulfurous Impersonation (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit multiple replicas; dial: the tether and passage requirement constrain separation; in-world, each apparent person remains part of the oblex.

rules.statement: An oinoloth can teleport itself and its worn or carried equipment up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Oinoloth — Teleport (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow short-range relocation; dial: 60 feet and visible destination constrain it; in-world, the fiend uses its magical mobility.

rules.statement: An oinoloth can blight a 30-foot-radius area centered on itself for 24 hours. Plants wither and die there, and creatures entering or starting there must make a DC 16 Constitution save or take 14 (4d6) poison damage and become poisoned; a successful save grants immunity to this effect for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Oinoloth — Bringer of Plagues (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the blight and entry/start saves; dial: the field lasts 24 hours and a successful save protects for that span; in-world, the fiend spreads pestilence.

rules.statement: A retriever follows one quarry assigned by its master: a personally known creature or object, or a previously seen general type. It always knows the quarry’s direction and distance while both are on the same plane, and always knows its master’s location; it can have only one quarry at a time.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Retriever — Faultless Tracker (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: provide tracking information; dial: only one assigned quarry and same-plane precision; in-world, the construct is programmed and directed by its master.

rules.statement: A retriever can cast plane shift three times per day, taking only itself and up to one incapacitated creature, which counts as willing, or cast web three times per day; it uses Wisdom and needs no material components.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Retriever — Spellcasting (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit the listed travel or restraint spell; dial: plane shift is limited to three daily uses and one incapacitated passenger; in-world, the construct’s mission enables capture and return.

rules.statement: A creature other than a demon that begins its turn within 30 feet of one or more rutterkins must make a DC 11 Wisdom save; with six or more nearby, it makes the save at disadvantage. On a failure it is frightened of them for 1 minute and also restrained, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect; on a success it is immune to all rutterkins’ crippling fear for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Rutterkin — Immobilizing Fear (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the fear field triggers each turn in range; dial the group-size disadvantage threshold if crowd control is too strong.

rules.statement: A rutterkin’s bite can infect a creature that fails a DC 13 Constitution save, poisoning it. The target can repeat the save at the end of each long rest to end the poison; if it reaches 0 hit points while poisoned this way, it dies and becomes a living manes, and only a wish spell can undo that transformation.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Rutterkin — Bite (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the lethal transformation and wish-only reversal; dial the disease’s lethality if long-term infection is too costly for play.

rules.statement: A sea spawn can breathe air and water, but must submerge in the sea for at least 1 minute each day or begin suffocating.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Sea Spawn — Limited Amphibiousness (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the daily sea visit is a survival requirement; dial the interval or setting-specific sea requirement to fit the campaign.

rules.statement: A sea spawn’s piscine anatomy attack is determined by a d6: 1–2 bites, 3–4 uses poison quills, and 5–6 uses a tentacle. A quill hit deals 3 (1d6) poison damage and requires a DC 12 Constitution save or the target is poisoned for 1 minute, with a save at the end of each turn to end it; a tentacle hit can grapple a Medium or smaller target (escape DC 12), and cannot be used on another target until that grapple ends.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Sea Spawn — Piscine Anatomy (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: anatomy selection remains random and the grapple occupies the tentacle; dial random selection if predictable abilities better suit the creature.

rules.statement: A shadow mastiff in dim light or darkness can become invisible, including its carried gear, as a bonus action. The invisibility ends when it attacks, is incapacitated, enters bright light, or uses a bonus action to end it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Shadow Mastiff — Shadow Blend (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: darkness enables concealment, while attack or bright light breaks it; dial the lighting conditions if stealth dominates encounters.

rules.statement: A shoosuva is bonded to a particular worshiper of Yeenoghu and fights alongside that master; it is granted to an especially powerful worshiper, usually after a war band’s great victory.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Shoosuva (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the demon serves one specific worshiper and is a status-bearing gift; dial the bond’s duration or obligations for campaign needs.

rules.statement: A shoosuva’s stinger hit requires a DC 14 Constitution save or the target is poisoned and paralyzed. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending both effects on a success.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Shoosuva — Tail Stinger (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one failed save imposes both conditions until a successful end-of-turn save; dial the save DC or duration if paralysis is overly restrictive.

rules.statement: A sibriex’s corruption aura extends 30 feet; vegetation in it withers, the ground is difficult terrain for other creatures, and creatures beginning their turns there must make a DC 20 Constitution save or take 14 (4d6) poison damage. A creature that succeeds is immune to that sibriex’s aura for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Sibriex — Contamination (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the aura continually harms and alters terrain; dial its radius or immunity interval to manage environmental pressure.

rules.statement: A sibriex can target up to three visible creatures within 120 feet with its warping effect; each makes a DC 20 Constitution save, becoming immune to that sibriex’s effect on a success. On a failure the target is poisoned and gains exhaustion, repeats the save at the start of each turn, and each failure adds another exhaustion level; three successes end the poison and remove exhaustion caused by it. At six exhaustion levels the target dies and becomes a manes under the sibriex’s control; only a wish spell can undo the bodily transformation.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Sibriex — Warp Creature (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repeated failures escalate toward death and controlled transformation; dial the escalating exhaustion or wish-only reversal for a less lethal campaign.

rules.statement: A creature can willingly undergo permanent flesh warping while within 30 feet of a sibriex; the painful process takes at least 1 hour, after which a percentile roll or chosen table result determines its bodily change. If warping occurs as part of the sibriex’s effect, the table result lasts only while that effect lasts, unless the creature becomes a manes, when it is permanent.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Variant: Flesh Warping (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: voluntary permanent change costs an hour of painful exposure; dial random versus chosen results to balance player agency and unpredictability.

rules.statement: A skulk can be summoned from the Shadowfell by ritual and must obey the summoner for 30 days; while bound, it is visible and resembles its master vaguely. It cannot return to the Shadowfell before it dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Skulk (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ritual grants a month of compulsory service but traps the summoned creature until death; dial the service term or return restriction to suit the ritual’s cost.

rules.statement: A shadow mastiff alpha’s howl affects Beasts and Humanoids within 300 feet: a failed DC 11 Wisdom save causes fear for 1 minute, with a repeat save at the end of each turn to end it. A creature that succeeds, or later ends the fear, is immune to any shadow mastiff’s howl for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Shadow Mastiff Alpha — Terrifying Howl (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the broad-range fear has a repeat save and day-long immunity; dial the range or duration if it overwhelms encounter play.

rules.statement: At the start of its turn, a spawn of Kyuss regains 10 hit points if it has at least 1 hit point and is in neither sunlight nor running water. Acid, fire, or radiant damage prevents this regeneration at the start of its next turn; if it starts a turn at 0 hit points and does not regenerate, it is destroyed.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Spawn of Kyuss — Regeneration (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the damage types or healing amount; regeneration is limited by environmental exposure and recent damage.

rules.statement: A Kyuss spawn can launch a worm at a visible Humanoid within 10 feet; a DC 11 Dexterity save avoids attachment. An attached worm can be killed normally or scraped off with an action; otherwise it burrows in at the end of the target’s next turn, then deals 2d6 necrotic damage at the end of each of the target’s turns, up to 10d6 per turn from all worms.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Spawn of Kyuss — Burrowing Worm (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial save DC, damage, and cap; infestation imposes escalating harm with a chance to remove the worm before it burrows.

rules.statement: If a worm-infested target reaches 0 hit points, it dies and rises 10 minutes later as a spawn of Kyuss. An effect that cures disease or removes a curse makes all worms infesting the target wither and removes the spawn’s Burrowing Worm action if used on the spawn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Spawn of Kyuss — Burrowing Worm; Worms (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the transformation delay and qualifying cures; infection can convert a victim, but disease- or curse-removal counters it.

rules.statement: A cultist with Borem’s Embrace can, once per day, touch a creature within 5 feet; a failed DC 15 Dexterity save coats it in mud for up to 1 minute. While coated, the creature’s speed is halved, it cannot take reactions, and it takes 3d6 fire damage at the start of each turn; water immersion, the cultist’s incapacitation, or the cultist’s death ends the effect.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Elder Evil Blessings — Cult of Borem (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the daily use, save, and duration; the cult gift binds a target temporarily and has clear escape conditions.

rules.statement: When the star spawn hulk takes psychic damage, each creature within 10 feet of it takes that damage instead, and the hulk takes none. Magic cannot discern the hulk’s thoughts or location.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Star Spawn Hulk — Psychic Mirror (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the transfer radius; psychic attacks are redirected to nearby creatures, while the hulk is shielded from magical detection.

rules.statement: When a larva mage reaches 0 hit points, it breaks apart into a swarm of insects in the same space; unless the swarm is destroyed, the mage reforms from it after 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Star Spawn Larva Mage — Return to Worms (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the recovery time or whether the swarm can be destroyed; defeating the mage requires dealing with its surviving remains.

rules.statement: When a larva mage uses Plague of Worms, each non-star-spawn creature within 10 feet must make a DC 19 Dexterity save or take 5d8 necrotic damage and become blinded and restrained. Affected creatures take another 5d8 damage at the start of each of the mage’s turns and can repeat the save at the end of each of their turns to end the effect.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Star Spawn Larva Mage — Plague of Worms (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the radius, damage, and save DC; the damaging restraint affects nearby non-star-spawn and can be ended by repeated saves.

rules.statement: When a creature within 20 feet of the larva mage fails a saving throw, the mage gains 10 temporary hit points.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Star Spawn Larva Mage — Feed on Weakness (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the trigger range and temporary hit points; an opponent’s failed defense strengthens the mage.

rules.statement: A star spawn seer can move through creatures and objects as though they were difficult terrain without provoking opportunity attacks; each creature it passes through takes 1d10 psychic damage, at most once per turn. If it ends its turn inside an object, it takes 1d10 force damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Star Spawn Seer — Out-of-Phase Movement (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the movement damage; phasing enables passage through obstacles but risks harm if the seer remains inside one.

rules.statement: When a seer uses Collapse Distance on a visible creature within 30 feet, the target makes a DC 19 Wisdom save. On a failure, the target and its carried equipment teleport up to 60 feet to a space the seer can see, and creatures within 10 feet of the target’s former space take 6d12 psychic damage; on a success, the target instead takes 3d12 psychic damage and is not moved.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Star Spawn Seer — Collapse Distance (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the range and damage; a failed save relocates the target and harms creatures left near its starting point.

rules.statement: A storm giant quintessent in its lair can disperse into the surrounding storm; while dispersed it cannot be targeted by attacks, spells, or other effects and can take only lair actions. At the start of any of its turns it can reform at a location it chooses within its lair; it cannot disperse outside its lair or while magic is suppressing the storm.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Storm Giant Quintessent — One with the Storm (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the lair boundary or suppression condition; the transformation grants protection but confines the giant to its storm and limits its actions.

rules.statement: A stone cursed’s claw hit forces a creature to make a DC 12 Constitution save or begin turning to stone and become restrained until the end of its next turn. The target then saves again; success ends the effect, while failure petrifies it for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Stone Cursed — Petrifying Claws (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the save DC or petrification duration; the two-stage effect gives the target a brief restrained phase and a second chance to resist.

rules.statement: A creature that contacts a single rot grub must make a DC 10 Constitution save or become poisoned as the grub burrows in; it takes 1d6 poison damage at the end of each turn. Whenever it takes fire damage it can repeat the save, ending the effect on a success; if it ends a turn at 0 hit points while poisoned this way, it dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Swarm of Rot Grubs — Single Rot Grub (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the save DC or damage; fire provides a repeated chance to end the infestation before it kills the host.

rules.statement: A steel predator can sense its designated target’s location across planar boundaries, but the reading is accurate only to within 1,000 yards; it must use sight and smell to close the remaining distance. It can use plane shift on itself up to three times per day.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Steel Predator — description; Spellcasting (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial detection precision or daily travel uses; the construct can pursue across planes but needs ordinary tracking to pinpoint its prey.

rules.statement: A ritual or demonic patron’s secret can transform a subject into a tanarukk Fiend, corrupting the subject; the resulting creature is volatile and may need imprisonment outside combat.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Tanarukk (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation requires a specific ritual or secret; dial: make the process repeatable or costly; in-world, the change corrupts the subject and creates a dangerous ally.

rules.statement: When a creature hits Titivilus with a melee attack, he can use his reaction to make one bite or sword attack against that attacker with advantage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: TITIVILUS — Unbridled Fury (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one retaliatory attack per reaction; dial: change its frequency or available attacks; in-world, his response is tied to being struck in melee.

rules.statement: Titivilus can charm one visible creature within 60 feet for 1 minute on a failed DC 21 saving throw; if he damages the charmed creature, it can try the save again, and a creature that succeeds is immune to this ability for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: TITIVILUS — Twisting Words (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed save binds the target briefly, with damage offering another save; dial: adjust duration or immunity; in-world, his manipulative speech has limits.

rules.statement: Titivilus can attempt to direct a creature already charmed by him within 60 feet: on a failed DC 21 Charisma save, he chooses how it acts during its next turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: TITIVILUS — Legendary Actions, Corrupting Guidance (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control lasts only for the target’s next turn and requires a failed save; dial: adjust range or duration; in-world, the target must already be under his influence.

rules.statement: A trapper can alter its outer color and texture to blend into stone, earth, or wood; if motionless on a floor, wall, or ceiling when combat begins, it has advantage on initiative, and an observer that has not seen it move must pass a DC 18 Investigation check to identify it as a creature.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: TRAPPER — False Appearance; TRAPPER description (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: concealment depends on a matching surface and stillness; dial: vary the check or surfaces; in-world, the trapper cannot copy every kind of terrain.

rules.statement: When a trapper grapples a Large or smaller creature with its smothering attack, the target is restrained, blinded, deprived of air, and takes 13 bludgeoning plus 3 acid damage at the start of each of its turns; the trapper can hold only one creature this way.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: TRAPPER — Smother (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one target at a time, with ongoing damage while held; dial: change the size limit or damage; in-world, the trapper’s body can wrap around only one prey creature.

rules.statement: A rot troll’s end-of-turn aura deals 11 necrotic damage to each creature within 5 feet, unless the troll took acid or fire damage since the end of its previous turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: RoTTROLL — Rancid Degeneration (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a nearby necrotic hazard recurs each turn and acid or fire suppresses it; dial: change radius or damage; in-world, the emanation reflects the troll’s necrotic corruption.

rules.statement: When a creature comes within 5 feet of russet mold, it must make a DC 13 Constitution save or become poisoned, taking 7 poison damage at the start of each turn; it can repeat the save at each turn’s end to end the effect.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Russet Mold — Effects of the Mold (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: proximity triggers exposure and repeated saves can end it; dial: alter the range or damage; in-world, the mold releases spores when approached.

rules.statement: If russet mold kills a Beast, Giant, or Humanoid, one or more vegepygmies emerge from the corpse after 24 hours, with the number determined by the corpse’s size: one Small, two Medium, four Large, eight Huge, or sixteen Gargantuan.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Russet Mold — Effects of the Mold (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: only specified creature types produce growths, after a day, in size-based quantities; dial: change eligibility or yield; in-world, the mold uses dead bodies as a means of propagation.

rules.statement: A vargouille can curse an incapacitated Humanoid within 5 feet that fails a DC 12 Charisma save; the target loses 1 Charisma each hour until it reaches 2 and dies, becoming a vargouille, but sunlight or a daylight spell pauses the progress, and suitable magic can end the curse and undo its changes.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: VARGOUILLE — Abyssal Curse (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the curse advances hourly but sunlight pauses it and magic can reverse it; dial: change the countdown or remedies; in-world, the curse’s bodily transformation has a gradual, interruptible course.

rules.statement: An ulitharid senses the distance, direction, and Intelligence score of each creature with Intelligence 4 or higher within 2 miles, but learns nothing else about them; mind blank, nondetection, or similar magic blocks this sense.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: ULITHARID — Creature Sense (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sensing is limited to location and Intelligence and can be blocked by specified magic; dial: change range or detail; in-world, the ability detects minds without revealing their other qualities.

rules.statement: If an elder brain links psychically with an ulitharid, it can link to creatures the ulitharid senses; those links end if the creature is beyond both telepathy ranges, while the ulitharid’s link to the elder brain works across any distance on the same plane and can be ended by the ulitharid when more than 5 miles away.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: ULITHARID — Psionic Hub (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the relay depends on an elder-brain link and ordinary creature links have a range limit; dial: adjust ranges or the ulitharid’s ability to sever its link; in-world, the connection relies on a shared psionic network.

rules.statement: Warlocks of the Archfey, Fiend, and Great Old One receive magical power through pacts with beings associated respectively with the Feywild, the Lower Planes, and strange distant realms. The passage gives no pact price or obligation, and notes that some warlocks oppose the beings that empower them.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Warlocks; Warlock of the Archfey; Warlock of the Fiend; Warlock of the Great Old One (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: pact supplies magical power; dial: patron terms and repayment are unspecified; in-world cost: no particular cost is established here.

rules.statement: The xvart warlock of Raxivort can cast its listed at-will spells and can cast burning hands and invisibility once each per day, using Charisma (save DC 11) and requiring no material components. When it reduces an enemy to 0 hit points, it gains 4 temporary hit points.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Xvart Warlock of Raxivort (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: the warlock's magic and temporary vitality work as stated; dial: spells have the listed daily limits; in-world cost: the passage states no further payment.

rules.statement: A vegepygmy can release a 5-foot-radius toxic spore cloud once per day, spreading around corners. Each non-Plant creature in it makes a DC 12 Constitution save or becomes poisoned, takes 2d8 poison damage at the start of each turn, and can repeat the save at each turn's end to end the effect on itself.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Vegepygmy, Spores (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: the cloud affects non-Plants in its area; dial: it is limited to once per day and can be ended by a successful repeat save; in-world cost: exposure brings recurring poison damage.

rules.statement: A thorny vegepygmy regains 5 hit points at the start of its turn, but cold, fire, or necrotic damage prevents this regeneration at the start of its next turn. It dies if it starts a turn at 0 hit points without regenerating.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Thorny Vegepygmy, Regeneration (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: regeneration restores the stated amount; dial: specified damage interrupts it for one turn; in-world cost: a failure to regenerate at 0 hit points is fatal.

rules.statement: The war priest can cast its listed at-will spells and each listed daily spell once per day, using Wisdom with save DC 15. Its healing bonus action recharges on a roll of 4–6 and restores 2d8+3 hit points to itself or a creature it chooses within 60 feet.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: War Priest, Spellcasting; Bonus Actions (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: spell access and healing follow the listed limits; dial: daily casts and recharge restrict repeated use; in-world cost: healing consumes a recharging opportunity.

rules.statement: When the Fiend warlock makes an ability check or saving throw, it can add 1d10 after rolling but before the roll's effects occur; this ability recharges after a short or long rest. Its visible-attacker retaliation can be used three times per day and makes that attacker save or take 4d10 necrotic damage, or half on a success.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Warlock of the Fiend, Dark One's Own Luck; Fiendish Rebuke (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: the warlock can adjust one eligible roll or retaliate as specified; dial: uses are rest- or day-limited; in-world cost: each use consumes a limited reserve.

rules.statement: The Great Old One warlock creates a momentary extraplanar rift as a scream-filled 20-foot cube within 60 feet. Creatures there make a DC 15 Wisdom save or take 2d8 psychic damage and become frightened of the warlock until its next turn begins; on a success they take half damage and are not frightened.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Warlock of the Great Old One, Howling Void (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: the rift produces the listed area effect; dial: the passage specifies no travel through it and the saving throw limits its impact; in-world cost: affected creatures risk psychic harm and fear.

rules.statement: The conjurer can teleport itself and its equipment up to 30 feet to a visible unoccupied space, or swap places with a willing Small or Medium creature in a visible space within range; this recharges on 4–6. Once per day it can summon one of four kinds of elemental within 60 feet, which obeys it and acts immediately after it for up to 1 hour, ending sooner if either dies or it dismisses the elemental as a bonus action.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Conjurer Wizard, Bonus Actions (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: teleportation and summoning follow their stated targets and durations; dial: teleportation recharges on 4–6 and summoning is once daily; in-world cost: the elemental's service ends on the listed events.

rules.statement: The diviner can replace an attack roll, saving throw, or ability check made by itself or a creature it can see with a d20 result it rolls, up to three times. The choice is made as a reaction when the qualifying roll occurs.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Diviner Wizard, Portent (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: the diviner's chosen die can replace the qualifying roll; dial: it is limited to three uses; in-world cost: each intervention spends one use.

rules.statement: The abjurer can use a reaction when it or a visible creature within 30 feet takes damage to create a barrier around either one, reducing that damage by 4d10+4, to a minimum of 0. The feature recharges on 4–6, and the barrier then vanishes.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Abjurer Wizard, Arcane Ward (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: one triggered barrier reduces a single instance of damage; dial: range and recharge constrain protection; in-world cost: the barrier disappears after absorbing damage.

rules.statement: A wastrilith befouls exposed water within 30 feet at the start of each of its turns; underwater, the effect lightly obscures the area until a current clears it, while water in containers remains corrupted until it evaporates. A creature consuming the water or swimming in it saves against DC 18: success grants immunity to that water for 24 hours, while failure deals 4d6 poison damage and poisons it for 1 minute, followed by another save; failure then deals 4d8 poison damage and leaves it poisoned until a long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Wastrilith, Corrupt Water (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: nearby water acquires the listed effects; dial: a successful save gives 24-hour immunity and containers remain affected only until evaporation; in-world cost: exposure can cause damage and lasting poisoning.

rules.statement: A wood woad can spend 10 feet of movement once on each of its turns to enter a living tree within 5 feet and emerge beside a visible living tree within 60 feet. Both trees must be Large or bigger, and it appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the destination tree.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Wood Woad, Tree Stride (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: movement links two qualifying trees; dial: once per turn, with size and distance limits; in-world cost: it must spend 10 feet of movement.

rules.statement: A yeth hound that starts its turn in natural sunlight is sent to the Ethereal Plane and cannot return to the Material Plane until after sunset. It returns at the place it vanished, and while in the Border Ethereal can cross back as an action when adjacent to its Material Plane master or packmate.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yeth Hound — Sunlight Banishment (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sunlight automatically triggers removal; dial: return requires sunset and proximity to a master or packmate.

rules.statement: A yeth hound on the same plane as its master can magically share its senses and communicate telepathically with its master. Across the Border Ethereal and Material Planes, the hound is visible from either side but cannot affect or be affected by anything on the other plane.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yeth Hound — Telepathic Bond; Sunlight Banishment (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bond works only on the same plane; dial: cross-plane visibility does not permit interaction.

rules.statement: A creature that hears a yeth hound’s bay must make a DC 13 Wisdom save or become frightened until the end of the hound’s next turn, or until the hound is incapacitated. While frightened and within 30 feet, it must use all its movement to flee by the most direct route, even through hazards; a successful save grants immunity to all yeth hounds’ baying for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yeth Hound — Baleful Baying (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the sound imposes fear and compulsory flight on a failed save; dial: successful resistance protects against the whole kind for 24 hours.

rules.statement: An anathema’s ritual transformation requires sacrificing hundreds of snakes and bathing in enemies’ blood; it is quick and painful. An anathema does not age after the transformation.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yuan-Ti Anathema — description (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation grants an ageless form; dial: it demands a large-scale sacrifice and painful blood ritual.

rules.statement: A yuan-ti broodguard’s transformation takes 1d6 + 6 days after it consumes the special potion. Before the process finishes, lesser restoration or remove curse can end it; after completion, only wish can reverse it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Making a Broodguard (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the potion gradually changes body and mind; dial: interruption is available only before completion, while reversal afterward requires exceptional magic.

rules.statement: A creature forced to drink the broodguard potion can make a DC 15 Constitution save; on success it takes 14 (4d6) poison damage and is otherwise unaffected. The transformation otherwise renders the subject incapacitated and alters both body and mind, including loss of its former identity and instinctive obedience to yuan-ti.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Making a Broodguard; Yuan-Ti Broodguard — description (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed resistance leads to incapacitation and lasting transformation; dial: a successful save avoids the change but still costs 4d6 poison damage.

rules.statement: A yuan-ti mind whisperer that reduces an enemy to 0 hit points gains 9 temporary hit points. Its patron pact with Sseth is described as the source of its religious influence, but the passage gives no explicit payment or terms of the bargain.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yuan-Ti Mind Whisperer — Sseth’s Blessing; description (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: defeating an enemy provides a temporary defensive reserve; dial: the passage describes patronage but specifies no bargain cost.

rules.statement: A nightmare speaker’s pact with Dendar grants power in the mortal world in exchange for feeding the deity victims’ fears and nightmares. The priest receives nightmarish visions interpreted as prophecies and acts to make those visions come true.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yuan-Ti Nightmare Speaker — description (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the pact supplies power and prophetic visions; dial: its stated price is delivering victims’ fear and nightmares.

rules.statement: A creature within 60 feet that the nightmare speaker can see must make a DC 13 Intelligence save against Invoke Nightmare. On a failure it takes 22 (4d10) psychic damage and is frightened by an immobile illusion of its deepest fears; the speaker must concentrate to maintain it for up to 1 minute, and the target repeats the save at each turn’s end, ending the effect on success or taking 11 (2d10) psychic damage on failure.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yuan-Ti Nightmare Speaker — Invoke Nightmare (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one failed save causes fear and recurring psychic harm; dial: the speaker must concentrate, and the target gets repeated chances to end it.

rules.statement: A zaratan that moves at least 10 feet on the ground can create a shock wave within 120 feet: the area becomes difficult terrain for 1 minute, and creatures concentrating must pass a DC 25 Constitution save or lose concentration. Structures in contact with the ground take 100 thunder damage; collapse can bury nearby creatures, who can be freed with a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check as an action.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Zaratan — Earth-Shaking Movement (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sufficient ground movement triggers an area-wide hazard; dial: the effect disrupts concentration, damages structures, and can trap creatures until they spend actions to escape.

rules.statement: A zaratan can retract into its shell as a legendary action, gaining resistance to all damage but becoming restrained until it emerges. While retracted, it can spend two legendary actions to regain 52 hit points; its next legendary action must be to emerge, which also includes a rock attack.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Zaratan — Legendary Actions (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retraction trades mobility for broad protection; dial: recovery costs legendary actions and forces a subsequent emergence.

rules.statement: Zariel’s pact-making is difficult to escape, and she seeks mortal souls to replenish her legions; she nevertheless allows servants to live out their lives if they keep honing their talents and increasing their value. Her rise to archdevil status followed Asmodeus’s offer of rulership of Avernus, which transformed her.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Zariel — description (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: service and cultivated ability can sustain a bargain; dial: the patron bargains hard and seeks souls, making exit difficult.

rules.statement: A creature within 9 miles of Zariel’s lair hears screaming voices and smells burning meat; within 1 mile, flames erupt at 60-foot intervals and deal 7 (2d6) fire damage to a creature or object on contact, at most once per round. Smoke heavily obscures the area from 500 feet to 2 miles from the lair and cannot be cleared; these effects fade 1d10 days after Zariel dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Zariel — Regional Effects (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lair imposes persistent sensory and environmental hazards; dial: the effects cover fixed ranges and remain until the ruler dies and 1d10 days pass.

rules.statement: A warlock who breaks an evil patron’s bargain may rise after death as an undead servant. Its former ambitions are displaced by the drive to carry out the patron’s interests, though it retains freedom to choose tactics; it may recruit helpers or be compelled to serve another powerful being to achieve a difficult objective.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Deathlocks, pp. 86–87 (dnd5e-motm#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a broken bargain can impose service after death; dial the patron’s control and the severity of the penalty to fit the pact.

rules.statement: At least three mind flayer arcanists can create an alhoon-making container through a three-day ritual of spellcasting and psionic communion, sacrificing one living victim’s soul per participant. Completing the ritual transforms the arcanists into free-willed undead; when an alhoon is destroyed, its mind transfers to the container rather than restoring its body.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Collaborative Undeath, p. 43 (dnd5e-motm#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the transformation costs multiple living souls and sustained cooperation; dial whether the resulting minds can later be restored.

rules.statement: A barghest can spend at least 1 minute consuming the corpse of a Fey or Humanoid it killed within the past 10 minutes, destroying the corpse and trapping its soul for 24 hours. Until digestion finishes, the soul can be restored only with a 50 percent chance of failure, and if the barghest dies first the soul is released; after digestion, the victim cannot be revived.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Barghest, p. 60 (dnd5e-motm#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: soul capture requires a recent kill and takes time, but completed digestion prevents revival; dial the window and interruption risk.

rules.statement: A swallowed creature is moved into an enclosed demiplane that only the dreadnought’s special access or planar-travel magic can reach. The demiplane has breathable air and gravity, and its contents are released around the dreadnought’s corpse if it dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Astral Dreadnought, p. 52 (dnd5e-motm#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the creature is trapped in a specialized space with limited exits, but the dreadnought’s death releases everything inside.

rules.statement: A dreadnought cannot leave the Astral Plane and cannot be banished or otherwise transported away from it. Its eye can project a 150-foot cone of antimagic, choosing the cone’s direction at the start of each turn; the cone stops working if the eye is closed or the dreadnought is blinded.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Astral Dreadnought, p. 52 (dnd5e-motm#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the creature is fixed to its plane and its antimagic field has clear positional and sensory limits.

rules.statement: When an alhoon critically hits a creature traveling by astral projection, it can cut that creature’s silver cord instead of dealing damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Alhoon, p. 44 (dnd5e-motm#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a critical hit can sever the projection’s tether; dial how often this specialized interruption is available.

rules.statement: An alhoon can cast plane shift on itself once per day, and a berbalang can do the same once per day; these listed uses do not require material components.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Alhoon, p. 44; Berbalang, p. 62 (dnd5e-motm#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: self-only planar travel is limited to one use per day; the passage gives no broader travel procedure or cost.

rules.statement: A barghest engulfed in flames at least 10 feet high or wide at the start of its turn must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or be banished instantly to Gehenna.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Barghest, p. 60 (dnd5e-motm#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a large fire creates a specific banishment risk, with a saving throw as the escape chance.

rules.statement: When an alkilith is motionless at the start of combat, it has advantage on initiative; a creature that has not seen it move or act must succeed on a DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to recognize that it is not ordinary slime or fungus.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Alkilith, p. 45 (dnd5e-motm#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: concealment depends on remaining still and the observer’s failure to inspect it successfully.

rules.statement: A creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of an alkilith, unless it is a demon, must make a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw or have disadvantage on its next attack roll, saving throw, or ability check. If it fails by 5 or more, it instead suffers the confusion spell’s effect for 1 minute, without concentration; a creature under that effect is immune to this ability while it lasts.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Alkilith, p. 45 (dnd5e-motm#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: proximity imposes a brief penalty or, on a worse failure, a longer confusion effect; demons are excluded and the stronger effect prevents repeat exposure.

rules.statement: A demon staff hit deals bludgeoning and psychic damage; its target must make a DC 19 Wisdom save or become frightened of the attacker for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each turn to end the effect on itself.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Drow, Demon Staff (dnd5e-motm#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the fear lasts at most 1 minute; dial: the failed save imposes fear, for the attacker’s psychic strike is terrifying.

rules.statement: After a tentacle rod hits the same target three times in one turn, the target must make a DC 15 Constitution save or, for 1 minute, have half speed, disadvantage on Dexterity saves, no reactions, and a choice of either an action or bonus action on its turn. It repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the effect on itself on a success.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Drow, Tentacle Rod (dnd5e-motm#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the restriction lasts up to 1 minute; dial: it requires three hits in one turn, reflecting sustained restraint.

rules.statement: A drow can cast listed spells without material components, using Charisma and a DC 20 spell save; the available spells have separate at-will, twice-per-day, or once-per-day limits. The list includes banishment and plane shift, among other spells.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Drow, Spellcasting (dnd5e-motm#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell frequency is capped by the listed uses; dial: choose spells from the stated list, representing the drow’s magical repertoire.

rules.statement: The drow can magically summon a glabrezu or yochlol once per day in an unoccupied space within 60 feet. It is an ally, cannot summon other demons, and remains for 10 minutes, until it or the summoner dies, or until dismissed by the summoner as an action.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Drow, Summon Servant (dnd5e-motm#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one servant lasts at most 10 minutes; dial: the summoner chooses between two demons, at the cost of a daily use.

rules.statement: An elder brain senses the distance, direction, and Intelligence score of creatures with Intelligence 4 or higher within 5 miles, but learns nothing else about them this way. Mind blank, nondetection, or similar magic blocks this sense.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Elder Brain, Creature Sense (dnd5e-motm#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sensing is limited to location and Intelligence; dial: protective magic blocks it, preserving a countermeasure.

rules.statement: The elder brain can establish a psychic link as a bonus action with an incapacitated creature it senses, up to ten links at once. It perceives the target’s senses; once able, the target knows of the link and can use an action to attempt a DC 18 Charisma save to break it, taking 3d6 psychic damage on a successful save; the link also ends beyond 5 miles or if the elder brain ends it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Elder Brain, Psychic Link (dnd5e-motm#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: links are capped at ten and 5 miles; dial: targets must be incapacitated to initiate the link, and resisting it inflicts psychic harm.

rules.statement: The elder brain can use a linked creature’s thoughts and emotional state, and can end that creature’s concentration on a spell, dealing 1d4 psychic damage per spell level. It can also end a link, imposing disadvantage on the target’s ability checks, attack rolls, and saves until the end of its next turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Elder Brain, Sense Thoughts and Legendary Actions (dnd5e-motm#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these effects require an existing link; dial: ending concentration or severing the link has a direct, bounded consequence.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of Geryon’s lair, travelers may see shimmering portals in places they regard as safe; passing through one always takes them somewhere in Stygia. The effect fades 1d10 days after Geryon dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Geryon, Regional Effects (dnd5e-motm#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the portal’s destination is restricted to Stygia; dial: the lair creates the portals, and their effect ends after the ruler’s death.

rules.statement: Geryon’s lair causes freezing winds and eerie screams within 1 mile; a creature finishing a short or long rest there must succeed on a DC 21 Wisdom save or gain no benefit from that rest. These regional effects fade 1d10 days after Geryon dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Geryon, Regional Effects (dnd5e-motm#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the rest penalty applies only on a failed save; dial: the field is limited to the lair’s vicinity and ends after the ruler’s death.

rules.statement: In Limbo, a githzerai anarch can spend 10 minutes stabilizing an area extending 5 miles from itself, shaping the unformed substance into chosen inanimate forms. It can stabilize objects created there and taken to the Material Plane for as long as it remains alive; after its death, the effects end after 1d6 rounds and the formed matter unravels.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Githzerai Anarch, Regional Effects (dnd5e-motm#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the shaped region is limited to 5 miles and is temporary after death; dial: creating lasting material requires the anarch’s continued existence.

rules.statement: A marut enforces a contract written on gold and placed in its chest after the parties pay the required fee. It applies the written terms literally, rejects vague, contradictory, or unenforceable terms, and punishes a party that breaks them; lethal force is used only if required by the contract, if it is fully broken, or if the marut is attacked.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Marut (dnd5e-motm#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enforcement follows only the recorded terms; dial: the parties pay to have the contract made, and ambiguity is rejected rather than interpreted.

rules.statement: A marut can use plane shift three times per day, either normally or to target a creature it sees within 60 feet. For the targeted option, a DC 20 Charisma save prevents the creature from being sent to a teleportation circle in Sigil’s Hall of Concordance.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Marut, Plane Shift (dnd5e-motm#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the forced travel is limited to three uses per day and allows a save; dial: failure sends the target to a fixed destination.

rules.statement: A morkoth’s island drifts on planar currents and is protected from most harmful effects outside it; it may travel among planes, follow a recurring route, remain tied to particular places, or move unpredictably. Some morkoths can direct the island’s movement.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Morkoth, island description (p. 185) (dnd5e-motm#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the island drifts and resists outside harm; dial: its route and whether the morkoth can steer it; the island’s core and planar currents explain its travel.

rules.statement: Infernal tack binds a nightmare to serve the creature wearing its spurs until that wearer dies or the tack is removed; the nightmare need not willingly accept the bond. An attuned wearer can use an action to summon it, and it appears within 20 feet at the start of the wearer’s next turn, serving as an ally on the wearer’s initiative. It remains for up to a day, until either dies, or until dismissed as an action; a slain nightmare reforms in the Hells within 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Magic Item: Infernal Tack (p. 190) (dnd5e-motm#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the spurs impose service and allow temporary summoning; dial: use requires attunement and a nightmare must first be subdued for the tack to be put on it.

rules.statement: Neogi masters draw magic from a pact made with aberrant entities encountered during their multiversal travels; the passage names such entities but gives no further terms, benefit schedule, or cost for the pact.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Neogi Master (p. 192) (dnd5e-motm#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the pact is the stated source of the masters’ magic; dial: the passage specifies neither obligations nor price, so those remain setting choices.

rules.statement: A retriever can cast plane shift three times per day, but only to transport itself and at most one incapacitated creature, which counts as willing for the spell. It can also cast dimension door three times per day, for itself only.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Retriever, Spellcasting (p. 210) (dnd5e-motm#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the construct has limited self-transport and can carry only one incapacitated passenger through plane shift; its built-in spellcasting sets the limits.

rules.statement: A phoenix that dies explodes, forcing creatures within 60 feet to make a DC 20 Dexterity save or take 22 fire damage, half on a success; unattended flammable objects ignite. Its body is replaced by an indestructible, five-pound cinder that burns a creature touching it for 21 fire damage no more than once per round, then hatches a new phoenix after 1d6 days.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Phoenix, Fiery Death and Rebirth (p. 206) (dnd5e-motm#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death triggers the blast and delayed rebirth; dial: the cinder remains hazardous while it exists, providing the in-world cost of approaching it.

rules.statement: A redcap comes into being in the Feywild or at a fey crossing when a sentient creature acts on an intense desire for bloodshed and blood from a slain person soaks the ground; moonlight on its emerging cap completes its awakening. It must soak its cap in fresh blood at least once every three days or vanish as though it never existed.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Redcap (p. 208) (dnd5e-motm#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: murderous intent, a slain victim’s blood, and moonlight enable its arrival; dial: the three-day blood requirement is the ongoing cost of its existence.

rules.statement: A warlock of the Fiend gets its powers through pacts with archfiends of the Lower Planes; the passage gives no pact terms or payment. The described warlock can add 1d10 to an ability check or saving throw after rolling but before the roll’s effects occur, once per short or long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Warlock of the Fiend; Dark One’s Own Luck (p. 255) (dnd5e-motm#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the archfiend pact is the source of power and the roll bonus is limited to one use per rest; dial: no bargain price is specified in this passage.

rules.statement: A warlock of the Great Old One gains power through a magical pact with entities from strange, distant realms; the passage supplies no terms or cost. The described warlock’s aura can deal 10 psychic damage to a chosen creature within 10 feet at the start of its turn if the warlock is not incapacitated, while its momentary rift can frighten creatures that fail a DC 15 Wisdom save until the warlock’s next turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Warlock of the Great Old One (p. 257) (dnd5e-motm#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a pact grants the described abilities, with the aura suppressed by incapacitation and the rift’s fear gated by a save; dial: the passage states no bargain or payment.

rules.statement: A yeth hound exposed to natural sunlight vanishes to the Deep Ethereal. It remains there until sunset, then returns to the Border Ethereal at the place it vanished; there it can be seen across the plane boundary but cannot affect or be affected by creatures or things on the other plane. As an action, it can return to the Material Plane when adjacent to its master or a pack mate there.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yeth Hound — Sunlight Banishment (dnd5e-motm#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; sunlight forces a temporary removal, and return is delayed until sunset and constrained by proximity.

rules.statement: While a yeth hound and its master are on the same plane, the hound can magically transmit its senses to the master and communicate telepathically with them. A pack’s master can give its hounds commands this way; if the master dies, the hounds seek a new master.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yeth Hound — Telepathic Bond; Yeth Hound (dnd5e-motm#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the companion bond enables communication and command, but depends on shared-plane presence and a living master.

rules.statement: Yeth hounds are granted by powerful Fey to individuals who please them; a powerful Fey can create a pack. The grant gives the recipient hunting companions, while the pack’s master can command them through their bond.
