locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yeth Hound (dnd5e-motm#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; a Fey patron supplies companions to a favored recipient, with command tied to the master relationship.

rules.statement: Zariel grants special abilities to her most loyal cultists: they may gain the ability to turn a noncritical hit into a critical hit, usable again after a short or long rest. Cult leaders may also gain the ability, immediately after initiative is rolled, to swap initiative results among themselves and up to three visible allies, provided the chosen creatures are not incapacitated.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Cultists of Zariel (dnd5e-motm#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; loyalty to a powerful patron provides combat benefits, limited by rest-based recovery and eligibility.

rules.statement: Zariel’s regional effects create a zone of screaming voices and burning-meat odor within 9 miles of her lair, flame jets at 60-foot intervals within 1 mile, and an unremovable, heavily obscuring smoke zone within 2 miles but at least 500 feet from the lair. A creature or object touching a flame jet takes 2d6 fire damage, at most once per round; if Zariel dies, the effects fade over 1d10 days.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Zariel — lair effects (dnd5e-motm#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the lair imposes persistent regional hazards, which end gradually when their source dies.

rules.statement: Zariel’s spellcasting uses Charisma, has a save DC of 26, and requires no material components; she can cast the listed at-will spells without a stated daily limit and each listed limited-use spell three times per day.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Zariel — Spellcasting (dnd5e-motm#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; spell use follows a fixed ability, save difficulty, component exemption, and stated daily limits.

rules.statement: A creature poisoned by Zariel’s touch is also blinded and deafened for up to 1 minute. It can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Zariel — Horrid Touch (dnd5e-motm#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; one failed save imposes multiple impairments, with a recurring chance to end them.

rules.statement: When an action’s outcome is uncertain, roll a d20 and add the relevant modifier; apply situational bonuses or penalties, then succeed if the total meets or exceeds the target number. Ability checks and saving throws use a Difficulty Class, while attacks use Armor Class.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: How to Play — The d20 (p. 8) (dnd5e-phb-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the target number sets the difficulty of the attempted action.

rules.statement: With advantage, roll two d20s and use the higher result; with disadvantage, roll two and use the lower. These rules apply to an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw when the circumstances grant either state.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: How to Play — Advantage and Disadvantage (p. 8) (dnd5e-phb-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; favorable or adverse circumstances change which roll determines the outcome.

rules.statement: A proficiency bonus can be added to a qualifying roll only once, even if multiple features would apply it; it can likewise be doubled or halved only once. A 1st-level character’s proficiency bonus is +2.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Step 2: Choose a Class — Proficiency Bonus (p. 13) (dnd5e-phb-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; proficiency reflects training, with a fixed limit on stacking its bonus.

rules.statement: To generate ability scores randomly, roll four six-sided dice, total the highest three, and repeat until you have six scores. Alternatively, use 15, 14, 13, 12, 10, and 8, then assign the scores to abilities and apply racial increases.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Step 3: Determine Ability Scores (p. 14) (dnd5e-phb-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial; the random method varies results, while the listed array gives predictable character capabilities.

rules.statement: If the DM permits point-buy, spend 27 points on ability scores; a score must be at least 8 and at most 15 before racial increases. The listed costs are 0 for 8, 1 for 9, 2 for 10, 3 for 11, 4 for 12, 5 for 13, 7 for 14, and 9 for 15.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Step 3: Determine Ability Scores — Variant: Customizing Ability Scores (p. 14) (dnd5e-phb-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; optional; point-buy trades randomness for player control within a limited budget.

rules.statement: For an ability score, calculate its modifier by subtracting 10 and dividing by 2, rounding down. Whenever a game calculation produces a fraction, round down, including fractions of one-half or more.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Step 3: Determine Ability Scores (p. 14); How to Play — Round Down (p. 8) (dnd5e-phb-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; consistent rounding keeps derived values determinate.

rules.statement: A 1st-level character has one Hit Die, whose type is set by class, and starts with hit points equal to the die’s highest possible roll plus the Constitution modifier. After resting, the character can spend Hit Dice to regain hit points.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Step 2: Choose a Class — Hit Points and Hit Dice (p. 13) (dnd5e-phb-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the class sets the starting durability die, while Constitution adjusts starting hit points.

rules.statement: A character typically begins at 1st level with 0 experience points and advances by gaining experience; a character starting above 1st level generally begins with the minimum experience needed for that level. The DM may instead set a higher starting level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Step 2: Choose a Class — Level (p. 12) (dnd5e-phb-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; the DM may choose a higher starting level; prior experience determines the character’s initial capabilities.

rules.statement: When a specific rule conflicts with a general rule, apply the specific rule instead. This allows particular traits, spells, items, and other features to create exceptions to the usual rules.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: How to Play — Specific Beats General (p. 8) (dnd5e-phb-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; specific effects take precedence over general rules when they conflict.

rules.statement: Starting gear comes from your class and background, or you may buy it using the gold allowance for your class; you may also take one trinket at no cost. Keep the total weight of your gear at or below your Strength score × 15 pounds as a guideline.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Step 5: Choose Equipment (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; starting wealth and carrying capacity limit what the character can bring.

rules.statement: Without armor or a shield, Armor Class is 10 + Dexterity modifier; otherwise calculate it using the applicable armor and shield rules. If multiple features offer different AC calculations, choose one to use, and lacking required armor or shield proficiency has drawbacks.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Armor Class (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; defensive equipment and proficiency determine the usable defense.

rules.statement: For a weapon attack, roll a d20 and add the relevant ability modifier, plus your proficiency bonus if you are proficient with that weapon. Use Strength for melee weapon attacks and damage, except a finesse weapon may use Dexterity; use Dexterity for ranged weapons, except a thrown weapon may use Strength.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Weapons (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; weapon type and training constrain the attack calculation.

rules.statement: Each time you gain a level, gain one Hit Die: roll it and add your Constitution modifier to your hit point maximum, or use the class’s fixed value instead. When your Constitution modifier rises, increase your hit point maximum by 1 for every level you have attained; class features and proficiency bonus also improve at the levels specified for your class, and ability-score increases cannot raise a score above 20.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Beyond 1st Level (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; advancement is gated by levels and class progression.

locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Character Advancement table (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; experience thresholds gate level and proficiency progression.

rules.statement: A dwarf has Constitution +2, Medium size, walking speed 25 feet that heavy armor does not reduce, and darkvision to 60 feet. The dwarf has advantage on saves against poison and resistance to poison damage, proficiency with battleaxe, handaxe, throwing hammer, and warhammer, one choice of smith’s tools, brewer’s supplies, or mason’s tools, and doubles proficiency on History checks about stonework origins.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Dwarf Traits (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; inherited ancestry traits grant fixed benefits and proficiencies.

rules.statement: A hill dwarf gains Wisdom +1 and increases hit point maximum by 1, with another +1 each time they gain a level. A mountain dwarf gains Strength +2 and proficiency with light and medium armor.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Hill Dwarf; Mountain Dwarf (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; choosing a subrace determines its additional inherited traits.

rules.statement: An elf has Dexterity +2, Medium size, walking speed 30 feet, darkvision to 60 feet, Perception proficiency, advantage on saves against being charmed, and cannot be put to sleep by magic. Instead of sleeping, the elf meditates for 4 hours to gain the benefit a human gets from 8 hours of sleep.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Elf Traits (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; inherited traits provide senses, defenses, and an alternate rest requirement.

rules.statement: A high elf gains Intelligence +1, proficiency with longsword, shortsword, shortbow, and longbow, one wizard-list cantrip using Intelligence, and one extra language. A wood elf gains Wisdom +1, the same weapon proficiencies, walking speed 35 feet, and may try to hide when only lightly obscured by natural phenomena; a drow gains Charisma +1, darkvision to 120 feet, disadvantage on sight-based attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks in direct sunlight, the dancing lights cantrip, and once-per-day faerie fire at level 3 and darkness at level 5, using Charisma for those spells.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: High Elf; Wood Elf; Dark Elf (Drow) (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; subrace choice grants specified proficiencies, spell uses, senses, or limitations.

rules.statement: A halfling has Dexterity +2, Small size, and walking speed 25 feet. When the halfling rolls a 1 on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, they may reroll and must use the new result; they have advantage on saves against being frightened and can move through the space of any creature larger than themselves.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Halfling Traits (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; ancestry grants a narrow reroll and movement and fear benefits.

rules.statement: A lightfoot halfling gains Charisma +1 and may try to hide while obscured only by a creature at least one size larger. A stout halfling gains Constitution +1, advantage on saves against poison, and resistance to poison damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Lightfoot; Stout (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; subrace choice determines additional traits.

rules.statement: A standard human increases each of its ability scores by 1, is Medium, and has a walking speed of 30 feet. It speaks, reads, and writes Common plus one language of its choice.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Human Traits, p. 31 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the listed traits; dial: none; language choice reflects the human’s contacts and upbringing.

rules.statement: If the optional feat rules are in use and the DM permits the variant, replace the standard ability increase with +1 to two different abilities, proficiency in one chosen skill, and one chosen feat.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Variant Human Traits, p. 31 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use standard human traits; dial: enable only with the optional feat rules and DM approval, trading the broad increase for chosen abilities, a skill, and a feat.

rules.statement: A dragonborn chooses one ancestry from the table, which sets its damage type, breath shape, and saving-throw type; the breath covers either a 5-by-30-foot line or a 15-foot cone. Each creature in it saves against DC 8 + Constitution modifier + proficiency bonus, taking 2d6 damage on a failure or half on success; damage rises to 3d6 at level 6, 4d6 at level 11, and 5d6 at level 16.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Dragonborn Traits—Draconic Ancestry, p. 33 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the chosen ancestry’s listed shape and damage; dial: breath is limited to once per short or long rest, reflecting recovery after exertion.

rules.statement: A dragonborn has resistance to the damage type associated with its chosen draconic ancestry.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Dragonborn Traits—Damage Resistance, p. 33 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant resistance to the ancestry’s damage type; dial: none; inherited draconic lineage sets the protection.

rules.statement: A gnome can spend 1 hour and 10 gp of materials with tinker's tools to make a Tiny clockwork device with AC 5 and 1 hit point. It stops working after 24 hours unless repaired for 1 hour, or when dismantled as an action; dismantling returns its materials, and no more than three devices can be active at once.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Rock Gnome Traits—Tinker, p. 38 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enforce the time, material, repair, and three-device limits; dial: the device’s function is limited to one of the listed simple options.

rules.statement: A clockwork toy moves 5 feet across the ground on each of its turns in a random direction and makes fitting sounds. A fire starter produces a small flame usable to light a candle, torch, or campfire, which takes an action; a music box plays one song at moderate volume until it ends or is closed.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Rock Gnome Traits—Tinker, p. 38 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use only the described behavior; dial: these are harmless, narrowly useful clockwork effects.

rules.statement: A half-elf gains proficiency in two skills of its choice and can speak, read, and write Common, Elvish, and one additional language of its choice.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Half-Elf Traits, p. 39 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant the chosen proficiencies and languages; dial: selections reflect the character’s mixed background.

rules.statement: A character’s class defines its main capabilities and gives it special features, including such things as weapon and armor mastery or spells; characters gain additional features as they advance in level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 3: Classes, p. 46 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use class and level to determine features; dial: the passage gives no specific feature mechanics beyond this general rule.

rules.statement: Barbarians can enter rage as a bonus action. While not in heavy armor, rage grants advantage on Strength checks and saves, extra damage on Strength-based melee weapon attacks according to level, and resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage; it prevents spellcasting and concentration. It lasts up to 1 minute, ends early if the barbarian falls unconscious or ends a turn without attacking a hostile creature or taking damage since the prior turn, and can be ended voluntarily as a bonus action; uses recover after a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Barbarian: Rage, p. 49 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: limit the heightened combat state by a finite daily reserve and clear interruption conditions; the in-world cost is that fury crowds out spell control.

rules.statement: Without armor, a barbarian's AC is 10 plus Dexterity and Constitution modifiers; a shield remains compatible. From 2nd level, the barbarian may gain advantage on Strength-based melee attacks for the turn by accepting advantage on attacks against them until their next turn.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Barbarian: Unarmored Defense; Reckless Attack, p. 49 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: trade defense for more reliable offense, with the exposed fighter paying an immediate tactical cost.

rules.statement: From 2nd level, the barbarian has advantage on Dexterity saves against visible effects if not blinded, deafened, or incapacitated. At 7th level, initiative rolls also gain advantage; if surprised but not incapacitated, the barbarian can act on the first turn only by raging before doing anything else.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Barbarian: Danger Sense, p. 49; Feral Instinct, p. 50 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: heightened instinct helps detect and respond to visible danger, but does not work when key senses or agency are impaired.

rules.statement: At 11th level, while raging and reduced to 0 hit points without dying outright, the barbarian can make a DC 10 Constitution save to remain at 1 hit point; each use after the first raises the DC by 5, resetting to 10 after a short or long rest. From 15th level, rage ends early only if the barbarian falls unconscious or chooses to end it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Barbarian: Relentless Rage; Persistent Rage, p. 50 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: repeated survival attempts become harder until rest, while persistence extends the combat state; the cost is escalating bodily strain.

rules.statement: The Berserker may choose to frenzy when entering rage, gaining one bonus-action melee weapon attack on each later turn while that rage lasts; when it ends, the barbarian gains one exhaustion level. At 6th level, rage prevents or suspends charm and fear effects.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Path of the Berserker: Frenzy; Mindless Rage, p. 50 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: extra attacks are purchased with exhaustion, while rage suppresses specified mental effects only for its duration.

rules.statement: At 10th level, a Berserker can use an action to frighten one visible creature within 30 feet that can see or hear them; a failed Wisdom save frightens it until the end of the Berserker's next turn. The effect can be extended with later actions, ends if the target's turn ends out of sight or more than 60 feet away, and a successful save bars reuse on that target for 24 hours.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Path of the Berserker: Intimidating Presence, p. 50 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: fear requires an action and a failed save, with range, visibility, and a successful-save cooldown limiting repeated use.

rules.statement: A Totem Warrior gains beast sense and speak with animals as rituals at 3rd level. It also chooses a spirit and needs a physical token incorporating material from that animal; the spirit grants a rage benefit, such as resistance to all damage except psychic for the bear, protection from opportunity attacks and bonus-action Dash for the eagle, or ally advantage on nearby hostile targets for the wolf.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Path of the Totem Warrior: Spirit Seeker; Totem Spirit, p. 51 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: spirit-linked benefits require a chosen animal identity and physical token; each option specializes the user's combat support or mobility.

rules.statement: At 6th level, a Totem Warrior chooses an animal aspect: bear doubles carrying capacity and improves certain Strength checks, eagle grants long-distance detailed sight and removes dim-light disadvantage on Perception, or wolf permits tracking at a fast pace and stealthy travel at a normal pace. At 10th level, the character can cast commune with nature as a ritual, with a spiritual animal conveying the information sought.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Path of the Totem Warrior: Aspect of the Beast; Spirit Walker, p. 51 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: animal-derived traits expand practical sensing and travel; the information-seeking spell remains ritual-limited.

rules.statement: A bard can cast a known spell as a ritual if it has the ritual tag, and can use a musical instrument as a spellcasting focus. Bard spell slots return after a long rest; a known spell must be of a level for which the bard has slots, and on gaining a bard level one known bard spell can be replaced with another eligible bard-list spell.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Bard: Spellcasting, pp. 53–54 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell use is constrained by known-spell choices, slot capacity, and recovery by long rest; ritual-tagged spells avoid a slot.

rules.statement: A bard can use a bonus action to give a hearing creature other than themself within 60 feet one inspiration die for 10 minutes; the recipient may add it to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw after seeing the d20 but before the outcome is announced. A creature holds only one such die, a spent die is lost, and the bard's uses equal Charisma modifier (minimum one), returning on a long rest; the die scales from d6 to d8 at level 5, d10 at 10, and d12 at 15.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Bard: Bardic Inspiration, pp. 54–55 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: a limited-use benefit is transferred to one listener at a time, with a short duration and a single-roll expenditure.

rules.statement: From 5th level, a bard recovers all Bardic Inspiration uses after a short or long rest. At 6th level, an action starts a performance lasting until the next turn that grants the bard and hearing allies within 30 feet advantage on saves against charm and fear; it ends early if the bard is incapacitated, silenced, or voluntarily stops.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Bard: Font of Inspiration; Countercharm, p. 55 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: the protective effect requires an action and audible performance, and fails when the performer cannot act or be heard.

rules.statement: At 2nd level, a cleric channels divine energy to create one chosen effect, including Turn Undead and a domain effect; after use, the cleric must finish a short or long rest before using Channel Divinity again. If an effect requires a save, its DC equals the cleric spell save DC.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Cleric: Channel Divinity, p. 58 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: divine power is accessed through a limited channel that refreshes with rest, and its resistance threshold is tied to spellcasting ability.

rules.statement: A cleric can use Channel Divinity a limited number of times between rests: twice, rising to three times at 18th level; a short or long rest restores all expended uses.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Cleric, Channel Divinity (p. 60) (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited uses; dial: use count and recovery rest; the cleric’s divine reserve is finite.

rules.statement: A cleric can present a holy symbol and spend an action to affect visible or audible undead within 30 feet that fail a Wisdom save: for 1 minute, they flee, cannot willingly approach within 30 feet, cannot take reactions, and have sharply restricted actions. The effect ends early if they take damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Cleric, Channel Divinity: Turn Undead (p. 60) (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed save imposes flight and action limits; dial: 30-foot range and 1-minute duration; damage breaks the effect.

rules.statement: A Knowledge cleric can spend an action and a Channel Divinity use to gain proficiency in one chosen skill or tool for 10 minutes.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Knowledge Domain, Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages (p. 59) (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: temporary learned competence; dial: one skill or tool for 10 minutes; the benefit consumes a limited divine use.

rules.statement: A Knowledge cleric can target a visible creature within 60 feet with an action and force a Wisdom save. On a failure, the cleric senses its surface thoughts for 1 minute and can end the effect with an action to cast suggestion on it without a spell slot; the target automatically fails that spell’s save.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Knowledge Domain, Channel Divinity: Read Thoughts (p. 60) (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: surface thoughts and one guaranteed suggestion; dial: 60-foot range, save, and 1-minute window; a successful save bars reuse on that target until a long rest.

rules.statement: A cleric’s Divine Intervention requires an action, a request for aid, and a percentile roll no higher than the cleric’s level; the DM determines the aid, with a cleric or domain spell effect as an example. Success bars reuse for 7 days, failure allows another attempt after a long rest, and at level 20 success is automatic.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Cleric, Divine Intervention (p. 60) (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: aid depends on divine intervention; dial: level-based odds, outcome, and cooldown; the deity controls the form of assistance.

rules.statement: A Life cleric’s healing spell of 1st level or higher restores the target additional hit points equal to 2 plus the spell’s level. When such a spell heals someone other than the cleric, the cleric also regains that amount.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Life Domain, Disciple of Life and Blessed Healer (pp. 61–62) (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: healing adds a level-scaled amount; dial: the same amount can also heal the caster; the bonus requires qualifying spell use.

rules.statement: A Life cleric can spend an action and a Channel Divinity use to distribute healing equal to five times cleric level among chosen creatures within 30 feet. No target can be raised above half its hit point maximum, and undead and constructs are ineligible.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Life Domain, Channel Divinity: Preserve Life (p. 61) (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: shared healing pool; dial: level-scaled total and half-maximum cap; creature types and range restrict eligibility.

rules.statement: A Tempest cleric can spend an action and a Channel Divinity use to dispel magical darkness within 30 feet and deal 2d10 plus cleric level radiant damage to hostile creatures there that fail a Constitution save, or half as much on a success. Total cover prevents the effect.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Light Domain, Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn (p. 62) (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: nearby magical darkness ends and hostile creatures take damage; dial: 30-foot area, save, and cover; the ability spends a limited use.

rules.statement: A War cleric can use a bonus action to make one weapon attack on a turn when it takes the Attack action, a number of times per long rest equal to its Wisdom modifier, minimum once. It can also spend a Channel Divinity use after seeing an attack roll to add 10 before the outcome is declared.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: War Domain, War Priest and Channel Divinity: Guided Strike (p. 64) (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: extra attacks and accuracy are limited resources; dial: Wisdom-based daily uses and a +10 adjustment; the accuracy choice must precede the result.

rules.statement: A druid can prepare a number of druid spells equal to druid level plus Wisdom modifier, minimum one, and change the list after a long rest by spending at least 1 minute per spell level on each prepared spell. Casting a prepared spell of 1st level or higher expends a slot of that level or higher; slots return after a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Druid, Preparing and Casting Spells (p. 67) (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: prepared spells and slots constrain casting; dial: preparation count, time, and slot levels; a long rest refreshes slots.

rules.statement: A druid can use an action to transform into a previously seen beast, twice per short or long rest, subject to level, challenge-rating, and movement-type limits. The form supplies its statistics and hit points while the druid retains specified mental abilities and proficiencies; at zero form hit points the druid reverts, and excess damage carries over.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Druid, Wild Shape (pp. 67–68) (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation replaces the physical stat block and hit points; dial: uses, duration, and eligible forms; excess damage threatens the original body.

rules.statement: A Circle of the Land druid can recover spell slots during a short rest once before a long rest; the recovered slots’ combined levels cannot exceed half druid level rounded up, and none can be 6th level or higher.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Circle of the Land, Natural Recovery (p. 68) (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: meditation restores a bounded reserve; dial: total slot levels and slot ceiling; use is limited to once per long-rest cycle.

rules.statement: At 18th level, a druid can cast many druid spells while in beast form, including their verbal and somatic components but not material components. At 20th level, Wild Shape uses become unlimited, and the druid can omit verbal and somatic components and material components that have neither a cost nor consumption, in either normal or beast form.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Druid, Beast Spells and Archdruid (pp. 68–69) (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: higher levels relax casting and transformation limits; dial: level thresholds and component restrictions; costly or consumed materials remain required.

rules.statement: A fighter can use a bonus action on their turn to regain hit points equal to 1d10 plus their fighter level, then must finish a short or long rest before using this again.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Second Wind, p. 73 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one use per short or long rest; dial: recovery amount; the fighter’s limited stamina is the in-world cost.

rules.statement: Once on their turn, a fighter can take one extra action; after using this, they must finish a short or long rest. From level 17, they can use it twice between rests, but not twice on the same turn.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Action Surge, p. 73 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited extra action; dial: uses between rests; pushing beyond normal limits explains the restricted frequency.

rules.statement: A Battle Master learns three combat maneuvers at level 3 and two more at each of levels 7, 10, and 15; they can replace one known maneuver whenever they learn new ones. They begin with four d8 superiority dice, regain all expended dice after a short or long rest, and gain one die at levels 7 and 15; the dice become d10s at level 10 and d12s at level 18.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Combat Superiority, pp. 74–75 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a finite pool fuels trained techniques; dial: dice count and size; fatigue and recovery limit repeated use.

rules.statement: An Eldritch Knight learns wizard cantrips and a limited number of wizard spells, mostly from abjuration or evocation; spell slots recover after a long rest. Intelligence sets the spell save DC and attack modifier, and gaining a fighter level can allow one known spell to be replaced subject to level and school restrictions.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Eldritch Knight Spellcasting, p. 76 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: learned magic is bounded by known spells and slots; dial: spell selection and slot progression; study and memorization limit access.

rules.statement: An Eldritch Knight can bond with a weapon through a one-hour ritual, which may occur during a short rest; they cannot be disarmed of it unless incapacitated. If it is on the same plane, they can summon it to their hand as a bonus action; they can bond with at most two weapons, and bonding a third ends one existing bond.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Weapon Bond, p. 76 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: at most two bonded weapons; dial: bonding time and summoning action; the weapon must be bound and on the same plane.

rules.statement: A monk has ki points equal to their monk level and spends them to use ki features; spent points return after a short or long rest that includes at least 30 minutes of meditation. Ki features that call for a saving throw use a DC of 8 plus proficiency bonus plus Wisdom modifier.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Ki, p. 79 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: points are limited by monk level; dial: recovery requires rest and meditation; maintaining the discipline costs time.

rules.statement: After taking the Attack action, a monk can spend 1 ki point to make two unarmed strikes as a bonus action; for 1 ki point they can take Dodge as a bonus action, or take Dash or Disengage as a bonus action and double their jump distance for that turn.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Flurry of Blows; Patient Defense; Step of the Wind, p. 79 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each option costs 1 ki point; dial: the monk chooses how to spend the reserve; the limited pool constrains bursts of activity.

rules.statement: When hit by a ranged weapon attack, a monk can use their reaction to reduce its damage by 1d10 plus their Dexterity modifier and monk level. If this reduces the damage to zero, they can catch a missile small enough for one hand if a hand is free, then spend 1 ki point to make a proficient ranged attack with it as part of the same reaction.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Deflect Missiles, p. 79 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: requires a reaction, and returning a caught missile costs 1 ki; dial: reduction scales with level; catching requires a free hand and a small enough missile.

rules.statement: After hitting a creature with a melee weapon attack, a monk can spend 1 ki point to force a Constitution save; on a failure, the target is stunned until the end of the monk’s next turn.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Stunning Strike, p. 80 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one ki point and a saving throw; dial: duration ends at the next-turn boundary; the target can resist the disruption.

rules.statement: In dim light or darkness, a Way of Shadow monk can use a bonus action to teleport up to 60 feet to a visible unoccupied space that is also in dim light or darkness; they have advantage on their first melee attack before that turn ends.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Shadow Step, p. 81 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: requires shadow at both ends and a bonus action; dial: range is capped at 60 feet; darkness limits where the passage can be made.

rules.statement: After hitting with an unarmed strike, a level 17 Way of Shadow monk can spend 3 ki points to set harmless vibrations in the target for a number of days equal to monk level. While both are on the same plane, the monk can use an action to end the vibrations: the target makes a Constitution save, falling to 0 hit points on failure or taking 10d10 necrotic damage on success; the monk can instead end the effect harmlessly without an action, and can affect only one creature at a time.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Quivering Palm, p. 81 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one target, 3 ki, and a Constitution save; dial: delayed activation can last monk-level days; the monk must be on the same plane to trigger it.

rules.statement: A Way of the Four Elements monk learns Elemental Attunement and one other discipline at level 3, then learns one more at levels 6, 11, and 17; when learning a new discipline, they may replace one known. Some disciplines cast spells by spending ki, and from level 5 the monk can spend extra ki to raise a spell’s level, subject to a maximum set by monk level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Disciple of the Elements; Spells and Ki Points, p. 81 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: disciplines consume the monk’s ki reserve; dial: learned options, spell scaling, and maximum spend are level-limited; greater elemental effects cost more ki.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, a paladin swears an oath that permanently binds them to a path and grants features at levels 3, 7, 15, and 20, including oath spells and ways to channel divine energy. Their power can arise from commitment to justice as well as devotion to a deity.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Sacred Oath, p. 86 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the oath binds the character and grants power; dial: the passage does not specify an automatic penalty for breaking it.

rules.statement: At 1st level, a paladin can use an action to sense celestials, fiends, and undead within 60 feet until the end of their next turn, unless they are behind total cover; the paladin learns each sensed creature’s type, not its identity. The sense also detects consecrated or desecrated places and objects in range, and has a number of uses equal to 1 plus Charisma modifier, regained after a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Divine Sense, p. 85 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the sense reveals nearby supernatural types and marked places; dial: total cover blocks creature detection, and use is limited by a rest-based pool.

rules.statement: A paladin’s healing pool holds hit points equal to five times their paladin level and refills after a long rest. By touch and an action, they can spend points to restore hit points, or spend 5 points per disease cured or poison neutralized; the feature does not affect undead or constructs.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Lay on Hands, p. 85 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: healing and cleansing draw from a shared reserve; dial: the reserve is finite, and undead and constructs are excluded.

rules.statement: A paladin can prepare a number of eligible paladin spells equal to Charisma modifier plus half paladin level, rounded down, with a minimum of one; the list can be changed after a long rest, taking at least 1 minute per spell level for each prepared spell. Spell slots are spent to cast spells of that level or lower and return after a long rest; a holy symbol can serve as a focus.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Preparing and Casting Spells, pp. 85–86 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preparation determines which spells are available and slots pay for casting; dial: the list is changeable only after a long rest and casting is bounded by slots.

rules.statement: Starting at 2nd level, when a paladin hits with a melee weapon attack, they may spend a spell slot to add radiant damage: 2d8 for a 1st-level slot, plus 1d8 per slot level above first, to a maximum of 5d8. The extra damage increases by 1d8 against an undead or fiend.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Divine Smite, p. 86 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a successful melee hit can convert a spell slot into burst damage; dial: the effect requires a hit and consumes a limited slot.

rules.statement: A paladin’s oath spells are always prepared once their listed level is reached and do not count against the number of spells they may prepare. Channel Divinity provides oath-specific effects; after using it, the paladin must finish a short or long rest before using it again, and any saving throw DC equals the paladin spell save DC.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Oath Spells and Channel Divinity, p. 86 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the oath supplies fixed spells and selectable divine effects; dial: Channel Divinity is limited to one use between short or long rests.

rules.statement: At 6th level, a conscious paladin and friendly creatures within 10 feet gain a bonus to saving throws equal to the paladin’s Charisma modifier, with a minimum of +1; at 18th level the range becomes 30 feet. At 10th level, the paladin and nearby friends cannot be frightened while the paladin is conscious, with the same range increase at 18th level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Aura of Protection and Aura of Courage, p. 86 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the conscious paladin protects nearby allies; dial: the benefits require proximity and cease when the paladin is unconscious.

rules.statement: A ranger can spend a spell slot and an action to sense whether specified supernatural creature types are present within 1 mile for 1 minute per slot level, or within 6 miles in favored terrain. The sense reveals neither the creatures’ number nor location.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Primeval Awareness, p. 93 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a spell slot buys a timed, broad-area presence check; dial: favored terrain extends range, but the result gives no count or location.

rules.statement: A ranger knows two 1st-level ranger spells at 2nd level and learns more as shown on the class table; each known spell must be of a level for which they have slots. When gaining a ranger level, they may replace one known spell with another eligible ranger spell; spell slots return after a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Spell Slots and Spells Known, pp. 92–93 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: known spells define the ranger’s casting options and slots fund them; dial: replacement is limited to gaining a ranger level.

rules.statement: While traveling for at least an hour in favored terrain, a ranger’s group is not slowed by difficult terrain and cannot become lost except by magic; the ranger stays alert during other travel activities, can move stealthily at normal pace when alone, finds twice as much food when foraging, and learns the number, sizes, and passage time of tracked creatures.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Natural Explorer, p. 92 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: favored terrain improves travel, foraging, and tracking; dial: the benefits depend on terrain and, for the travel package, at least an hour of travel.

rules.statement: At 8th level, a ranger moves through nonmagical difficult terrain without extra movement and can pass through hazardous nonmagical plants without being slowed or harmed; they also have advantage on saves against magically created or manipulated plants that impede movement.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Land’s Stride, p. 93 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ordinary terrain and plants cannot impede the ranger in these ways; dial: magical plant effects are resisted rather than automatically ignored.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, the ranger gains a beast no larger than Medium and with challenge rating 1/4 or lower. The beast adds the ranger’s proficiency bonus to its AC, attacks, damage, proficient saves, and proficient skills, and its hit point maximum is the greater of its normal maximum or four times the ranger’s level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Beast Master — Ranger’s Companion (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: companion benefits scale with the ranger; dial: the restricted size and challenge rating limit; in-world reason: the bond is with a modest beast, not an unrestricted combat force.

rules.statement: The beast acts on the ranger’s initiative and takes no action unless commanded; the ranger can direct its movement verbally without an action, or spend an action to command it to Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Help. Once the ranger has Extra Attack, commanding an Attack also allows the ranger one weapon attack.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Beast Master — Ranger’s Companion (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: commands govern the companion’s actions; dial: only listed actions can be commanded this way; in-world reason: training and coordination constrain the partnership.

rules.statement: If the companion dies, the ranger can bond with another non-hostile beast over 8 hours, choosing the same kind or a different one.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Beast Master — Ranger’s Companion (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a replacement bond is possible; dial: it requires 8 hours and a non-hostile beast; in-world reason: rebuilding trust takes time.

rules.statement: At 15th level, when the ranger casts a spell targeting only themself, the spell can also affect their companion if it is within 30 feet.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Beast Master — Share Spells (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: self-directed magic can extend to the bonded beast; dial: the companion must be within 30 feet; in-world reason: the shared bond links their magical effects.

rules.statement: A Wild Magic sorcerer’s spell of 1st level or higher can trigger a surge immediately after casting: the DM may call for a d20 roll, and a result of 1 causes a roll on the surge table. Before the sorcerer regains Tides of Chaos, the DM can instead trigger a table roll immediately after such a spell, which also restores that feature.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic — Wild Magic Surge; Tides of Chaos (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the surge is possible after qualifying spells; dial: the DM decides whether to call for the initial roll and can force the later surge; in-world reason: chaotic magic is unpredictable and can reclaim control.

rules.statement: A Wild Magic sorcerer can spend their once-per-long-rest Tides of Chaos use to gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. The use returns when the DM triggers a surge under the feature’s stated condition.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic — Tides of Chaos (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one chosen roll gains advantage; dial: the benefit is limited to once per long rest unless a surge is triggered; in-world reason: bending chance invites chaotic backlash.

rules.statement: At 14th level, whenever a Wild Magic sorcerer rolls on the surge table, they roll twice and choose which result takes effect.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic — Controlled Chaos (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: two possible outcomes are generated; dial: only one is applied; in-world reason: experience gives partial control without eliminating the surges.

rules.statement: A surge-table result can impose a random effect with its own duration, target, or resolution; examples include casting a specified spell, changing a creature’s state, or restoring a resource. The table uses a d100 result, and each listed result determines the effect.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic Surge table (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve the effect assigned to the d100 result; dial: outcomes vary substantially in scope and duration; in-world reason: the source is chaotic rather than deliberately selected.

rules.statement: A sorcerer has sorcery points equal to the amount shown for their level, cannot exceed that amount, and regains all spent points after a long rest. Beginning at 2nd level, they can use a bonus action to turn points into a spell slot of 1st–5th level at the listed cost, or expend a spell slot for points equal to that slot’s level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Sorcerer — Font of Magic; Creating Spell Slots table (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: points and slots can be exchanged; dial: point capacity and slot creation are capped by level and the table; in-world reason: internal magical reserves are finite.

rules.statement: When casting, a sorcerer can apply one chosen Metamagic option, with an additional option allowed for Empowered Spell; options spend specified sorcery points to change a spell’s range, duration, casting time, damage dice, components, targets, or saving-throw difficulty. Twinned Spell applies only to a spell targeting one creature that does not have a range of self, and its point cost equals the spell’s level or 1 for a cantrip.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Sorcerer — Metamagic (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: metamagic modifies a spell at the stated cost; dial: most spells receive only one option, and each option has eligibility limits; in-world reason: reshaping magic consumes a limited personal reserve.

rules.statement: At 17th level, an Arcane Trickster can use a reaction after a creature casts a spell that targets them or includes them in its area; the caster makes a save using its spellcasting ability against the rogue’s spell save DC. On failure, the spell has no effect on the rogue, and if it is at least 1st level and of a level the rogue can cast, the rogue knows it and can cast it with spell slots for 8 hours while the caster cannot cast it; the feature recharges on a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Arcane Trickster — Spell Thief (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save transfers temporary spell knowledge and blocks the caster from using that spell; dial: it requires a reaction, applies only to qualifying spells, and lasts 8 hours; in-world reason: interception requires precise timing and temporary magical capacity.

rules.statement: For the next minute, the character has advantage on sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic Surge table (fragment), p. 104 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; brief heightened vision lasts one minute and grants no other benefit.

rules.statement: For the next minute, spells whose normal casting time is one action instead take one bonus action to cast.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic Surge table (fragment), p. 104 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the acceleration is temporary and applies only to the stated spells.

rules.statement: The character teleports up to 60 feet to a visible, unoccupied space of their choice.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic Surge table (fragment), p. 104 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; distance and destination visibility and occupancy constrain the move.

rules.statement: The character is sent to the Astral Plane until the end of their next turn, then returns to the prior space or the nearest unoccupied space if it is occupied.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic Surge table (fragment), p. 104 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; this is a short forced planar displacement with a specified return point.

rules.statement: The next damaging spell the character casts within one minute deals maximized damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic Surge table (fragment), p. 104 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the benefit is consumed by the next qualifying spell or expires after one minute.

rules.statement: A d10 determines an age change in years: an odd result makes the character younger, but not younger than one year old; an even result makes them older.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic Surge table (fragment), p. 104 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the random result changes age by a bounded amount, with a minimum age.

rules.statement: The DM places 1d6 flumphs in unoccupied spaces within 60 feet; they are frightened of the character and vanish after one minute.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic Surge table (fragment), p. 104 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; a small, temporary group appears under DM control and has a specified fear response.

rules.statement: The character regains 2d10 hit points.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic Surge table (fragment), p. 104 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; healing is limited to the rolled amount.

rules.statement: The character becomes a potted plant until the start of their next turn, is incapacitated, and is vulnerable to all damage; dropping to 0 hit points breaks the pot and restores their form.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic Surge table (fragment), p. 104 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the temporary form imposes incapacitation and increased damage susceptibility, with an early exit at 0 hit points.

rules.statement: For one minute, the character can teleport up to 20 feet as a bonus action on each of their turns.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic Surge table (fragment), p. 104 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; repeated short-range movement is limited by a one-minute duration and bonus-action use.

rules.statement: A warlock’s pact with an otherworldly patron grants class features at 1st, 6th, 10th, and 14th level; the arrangement may also require services for the patron, and the granted magic can range from lasting alterations to access to powerful spells.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Warlock: Sworn and Beholden; Otherworldly Patron, pp. 106, 108 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the patron supplies powers while the pact can impose services as its cost.

rules.statement: A wizard can prepare a number of eligible spells from their spellbook equal to Intelligence modifier plus wizard level, minimum one, and can change the prepared list after a long rest; casting a prepared spell expends a slot of its level or higher, while a ritual-tagged spell in the book can be cast as a ritual without being prepared.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wizard: Preparing and Casting Spells; Ritual Casting, p. 115 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; preparation is limited by a stat-and-level capacity, slots are expended on casting, and list changes require a long rest.

rules.statement: When you cast an abjuration spell of 1st level or higher, you can create a self-protective ward with hit points equal to twice your wizard level plus your Intelligence modifier. It lasts until you finish a long rest, absorbs damage you take before you do, and regains hit points equal to twice the level of each qualifying abjuration spell you cast; once created, you cannot create it again until you finish a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: School of Abjuration: Arcane Ward, p. 117 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ward is limited by its hit-point pool and long-rest creation limit; dial: allow a broader shield only if it has a comparable finite reserve.

rules.statement: When a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage, you can use your reaction to have your ward absorb that damage instead; if the ward is depleted, the creature takes the remainder. This is available from 6th level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: School of Abjuration: Projected Ward, p. 117 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: this redirects damage through an existing ward and spends your reaction; dial: extend the range or remove the reaction cost only with a compensating limit.

rules.statement: At 2nd level, you can use an action to create a visibly magical, dimly glowing inanimate object you have seen, in your hand or in a visible unoccupied space within 10 feet. It can be at most 3 feet on a side and 10 pounds, and disappears after an hour, when you use the feature again, or if it takes damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: School of Conjuration: Minor Conjuration, p. 117 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: creation is restricted by size, weight, prior observation, and a short duration; dial: persistent or larger creations should carry a greater cost.

rules.statement: After a long rest, a 2nd-level diviner records two d20 results. Before an attack roll, saving throw, or ability check by you or a creature you can see, you may replace its roll with one recorded result; each result is usable once, no more than one replacement occurs per turn, and unused results vanish after your next long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: School of Divination: Portent, p. 117 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: foreknowledge is represented by a small, expiring stock of fixed results; dial: more substitutions should require a larger cost or narrower targets.

rules.statement: As an action, a 2nd-level enchanter can target a creature they can see within 5 feet; if it can see or hear the enchanter and fails a Wisdom save, it is charmed, incapacitated, and has speed 0 until the end of the enchanter’s next turn. The enchanter can spend later actions to extend the effect by a turn, but it ends if the enchanter moves more than 5 feet away, the target can neither see nor hear them, or the target takes damage; that target is then immune to this feature until the enchanter finishes a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: School of Enchantment: Hypnotic Gaze, p. 118 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: close range, a saving throw, repeated action costs, and clear interruption conditions constrain control; dial: longer or stronger control should increase exposure or cost.

rules.statement: When a 2nd-level evoker casts an evocation spell affecting other creatures they can see, they can choose a number of those creatures up to 1 plus the spell’s level. Chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saves and take no damage from the spell when a successful save would normally halve it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: School of Evocation: Sculpt Spells, p. 118 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: protection applies only to a limited number of visible creatures affected by the evocation; dial: wider protection should require a larger limit or a separate cost.

rules.statement: From 14th level, when you cast a damaging wizard spell of 5th level or lower, you can make it deal maximum damage. The first use after a long rest has no adverse effect; each further use before that rest ends deals immediate necrotic damage equal to 2d12 per spell level, increasing by 1d12 per spell level for every additional use, and this damage ignores resistance and immunity.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: School of Evocation: Overchannel, p. 118 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: maximized output is restricted by spell level and escalating unavoidable self-damage; dial: reduce the injury only if another meaningful limit replaces it.

rules.statement: At 14th level, you can use an action to target one undead you can see within 60 feet; on a failed Charisma save it becomes friendly and obeys your commands until you use this feature again. Undead with Intelligence 8 or higher have advantage on the save, and one with Intelligence 12 or higher that fails can repeat the save hourly until it succeeds.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: School of Necromancy: Command Undead, p. 120 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control requires an action and a failed save, can be displaced by another use, and intelligent targets can break free; dial: permanent control needs a stronger ongoing cost.

rules.statement: At 6th level, you can spend 8 hours making a stone that grants one chosen benefit to whoever possesses it: 60-foot darkvision, 10 feet of extra speed while unencumbered, Constitution-save proficiency, or resistance to one chosen damage type from the listed options. Casting a transmutation spell of 1st level or higher lets you change its benefit while it is on your person; making another stone disables the previous one.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: School of Transmutation: Transmuter’s Stone, p. 120 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: making the item takes 8 hours, it grants only one selected benefit, and only one functioning stone is maintained; dial: stronger or multiple benefits should require greater upkeep.

rules.statement: You can maintain a second identity using its documentation, known associates, and disguises. You can also forge official papers or personal letters if you have seen an example of that document type or handwriting.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Charlatan: Feature—False Identity (p. 128) (dnd5e-phb-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the alternate identity and forgery access work as described; dial: limit recognition or forgery consequences to fit local scrutiny; in-world reason: documents and acquaintances can be checked.

rules.statement: You have a dependable contact who links you to a wider criminal network. You know local messengers and corrupt or disreputable travelers who can carry messages to and from that contact over great distances.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Criminal: Feature—Criminal Contact (p. 130) (dnd5e-phb-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: messages can reach the contact through the network; dial: vary delivery time and reliability; in-world reason: intermediaries must travel and may face danger.

rules.statement: At a place where you perform, you receive modest or comfortable lodging and food if you perform each night. In a town where you have performed, strangers who recognize you typically respond favorably.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Entertainer: Feature—By Popular Demand (p. 131) (dnd5e-phb-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: nightly performance earns basic hospitality and local goodwill; dial: vary the lodging standard with the establishment; in-world reason: the venue and audience reward the performance.

rules.statement: Commoners will generally let you hide, rest, or recover among them unless you have endangered them. They may shield you from authorities or pursuers, but will not risk their own lives for you.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Folk Hero: Feature—Rustic Hospitality (p. 132) (dnd5e-phb-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: commoners provide concealment and shelter while avoiding lethal risk; dial: set the help available to the community’s means; in-world reason: they sympathize but protect their own safety.

rules.statement: Guild members provide you lodging and food when needed and pay for your funeral. A guild may support you in a criminal accusation if a good case supports your innocence or the offense is justifiable, and may connect you with powerful political figures. Those connections can require money or magic-item donations; dues are 5 gp monthly, and missed dues must be repaid to stay in good standing.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Guild Artisan: Feature—Guild Membership (p. 134) (dnd5e-phb-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: membership grants the stated support and access; dial: determine whether a case merits guild backing and what a connection costs; in-world reason: the guild spends resources and political influence on members.

rules.statement: Your extended seclusion gave you a unique, powerful discovery, whose nature and campaign impact are determined with the DM. It may be cosmic or planar truth, an unseen site, forgotten knowledge, a historical relic, or damaging information.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Hermit: Feature—Discovery (p. 135) (dnd5e-phb-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the character has one significant discovery; dial: define its scope and consequences with the DM; in-world reason: the revelation’s importance depends on what was found.

rules.statement: Because of your noble birth, people tend to assume you belong in high society, commoners try to accommodate you, and high-born people treat you as their peer. You can obtain an audience with a local noble when needed.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Noble: Feature—Position of Privilege (p. 136) (dnd5e-phb-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: social standing grants welcome and a route to a local noble; dial: adjust access for reputation and local custom; in-world reason: status shapes how people receive you.

rules.statement: You have three retainers loyal to your family who can perform ordinary tasks, such as serving or carrying messages. They do not fight for you or enter obviously dangerous places, and leave if frequently endangered or abused.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Noble: Variant Feature—Retainers (p. 137) (dnd5e-phb-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: three loyal retainers provide mundane assistance within the stated limits; dial: track their availability and tasks; in-world reason: they serve loyally but will not accept repeated danger or mistreatment.

rules.statement: You can recall the general layout of terrain, settlements, and other nearby features. Each day, you can find food and fresh water for yourself and up to five others, provided the land has suitable resources.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Outlander: Feature—Wanderer (p. 137) (dnd5e-phb-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recall local geography and find provisions for up to six people; dial: supply nothing when the land lacks resources; in-world reason: survival depends on what the environment offers.

rules.statement: When you seek lore you do not know, you often know where or from whom it could be obtained, such as a library, university, sage, or learned creature. The information may be inaccessible or impossible to find, and uncovering deep secrets can require an adventure.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Sage: Feature—Researcher (p. 139) (dnd5e-phb-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: identify a likely source for unknown lore; dial: make the source difficult or impossible to access; in-world reason: knowledge may be secret, remote, or nonexistent.

rules.statement: In a civilized settlement, your feared reputation lets you get away with minor crimes, such as refusing a tavern bill or breaking a shop door, because most people will not report you to the authorities.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Variant Sailor: Feature—Bad Reputation (p. 140) (dnd5e-phb-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: minor offenses go unreported due to fear; dial: limit this to offenses people consider minor; in-world reason: fear discourages witnesses from involving authorities.

rules.statement: A sailor can obtain free passage for themself and companions aboard a sailing ship through a favor or good relationship. The travelers are expected to help the crew, and the ship’s route and timing are not guaranteed.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Sailor — Feature: Ship’s Passage (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: passage is available through an established favor; dial: the ship’s route and delay; the cost is service to the crew.

rules.statement: A former soldier can use recognized rank to influence lower-ranking soldiers, temporarily requisition simple equipment or horses, and usually enter friendly military camps and fortresses where that rank is accepted.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Soldier — Feature: Military Rank (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recognized rank grants limited military access; dial: recognition and willingness depend on the organization and location; the cost is reliance on past affiliation.

rules.statement: Outside combat, an urchin can lead companions between two city locations at twice their normal travel speed by using routes and passages others miss.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Urchin — Feature: City Secrets (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the urban route advantage applies; dial: the locations must be within the same city; the reason is the urchin’s learned knowledge of its hidden flow.

rules.statement: Ten silver pieces equal one gold piece, ten copper pieces equal one silver piece, an electrum piece equals five silver pieces, and a platinum piece equals ten gold pieces. A standard coin weighs about one-third of an ounce, so fifty coins weigh one pound.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 5: Equipment — Coinage; Standard Exchange Rates (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: listed exchange values and weights apply; dial: none; the cost is carrying the coins’ weight.

rules.statement: Undamaged mundane weapons, armor, and other equipment generally sell for half their purchase cost. Gems, jewelry, art objects, and trade goods retain their full market value, though unusually valuable items may require a buyer in a large community.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Selling Treasure (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the stated resale values; dial: whether a suitable buyer can be found; the cost is reduced value or time spent seeking a buyer.

rules.statement: Wearing armor without proficiency gives disadvantage on Strength- or Dexterity-involving ability checks, saving throws, and attack rolls, and prevents spellcasting. Heavy armor can reduce speed by 10 feet if its listed Strength requirement is unmet; armor marked for Stealth imposes disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Armor and Shields (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply proficiency, Strength, and Stealth penalties as listed; dial: none; the cost is impaired movement, stealth, or use of abilities.

rules.statement: A shield increases Armor Class by 2, but a creature can benefit from only one shield at a time. Armor provides its listed base Armor Class; light armor adds the wearer’s Dexterity modifier, medium armor adds it up to +2, and heavy armor does not add it or penalize a negative modifier.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Armor and Shields — Armor Class; Light Armor; Medium Armor; Heavy Armor (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the armor category’s stated Armor Class calculation; dial: armor choice; the cost is the protection and movement tradeoff inherent in the chosen armor.

rules.statement: Donning light, medium, or heavy armor takes 1, 5, or 10 minutes, respectively; removing it takes 1, 1, or 5 minutes. Help halves the time to remove armor, while putting on a shield or taking it off takes 1 action.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Getting Into and Out of Armor (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed time; dial: assistance halves removal time; the cost is time spent changing equipment.

rules.statement: A proficient wielder adds their proficiency bonus to weapon attack rolls; a nonproficient wielder does not. Ammunition weapons expend one piece per attack, and a weapon with the loading property can fire only once per action, bonus action, or reaction used to fire it, regardless of the wielder’s number of attacks.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Weapon Proficiency; Weapon Properties — Ammunition; Loading (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply proficiency and weapon-property limits; dial: none; the cost is ammunition and, for loading weapons, restricted firing rate.

rules.statement: A Large or smaller creature hit by a net is restrained unless it is formless; Huge or larger creatures are unaffected. The restrained creature, or someone within reach, can use an action to free it with a successful DC 10 Strength check; alternatively, dealing 5 slashing damage to the net (AC 10) frees the creature and destroys the net. An attack made with a net permits only one attack, regardless of how many attacks the user could normally make.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Special Weapons — Net (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the net’s size and form limits; dial: escape attempts use the stated check or damage; the cost is an action or damage to the net.

rules.statement: An improvised weapon that does not resemble a normal weapon deals 1d4 damage of a type chosen by the DM; a thrown improvised weapon has a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet. Making a melee attack with a ranged weapon, or throwing a melee weapon without the thrown property, also deals 1d4 damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Improvised Weapons (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the improvised-weapon damage and range; dial: the DM assigns an appropriate damage type and may treat a similar object as a normal weapon; the cost is reduced effectiveness.

rules.statement: A cleric or paladin can make holy water by spending 1 hour, 25 gp worth of powdered silver, and a 1st-level spell slot. A flask used against a fiend or undead deals 2d6 radiant damage on a hit.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Adventuring Gear — Holy Water (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ritual and damage use the listed costs and values; dial: the target must be a fiend or undead for the damage; the cost is silver, time, and a spell slot.

rules.statement: A tool proficiency adds the character’s proficiency bonus to an ability check made using that tool; the relevant ability depends on the task. Each artisan’s tool type and each listed gaming set or musical instrument requires its own proficiency.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Tools, p. 155 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; proficiency is a trained bonus applied only to checks that use the tool.

rules.statement: Proficiency with an herbalism kit adds the proficiency bonus to checks to identify or apply herbs, and is required to make antitoxin or healing potions. Proficiency with a poisoner’s kit adds the bonus to checks to craft or use poisons.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Tools, p. 155 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; specialized remedies and poisons require the appropriate training and equipment.

rules.statement: A basic poison can be applied as an action to one slashing or piercing weapon or up to three pieces of ammunition. A target hit must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution save or take 1d4 poison damage; the coating dries after 1 minute.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Equipment, p. 153 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the poison is a short-lived consumable coating with a save to resist its harm.

rules.statement: Oil poured onto level ground covers a 5-foot square and burns for 2 rounds once lit, dealing 5 fire damage to a creature that enters it or ends its turn there; a creature can take this damage only once per turn.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Equipment, p. 153 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
