rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the burning patch is limited by its small area, brief duration, and once-per-turn damage limit.

rules.statement: A character who drinks a healing potion, or administers it to another creature, uses an action and restores 2d4 + 2 hit points to the drinker or recipient.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Equipment, p. 153 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the potion is a consumable item that restores a fixed random amount of health.

rules.statement: A proficient navigator can chart a ship’s course and follow navigation charts, and adds the proficiency bonus to checks to avoid getting lost at sea. Proficiency with a vehicle adds the proficiency bonus to checks to control that kind of vehicle in difficult circumstances.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Tools, p. 155; Mounts and Vehicles, p. 156 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; navigation and vehicle control benefit from relevant training only when a check is called for.

rules.statement: A trained rider using a military saddle has advantage on checks to remain mounted in battle; riding an aquatic or flying mount requires an exotic saddle. Barding costs four times equivalent humanoid armor and weighs twice as much.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Mounts and Vehicles, p. 156 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; specialized riding equipment improves stability or protects an animal at substantial cost and weight.

rules.statement: At the start of each week or month, choose a lifestyle and pay its listed daily price for each day of the period; self-sufficiency costs no coin but consumes time. Survival proficiency supports a comfortable lifestyle, while practicing a profession supports a poor one.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Lifestyle Expenses, pp. 157–159; Self-Sufficiency, p. 160 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; lifestyle upkeep drains funds, while self-sufficiency trades money for time and skill.

rules.statement: Hiring a spellcaster has no standard price and may be difficult; common 1st- or 2nd-level spells in a town or city may cost 10–50 gp plus expensive material components. Higher-level spellcasting may require travel to a larger city and a service in place of payment.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Spellcasting Services, p. 160 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; access to another person’s magic depends on availability and payment, which rises with spell level.

rules.statement: When multiclassing, a character must meet the ability-score prerequisites for both current and new classes; total character level determines proficiency bonus and experience thresholds. The character gains the new class’s features and hit points for that level, but receives only its listed multiclass proficiencies.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Multiclassing, pp. 164–165 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; class capabilities can be combined, but prerequisites and reduced starting proficiencies constrain the change.

rules.statement: A multiclass spellcaster determines spells known or prepared separately for each class, using that class’s spellcasting ability and focus. Spell slots are calculated from combined caster levels using the specified fractions; a slot above the level of spells known can cast a lower-level spell, and Pact Magic slots and Spellcasting slots can cast spells from either feature.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Multiclassing: Spellcasting, p. 165 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; class-specific spell knowledge remains separate, while combined training pools slot capacity.

rules.statement: If a character gains Channel Divinity from more than one class, the available effects combine but uses do not, except where a class level explicitly grants more uses. Extra Attack features from different classes do not stack to grant more attacks, subject to a feature that expressly says otherwise; Unarmored Defense cannot be gained twice.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Multiclassing: Class Features, p. 165 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; overlapping class features have explicit limits to prevent duplicate benefits.

rules.statement: A feat may replace an Ability Score Improvement when the class grants that feature, if the optional feats rule is in use; a feat can be taken only once unless its description allows otherwise, and losing its prerequisite suspends its benefits until the prerequisite returns.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Feats, p. 166 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; special capabilities are exchanged for an ability increase and remain conditional on prerequisites.

rules.statement: Lucky provides 3 points, all restored after a long rest. After rolling an attack, ability check, or save but before its result is known, spend a point to roll another d20 and choose which die counts; when attacked, spend a point to roll a d20 and choose whether your die or the attacker’s die is used. If multiple creatures spend points on the same roll, their points cancel and no extra dice are rolled.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Lucky, p. 168 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: cap uses at 3 points per long rest; improbable luck has a scarce, recoverable cost.

rules.statement: A creature hidden from another creature can remain undiscovered unless the latter actively searches and wins a Wisdom (Perception) contest against the hider’s Dexterity (Stealth) check; a creature that can see the hider, or that gives away its position by making noise, cannot be hidden from it. For creatures not searching, compare the Stealth result with passive Perception, calculated as 10 plus applicable modifiers, with 5 added for advantage or subtracted for disadvantage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Hiding, p. 177 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: hiding depends on line of sight, noise, and observers’ awareness, rather than granting automatic invisibility.

rules.statement: The Skulker feat lets a Dexterity 13-or-higher character attempt to hide while only lightly obscured, avoid revealing their position when a ranged weapon attack misses while they are hidden, and make sight-based Perception checks in dim light without disadvantage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Skulker, p. 170 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: concealment improves only under specified lighting and attack conditions; it does not make the user undetectable.

rules.statement: Magic Initiate grants two chosen cantrips and one chosen 1st-level spell from the same eligible class list. The spell can be cast once at its lowest level, with another use available after a long rest; the selected class determines the spellcasting ability.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Magic Initiate, p. 168 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: the granted 1st-level spell is limited to one use per long rest, while cantrips are separately learned.

rules.statement: Ritual Caster requires Intelligence or Wisdom 13 or higher and grants a ritual book containing two chosen 1st-level ritual spells from one eligible class. Casting one requires holding the book; a qualifying written ritual can be copied into it if its level is no higher than half the character’s level rounded up, at a cost of 2 hours and 50 gp per spell level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Ritual Caster, p. 170 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: ritual access depends on a carried book, eligible written spells, time, and material expense.

rules.statement: Spell attack ranges are doubled by Spell Sniper, and the character’s ranged spell attacks ignore half and three-quarters cover. The feat also teaches one attack-roll cantrip from an eligible class list, using that class’s spellcasting ability; it requires the ability to cast at least one spell.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Spell Sniper, p. 170 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: range and cover benefits apply to defined spell attacks, and the added cantrip requires prior spellcasting.

rules.statement: A proficient spellcaster with War Caster has advantage on Constitution saves made to maintain concentration after taking damage, can perform somatic spell components while holding weapons or a shield, and can use a reaction to cast a one-action spell at a single creature that provokes an opportunity attack. The feat requires the ability to cast at least one spell.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: War Caster, p. 171 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: the reaction spell is limited to one action and a single provoking creature; the feat requires existing spellcasting.

rules.statement: To make an ability check, roll a d20, add the relevant ability modifier and applicable bonuses or penalties, and succeed if the total meets or exceeds the task’s DC. Typical DCs range from 5 for very easy tasks to 30 for nearly impossible ones; the DM sets the relevant ability and DC.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Ability Checks, p. 175 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: uncertainty is resolved against a task-specific difficulty, with the DM setting the ability and target.

rules.statement: For a contest, both participants make appropriate ability checks and compare totals; the higher total succeeds or prevents the other participant’s success. A tie leaves the situation as it was.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Contests, p. 175 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: opposed effort is resolved by comparative checks, and a tie preserves the existing state.

rules.statement: A passive check is 10 plus the modifiers that normally apply to the check, with 5 added for advantage or subtracted for disadvantage. It can represent repeated activity or let the DM determine an outcome without rolling dice.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Passive Checks, p. 176 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: passive scores model routine or secretly assessed tasks without a new die roll.

rules.statement: When a group makes an ability check, every member rolls; the group succeeds if at least half succeed, and otherwise the group fails. When characters help with a task that benefits from teamwork, the leader or character with the highest relevant ability modifier makes the check with advantage, but a helper must be capable of attempting the task alone.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Working Together; Group Checks, p. 176 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: group outcomes depend on a majority, while assistance is limited to tasks where cooperation can help.

rules.statement: A saving throw is a d20 roll plus the relevant ability modifier and any applicable bonuses or penalties; proficiency adds the proficiency bonus when the character is proficient in that save. The effect sets the DC and specifies what success or failure does; success usually avoids harm or reduces it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Saving Throws, p. 180 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: saves resist specified threats using an effect-defined DC and outcome; no universal success result is imposed.

rules.statement: A spellcaster must know or prepare a spell, or access it through a magic item, before casting; the number kept ready depends on character level. Casting in armor requires proficiency with that armor.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 10: Spellcasting — Known and Prepared Spells; Casting in Armor (pp. 202–203) (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; readiness and armor proficiency restrict who can cast.

rules.statement: Casting a spell usually expends a slot of its level or higher; a long rest restores expended slots. A cantrip requires no slot or advance preparation, and a ritual takes 10 minutes longer, uses no slot, and cannot be cast at a higher level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 10: Spellcasting — Spell Slots; Cantrips; Rituals (pp. 202–203) (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; casting is limited by slots, time, and access to ritual casting.

rules.statement: A spell cast with a bonus action requires that action on the caster’s turn; that turn, the caster cannot cast another spell except an action-time cantrip. A spell readied for release must have a casting time of one action and requires concentration; if concentration breaks before release, it dissipates.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 10: Spellcasting — Casting Time; Ready (pp. 193, 203) (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; action economy and concentration constrain rapid or delayed casting.

rules.statement: A spell with a casting time longer than one action or reaction requires the caster to spend an action casting on each turn and maintain concentration; if concentration breaks, the spell fails without expending a slot, and recasting requires starting over.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 10: Spellcasting — Longer Casting Times (p. 203) (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; extended casting is vulnerable to interruption but does not consume a slot on failure.

rules.statement: A caster cannot concentrate on two spells at once; casting another concentration spell, becoming incapacitated, or dying ends the current spell. Damage requires a Constitution save to maintain concentration, with DC 10 or half the damage, whichever is higher; each separate damage source requires a separate save.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 10: Spellcasting — Concentration (pp. 203–204) (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; maintaining an ongoing effect costs attention and can be disrupted.

rules.statement: A spell requires its listed verbal, somatic, and material components; lacking any required component prevents casting. A component pouch or focus can replace listed materials unless a cost is specified, and a consumed component must be supplied for every casting.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 10: Spellcasting — Components (p. 204) (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; speech, a free hand, or specified materials can limit access to magic.

rules.statement: A spell that requires concentration ends when concentration is lost, and the caster can end it at any time without an action. A spell’s instantaneous effects cannot be dispelled because the magic lasts only an instant.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 10: Spellcasting — Duration; Concentration (pp. 204–205) (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; continuing effects depend on concentration, while completed instantaneous effects persist.

rules.statement: A spell generally needs a clear path to its target and cannot target something behind total cover; an area placed at an unseen point blocked by an obstruction begins on the near side. Area effects spread in straight lines, and total cover blocks a location from the area.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 10: Spellcasting — Targets; A Clear Path to the Target; Areas of Effect (pp. 205–206) (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; obstructions limit targeting and the reach of area effects.

rules.statement: A target of a spell may make the saving throw specified by that spell, using the named ability; the spell defines the result of success or failure. The caster’s spell save DC is 8 plus spellcasting ability modifier, proficiency bonus, and any special modifiers.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 10: Spellcasting — Saving Throws (p. 206) (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; targets can resist according to the spell’s stated save and the caster’s capability.

rules.statement: A spell attack hits if its attack roll meets or exceeds the target’s AC; its attack bonus is the caster’s spellcasting ability modifier plus proficiency bonus. A natural 20 hits regardless of AC and is critical; a natural 1 misses regardless of modifiers.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 10: Spellcasting — Attack Rolls (p. 206); Making an Attack (p. 195) (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; spell attacks use a bounded accuracy check with fixed extreme outcomes.

rules.statement: Effects of different spells combine while their durations overlap; repeated castings of the same spell do not combine, and only the strongest effect, such as the highest bonus, applies.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 10: Spellcasting — Combining Magical Effects (p. 206) (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; overlapping magic is limited to prevent repeated identical effects from accumulating.

rules.statement: A creature can be grappled only by a successful contested Strength (Athletics) check, using a free hand and a target no more than one size larger within reach; the target can escape with an action and a successful contested Athletics or Acrobatics check. The grappler can release it without an action, and dragging it halves the grappler’s speed unless it is at least two sizes smaller.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Grappling (pp. 196–197) (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; restraint requires a contest, occupies a hand, and limits movement.

rules.statement: When effects with the same name overlap in duration, a creature receives the benefit only once; for example, two overlapping Bless spells do not grant two bonus dice.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: p. 207, spellcasting rules (preceding “The Weave of Magic”) (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: none; duplicate castings do not multiply the same spell’s benefit.

rules.statement: Raw magic cannot be shaped directly by mortals: spellcasters use a magical interface to reach it, and magic fails in an area where that interface is torn. Divination can reveal the interface, while dispelling smooths it and antimagic redirects magic around an affected area.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: The Weave of Magic, p. 207 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: access requires an interface; a damaged interface prevents magical effects.

rules.statement: An antimagic sphere moves with its caster and suppresses spells, magical effects, and magic-item properties inside it; spells cannot be cast there, and magical travel fails if the sphere is either its origin or destination. Portals and extradimensional openings there close temporarily, while summoned or magically created creatures and objects disappear until the sphere no longer covers their space.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Antimagic Field, pp. 213–214 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the moving field suppresses magic and blocks magical travel within its boundary.

rules.statement: Arcane Gate opens two linked, visible-from-one-side portals, each 10 feet across, at two ground points the caster can see: one within 10 feet and the other within 500 feet. Creatures and objects entering an active side exit the other portal; the caster can rotate the portals’ active sides as a bonus action, and the portals last for concentration up to 10 minutes.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Arcane Gate, pp. 214–215 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: passage is limited to the linked locations and the spell’s concentration duration.

rules.statement: Astral Projection sends the caster and up to eight willing nearby creatures to the Astral Plane, consuming for each participant a gem worth at least 1,000 gp and a carved silver bar worth at least 100 gp. Their physical bodies remain unconscious and suspended; each astral form is tethered by a silver cord, and severing that cord kills its owner. The travelers can use Astral Plane portals to reach other planes, with their bodies and possessions following the cord; dismissing the spell, dispelling it, or either form reaching 0 hit points ends an individual’s projection.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Astral Projection, p. 215 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: costly components and a vulnerable tether constrain travel; severance is fatal.

rules.statement: Banishment sends a creature that fails its Charisma save away from the caster’s plane. A creature native to that plane is held incapacitated in a harmless demiplane and returns when the spell ends; one native to another plane returns to its home plane, and returns only if the spell ends before one minute has passed.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Banishment, p. 216 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: return depends on the target’s home plane and how long the spell persists.

rules.statement: Animal Friendship can charm a visible beast within 30 feet that can see and hear the caster, if its Intelligence is below 4 and it fails a Wisdom save; the charm lasts 24 hours. Harm by the caster or an ally ends it, and casting with a slot above 1st level adds one eligible beast per slot level above 1st.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Animal Friendship, p. 212 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the effect is limited by target type, a save, a fixed duration, and harm.

rules.statement: Animate Dead raises one Small or Medium humanoid corpse as a zombie or a pile of its bones as a skeleton. The caster can mentally command creations within 60 feet as a bonus action; control lasts 24 hours, and casting again before it expires maintains control of up to four such creatures. A slot above 3rd level animates or reasserts control over two additional undead per slot level above 3rd.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Animate Dead, pp. 212–213 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: control requires repeated casting every 24 hours and depends on available remains.

rules.statement: Alter Self transforms the caster for up to one hour while concentration lasts, allowing aquatic adaptation, appearance changes that preserve basic shape and size, or a magical natural weapon that grants proficient unarmed strikes dealing 1d6 damage and +1 to attack and damage rolls. During the spell, the caster can use an action to replace the chosen option with another.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Alter Self, pp. 211–212 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the transformation is temporary, concentration-bound, and limited by the chosen option’s rules.

rules.statement: Arcane Lock wards a touched closed entryway until dispelled, letting designated creatures open it normally; a chosen spoken password suppresses the ward for one minute. Otherwise the entryway is impassable until broken, dispelled, or suppressed, and its break or lock-picking DC increases by 10; Knock suppresses the ward for 10 minutes, and the spell consumes gold dust worth at least 25 gp.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Arcane Lock, p. 215 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: access is restricted, but designated users, a password, Knock, or force can bypass the ward.

rules.statement: Augury provides an omen about a specific planned course of action within the next 30 minutes, with the possible results distinguishing good, bad, mixed, or neither result. Each casting after the first before the caster completes a long rest has a cumulative 25 percent chance of a random reading.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Augury, p. 216 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the guidance is limited to a near-term plan and repeated use risks unreliable readings.

rules.statement: A blade barrier can form as a straight wall up to 100 feet long or a ring up to 60 feet across; it lasts up to 10 minutes while you concentrate. Its space is difficult terrain and gives three-quarters cover from behind it, and a creature entering it for the first time on a turn or starting its turn there takes 6d10 slashing damage, or half on a successful Dexterity save.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Blade Barrier, p. 220 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the wall’s shape and placement; the caster must maintain concentration.

rules.statement: Until the end of your next turn, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from weapon attacks.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Blade Ward, p. 220 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the short duration; the protection applies only to weapon damage of the listed kinds.

rules.statement: Bless affects up to three creatures within 30 feet for up to 1 minute while you concentrate. Each affected creature may add 1d4 to each attack roll or saving throw it makes before the spell ends; each slot level above 1st adds one target.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Bless, p. 220 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the number of recipients; the effect requires concentration and consumes a spell slot.

rules.statement: Blight deals 8d8 necrotic damage to a visible creature within 30 feet, halved on a successful Constitution save; undead and constructs are unaffected. Plants make that save with disadvantage and take maximum damage, while a nonmagical plant that is not a creature simply withers and dies; each slot level above 4th adds 1d8 damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Blight, p. 220 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the target category; the spell is ineffective against undead and constructs.

rules.statement: For up to 1 minute, roll a d20 at the end of each of your turns; on 11 or higher you shift from your current plane to the Ethereal Plane. At the start of your next turn, or when the spell ends while you are there, you return to a visible unoccupied space within 10 feet of where you vanished, or to the nearest such space if none is available nearby; while ethereal, you can see and hear the originating plane within 60 feet but interact only with creatures there.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Blink, p. 220 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the chance of shifting; each shift is temporary and return space can be constrained.

rules.statement: A clone grown in a sealed vessel reaches maturity after 120 days and remains inert indefinitely if undisturbed. If the original later dies, its free and willing soul transfers to the mature clone, which has the original’s body, memories, personality, and abilities but none of its equipment; the original remains cannot then be restored to life.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Clone, p. 222 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the delayed backup; it requires a costly vessel, consumed material, and a willing, free soul.

rules.statement: A 5-foot cube of spinning daggers lasts up to 1 minute while you concentrate; a creature takes 4d4 slashing damage when it enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there. Each slot level above 2nd adds 2d4 damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Cloud of Daggers, p. 222 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the fixed area; the damage is limited to creatures entering or remaining in it.

rules.statement: A cloudkill creates a 20-foot-radius, heavily obscuring poisonous fog for up to 10 minutes while you concentrate; strong wind disperses it and ends the spell. Creatures entering it for the first time on a turn or starting their turn there take 5d8 poison damage, half on a successful Constitution save, and the fog moves 10 feet away from you at the start of each of your turns; each slot level above 5th adds 1d8 damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Cloudkill, p. 222 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the wind and drift; the cloud harms even creatures that do not breathe.

rules.statement: A creature that fails a Wisdom save against charm person is charmed for up to 1 hour and regards the caster as a friendly acquaintance; the spell ends early if the caster or their companions harm it. The target has advantage on its save if the caster or companions are fighting it, and when the spell ends it knows it was charmed.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Charm Person, p. 221 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the duration and hostile-action break; the target can resist, especially during a fight.

rules.statement: Command makes a creature that understands the caster’s language obey a one-word instruction on its next turn if it fails a Wisdom save; it has no effect on undead or on a directly harmful command. The spell ends if the creature cannot comply, and higher-level slots can include one additional target per level above 1st, with targets within 30 feet of one another.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Command, p. 224 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the command’s scope; language, comprehension, target type, and direct harm limit it.

rules.statement: Conjure animals summons friendly fey-shaped beasts into visible unoccupied spaces within 60 feet, choosing one creature of challenge rating 2 or lower, two of rating 1 or lower, four of rating 1/2 or lower, or eight of rating 1/4 or lower. They act as a group on their own turn, follow verbal commands without using your action, and otherwise defend themselves; they disappear at 0 hit points or when concentration ends, and specified higher-level slots multiply their number.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Conjure Animals, p. 226 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the number and strength of creatures; control lasts only while concentration holds.

rules.statement: If concentration on conjure elemental is broken, the summoned elemental does not disappear: it becomes hostile, cannot be dismissed by the caster, and disappears one hour after being summoned. The spell otherwise calls a friendly elemental of challenge rating 5 or lower from a suitable area, lasting up to 1 hour while concentration continues; each slot level above 5th raises its maximum challenge rating by 1.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Conjure Elemental, p. 225 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the loss-of-control consequence; breaking concentration turns a summoned ally hostile rather than ending its presence.

rules.statement: Contingency stores one spell of 5th level or lower that you can cast in one action and that can target you, paying the slots for both spells when cast; the stored spell triggers immediately the first time its specified circumstance occurs, whether or not you want it to. It lasts up to 10 days, only one can be active on you, and it ends if its costly material component is no longer on your person.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Contingency, p. 227 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the trigger circumstance; prepayment, a single active contingency, and keeping its component impose limits.

rules.statement: When you try to interrupt a creature within 60 feet as it casts a spell, a spell of 3rd level or lower fails automatically; for a higher-level spell, make a spellcasting-ability check against DC 10 plus its level, and the spell fails on success. Using a slot at least as high as the interrupted spell makes it fail automatically.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Counterspell, p. 229 (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: interruption requires timing and a spell resource; dial: a sufficiently high slot removes the uncertainty.

rules.statement: You can animate up to three eligible humanoid corpses as ghouls at night, using the specified grave materials and a 150 gp onyx per corpse. You command them mentally as a bonus action within 120 feet; control lasts 24 hours, and recasting before it expires can renew control, with higher-level slots allowing different or larger groups.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Create Undead, p. 229 (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control is temporary and consumes costly materials; dial: higher slots buy a larger or more capable controlled group.

rules.statement: A 2nd-level-or-lower magical light overlapping the darkness is dispelled; covering the darkness's source with an opaque object blocks it. Conversely, daylight dispels overlapping darkness created by a spell of 3rd level or lower.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Darkness; Daylight, p. 230 (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: area effects interact by spell level; dial: stronger darkness or light can resist the stated opposing effect.

rules.statement: Death ward lasts 8 hours and is consumed the first time damage would reduce its target to 0 hit points, leaving the target at 1 instead; it also negates one effect that would kill the target instantly without damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Death Ward, p. 230 (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one-use protection expires when it prevents a fatal outcome; dial: the ward's duration and single trigger limit its reliability.

rules.statement: A delayed blast fireball accumulates damage while you concentrate: it starts at 12d6 and gains 1d6 at the end of each of your turns before detonation. When it ends, it explodes in a 20-foot-radius sphere; a creature touching the bead can trigger it, and a successful save lets that creature throw it up to 40 feet before it explodes on impact.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Delayed Blast Fireball, p. 231 (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: waiting increases damage but risks losing control of the bead; dial: more delay raises the eventual harm.

rules.statement: You can create a doorway to a new or known demiplane, a 30-foot-per-side room, for up to 1 hour. When the spell ends, the doorway vanishes and creatures and objects inside remain trapped there.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Demiplane, p. 232 (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the destination is enclosed and the exit is temporary; dial: choosing a known demiplane trades isolation for access to an established space.

rules.statement: For up to 10 minutes, you can sense magic within 30 feet and use an action to see an aura and learn its school on a visible magical creature or object. A foot of stone, an inch of common metal, thin lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt blocks the sensing.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Detect Magic, p. 231 (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sensing is local and concentration-limited; dial: barriers provide a straightforward way to conceal magic.

rules.statement: You can teleport yourself up to 500 feet to a place you see, visualize, or describe, bringing carried objects and one willing nearby creature of your size or smaller. If the destination is occupied, the spell fails and each traveler takes 4d6 force damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Dimension Door, p. 234 (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: precise short-range travel avoids the route but not destination risk; dial: carrying another traveler increases the benefit without removing collision danger.

rules.statement: For up to 1 minute, you can read a creature's surface thoughts if it is within 30 feet and has Intelligence above 3 and speaks a language. Probing deeper requires a Wisdom save; failure reveals reasoning, emotions, and a prominent concern, while success ends the spell, and the target knows you probed.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Detect Thoughts, pp. 232–234 (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: deeper access risks ending the effect and alerts the target; dial: surface thoughts are less intrusive but less informative.

rules.statement: A creature that fails its Wisdom save against a dominate spell is charmed and can receive telepathic commands while you are conscious and on the same plane. You may use an action for precise control through your next turn; whenever the target takes damage it saves again, ending the spell on success.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Dominate Beast; Dominate Monster; Dominate Person, pp. 235–236 (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control depends on concentration and can be broken by damage-induced saves; dial: precise control costs your action.

rules.statement: Etherealness lets you enter the Border Ethereal for up to 8 hours, where you can move through objects and interact only with beings on that plane. When it ends, you return to your originating plane; if that space is occupied, you are moved to the nearest open space and take force damage equal to twice the distance moved in feet.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Etherealness, pp. 237–238 (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: crossing planes grants passage through ordinary obstacles but makes return placement hazardous; dial: extra travel time for vertical movement limits mobility.

rules.statement: A divination asks one question about a specific goal, event, or activity expected within 7 days, and the DM gives a truthful reply that may be brief or cryptic and does not account for changing circumstances. Before your next long rest, each casting after the first adds a cumulative 25% chance of a random reading.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Divination, p. 234 (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: guidance is truthful but incomplete; dial: repeated questions increase the chance of an unreliable answer.

rules.statement: You turn visible raw materials within 120 feet into an object made from the same material, up to Large size in most materials or Medium size for minerals; the result’s quality depends on the input. You cannot make creatures or magic items, and items requiring fine craftsmanship require the relevant artisan-tool proficiency.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Fabricate (dnd5e-phb-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: material quantity, size, and craft-skill limits; the maker cannot conjure resources or bypass expertise.

rules.statement: A creature that fails its save in the area becomes outlined, cannot benefit from invisibility, and is easier to hit: attacks against it have advantage if the attacker can see it. Objects in the area are outlined as well.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Faerie Fire (dnd5e-phb-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: failed save and concentration; the outline reveals targets but does not itself let an attacker see them through obstacles.

rules.statement: A creature that fails its save in the cone drops what it holds and becomes frightened. On its turns it must Dash away by the safest available route; if it ends a turn unable to see the caster, it can save again to end the effect on itself.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Fear (dnd5e-phb-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: failed save, line of sight, and concentration; the target’s fear constrains its actions but can end when it breaks sight and succeeds on a save.

rules.statement: A failed Intelligence save sets the target’s Intelligence and Charisma to 1 and prevents it from casting spells, activating magic items, understanding language, or intelligibly communicating. It can retry after each 30 days; success ends the effect, as can greater restoration, heal, or wish.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Feeblemind (p. 241) (dnd5e-phb-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: failed save and long recovery interval; profound cognitive loss persists unless a rare remedy ends it.

rules.statement: You summon one spirit in a chosen animal form; it obeys commands but cannot attack. At 0 hit points it disappears and returns only when you cast the spell again; you can dismiss it to a pocket dimension or end its service, and you cannot have more than one familiar at once. Within 100 feet, you can communicate telepathically or use an action to perceive through its senses until your next turn, sacrificing your own sight and hearing during that time; it can also deliver your touch-range spell using its reaction.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Find Familiar (p. 241) (dnd5e-phb-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: one companion slot and a costly consumed offering; remote perception temporarily disables the caster’s own senses.

rules.statement: For up to a day, you know the distance and direction to a familiar, fixed destination on your current plane and automatically identify the shortest, most direct route at each path choice. It fails for another plane, a moving destination, or a destination that is not specific; it does not identify the safest route.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Find the Path (p. 242) (dnd5e-phb-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: requires familiarity, a location token, same-plane travel, and concentration; the information optimizes distance, not safety.

rules.statement: You ward up to 40,000 square feet of floor area to a height of 30 feet for a day, blocking teleportation, portals, and planar access into it. Chosen creature types that enter for the first time on a turn or start their turn there take 5d10 radiant or necrotic damage; a spoken password prevents that damage. Casting it daily in the same place for 30 days makes it last until dispelled.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Forbiddance (p. 244) (dnd5e-phb-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: costly ritual setup, bounded area, and duration; the ward protects a place but authorized password speakers bypass its damage.

rules.statement: You open a 5-to-20-foot portal between a visible space and a precise location on another plane; creatures can cross only through its front, and the portal lasts while you concentrate, up to a minute. Naming a specific creature on another plane instead opens the portal near it and draws it through; planar rulers can prevent the portal from opening in their presence or domain.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Gate (p. 245) (dnd5e-phb-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: a high-value material component and brief concentration duration; a named target is transported without being controlled.

rules.statement: A creature that understands your command and fails its save is charmed for 30 days and takes 5d10 psychic damage when it directly disobeys, at most once per day. The command cannot require certain death; a suicidal command ends the spell, and specified restorative magic or the caster can end it early. Higher-level slots extend the duration to a year or, at the highest level, until ended by the listed remedies.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Geas (p. 246) (dnd5e-phb-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the target must understand the command and fail a save; disobedience costs health, while a suicidal order breaks the binding.

rules.statement: You can place a nearly invisible glyph on a surface or fixed object, define its trigger and exclusions, and choose either an area burst dealing 5d8 chosen elemental damage on a failed save or a stored prepared spell of 3rd level or lower. The glyph ends when triggered; moving its inscribed object more than 10 feet breaks it without triggering, and greater spell slots increase the burst or storage limit.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Glyph of Warding (pp. 246–247) (dnd5e-phb-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: one-hour inscription, consumed costly materials, and a fixed object location; the trap is potent but vulnerable to moving its container.

rules.statement: A creature you touch becomes mist, can fly 10 feet, pass through narrow gaps, and hover; it resists nonmagical damage and has advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saves. It cannot speak, manipulate or use carried objects, attack, or cast spells, and the transformation ends at 0 hit points.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Gaseous Form (p. 245) (dnd5e-phb-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: willing target and concentration; passage through gaps comes at the cost of ordinary physical interaction and offense.

rules.statement: A willing creature you touch gains double speed, a +2 AC bonus, advantage on Dexterity saves, and one additional restricted action on each turn for up to a minute. When the effect ends, the target cannot move or take actions until after its next turn.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Haste (p. 251; excerpt ends mid-entry) (dnd5e-phb-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: concentration and a debilitating recovery turn; the burst of speed and action economy has a sharp exhaustion-like aftermath.

rules.statement: A 6th-level casting restores 70 hit points to one visible creature within 60 feet and ends its blindness, deafness, and diseases; it does nothing to constructs or undead. Each slot level above 6th adds 10 hit points restored.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Heal, p. 251 (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; healing is limited by the target types and the spell slot spent.

rules.statement: A 2nd-level casting heats one visible manufactured metal object within 60 feet while concentration lasts, up to 1 minute. Contact deals 2d8 fire damage on casting and again when the caster uses a bonus action on later turns; a creature holding or wearing it must save or drop it, and otherwise has disadvantage on attacks and ability checks until its next turn. Higher slots add 1d8 damage per level above 2nd.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Heat Metal, p. 251 (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; repeated damage requires concentration and a bonus action, and the target must be metal.

rules.statement: A 1st-level curse on a visible creature within 90 feet adds 1d6 necrotic damage whenever the caster hits it with an attack and gives it disadvantage on checks using one chosen ability. If the target reaches 0 hit points, the caster can use a later bonus action to curse another creature; remove curse ends the effect, while higher slots can extend concentration to 8 or 24 hours.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Hex, p. 252 (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the curse takes concentration and ends early if removed.

rules.statement: A creature that fails its Wisdom save against hold monster is paralyzed for up to 1 minute while the caster concentrates, but can repeat the save at the end of each turn to end the effect. Undead are unaffected; slots above 5th can add one target per slot level, with targets within 30 feet of one another.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Hold Monster, p. 252 (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; a successful save or later repeated save prevents or ends control.

rules.statement: A 3rd-level casting opens a 20-foot-radius sphere of darkness and bitter cold within 150 feet for up to 1 minute, requiring concentration. Light cannot illuminate it and creatures fully inside are blinded; the area is difficult terrain, deals 2d6 cold damage to a creature starting its turn there, and may deal 2d6 acid damage to one ending its turn there if it fails a Dexterity save.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Hunger of Hadar, p. 252 (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the hazardous area is temporary and requires concentration.

rules.statement: A 3rd-level pattern affects creatures in a 30-foot cube that see it: each must make a Wisdom save or become charmed, incapacitated, and unable to move for up to 1 minute while the caster concentrates. Damage to an affected creature or another creature using an action to shake it ends the effect for that creature.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Hypnotic Pattern, p. 253 (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the effect is limited to creatures that see the pattern and ends through harm or intervention.

rules.statement: A 1st-level ritual identifies a touched magic object’s properties, use, attunement requirement, charges, current spells, and—if spell-created—which spell made it; alternatively, touching a creature reveals its current spells. Casting takes 1 minute and requires a pearl worth at least 100 gp and an owl feather.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Identify, p. 253 (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the caster must maintain touch during a minute-long casting and provide a valuable pearl.

rules.statement: A 9th-level imprisonment can bind a visible creature within 30 feet that fails a Wisdom save, using a chosen form of confinement; the target no longer needs food, water, or air, does not age, and cannot be located or perceived by divination. The caster may set a reasonable release condition; otherwise only a 9th-level dispel magic ends it, and reusing the same special component frees its previous prisoner.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Imprisonment, pp. 253–254 (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; confinement requires an expensive component, a failed save, and a narrow release method.

rules.statement: A 3rd-level magic circle creates a 10-foot-radius, 20-foot-high cylinder for 1 hour, choosing celestials, elementals, fey, fiends, or undead. Chosen creatures cannot enter by nonmagical means and must pass a Charisma save to enter by teleportation or planar travel; they have disadvantage on attacks against those inside, who cannot be charmed, frightened, or possessed by them. The caster may reverse the protection to prevent chosen creatures from leaving.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Magic Circle, p. 257 (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the circle is temporary, consumes costly materials, and protects against selected creature types only.

rules.statement: Magic jar moves the caster’s soul into a valuable container while the caster’s body lies catatonic; from the container the caster can project up to 100 feet to return to the body or attempt to possess a visible humanoid. A failed Charisma save lets the caster control the host while the host’s soul is trapped in the jar; destroying the jar or ending the spell returns souls only if their bodies are alive and within 100 feet, otherwise they die.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Magic Jar, p. 258 (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; possession risks death for both souls if the jar, body, or return distance fails.

rules.statement: A 2nd-level knock opens one visible object held shut by an ordinary lock, obstruction, or bar; if it has multiple locks, only one is opened. Against arcane lock it suppresses the spell for 10 minutes, and casting makes a knock audible up to 300 feet away.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Knock, p. 255 (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the spell is conspicuous and does not remove multiple locks at once.

rules.statement: A 4th-level secret chest stores a touched chest and its contents—up to 12 cubic feet of nonliving material—on the Ethereal Plane; an action touching the replica recalls it within 5 feet, and another action touching both sends it back. After 60 days, there is a cumulative 5% daily chance the effect ends; recasting, destroying the replica, or dismissing the spell also ends it, and a chest left on the Ethereal Plane is irretrievably lost.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Leomund’s Secret Chest, p. 255 (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; storage depends on a costly chest and replica and risks permanent loss over time.

rules.statement: A caster can alter one visible creature’s memories of an event from the last 24 hours that lasted no more than 10 minutes, but first the target must fail a Wisdom save (with advantage if the caster is fighting it). While charmed and incapacitated, the target must understand the caster’s spoken account; damage or another spell interrupts the process, and remove curse or greater restoration restores the true memory. Higher-level slots extend how far back the event may be: 7 days at 6th, 30 days at 7th, 1 year at 8th, or any time in the past at 9th.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Modify Memory, p. 262 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the target’s memory susceptibility; the target’s save, understanding, and possible restoration constrain the alteration.

rules.statement: A caster may ask a known cosmic entity to send a loyal celestial, elemental, or fiend to help, but the arrival is not compelled to serve. The caster and creature must bargain; suggested payment is 100 gp per minute, 1,000 gp per hour, or 10,000 gp per day (up to 10 days), with adjustments for danger, safety, or alignment, and the creature returns home when its service ends or bargaining fails.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Planar Ally, p. 266 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the bargain’s price and terms; the entity retains the choice to refuse and may demand payment, a sacrifice, or a quest.

rules.statement: A caster can attempt to bind a nearby celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend after a one-hour casting and a consumed jewel worth at least 1,000 gp; a failed Charisma save makes the creature serve for 24 hours. It must follow instructions to the best of its ability but may twist a hostile caster’s wording; higher-level slots extend service to 10 days, 30 days, 180 days, or a year and a day.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Planar Binding, p. 266 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the binding’s duration and resistance; the caster pays a costly consumed jewel and risks a hostile servant exploiting ambiguous orders.

rules.statement: A caster can transport themself and up to eight willing creatures holding hands to another plane, arriving at a broadly named destination or at a known teleportation-circle sequence; an overcrowded circle places excess travelers nearby. Alternatively, a successful melee spell attack followed by a failed Charisma save sends an unwilling creature to a random location on a specified plane, leaving it to find its own way back.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Plane Shift, p. 267 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial destination precision; plane travel requires a costly, plane-attuned forked rod, while forced travelers face the cost of finding their own way home.

rules.statement: A caster creates an extradimensional dwelling for 24 hours, with a single chosen entrance that designated creatures may use while it is open; the caster can open or close it within 30 feet. Its floor plan is limited to 50 ten-foot cubes, and its created furnishings and servants cannot leave; when the effect ends, occupants are expelled into open spaces nearest the entrance.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Mordenkainen’s Magnificent Mansion, pp. 261–263 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the dwelling’s size and access; entry depends on the caster’s designation and the space ends after a day, ejecting occupants.

rules.statement: A caster wards a cube between 5 and 100 feet per side for 24 hours, choosing any combination of barriers that stop sound, block vision, prevent divination sensors from appearing or passing through, prevent divination targeting, stop teleportation, or block planar travel. Recasting on the same location daily for a year makes the ward permanent; a higher-level slot increases the maximum side length by 100 feet per level above 4th.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Mordenkainen’s Private Sanctum, p. 263 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the ward’s size and selected barriers; maintaining a permanent ward demands daily recasting at the same place for a year.

rules.statement: A caster can transform a visible creature into a beast whose challenge rating does not exceed the target’s rating or level; an unwilling target may resist with a Wisdom save, while a shapechanger succeeds automatically. The beast’s statistics, including mental ability scores, replace the target’s, its equipment becomes unusable, and the effect lasts up to an hour or until the target reaches 0 hit points or dies, with its prior hit points restored on return and excess damage carried over.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Polymorph, p. 267 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the permitted beast strength; the form restricts actions and equipment use, and harm can carry back to the original body.

rules.statement: A caster creates a 5-foot-radius, 40-foot-high beam for up to a minute; a creature entering it for the first time on a turn or starting there makes a Constitution save, taking 2d10 radiant damage or half on success. A shapechanger has disadvantage on that save and, on failure, reverts to its original form and cannot change again until it leaves the light; the caster can move the beam up to 60 feet as an action on later turns.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Moonbeam, p. 260 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the beam’s movement and duration; creatures must face repeated exposure while the caster concentrates and redirects it.

rules.statement: A caster can enclose a Large-or-smaller creature or object in an immobile, damage-immune sphere of force for up to a minute; an unwilling creature may resist with a Dexterity save. Nothing can pass through, and occupants cannot affect the outside or be harmed by attacks or effects from outside; disintegrate destroys the sphere without harming its contents.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Otiluke’s Resilient Sphere, p. 265 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial which target is enclosed; the sphere protects occupants but also prevents them from affecting anything outside.

rules.statement: A caster opens a passage through a visible wooden, plaster, or stone surface, up to 5 feet wide, 8 feet tall, and 20 feet deep, for one hour without destabilizing the surrounding structure. When it closes, creatures or objects still inside are safely ejected to an unoccupied space nearest the surface.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Passwall, p. 265 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the passage’s dimensions; access is temporary and anything left inside is displaced when it closes.

rules.statement: A caster implants a visible phantasm, no larger than a 10-foot cube, in one creature’s mind after it fails an Intelligence save; undead and constructs are unaffected. The target treats it as real and may take 1d6 psychic damage each round if the imagined creature or hazard could plausibly harm it, but a successful action-based Investigation check against the caster’s spell save DC ends the effect.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Phantasmal Force, p. 265 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the phantasm’s plausible danger; the target’s successful examination can end it, and only that target perceives it.

rules.statement: A caster sends eight differently colored rays through a 60-foot cone, rolling separately for each creature to determine the ray; a failed Dexterity save causes the ray’s listed effect, including damage or restraint. Indigo restraint can end after three successful Constitution saves, but three failures permanently petrify the target; violet blindness may instead send a creature to another plane if it fails a follow-up Wisdom save.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Prismatic Spray, p. 268 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the random ray outcome; each target’s fate depends on a separate roll and, for some rays, further saving throws.

rules.statement: A touch can restore a dead creature to life if it died within 10 days, is not undead, and its soul is willing and free to return; it returns with 1 hit point. The spell consumes a diamond worth at least 500 gp, neutralizes poisons and nonmagical diseases present at death, but leaves magical diseases and curses in place to take effect on return.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Raise Dead, p. 272 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: revival is possible; dial: 10-day window and 500 gp consumed; in-world cost is a rare gem and a soul willing and able to return.

rules.statement: Touching a dead humanoid, or a piece of one, can call its willing, free soul into a newly formed adult body if it has been dead no more than 10 days; the new body may have a different race, determined by a d100 table or the DM. The spell consumes rare oils and unguents worth at least 1,000 gp.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Reincarnate, p. 272 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: return uses a new body; dial: 10-day limit and 1,000 gp consumed; the body’s ancestry may change.

rules.statement: A willing, free soul can be returned to a non-undead creature that has been dead no more than a century and did not die of old age; it returns with all hit points. A diamond worth at least 1,000 gp is consumed, and the spell cures ordinary disease and poison, closes mortal wounds, and restores missing body parts, but not magical disease or curses.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Resurrection, p. 273 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: extensive restoration is possible; dial: century limit, soul consent, and a consumed 1,000 gp diamond; return from death exacts a recovery penalty.

rules.statement: Touching a creature that died within the last minute can return it to life with 1 hit point, unless it died of old age; the spell does not restore missing body parts. Casting consumes diamonds worth 300 gp.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Revivify, p. 273 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: rapid revival is possible; dial: one-minute window and 300 gp consumed; the narrow window limits recovery to immediate intervention.

rules.statement: Touching a creature or object ends all curses affecting it, except a cursed magic item retains its curse. For such an item, the spell instead breaks the owner’s attunement so the item can be removed or discarded.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Remove Curse, p. 272 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: curses can be ended; dial: a cursed item’s curse persists and only its bond is broken; the item remains hazardous.

rules.statement: A rope up to 60 feet long can open an invisible entrance at its upper end into an extradimensional space lasting 1 hour, with room for up to eight Medium or smaller creatures. Attacks and spells cannot cross the entrance, occupants can see out through a small window, and everything inside falls out when the spell ends.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Rope Trick, p. 273 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: a temporary refuge is possible; dial: capacity is eight and duration is one hour; occupants are released when the space ends.

rules.statement: A willing creature or object touched becomes invisible and immune to divination targeting and divination scrying sensors; a creature also enters suspended animation and does not age. The caster may set an early-ending condition that must occur or be visible within 1 mile, and any damage to the target ends the spell.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Sequester, p. 275 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: concealment and stasis are possible; dial: damage breaks the effect and an early trigger must be local; safety depends on keeping the target undisturbed.

rules.statement: You can assume a seen creature’s form for up to 1 hour, provided its challenge rating is no greater than your level and it is neither a construct nor undead; your statistics are mostly replaced, while alignment and mental ability scores remain. You take the new form’s hit points, revert to your prior hit points when the spell ends, and can change form again using an action; excess damage can carry over if you revert at 0 hit points.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Shapechange, p. 275 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: temporary transformation is possible; dial: form must be seen and within the challenge-rating cap; injury can carry across the return.

rules.statement: The spell rolls 5d8 for a pool of hit points and affects creatures in a 20-foot radius in order from lowest current hit points upward, making affected creatures unconscious. The sleep ends after 1 minute, when a sleeper takes damage, or when someone uses an action to wake it; undead and creatures immune to charm are unaffected.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Sleep, p. 277 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: magical sleep can disable targets; dial: the 5d8 pool is spent on the weakest targets first; damage or an action can end sleep early.

rules.statement: Up to six creatures in a 40-foot cube must succeed on Wisdom saves or have their speed halved, take −2 to AC and Dexterity saves, lose reactions, and be limited to either an action or bonus action on a turn and one attack. An attempted one-action spell may be delayed on an 11 or higher on a d20, and an affected creature repeats its Wisdom save at the end of each turn.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Slow, p. 278 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: multiple targets can be hindered; dial: six-target area, concentration, and repeated saves limit duration; affected creatures can resist at each turn’s end.

rules.statement: A corpse with a mouth that is not undead can answer up to five questions over 10 minutes, but the spell does not return its soul, restore its ability to learn, or reveal events after death. It fails if that corpse was questioned by this spell in the previous 10 days, and the corpse need not answer truthfully to a hostile or recognized enemy.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Speak with Dead, p. 277 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: limited information can be obtained from a corpse; dial: five questions and a 10-day reuse limit; answers are constrained by its former knowledge and may be untruthful.

rules.statement: A creature that can hear and understand a reasonable suggested course of action must make a Wisdom save or pursue it for up to 8 hours; an obviously harmful request makes the spell end. The spell also ends if the caster or an ally damages the target, and it cannot affect creatures immune to charm.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Suggestion, p. 279 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: magical influence can guide a target’s behavior; dial: the request must sound reasonable and lasts at most 8 hours; harm or damage breaks the influence.

rules.statement: Teleport moves you and up to eight willing creatures you can see within 10 feet, or one qualifying unattended object, to a known destination on the same plane. A d100 result depends on how familiar you are with the destination and can produce an exact arrival, an arrival off target, a similar location, or a damaging mishap; a mishap deals 3d10 force damage to each traveler or the object and triggers another table roll.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Teleport, p. 282 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: arrival is limited to known destinations on the same plane; dial: increase misarrival risk for poorly known destinations, reflecting uncertain magical navigation.

rules.statement: Teleportation Circle consumes 50 gp of special materials to open a portal for one round, linking a 10-foot circle to a known permanent circle on the same plane; entrants emerge within 5 feet of the destination. Casting it in the same location every day for a year makes that location’s circle permanent.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Teleportation Circle, p. 283 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: travel requires a known sigil sequence and a brief portal; dial: adjust the year-long establishment cost, reflecting the effort of making a lasting route.

rules.statement: Telepathy links you to a familiar, willing creature anywhere on your plane for 24 hours, allowing instantaneous exchange of words and sensory messages. The link ends if either of you leaves that plane.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Telepathy, p. 282 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: the link is consensual, familiar-targeted, and plane-limited; dial: vary its duration or message bandwidth, reflecting the strength of the connection.

rules.statement: Time Stop grants you 1d4 + 1 consecutive turns while no time passes for other creatures. It ends if your actions or created effects affect another creature or an object worn or carried by someone else, or if you move more than 1,000 feet from where you cast it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Time Stop, p. 284 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: extra turns cannot be used to affect others and are bounded by a 1,000-foot radius; dial: alter the turn count or boundary, reflecting the instability of suspended time.

rules.statement: True Polymorph transforms a visible creature or eligible nonmagical object within 30 feet for up to an hour while concentration lasts; maintaining concentration for the full hour makes the change permanent. An unwilling creature can resist with a successful Wisdom save, and the transformation ends early if the target reaches 0 hit points or dies.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: True Polymorph, pp. 284–285 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: transformation is temporary unless sustained for the full duration and can be resisted; dial: change what forms are eligible, reflecting the spell’s transformative reach.

rules.statement: True Resurrection restores a creature dead no more than 200 years, unless it died of old age, if its soul is free and willing. It restores full hit points, cures wounds, poison, disease, and curses present at death, replaces missing body parts, and can create a new body; the casting consumes diamonds and holy water worth at least 25,000 gp.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: True Resurrection, p. 285 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: revival depends on the soul’s consent and freedom and has a costly consumed component; dial: alter the death-age limit or price, reflecting the difficulty of restoring life.

rules.statement: A Wall of Force blocks physical passage, is immune to damage, and cannot be dispelled by Dispel Magic; Disintegrate destroys it. It also blocks travel through the Ethereal Plane, and a creature whose space it occupies when created is pushed to one side.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wall of Force, p. 286 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: the barrier blocks physical and ethereal passage but has a specific magical counter; dial: vary its shape or duration, reflecting the caster’s control.

rules.statement: Wish can duplicate any spell of 8th level or lower without its requirements, or produce listed large-scale effects such as creating a nonmagical object worth up to 25,000 gp or undoing a roll from the last round. A non-duplicating use weakens the caster: later spells before a long rest deal unavoidable necrotic damage equal to spell level, Strength becomes 3 for 2d4 days, and there is a 33% chance the caster can never cast Wish again; broader wishes may fail or have unintended consequences.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wish, pp. 289–290 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: powerful reality changes carry physical, magical, and permanent risks; dial: increase the cost or uncertainty for broader wishes, reflecting the strain of altering reality.

rules.statement: A condition lasts until countered or until its imposing effect’s duration ends; separate instances have separate durations but do not intensify one another. A creature either has a condition or does not.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix A: Conditions, p. 291 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: conditions are discrete states with independently tracked durations; dial: none, because this is a general resolution rule.

rules.statement: Blinded creatures cannot see, automatically fail checks requiring sight, and have disadvantage on attacks; attacks against them have advantage. Charmed creatures cannot attack or harmfully target their charmer and give the charmer advantage on social checks against them; deafened creatures cannot hear and automatically fail checks requiring hearing.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix A: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, p. 291 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: sensory loss and charm impose defined mechanical limits; dial: none, since the effects are directly specified.

rules.statement: A frightened creature has disadvantage on checks and attacks while its fear’s source is in sight and cannot willingly move closer to it. A grappled creature has speed 0 and cannot benefit from speed bonuses; the grapple ends if its grappler is incapacitated or an effect removes the target from the grappler’s reach.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix A: Frightened, Grappled, p. 291 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: fear restricts approach and grappling restricts movement until specified escape circumstances; dial: none, because the source defines the limits and ending rules.

rules.statement: Exhaustion has six cumulative levels: successive levels impose disadvantage on checks, half speed, disadvantage on attacks and saves, half hit-point maximum, speed 0, then death. A long rest with food and drink reduces exhaustion by one level; other effects reduce it by their stated amount, with no effects remaining below level 1.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix A: Exhaustion, p. 292 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: accumulating levels progressively impair the creature and the stated rest requirement limits recovery; dial: change recovery rate, reflecting access to food, drink, and rest.

rules.statement: A restrained creature has speed 0 and cannot gain bonuses to speed. Attacks against it have advantage, its attacks and Dexterity saves have disadvantage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix A: Conditions, p. 294 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply these movement and roll modifiers while restrained; the state ends when the effect imposing it ends.

rules.statement: A stunned creature is incapacitated, cannot move, and can speak only falteringly; it automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves, and attacks against it have advantage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix A: Conditions, p. 294 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enforce the listed action, speech, movement, and saving-throw limits while stunned; the state ends when its cause ends.

rules.statement: In the planes, an aligned character feels in tune with a plane, while a character whose alignment conflicts with it experiences profound dissonance and discomfort.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix C: Other Planes, p. 303 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: alignment changes the visitor's subjective experience; dial up only if the campaign gives dissonance additional mechanical consequences.

rules.statement: Travel beyond the Material Plane can occur through spells or planar portals.
