Plane shift and gate transport travelers directly with differing precision; etherealness reaches the Ethereal Plane and routes through planes it touches, while astral projection sends travelers to the Astral Plane for onward travel to Outer Planes.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix C: Planar Travel, p. 302 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require the relevant spell and its own costs or limits; a portal is the alternative route.

rules.statement: A portal is a stationary connection between specific locations on two planes; it may be a passage to step through, a site or object present across planes or shifting between them, or a vortex linking similar locations, often between an Elemental Plane and the Material Plane.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix C: Planar Travel, p. 302 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: travel is limited to the portal's linked endpoints; the passage specifies no universal toll.

rules.statement: The Ethereal Plane overlaps the Material and Inner Planes at its Border Ethereal, giving each location there a corresponding Ethereal location; some creatures and specified magic can perceive into it, and some force effects extend into it. The deeper Ethereal consists of swirling mists and fogs.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix C: Transitive Planes, p. 302 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: treat the Border Ethereal as corresponding to locations on adjacent planes; perception and cross-boundary effects are limited to those specified.

rules.statement: A demiplane can be entered at a single point where it touches another plane. Plane shift can reach one in theory, but requires an exceptionally hard-to-obtain tuning-fork frequency; gate is more dependable if the caster knows the demiplane.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix C: Demiplanes, p. 303 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: access is constrained by the single entry point or costly-to-acquire tuning information; gate also requires knowledge of the destination.

rules.statement: Outer Planes have nearly meaningless distance: travel across a layer may take a day if its powers allow, or weeks for a difficult trek. The landscape can change at the whims of powerful inhabitants, who may remake it to suit their needs.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix C: Other Planes, p. 303 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: distance and terrain are subject to the plane and its powerful residents; use travel time as a dial rather than a fixed map scale.

rules.statement: The Outlands has sixteen gate-towns around its rim, each built around a portal to an Outer Plane; each town reflects traits of its destination. Sigil contains countless portals, and portal keys such as command words or objects are traded as necessary means to operate particular portals.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix C: Sigil and the Outlands, p. 303 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: portal access may require a specific key or command word, which limits passage and creates an information or acquisition cost.

rules.statement: The Far Realm has no known viable portals; ancient elves once opened one, but its location and home world are forgotten, though other portals may exist where alien forces leak through and corrupt nearby matter and life.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix C: The Far Realm, p. 303 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: access is unavailable by known portals, and any breach risks corruption of its surroundings.

rules.statement: A cleric can choose the Life domain while serving any non-evil deity; Death-domain deities are mostly evil, and most Death clerics are evil NPCs, though a DM may allow a cleric of death who is not evil.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix B: The Life and Death Domains, p. 293 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: deity alignment limits the Life-domain choice only for evil deities; Death-domain use is normally restricted by DM approval.

rules.statement: After you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, the DM may call for a d20 roll; on a 1, roll on the Wild Magic Surge table and apply the random effect rolled.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic — Wild Magic Surge (p. 104) (dnd5e-phb-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the DM decides whether to trigger the check; dial: use the surge table on a 1, because uncontrolled magic can produce unpredictable effects.

rules.statement: Before you regain Tides of Chaos, the DM may trigger a surge-table roll immediately after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher; doing so restores your use of Tides of Chaos.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic — Tides of Chaos (p. 104) (dnd5e-phb-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the DM chooses whether to call for the surge; dial: the feature use returns when the DM does so, trading restored luck for chaotic consequences.

rules.statement: When a surge-table result directs a roll at the start of each of your turns for the next minute, keep rolling then, but ignore that same result if it comes up again.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic Surge table (pp. 105–106) (dnd5e-phb-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repeated turn-start rolls last one minute; dial: repeated copies of this result do not restart the effect, limiting recursive surges.

rules.statement: A warlock makes a pact with an otherworldly patron, which grants class features and magical abilities; the arrangement can require occasional services on the patron’s behalf, and different patrons may demand favors or grant knowledge more or less freely.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Warlock — Sworn and Beholden; Otherworldly Patron (pp. 105, 108–109) (dnd5e-phb-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the pact grants power; dial: a patron’s demands and generosity vary, with service and obligations as the in-world cost.

rules.statement: A warlock regains all expended Pact Magic spell slots after a short or long rest; all slots are the same level, and a spell cast with one uses that slot level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Warlock — Pact Magic (p. 108) (dnd5e-phb-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell slots refresh on either kind of rest; dial: the slots’ shared level restricts spellcasting options while allowing higher-level casting.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, a warlock chooses one pact boon. Chain grants a familiar and permits it to attack instead of one of the warlock’s attacks; Blade creates a proficient magical melee weapon, with limits on bonding and dismissal; Tome grants three chosen cantrips that can be cast at will while its book is carried, and a lost book can be replaced by a one-hour ceremony.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Warlock — Pact Boon (pp. 108–109) (dnd5e-phb-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: choose one boon; dial: the boon’s companion, weapon, or book has specific use and replacement limits that tie the benefit to its pact.

rules.statement: A bonded pact weapon cannot be taken from its warlock unless the warlock is incapacitated; if it is on the same plane, the warlock can summon it to hand as a bonus action, but can summon only one of up to two bonded weapons at a time.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Eldritch Knight — Weapon Bond (p. 76) (dnd5e-phb-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a bonded weapon can be summoned only from the same plane and only one at a time; dial: two bonds permit choice but limit simultaneous access.

rules.statement: A warlock can spend one minute entreating their patron to regain every expended Pact Magic slot; after using this feature, they must finish a long rest before using it again.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Warlock — Eldritch Master (p. 109) (dnd5e-phb-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: all Pact Magic slots return after a minute of entreaty; dial: the benefit is limited to once per long rest, framing renewal as patron aid.

rules.statement: At 1st level, a Fiend patron grants temporary hit points equal to the warlock’s Charisma modifier plus warlock level when the warlock reduces a hostile creature to 0 hit points, with a minimum of 1.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: The Fiend — Dark One’s Blessing (p. 110) (dnd5e-phb-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the temporary protection follows a hostile creature’s defeat; dial: it depends on the warlock’s own Charisma and level, and requires a final blow.

rules.statement: At 14th level, a Fiend warlock who hits a creature can send it through the lower planes; it returns at the end of the warlock’s next turn to its previous or nearest unoccupied space, and a non-fiend takes 10d10 psychic damage. This can be used once per long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: The Fiend — Hurl Through Hell (p. 110) (dnd5e-phb-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the target returns after the warlock’s next turn; dial: only non-fiends take the stated damage, and the effect is limited to once per long rest.

rules.statement: A Great Old One warlock can communicate telepathically with a creature they can see within 30 feet without sharing a language, provided the creature understands at least one language.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: The Great Old One — Awakened Mind (p. 111) (dnd5e-phb-2014#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: communication requires sight, a 30-foot range, and a recipient with some language comprehension; the feature does not require a shared language.

rules.statement: When you finish a long rest, roll two d20s and record them. Before an attack roll, saving throw, or ability check by you or a creature you can see, you may substitute one recorded result; each result is usable once, you can do this no more than once per turn, and unused results vanish at your next long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wizard: School of Divination — Portent, p. 113 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: foreknowledge is limited to two recorded rolls per rest and requires a visible target and advance choice.

rules.statement: When you cast a divination spell of 2nd level or higher using a spell slot, regain one expended slot of a lower level than the spell, no higher than 5th level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wizard: School of Divination — Expert Divination, p. 113 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: returned casting capacity is restricted to a lower-level slot capped at 5th level.

rules.statement: A 10-foot-radius antimagic sphere moves centered on you for up to 1 hour while you concentrate. Inside it, spells and magical effects are suppressed, summoned or magically created beings and objects temporarily disappear, magic items lose their powers, teleportation and planar travel fail, and portals and extradimensional openings close temporarily; artifacts and effects created by deities are exceptions, and dispelling does not remove the sphere.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Antimagic Field, pp. 213–215 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: magical functions are blocked only within the moving sphere, with stated artifact and deity exceptions.

rules.statement: You create two linked, 10-foot-diameter portals at visible ground points: one within 10 feet and one within 500 feet. They last while you concentrate, for up to 10 minutes; creatures and objects passing through the active side exit at the other portal, vision through the mist is blocked, and you can rotate both rings as a bonus action.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Arcane Gate, pp. 215–216 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: passage connects only two visible nearby locations and remains open only while concentration lasts.

rules.statement: You and up to eight willing creatures within 10 feet project astral bodies to the Astral Plane; each participant requires consumed gems worth at least 1,100 gp. Physical bodies become unconscious and suspended, while a silver cord tethers each projection; cutting a cord kills that creature, and reaching another plane through an Astral portal transports its body there along the cord. The spell ends by dismissal, dispelling, or either body reaching 0 hit points, after which an intact cord returns the projection to its body.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Astral Projection, pp. 216–217 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: astral travel costs valuable consumed components and risks instant death if a tether is severed.

rules.statement: For up to 8 hours, you enter the Border Ethereal, where you can move in any direction but each foot of upward or downward movement costs an extra foot. You ignore objects and effects outside that plane and can affect or be affected only by beings there; when the spell ends, you return to your original plane, taking force damage equal to twice the feet moved if an obstruction forces you into the nearest unoccupied space.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Etherealness, pp. 239–240 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: access lasts at most 8 hours, excludes most cross-plane interaction, and forced reentry can injure you.

rules.statement: For 1 day, this ward protects up to 40,000 square feet of floor area and 30 feet of height against teleportation, portals, and planar entry, including access through the Astral, Ethereal, Feywild, Shadowfell, or a plane-shifting spell. You may choose creature types from celestials, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead to take 5d10 radiant or necrotic damage when entering or starting a turn in the area; a spoken password prevents that damage. Recasting it daily in the same place for 30 days makes it last until dispelled.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Forbiddance, p. 240 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: a large ward consumes costly materials and normally lasts only one day, with a password exception.

rules.statement: A locked entryway affected by this spell can be opened normally by you and creatures you designate. A password spoken within 5 feet suppresses the lock for 1 minute; the lock is otherwise impassable until broken, dispelled, or suppressed, and its break or lock-picking DC increases by 10. The spell consumes gold dust worth at least 25 gp, and the knock spell suppresses it for 10 minutes.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Arcane Lock, p. 216 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the ward costs consumed materials and has designated-user, password, and counterspell openings.

rules.statement: At 5th level, the Pact of the Blade invocation lets you attack twice with your pact weapon, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Warlock Invocations — Thirsting Blade (dnd5e-phb-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the extra attack requires 5th level, a pact weapon, and taking the Attack action.

rules.statement: When you hit a creature with eldritch blast, you may push it up to 10 feet directly away from you; this requires the eldritch blast cantrip.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Warlock Invocations — Repelling Blast (dnd5e-phb-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: displacement is limited to a hit from one specified cantrip and a 10-foot straight push.

rules.statement: While you and your familiar are on the same plane, you can communicate telepathically and perceive through its senses; while doing so, you can speak through it in your own voice even if it cannot normally speak.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Warlock Invocations — Voice of the Chain Master (dnd5e-phb-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: remote perception and communication require the familiar and end as a cross-plane capability when you are not on the same plane.

rules.statement: You can hire someone to cast a common 1st- or 2nd-level spell in a city or town for about 10–50 gp, plus costly material components. Higher-level spells are harder to arrange and cost more; the caster may instead demand an adventuring service, such as recovering a rare item or carrying something through dangerous wilderness.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Spellcasting Services (dnd5e-phb-2014#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: access to another caster's magic requires money, costly components, or a risky service, with no fixed rates for higher-level spells.

rules.statement: A caster opens a 5–20-foot circular portal for up to 1 minute, linking a visible unoccupied space within 60 feet to a precise location on another plane; passage works only through the portal’s front, and travelers arrive in the nearest unoccupied space. A planar ruler can prevent the portal from opening in its presence or domain; the caster can instead name a specific creature on another plane, drawing it through to the caster’s side without gaining control over it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Gate (dnd5e-phb-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial portal availability and ruler vetoes; planar authorities can deny access within their domains.

rules.statement: The caster and up to eight willing creatures holding hands can travel to another plane, arriving in or near a broadly specified destination; knowing a teleportation circle’s sigil sequence instead permits arrival at that circle. Alternatively, a melee spell attack can banish an unwilling creature that fails a Charisma save to a random location on a specified plane, leaving it to find its own way back.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Plane Shift (dnd5e-phb-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial destination precision and access to sigil sequences; inaccurate destination knowledge can leave travelers merely near their goal.

rules.statement: A caster spends 1 minute and 50 gp in consumed materials to open, until the end of the next turn, a portal to a known permanent circle on the same plane; arrivals appear within 5 feet of it or in the nearest free space. Learning a new sequence takes 1 minute of study, and casting at the same location every day for a year makes that circle permanent without requiring travel through it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Teleportation Circle (dnd5e-phb-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial which destinations have known sequences; travel requires prior knowledge and consumable materials.

rules.statement: A touched willing creature gains, for 8 hours, immunity to surprise, advantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws, while attackers have disadvantage on attack rolls against it. Casting the spell again before the first duration ends ends the earlier effect.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Foresight (dnd5e-phb-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial duration; the benefit is temporary and replacing it early ends the previous instance.

rules.statement: A creature affected by the command spell must understand the caster and fail a Wisdom save to become charmed for 30 days; directly disobeying causes 5d10 psychic damage, at most once per day. A suicidal instruction ends the spell, and the caster can dismiss it with an action; remove curse, greater restoration, or wish also ends it. A 7th- or 8th-level slot extends the duration to 1 year, while a 9th-level slot lasts until ended by one of those listed spells.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Geas (dnd5e-phb-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial command scope; the target can resist initially, and lethal instructions break the effect.

rules.statement: For up to 1 minute, a chosen willing creature’s speed doubles, it gains +2 AC and advantage on Dexterity saves, and it can take one restricted extra action each turn: one weapon attack, Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Use an Object. When the spell ends, the target cannot move or take actions until after its next turn.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Haste (dnd5e-phb-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial duration; the temporary speed and action increase is followed by a full turn of lethargy.

rules.statement: A caster transforms a willing touched creature and its carried or worn belongings into mist for up to 1 hour, ending the effect if the target reaches 0 hit points; incorporeal creatures are unaffected. The mist flies at 10 feet, resists nonmagical damage, has advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saves, and passes through narrow gaps but not liquids; it cannot speak, manipulate or use objects, attack, or cast spells.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Gaseous Form (dnd5e-phb-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial access to narrow passages; the form’s mobility comes at the cost of speech, object use, attacks, and spellcasting.

rules.statement: A caster can use an action to hide a chest and its contents, up to 12 cubic feet of nonliving material, on the Ethereal Plane, then use an action while touching the replica to recall it into a free space on the ground within 5 feet; another action sends it back. The effect ends if recast, if the replica is destroyed, or if dismissed; after 60 days there is a cumulative 5% daily chance it ends, and a chest still on the Ethereal Plane when the spell ends is irretrievably lost.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Leomund’s Secret Chest (dnd5e-phb-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the risk of long-term storage; the chest can be permanently lost if the spell ends while it is away.

rules.statement: An immobile 10-foot-radius force dome lasts 8 hours or until its caster leaves; it holds the caster and up to nine other creatures of Medium size or smaller, but fails if a larger creature or more than nine creatures are included. Those inside when it forms can pass freely, while other creatures, objects, spells, and magical effects cannot pass through; the interior stays dry and comfortable and can be made dim or dark.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Leomund’s Tiny Hut (dnd5e-phb-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the permitted occupants; the shelter is stationary and ends if its caster leaves.

rules.statement: An invisible force wall can be shaped as a flat barrier of ten contiguous 10-foot-square panels, a dome, or a sphere with a radius up to 10 feet, and lasts up to 10 minutes with concentration. It blocks physical passage, is immune to damage, cannot be ended by dispel magic, and extends into the Ethereal Plane; disintegrate destroys it, and a creature whose space it appears in is pushed to one side.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wall of Force (dnd5e-phb-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial placement and shape; the barrier blocks both ordinary and Ethereal travel but can be destroyed by disintegrate.

rules.statement: A 10-foot-radius, 40-foot-high cylinder of dim light deals 2d10 radiant damage when a creature first enters it on a turn or starts a turn there, with a Constitution save for half damage; a shapechanger saves with disadvantage and, on failure, reverts to its original form and cannot change form until it leaves the light. On later turns the caster can use an action to move the beam up to 60 feet.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Moonbeam (dnd5e-phb-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the beam’s path; movement and transformation restrictions apply only while creatures are in its light.

rules.statement: A willing creature touched for up to 1 hour ignores difficult terrain, cannot have its speed reduced or be paralyzed or restrained by spells or other magical effects, and can spend 5 feet of movement to escape nonmagical restraints automatically. Underwater movement and attacks impose no penalties on it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Freedom of Movement (dnd5e-phb-2014#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial duration; the protection is temporary and does not provide a general escape from magical restraints.

rules.statement: Travel beyond the Material Plane can be achieved by spells or planar portals. Plane shift and gate provide direct travel to other planes, etherealness reaches the Ethereal Plane and planes it touches, and astral projection enables travel from the Astral Plane to the Outer Planes.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Planar Travel, p. 302 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: travel requires a suitable spell or route; dial: spell precision and access vary by method.

rules.statement: A portal connects particular locations on two planes and may be crossed directly, or may take the form of a place or vehicle that exists on multiple planes or shifts between them. Vortices commonly link an Elemental Plane to a similar Material Plane location, such as a volcano or ocean depth.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Planar Travel, p. 302 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: portals connect fixed or specified places; dial: some shift or occupy multiple planes, making access less predictable.

rules.statement: The Ethereal and Astral Planes serve mainly as routes between planes. The Ethereal Plane’s Border region overlaps the Material and Inner Planes, giving each location there a corresponding Ethereal location; the Astral Plane is a route for disembodied souls toward divine and demonic planes.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Transitive Planes, p. 302 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these realms provide transit rather than ordinary destinations; dial: travel and access depend on the relevant plane or spell.

rules.statement: Some creatures can see into the Border Ethereal, and see invisibility or true seeing grants that ability. Some effects from the Material Plane, especially those using force, also extend into the Border Ethereal.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Transitive Planes, p. 302 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: Ethereal visibility and effect reach are limited; dial: specified senses or force effects cross the boundary.

rules.statement: The Inner Planes encircle the Material Plane, with the four elemental realms arranged around it within Elemental Chaos. Near the Material Plane they resemble a familiar world; farther out, each element becomes more purely expressed, and at the outer reaches the elements merge into chaos.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Inner Planes, p. 302 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: elemental regions change with distance from the Material Plane; dial: the farther reaches are more alien and hostile.

rules.statement: Outer Planes express spiritual principles and are associated with deities. Powerful forces there can remake the landscape to suit their desires, even erasing and rebuilding existence.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Outer Planes, p. 302 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a plane’s powerful inhabitants can reshape it; dial: the extent of change depends on their desires and power.

rules.statement: A creature whose alignment conflicts with a plane’s alignment experiences profound dissonance there; a matching alignment instead feels in tune with the plane.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Other Planes, p. 303 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: alignment mismatch causes discomfort rather than a specified mechanical penalty; dial: the intensity is described qualitatively.

rules.statement: Distance on the Outer Planes has no dependable scale: a journey across a layer may take a day if the plane’s powers allow it, or weeks under difficult conditions.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Other Planes, p. 303 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: travel time is flexible; dial: the plane’s powers and journey conditions determine duration.

rules.statement: A demiplane is a small extradimensional space with its own rules and can be entered at a single point where it touches another plane. Plane shift can theoretically reach one, but requires an exceptionally difficult-to-obtain tuning frequency; gate is more reliable if the caster knows the demiplane.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Demiplanes, p. 303 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: entry is localized; dial: plane shift requires a rare tuning frequency, while gate requires knowledge of the destination.

rules.statement: Stray energy from the Far Realm can warp life and matter into alien forms that defy ordinary geometry and biology. No currently viable portal to the Far Realm is known, though a portal may have existed in the past and other hidden portals may remain.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: The Far Realm, p. 303 (dnd5e-phb-2014#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: Far Realm influence can cause transformation; dial: portal access is unknown and any surviving route is hidden or uncertain.

rules.statement: While raging, the first creature you hit on your turn is hindered until your next turn: it has disadvantage on attacks against anyone but you, and anyone else it hits has resistance to that attack’s damage. The hindrance ends early if your rage ends.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Path of the Ancestral Guardian — Ancestral Protectors (dnd5e-xanathar#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the first hit each turn selects the target; dial: duration lasts only until your next turn or rage ends; in-world, ancestral spirits draw the foe’s attention toward you.

rules.statement: While raging, when a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage, you can use your reaction to reduce that damage by 2d6; this reduction becomes 3d6 at barbarian level 10 and 4d6 at level 14.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Path of the Ancestral Guardian — Spirit Shield (dnd5e-xanathar#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one reaction protects a visible creature within 30 feet; dial: protection requires an active rage and uses the reaction; in-world, guardian spirits interpose themselves.

rules.statement: At level 10, you can cast augury or clairvoyance without a spell slot or material components, using Wisdom; for clairvoyance, an ancestral spirit is invisibly summoned to the chosen location instead of creating a spherical sensor. After either use, you must finish a short or long rest before using this feature again.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Path of the Ancestral Guardian — Consult the Spirits (dnd5e-xanathar#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: choose one of two divinations; dial: once per short or long rest and the spirit substitutes for the usual sensor; in-world, ancestors provide limited guidance.

rules.statement: At level 14, whenever your Spirit Shield reduces damage from an attack, the attacker takes force damage equal to the amount prevented.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Path of the Ancestral Guardian — Vengeful Ancestors (dnd5e-xanathar#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retaliation matches the prevented damage exactly; dial: it occurs only when Spirit Shield reduces an attack’s damage; in-world, the guardian spirits answer the assault.

rules.statement: While raging, you project a magical aura 10 feet around you, blocked by total cover. Choose desert, sea, or tundra; its effect occurs when you enter rage and can be activated again on each of your turns as a bonus action, and you may change the environment when you gain a barbarian level. Any saving-throw DC is 8 + proficiency bonus + Constitution modifier.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Path of the Storm Herald — Storm Aura (dnd5e-xanathar#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one chosen environment governs the aura; dial: it requires rage and repeat activations use a bonus action; in-world, primal storm magic surrounds the barbarian.

rules.statement: With the desert aura, activating its effect deals fire damage to every other creature in the aura: 2 initially, rising to 3 at level 5, 4 at 10, 5 at 15, and 6 at 20.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Path of the Storm Herald — Storm Aura (Desert) (dnd5e-xanathar#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: all other creatures in the aura are affected; dial: the damage is small but scales by level and recurs only on activation; in-world, scorching heat radiates outward.

rules.statement: With the sea aura, activating its effect lets you choose one other creature you can see in the aura; it makes a Dexterity save, taking 1d6 lightning damage on a failure or half on a success. The damage rises to 2d6 at level 10, 3d6 at 15, and 4d6 at 20.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Path of the Storm Herald — Storm Aura (Sea) (dnd5e-xanathar#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: choose one visible creature within the aura; dial: a saving throw halves the damage and later levels raise its dice; in-world, the storm channels a lightning strike.

rules.statement: With the tundra aura, activating its effect grants 2 temporary hit points to each creature of your choice in the aura, as icy spirits bolster them.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Path of the Storm Herald — Storm Aura (Tundra) (dnd5e-xanathar#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: choose which creatures in the aura benefit; dial: the passage gives a fixed 2 temporary hit points here; in-world, icy spirits lend brief resilience.

rules.statement: At 6th level, the storm barbarian gains a benefit based on the chosen aura environment even when the aura is inactive: desert grants fire resistance and immunity to extreme heat, sea grants lightning resistance, underwater breathing, and a 30-foot swim speed, while tundra grants cold resistance and immunity to extreme cold. As an action, the desert barbarian can ignite an unattended flammable object by touch, or the tundra barbarian can freeze an unoccupied 5-foot cube of water for 1 minute.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Storm Soul, p. 12 (dnd5e-xanathar#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: low; the chosen storm environment determines which persistent adaptation is available.

rules.statement: At 10th level, creatures the storm barbarian chooses gain the damage resistance from Storm Soul while they remain in the barbarian’s Storm Aura.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Shielding Storm, p. 12 (dnd5e-xanathar#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: medium; protection is limited to chosen creatures inside the active aura.

rules.statement: At 14th level, the storm barbarian can use a reaction to impose an environment-specific effect on a creature in the aura: desert can deal fire damage equal to half the barbarian’s level after that creature hits the barbarian, sea can knock a creature prone after the barbarian hits it, and tundra can reduce a visible creature’s speed to 0 until the barbarian’s next turn when the aura effect activates. The target gets the saving throw specified for that environment.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Raging Storm, p. 12 (dnd5e-xanathar#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: medium; the effect is conditional on the selected environment and, in two cases, costs a reaction.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, while raging, the zealot barbarian deals an extra 1d6 plus half their barbarian level in radiant or necrotic damage to the first creature they hit with a weapon attack on each turn; the damage type is chosen when the feature is gained. A spell whose sole effect is restoring the zealot to life does not require material components when cast on them, provided it does not restore them as undead.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Divine Fury; Warrior of the Gods, p. 12 (dnd5e-xanathar#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: medium; the extra damage requires rage and is limited to the first weapon hit each turn, while the revival benefit applies only to qualifying spells.

rules.statement: At 6th level, a zealot raging when they fail a saving throw can reroll it, but must use the new result; this can be done once per rage.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Fanatical Focus, p. 12 (dnd5e-xanathar#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: low; the reroll is a limited safeguard, usable only once in each rage.

rules.statement: At 14th level, while raging, the zealot remains conscious at 0 hit points and still makes death saves and suffers the normal consequences of damage at 0 hit points. If failed death saves would kill them, death is delayed until the rage ends; they die then only if still at 0 hit points.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Rage Beyond Death, p. 12 (dnd5e-xanathar#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: high; rage postpones death but does not prevent death saves or guarantee survival when the rage ends.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, the College of Glamour bard can spend one Bardic Inspiration use as a bonus action to give themselves a magical appearance and grant up to a number of visible creatures who can see them equal to their Charisma modifier (minimum one) 5 temporary hit points. Each recipient can immediately use its reaction to move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks; the temporary hit points rise to 8 at bard level 5, 11 at 10, and 14 at 15.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Mantle of Inspiration, p. 15 (dnd5e-xanathar#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: medium; the benefit consumes Bardic Inspiration, and each recipient must spend a reaction to move.

rules.statement: After performing for at least 1 minute, a College of Glamour bard can target up to a number of humanoids who watched and listened throughout the performance equal to their Charisma modifier (minimum one); each must make a Wisdom save or be charmed for 1 hour. The charmed target idolizes and promotes the bard and hinders opponents, but avoids violence unless already inclined to fight for the bard; damage to the target, the bard attacking it, or it witnessing the bard harm an ally ends the effect, and success leaves the target unaware of the attempt.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Enthralling Performance, p. 15 (dnd5e-xanathar#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: medium; the effect requires a full minute of performance and ends early under specified hostile circumstances.

rules.statement: At 6th level, a College of Glamour bard can once per long rest use a bonus action to cast Command without a spell slot and assume a fey appearance for up to 1 minute, ending if concentration ends. During that time, the bard can cast Command as a bonus action each turn without a spell slot, and creatures already charmed by the bard automatically fail saves against these commands.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Mantle of Majesty, p. 15 (dnd5e-xanathar#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: high; repeated commands are limited to a short duration, require concentration, and the feature refreshes only after a long rest.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, when a College of Whispers bard hits with a weapon attack, they can expend Bardic Inspiration to deal an extra 2d6 psychic damage, once per round on their turn; this rises to 3d6 at bard level 5, 5d6 at 10, and 8d6 at 15. They can also speak privately with a humanoid for at least 1 minute and attempt to frighten it for 1 hour on a failed Wisdom save; the fear ends if it is attacked or damaged, or witnesses its allies being attacked or damaged, and the use returns after a short or long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Psychic Blades; Words of Terror, p. 17 (dnd5e-xanathar#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: medium; added damage spends Bardic Inspiration, and the fear attempt requires a private conversation and a saving throw.

rules.statement: At the end of a long rest, a Forge cleric can touch one nonmagical suit of armor or simple or martial weapon, making it magical until the next long rest or the cleric’s death; armor grants +1 AC, while a weapon grants +1 to attack and damage rolls. The feature can be used once per long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Blessing of the Forge, p. 20 (dnd5e-xanathar#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: medium; only one eligible object receives the modest enchantment, which expires at rest or death.

rules.statement: A Forge cleric can expend Channel Divinity to perform a one-hour ritual that creates a nonmagical item worth at most 100 gp, provided it includes metal; metal worth the item’s value is irretrievably transformed, and the finished item appears in an unoccupied space on a surface within 5 feet. The ritual can duplicate a nonmagical metal-containing item if the cleric possesses the original during the ritual.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Channel Divinity: Artisan’s Blessing, p. 20 (dnd5e-xanathar#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: high; creation costs equivalent metal that is consumed, takes an hour, and is capped at 100 gp.

rules.statement: A Grave cleric’s healing spell dice use their maximum values when restoring hit points to a creature at 0 hit points; the cleric also learns Spare the Dying, which has a 30-foot range for them and can be cast as a bonus action. As an action, the cleric can sense undead locations within 60 feet until the end of their next turn, except those behind total cover or protected from divination; this use is limited to their Wisdom modifier per long rest, minimum once.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Circle of Mortality; Eyes of the Grave, p. 21 (dnd5e-xanathar#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: medium; the enhanced healing applies only to targets at 0 hit points, and undead sensing has restricted range, duration, and daily uses.

rules.statement: At 2nd level, spend up to half your druid level in d6s from a pool equal to your druid level to heal one visible creature within 120 feet; it also gains 1 temporary hit point per die spent. The pool refreshes after a long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Balm of the Summer Court (dnd5e-xanathar#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: finite healing reserve; dial: die count and range; the fey gift replenishes only after a long rest.

rules.statement: At 6th level, when you begin a rest, create an invisible 30-foot-radius sphere centered on a point you touch; total cover blocks it. You and allies inside gain +5 to Stealth and Perception checks, and open-flame light inside cannot be seen outside; the sphere ends when the rest ends or you leave it.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Hearth of Moonlight and Shadow (dnd5e-xanathar#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a localized respite ward; dial: its 30-foot radius and rest duration; leaving the sphere ends its protection.

rules.statement: At 10th level, as a bonus action, teleport yourself up to 60 feet to a visible unoccupied space, or use an action to teleport a willing creature you touch up to 30 feet to one. Uses equal your Wisdom modifier, minimum one, return after a long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Hidden Paths (dnd5e-xanathar#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: short-range fey passage; dial: distance and uses; it requires a visible destination and a long rest to recharge.

rules.statement: At 14th level, after a short rest, cast dream, scrying, or teleportation circle without a spell slot or material components; the circle instead opens to the last place you finished a long rest on your current plane. If you have not finished a long rest there, that choice fails without using the feature; after any successful use, recharge it on a long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Walker in Dreams (dnd5e-xanathar#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one dreamland journey or vision; dial: fixed destination and once-per-long-rest use; the destination must be a prior rest place on the same plane.

rules.statement: At 2nd level, beasts understand your speech, and you can interpret their noises and motions; this does not make them friendly. You also learn to speak, read, and write Sylvan.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Speech of the Woods (dnd5e-xanathar#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: communication across species; dial: beasts convey only what their intelligence permits, and no allegiance is granted.

rules.statement: At 2nd level, summon an incorporeal spirit as a bonus action at a visible point within 60 feet; its aura has a 30-foot radius, lasts 1 minute or until you are incapacitated, and can be moved up to 60 feet to a visible point as a bonus action. Once used, it recharges after a short or long rest; choose bear for temporary hit points equal to 5 plus druid level and advantage on Strength checks and saves, hawk for a reaction that grants advantage to an attack against a target in the aura and advantage on allies’ Perception checks, or unicorn for advantage on checks to detect creatures and extra healing equal to druid level for chosen creatures in the aura when you cast a healing spell using a slot.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Spirit Totem (dnd5e-xanathar#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one brief, movable spirit influence; dial: aura size, duration, and rest-based recharge; its benefit depends on the selected spirit.

rules.statement: At 6th level, beasts and fey summoned or created by your spells gain 2 extra hit points per Hit Die, and their natural-weapon damage counts as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Mighty Summoner (dnd5e-xanathar#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the feature strengthens only spell-summoned or spell-created beasts and fey; dial: fixed extra hit points and a limited damage-classification change.

rules.statement: At 10th level, a beast or fey you summoned or created with a spell regains hit points equal to half your druid level if it ends its turn in your Spirit Totem aura.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Guardian Spirit (dnd5e-xanathar#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: summoned allies recover gradually; dial: healing requires ending a turn in the aura and is limited by druid level.

rules.statement: At 14th level, when reduced to 0 hit points or incapacitated against your will, immediately gain the effects of conjure animals as though cast with a 9th-level slot: four chosen beasts of challenge rating 2 or lower appear within 20 feet. They last 1 hour without concentration or until dismissed, protect and attack if not commanded, and the feature recharges after a long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Faithful Summons (dnd5e-xanathar#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: emergency animal protection; dial: crisis trigger, four-beast limit, and once-per-long-rest use; uncommanded beasts defend their summoner.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, twice per short or long rest, when a shortbow or longbow arrow hits, apply one chosen Arcane Shot option, at most once per turn; the option is selected on a hit unless it has no attack roll. The save DC is 8 + proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier, and the number of known options increases at fighter levels 7, 10, 15, and 18; at 18th level the options improve.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Arcane Shot (dnd5e-xanathar#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: magical effects ride on limited bow attacks; dial: two uses per rest, one per turn, and a defined save DC; higher levels expand and improve the options.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, after hitting a creature with a melee weapon attack, mark it until the end of your next turn; the mark ends early if you are incapacitated, die, or another creature marks it. While within 5 feet of you, it has disadvantage on attacks that do not target you; if it harms someone else, you may make an advantaged special melee attack against it as a bonus action on your next turn, dealing extra damage equal to half your fighter level on a hit, with uses equal to Strength modifier, minimum one, per long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Unwavering Mark (dnd5e-xanathar#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a short-lived challenge that pressures a foe to engage its marker; dial: proximity, duration, and limited punishing attacks.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, three times per long rest, use a bonus action to gain advantage on weapon attack rolls until the turn ends and gain 5 temporary hit points; the temporary hit points increase to 10 at fighter level 10 and 15 at level 15. At level 10, regain one use when initiative is rolled if none remain.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Fighting Spirit; Tireless Spirit (dnd5e-xanathar#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a limited burst of battle focus; dial: three uses per long rest, with one-use recovery at initiative only when depleted.

rules.statement: Once per turn when you hit with a kensei weapon, you can spend 1 ki point to add damage equal to your Martial Arts die. At 6th level, attacks with kensei weapons count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: One with the Blade; Magic Kensei Weapons and Deft Strike, p. 36 (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ki cost and once-per-turn limit; dial: damage die; the warrior channels limited inner energy through a chosen weapon.

rules.statement: When taking the Attack action, a Sun Soul monk can spend 1 ki point to make two radiant ranged spell attacks as a bonus action; each has a 30-foot range and deals radiant damage using the monk’s Martial Arts die. The attacks use Dexterity for attack and damage rolls, and can replace attacks within the Attack action once the monk has Extra Attack.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Radiant Sun Bolt, p. 36 (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one ki point and the action structure; dial: range and damage die; the monk converts life energy into limited ranged strikes.

rules.statement: Immediately after taking the Attack action, a 6th-level Sun Soul monk can spend 2 ki points to cast burning hands as a bonus action. Each additional ki point raises the spell’s level by one, and total ki spent cannot exceed half the monk’s level.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Searing Arc Strike, p. 36 (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ki cost, timing, and level-based spending cap; dial: spell level; the burst consumes the monk’s finite energy.

rules.statement: As an action, an 11th-level Sun Soul monk creates and throws a radiant orb to a point within 150 feet; creatures in its 20-foot-radius sphere make Constitution saves or take 2d6 radiant damage. Opaque total cover avoids the save, and up to 3 ki points can each add 2d6 damage.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Searing Sunburst, p. 36 (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: action, save, cover exception, and three-point ki limit; dial: damage; the monk trades reserve energy for a stronger area burst.

rules.statement: At 17th level, a Sun Soul monk can use a bonus action to turn their magical light on or off; when on, it sheds bright light 30 feet and dim light for another 30 feet. While it shines, a melee attacker that hits the monk can be dealt radiant damage equal to 5 plus the monk’s Wisdom modifier, using the monk’s reaction.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Sun Shield, p. 36 (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: light radius and reaction cost; dial: damage; the luminous defense is available only while the monk maintains the light.

rules.statement: A Conquest paladin can use Channel Divinity as an action to make chosen visible creatures within 30 feet attempt Wisdom saves; a creature that fails is frightened for 1 minute and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. The paladin can instead use Channel Divinity after seeing an attack roll to add 10 to it, before its outcome is declared.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Oath of Conquest: Channel Divinity, p. 39 (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: action or Channel Divinity use, range, save, and duration; dial: affected targets; authority and supernatural accuracy draw on the paladin’s oath-granted power.

rules.statement: From 7th level, a Conquest paladin emits a 10-foot aura while not incapacitated; at 18th level its radius becomes 30 feet, and it does not pass through total cover. A creature frightened of the paladin has speed 0 in the aura and takes psychic damage equal to half the paladin’s level if it starts its turn there.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Aura of Conquest, p. 39 (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: incapacitation, cover, range, and level-scaled damage limits; dial: aura radius; fear turns the paladin’s nearby presence into a bounded hostile zone.

rules.statement: When a creature within 10 feet of a Redemption paladin takes damage, the paladin can use a reaction to take that damage instead; at 18th level the range becomes 30 feet. The damage cannot be reduced, and other effects accompanying it do not transfer.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Aura of the Guardian, p. 40 (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reaction, range, and no-reduction rule; dial: protected distance; the paladin protects another by personally bearing the harm.

rules.statement: A Horizon Walker can use an action to sense the distance and direction to the nearest planar portal within 1 mile, once per short or long rest. At 7th level, the ranger can cast etherealness as a bonus action without a spell slot, but it ends at the end of that turn and the feature recharges after a short or long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Horizon Walker: Detect Portal and Ethereal Step, p. 43–44 (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one-mile sensing range, action, recharge, and one-turn travel limit; dial: range and duration; planar passage is brief and periodically available.

rules.statement: A Horizon Walker can teleport up to 10 feet to a visible unoccupied space before each attack made as part of the Attack action. If the ranger attacks at least two different creatures with that action, they can make one additional attack against a third creature.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Horizon Walker: Distant Strike, p. 44 (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: 10-foot movement per attack and the distinct-target condition; dial: additional attack; the ranger briefly crosses planar boundaries to reposition.

rules.statement: When a Horizon Walker takes damage from an attack, they can use a reaction to gain resistance to all damage from that attack for the turn. When they see a creature within 60 feet cast a spell or teleport, a Monster Slayer can instead use a reaction to force a Wisdom save against their spell save DC; failure makes the spell or teleport fail and be wasted, and the feature recharges after a short or long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Horizon Walker: Spectral Defense; Monster Slayer: Magic-User’s Nemesis, pp. 44 (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reaction timing, range, save, and rest-based recharge; dial: which attack or magical act is affected; the ranger’s specialized training briefly deflects harm or disrupts hostile magic.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, you can take the Help action as a bonus action. When helping an ally attack, you can aid them against a target up to 30 feet away if it can see or hear you, rather than requiring it to be within 5 feet.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Mastermind: Master of Tactics, p. 47 (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: aid one ally’s attack; dial: extend assistance to 30 feet; the target must perceive your help.

rules.statement: After at least 1 minute observing or interacting with a creature outside combat, choose two listed traits; the DM tells you whether the creature is equal, superior, or inferior to you in each. At the DM’s option, you may also learn one historical fact or personality trait.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Mastermind: Insightful Manipulator, p. 47 (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: compare two capabilities; dial: optional personal insight; it requires a minute of attention outside combat and the DM may withhold the extra detail.

rules.statement: When an attack targets you and a creature within 5 feet is giving you cover against it, you can use your reaction to make that creature the target instead.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Mastermind: Misdirection, p. 47 (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: redirect one attack; dial: reaction and an adjacent creature must already be providing cover.

rules.statement: Your thoughts cannot be read unless you permit it. You can pass off false thoughts by winning a Charisma (Deception) check contested by the reader’s Wisdom (Insight); magic that checks truth treats your statements as truthful if you choose, and magic cannot compel you to tell the truth.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Mastermind: Soul of Deceit, p. 47 (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: block thought-reading and magical truth compulsion; dial: false thoughts require a successful contested check, while the truth indication is optional.

rules.statement: When an enemy ends its turn within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Scout: Skirmisher, p. 48 (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: evade a nearby foe; dial: movement is limited to half speed and consumes your reaction.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, you gain Nature and Survival proficiency if you lack them, and double your proficiency bonus on checks using either skill.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Scout: Survivalist, p. 48 (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: improve two wilderness skills; dial: the doubled bonus applies only to checks using those proficiencies.

rules.statement: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet; the same increase applies to any climbing or swimming speed you have.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Scout: Superior Mobility, p. 48 (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: add 10 feet to applicable speeds; dial: only walking, climbing, and swimming speeds benefit.

rules.statement: You have advantage on initiative rolls. The first creature you hit in the first combat round grants advantage on attack rolls against it until the start of your next turn.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Scout: Ambush Master, p. 48 (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: improve initiative and expose one target; dial: the shared advantage lasts only until your next turn begins.

rules.statement: If you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make one extra attack as a bonus action. That attack may benefit from Sneak Attack even if you already used it this turn, but you cannot apply Sneak Attack to the same target more than once that turn.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Scout: Sudden Strike, p. 48 (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one additional bonus-action attack; dial: requires the Attack action and limits repeated Sneak Attack on a target.

rules.statement: After a melee attack against a creature on your turn, that creature cannot make opportunity attacks against you for the rest of that turn.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Swashbuckler: Fancy Footwork, p. 48 (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: safely disengage from a struck foe; dial: protection applies only to that creature and only for the current turn.

rules.statement: You add your Charisma modifier to initiative. You can use Sneak Attack against a creature within 5 feet without advantage if no other creature is within 5 feet of you and you have no disadvantage; the other Sneak Attack rules still apply.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Swashbuckler: Rakish Audacity, p. 48 (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: faster initiative and a close-quarters Sneak Attack route; dial: the special route requires isolation and no disadvantage.

rules.statement: As an action, make a Charisma (Persuasion) check contested by a creature’s Wisdom (Insight); it must hear you and share a language with you. On success, a hostile target has disadvantage attacking anyone but you and cannot make opportunity attacks against others for 1 minute, ending early if an ally attacks or affects it with a spell, or if you move more than 60 feet apart; a nonhostile target is charmed for 1 minute, ending immediately if you or your companions harm it.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Swashbuckler: Panache, p. 48 (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: influence one creature after a contested social check; dial: hearing, shared language, proximity, and distinct early-ending triggers constrain the effect.

rules.statement: Instead of using a dragonborn’s breath weapon, expend one use to make chosen creatures within 30 feet save against DC 8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier or become frightened of you for 1 minute. A target that cannot hear or see you succeeds automatically, and a frightened target can repeat its save when it takes damage, ending the effect on a success.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: p. 75, Dragon Fear (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the roar can frighten selected nearby creatures; dial: it consumes a breath-weapon use and ends early on a successful repeat save.

rules.statement: A gnome who takes damage can use a reaction to become invisible until the end of their next turn, or until they attack, deal damage, or force a saving throw. This can be used again after a short or long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: p. 75, Fade Away (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: damage can trigger brief invisibility; dial: reaction, limited duration, and rest-based reuse restrict it.

rules.statement: A high elf learns misty step and can cast it once without a spell slot, regaining that use after a short or long rest; Intelligence is the spellcasting ability. Its description presents the movement as briefly passing through the Feywild.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: p. 75, Fey Teleportation (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one spell-slot-free teleport between rests; dial: one use per rest interval, with no broader planar-travel procedure given.

rules.statement: When you cast a spell that deals fire damage, you can wreathe yourself in harmless flames until the end of your next turn. The flames shed bright light for 30 feet and dim light for another 30 feet, and a creature within 5 feet that hits you with a melee attack takes 1d4 fire damage.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: pp. 75–76, Flames of Phlegethos (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: casting a fire-damage spell can add a short-lived damaging aura; dial: it lasts only until your next turn ends and requires a qualifying spell.

rules.statement: A dwarf who takes the Dodge action can spend one Hit Die to regain hit points equal to the die roll plus Constitution modifier, with a minimum of 1 hit point. The feat also increases Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: p. 75, Dwarven Fortitude (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spend a Hit Die to heal while Dodging; dial: the die is a limited recovery resource and the action must be used in combat.

rules.statement: When you have advantage on an attack roll using Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma, you can reroll one of the dice once. The feat also increases one of those ability scores by 1, to a maximum of 20.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: p. 75, Elven Accuracy (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reroll one die on qualifying advantaged attacks; dial: it applies only to four ability-score attack types and only when advantage already exists.

rules.statement: A tiefling who rolls fire damage for a spell they cast can reroll any fire-damage die showing 1, but must use the new result even if it is also 1. The feat also increases Intelligence or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: p. 75, Flames of Phlegethos (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reroll fire spell damage dice showing 1; dial: only fire damage from spells qualifies, and the new result is mandatory.

rules.statement: A creature that is naturally asleep wakes if it takes damage, is shaken or slapped awake with an action, or hears a sudden loud noise. Whispers wake it only if it has passive Wisdom (Perception) 20 or higher and is within 10 feet; ordinary-volume speech wakes it in an otherwise silent environment if that score is 15 or higher.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: p. 78, Waking Someone (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: specified stimuli end natural sleep; dial: hearing thresholds depend on distance, noise, and passive Perception.

rules.statement: After a long rest spent sleeping in medium or heavy armor, a creature regains only one quarter of its spent Hit Dice, with a minimum of one die, and the rest does not reduce exhaustion. Sleeping in light armor has no such penalty.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: pp. 78–79, Sleeping in Armor (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: medium or heavy armor reduces recovery from a long rest; dial: the restriction applies only to the rest spent sleeping in that armor.

rules.statement: For each 24-hour period without a long rest, a creature must make a DC 10 Constitution save or gain one exhaustion level. The DC rises by 5 for every consecutive 24-hour period without a long rest and resets to 10 when the creature finishes one.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: p. 79, Going Without a Long Rest (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: missed long rests call for escalating exhaustion saves; dial: the DC resets after a long rest.

rules.statement: As part of a long rest, a proficient cook with sufficient food can prepare a meal for themselves and up to five chosen creatures; each regains 1 additional hit point per Hit Die spent during a short rest. The benefit requires access to the cook’s utensils.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: p. 82, Cook’s Utensils—Prepare Meals (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a prepared meal adds healing per Hit Die spent; dial: it requires proficiency, supplies, and preparation during a long rest.

rules.statement: A spell’s casting can be noticed when it uses verbal, somatic, or material components. If a special ability removes the need for all components, the casting cannot be perceived; if it nevertheless causes an observable effect, the caster’s identity normally remains unknown without other evidence.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Perceiving a Caster at Work, p. 86 (dnd5e-xanathar#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: component use exposes the act of casting; dial: special abilities can remove that cue, making attribution harder.

rules.statement: A character can use a reaction while a spell is being cast, or an action afterward, to try to identify it with an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 15 plus the spell’s level. The check has advantage if the spell was cast as a class spell and the observer belongs to that class.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Identifying a Spell, p. 86 (dnd5e-xanathar#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: identification costs a reaction or action and a check; dial: class familiarity improves the odds.

rules.statement: If a spell targets something it cannot affect, that target suffers no effect, but any spell slot spent is still used. If the spell would ordinarily have no effect after a successful save, the invalid target appears to have saved; otherwise the caster can tell that nothing happened.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Invalid Spell Targets, p. 87 (dnd5e-xanathar#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: invalid targeting wastes the slot; the apparent outcome depends on the spell’s saving-throw rules.

rules.statement: With the template method for grid areas, each 5 feet of the area corresponds to 1 inch of template, and every square partly or fully covered by the template is affected. Without a grid, a creature is affected if any part of its miniature’s base overlaps the template.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Areas of Effect on a Grid: Template Method, pp. 87–88 (dnd5e-xanathar#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: any overlap counts; dial: templates give more spatial precision than square-token approximations.

rules.statement: With the token method, each 5-foot square of an area is represented by a token placed inside that square, and any square containing a token is affected. Circles become squares with sides equal to the circle’s diameter; cones use successive adjoining rows, with the number of rows equal to the cone’s length divided by 5 feet, and lines may extend orthogonally or diagonally.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Areas of Effect on a Grid: Token Method, pp. 88–89 (dnd5e-xanathar#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: token placement determines affected squares; dial: simplified square shapes trade geometric accuracy for ease of play.

rules.statement: With access to tools and a sufficiently hot open flame, a smith can repair a damaged metal object, restoring 10 hit points for each hour of work.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Smith’s Tools: Repair, p. 85 (dnd5e-xanathar#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repair takes an hour per 10 hit points restored and requires tools, heat, and access.

rules.statement: As part of a short rest, a character using thieves’ tools can set a trap from items on hand; the check total becomes the DC to find or disable it. The trap deals damage appropriate to its materials or damage equal to half the check total, as the DM judges suitable.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Thieves’ Tools: Set a Trap, p. 85 (dnd5e-xanathar#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: trap construction costs a short rest and available materials; effectiveness depends on the check and materials.

rules.statement: A character with tinker's tools can restore 10 hit points to a damaged object per hour, provided they have the necessary raw materials. Metal objects additionally require a hot enough open flame to make the metal pliable.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Tinker’s Tools: Repair, p. 86 (dnd5e-xanathar#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repair is limited by time, raw materials, and— for metal—adequate heat.

rules.statement: Proficiency with a vehicle type lets a character add their proficiency bonus to that vehicle’s AC and saving throws while piloting it.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Land and Water Vehicles: Vehicle Handling, p. 84 (dnd5e-xanathar#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bonus applies only while piloting a vehicle type the character is proficient with.

rules.statement: A character proficient with woodcarver’s tools can craft up to five arrows during a short rest or up to twenty during a long rest, provided enough wood is available.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Woodcarver’s Tools: Craft Arrows, p. 86 (dnd5e-xanathar#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: production is capped by rest length and available wood.

rules.statement: A simple trap activates once when its stated trigger occurs, then applies its specified effect; its description sets the target, attack or save numbers, and consequences. A character can counter it using the stated checks or magic, and a failed disabling attempt can set it off.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Traps Revisited—Elements of a Simple Trap; Running a Simple Trap, p. 114 (dnd5e-xanathar#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the trap’s printed trigger and resolution; dial: adjust its level and threat; in-world, its construction and purpose determine its danger.

rules.statement: Trap level is selected from the ranges 1–4, 5–10, 11–16, or 17–20, and its threat is moderate, dangerous, or deadly. The guideline table sets save and check DCs at 10, 15, or 20 and attack bonuses at +5, +8, or +12 respectively.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Traps Revisited—Level and Lethality, p. 117 (dnd5e-xanathar#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: follow the level-and-threat guidance; dial: choose a higher or lower threat; in-world, the trap’s maker sets its potency.

rules.statement: A creature stepping on the bear trap is attacked at +8 for 1d10 piercing damage; on a hit its speed becomes 0 until it or an adjacent creature succeeds on a DC 15 Strength check to free it. A DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check finds the trap, and DC 10 Dexterity with thieves’ tools disables it.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Example Simple Traps—Bear Trap, p. 115 (dnd5e-xanathar#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the stated attack and escape check; dial: allow an adjacent helper to free the victim; in-world, the jaws clamp onto the leg.

rules.statement: A trip wire activates two crossbow attacks against the creature that crosses it, each at +8 and dealing 1d10 piercing damage on a hit; neither attack can gain advantage or disadvantage. DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) finds the wire, and DC 15 Dexterity with thieves’ tools disables it, but a result of 5 or lower triggers the trap.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Example Simple Traps—Crossbow Trap, p. 115 (dnd5e-xanathar#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve both attacks and the disabling check as stated; dial: none; in-world, a concealed wire releases two aimed crossbows.

rules.statement: A creature that triggers a net trap causes a net to fall over a 10-by-10-foot area and a bell to ring; creatures fully in the area must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity save or become restrained. A restrained creature can use its action for a DC 10 Strength check to escape, or the net can be cut with 5 slashing damage; DC 15 Dexterity with thieves’ tools disables the wire, but failure triggers the trap.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Example Simple Traps—Net Trap, pp. 115–116 (dnd5e-xanathar#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the net restrains and the bell alerts nearby guards; dial: none; in-world, the trap is designed to capture intruders intact.

rules.statement: A creature stepping onto the concealed canvas over a pit must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity save or fall 10 feet and take 1d6 bludgeoning damage. A DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check reveals the canvas and the safe one-foot ledge around the pit.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Example Simple Traps—Pit Trap, p. 116 (dnd5e-xanathar#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the save to determine whether the creature falls; dial: none; in-world, the concealed pit delays or injures intruders.

rules.statement: A creature attempting to pick or open the poisoned lock makes a DC 20 Constitution save; on failure it takes 4d6 poison damage and is poisoned for 10 minutes, during which it is paralyzed, while success halves the damage and avoids the condition. A DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) check while inspecting the lock reveals the needle, and DC 20 Dexterity with thieves’ tools disables it; a result of 10 or lower triggers it.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Example Simple Traps—Poison Needle, p. 116 (dnd5e-xanathar#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the save, damage, and timed condition; dial: none; in-world, the hidden needle punishes anyone tampering with the lock.
