rules.statement: A complex trap acts on initiative count 10, 20, or both, after creatures with the same count; its active effects resolve on its turns, while constant effects can trigger at the end of creatures’ turns. A complex trap generally takes three successful checks to disable each element, and successful checks can weaken an element before disabling it.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Complex Traps—Describing a Complex Trap; Running a Complex Trap, pp. 119–120 (dnd5e-xanathar#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: run the trap on its listed initiative and require repeated checks; dial: its elements and pace vary by design; in-world, a persistent mechanism keeps operating until defeated.

rules.statement: The Path of Blades activates when a non-undead creature enters its hallway and remains active while one is there; it acts at initiative counts 20 and 10. Its blades attack at +5 for 2d10 slashing damage, pillars force a DC 15 Dexterity save for 2d10 bludgeoning damage and possible prone, and its fear rune forces a DC 15 Wisdom save, potentially frightening a creature and using its reaction to move it toward the pillars.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Example Complex Traps—Path of Blades, pp. 119–120 (dnd5e-xanathar#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve the listed elements on their initiative counts; dial: escalating blade and rune effects apply as specified; in-world, the hallway’s mechanisms punish and drive intruders.

rules.statement: A creature frightened by the Path of Blades rune can use its action to make a DC 15 Wisdom save, ending that frightened condition on a success; while frightened, it cannot move closer to the far end of the hallway. Successful attempts to disable the rune increase the trap’s damage and save DC as described.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Path of Blades—Rune of Fear and Dynamic Elements, p. 120 (dnd5e-xanathar#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the action and save to end the condition; dial: disabling attempts strengthen the trap; in-world, tampering with the rune feeds its defenses.

rules.statement: A rolling steel sphere attacks creatures in its path on initiative 10, requiring a DC 20 Strength save; failure deals 4d10 bludgeoning damage and knocks the creature prone, while success deals half damage without knocking it prone. Blocking objects take maximum damage; after each turn its damage rises by 2d10, and once it reaches 10d10 it acts on initiative 20 as well as 10.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Sphere of Crushing Doom, p. 121 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial the damage growth and initiative schedule; the sphere accelerates as it repeatedly cycles.

rules.statement: A creature can disrupt either portal by examining its runes and then making three successful DC 20 Intelligence (Arcana) checks, each requiring an action; each success reduces the sphere's damage by 2d10. Alternatively, three successful castings of dispel magic against a rune set disable it; destroying the southern portal stops the sphere at the wall.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Sphere of Crushing Doom—Countermeasures, p. 121 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial the number and difficulty of actions; the portal mechanism is vulnerable only through sustained interference.

rules.statement: When a ruby is removed from a serpent statue, the doors lock and poison gas fills the room; each creature makes a DC 20 Constitution save, taking 6d10 poison damage on a failure or half on a success. On each initiative 10, roll a d6 for an additional room effect, including impaired checks, an explosion if an open flame is present, forced prone, obscured vision, or another poison attack; the initial gas damage rises by 2d10 per round to 10d10.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Poisoned Tempest, pp. 121–122 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial the random effect and escalating poison; the trapped room compounds danger over time.

rules.statement: A statue can be blocked with a successful DC 20 Dexterity check using thieves’ tools or a DC 15 Strength check, reducing poison damage by 1d10; someone must remain beside it to maintain the blockage. Blocking all four statues deactivates the trap; breaking or reducing a statue to 0 hit points instead increases poison damage by 1d10.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Poisoned Tempest—Disable the Statues, p. 122 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial the number of statues and damage adjustment; maintaining the physical blockage occupies a creature.

rules.statement: A complex trap’s active parts can act each round at chosen initiative counts, while a constant hazard affects creatures that end their turns in its area; as a guideline, use the active effect’s save DC or attack bonus but halve its damage for the constant hazard. Avoid making every area constantly dangerous so creatures have chances to find safer positions.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Active Elements; Constant Elements, p. 122 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial coverage and recurrence; safe spaces and timing create opportunities to respond.

rules.statement: A trap’s changing elements may follow a schedule, react to characters’ actions, or produce a random effect each round; their changes can alter targets, damage, effects, or affected areas. Examining how the mechanism works may let characters anticipate its future behavior.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Dynamic Elements, pp. 122–123 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial whether changes are scheduled, reactive, or random; observable operation can reveal what comes next.

rules.statement: A complex trap cannot be defeated with one check: characters overcome its parts separately, usually needing to be near the part they target. As a default, three successful checks or actions disable an element, progressively reducing its effectiveness; after one character succeeds, another cannot attempt the same check against that element until the end of the first character’s next turn.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Defeating Complex Traps, p. 124 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial checks and access requirements; disabling the whole mechanism takes coordinated, sustained effort.

rules.statement: A downtime activity generally takes at least five days, with at least eight hours of work per counted day; its days need not be consecutive, but the total span should not exceed twice the required time or complications and possibly doubled costs apply. A rival can advance a plan whenever one or more workweeks of downtime are resolved.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Downtime Activities—Resolving Activities; Creating a Rival, pp. 125–127 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial the activity duration and rival response; time spent away from adventures allows plans to progress.

rules.statement: Seeking a magic item costs at least one workweek and 100 gp; a Charisma (Persuasion) check determines available item quality, gaining +1 for each additional workweek or 100 gp spent, up to +10. The DM sets the items and final prices; consumables cost half the listed asking price, and low- or high-magic campaigns can apply a −10 or +10 check adjustment.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Buying a Magic Item, p. 127 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial search time, expense, and availability; finding a seller is uncertain and depends on the campaign’s market.

rules.statement: A week of carousing costs 10 gp with lower-class folk, 50 gp with the middle class, or 250 gp with the upper class, and a Charisma (Persuasion) check determines whether the character gains hostile, no, one, two, or three allied contacts. A character can hold unspecified allied contacts up to 1 plus their Charisma modifier (minimum one); each contact provides help or hindrance only once, and carousing has a 10% complication chance per workweek.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Carousing, pp. 127–129 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial social tier, check result, and contact capacity; money and social effort create limited, conditional relationships.

rules.statement: A character crafting nonmagical gear needs appropriate tools and proficiency, equipment, and raw materials worth half the item’s selling price; each 50 gp of item value requires one workweek. Collaborators with the needed proficiency can divide the time, and completed goods can be sold at the listed price.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Crafting an Item, p. 129 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial item value and eligible collaborators; materials, tools, and work time constrain production.

rules.statement: Creating a magic item requires a formula listing its materials and steps, an exotic ingredient, the listed time and gold cost, and either relevant tool proficiency or Arcana proficiency. The ingredient is obtained through an adventure; its suggested guardian or challenge rating ranges from CR 1–3 for common items up to CR 19+ for legendary items.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Crafting Magic Items, p. 130 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: require every listed prerequisite; dial: choose the ingredient and adventure challenge; the rare material makes creation an expedition.

rules.statement: Crafting normally takes 1 workweek and costs 50 gp for a common item, rising to 50 workweeks and 100,000 gp for a legendary item; the intermediate rarity costs and times are 2/200 gp, 10/2,000 gp, and 25/20,000 gp. Halve both time and cost for consumable items.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Magic Item Crafting Time and Cost, p. 130 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: use the rarity schedule; dial: none; time and expense limit production.

rules.statement: For every five workweeks spent crafting a magic item, there is a 10% chance of a complication. Possible complications include stolen tools, scrutiny, rumors of danger, or a rival or claimant interfering.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Complications, p. 130 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: roll once per five workweeks; dial: select or invent the complication; crafting attracts risks beyond its material cost.

rules.statement: A character proficient with an herbalism kit can make healing potions: a basic potion takes 1 day and 25 gp, while greater, superior, and supreme potions take 1, 3, and 4 workweeks and cost 100, 1,000, and 10,000 gp, respectively.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Brewing Potions of Healing, p. 131 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: require herbalism proficiency and the listed time and cost; dial: none; potion strength determines the production burden.

rules.statement: Scribing a spell scroll requires Arcana proficiency, the spell prepared or known, and any material components required to cast it. A cantrip scroll functions as though cast by a 1st-level caster; higher-level scrolls use the listed level-based time and cost, from 1 day and 25 gp for 1st level to 48 workweeks and 250,000 gp for 9th level.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Scribing a Spell Scroll, p. 134 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: enforce eligibility, components, time, and cost; dial: none; inscribing stores a spell through demanding work.

rules.statement: A warlock attuned to a dark shard amulet can use it as a focus for warlock spells and, once per long rest, attempt to cast an unknown warlock-list cantrip with a DC 10 Intelligence (Arcana) check. On failure the spell does not work and the action is spent.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Dark Shard Amulet, p. 138 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: require warlock attunement and limit the attempt to once per long rest; dial: none; an uncertain borrowed cantrip can waste an action.

rules.statement: A wizard attuned to a hat of wizardry can use it as a focus for wizard spells and, once per long rest, attempt an unknown wizard-list cantrip using a DC 10 Intelligence (Arcana) check. Failure wastes the action without casting the spell.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Hat of Wizardry, p. 138 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: require wizard attunement and limit the attempt to once per long rest; dial: none; the item offers limited access to an unlearned spell.

rules.statement: A creature attuned to a charlatan’s die can choose the result whenever it rolls the die.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Charlatan’s Die, p. 137 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: require attunement; dial: none; the item grants direct control over its own roll.

rules.statement: A creature attuned to an instrument of scribing can spend one of its 3 charges while playing it to write a magical message of up to six known-language words on a visible nonmagical object or surface within 30 feet. A bard can add seven words and make the message visible in nonmagical darkness; dispel magic erases it, otherwise it fades after 24 hours, and the instrument regains its charges at dawn.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Instrument of Scribing, p. 139 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: require attunement, playing, and a charge; dial: none; the message is brief and temporary.

rules.statement: Planting an ordinary shrub in a pot of awakening and leaving it to grow for 30 days transforms it into an awakened shrub. The shrub is friendly to the planter but takes no action without commands; its roots break and destroy the pot when it awakens.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Pot of Awakening, p. 139 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: require an ordinary shrub and 30 days; dial: none; awakening consumes the pot and leaves the shrub dependent on commands.

rules.statement: Attuning a ruby of the war mage lets its wearer use an attached simple or martial weapon as a spellcasting focus. Attachment takes at least 10 minutes; it can later be detached as an action, falls away if attunement ends, and is not dislodged by an antimagic field.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Ruby of the War Mage, p. 139 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: require spellcaster attunement and attachment to a weapon; dial: none; the focus benefit is tied to the ruby’s bond.

rules.statement: A wearer of an ear horn of hearing can hold it to the ear to suppress the deafened condition and hear normally while doing so.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Ear Horn of Hearing, p. 138 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: require holding the horn to the ear; dial: none; its benefit applies while used.

rules.statement: A staff holding a floating-object effect can keep at most three objects hovering above its tip; while holding it, the user can make one or more of them rotate slowly. The objects remain only until removed or the staff is no longer in the user's possession.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Staff of adornment (p. 140) (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited to three objects and requires holding the staff; dial: cosmetic control only, with possession ending the effect.

rules.statement: The birdcall staff has 10 charges; an action and one charge create one chosen bird sound audible within 60 feet. It regains 1d6 + 4 charges at dawn, and spending its last charge has a 1-in-20 chance of destroying it harmlessly.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Staff of birdcalls (p. 140) (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one sound per action and charge; dial: dawn recharge and a small destruction risk limit repeat use.

rules.statement: The flower staff has 10 charges; an action and one charge makes a harmless, nonmagical flower sprout from soil within 5 feet or from the staff. It regains 1d6 + 4 charges at dawn, and spending its last charge has a 1-in-20 chance of turning it into petals and destroying it.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Staff of flowers (p. 140) (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one flower per action and charge; dial: the effect is harmless and limited by charges, with a small item-loss risk.

rules.statement: While attuned, a user within 5 feet of the talking doll can spend a short rest teaching it up to six phrases, each no longer than six words, and assigning each a trigger that occurs within 5 feet of the doll. Phrases can be replaced, and all stored phrases disappear when attunement ends.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Talking doll (p. 140) (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement binds the programmed phrases to the doll; dial: six short phrases, local triggers, and loss of programming when the bond ends.

rules.statement: A drinker can consume ordinary, nonmagical alcoholic drinks from the tankard without becoming intoxicated. It does not protect against magical liquids or harmful substances such as poison.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Tankard of sobriety (p. 140) (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: blocks ordinary alcohol's intoxicating effect; dial: magical drinks and harmful substances are expressly outside its protection.

rules.statement: Grasping the cane and using a bonus action to speak its command transforms it into an ordinary longsword, ending its magical nature.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Veteran's cane (p. 140) (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a spoken command and bonus action trigger the change; dial: the result is mundane and no longer magical.

rules.statement: The conducting wand has 3 charges; an action and one charge produce orchestral music audible within 60 feet, which stops when the user stops waving the wand. It regains all charges at dawn; after spending the last one, a roll of 1 on a d20 destroys it.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Wand of conducting (p. 141) (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sound requires active waving and ends with it; dial: three charges, daily recovery, and a small destruction risk govern use.

rules.statement: The pyrotechnics wand has 7 charges; an action and one charge create a harmless burst of torch-bright multicolored light at a visible point within 60 feet, with a crackle audible within 300 feet, lasting one second. It regains 1d6 + 1 charges at dawn, and spending its last charge has a 1-in-20 chance of destroying it harmlessly.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Wand of pyrotechnics (p. 141) (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a brief harmless sensory effect costs one charge and an action; dial: range, duration, recharge, and destruction risk constrain it.

rules.statement: The scowls wand has 3 charges; an action and one charge targets a visible humanoid within 30 feet, which must make a DC 10 Charisma save or scowl for 1 minute. It regains all charges at dawn; spending its last charge has a 1-in-20 chance to turn it into a smiles wand.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Wand of scowls (p. 141) (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the wand can impose a brief facial state; dial: one target, a save, limited charges, and a chance of changing into its counterpart.

rules.statement: The smiles wand has 3 charges; an action and one charge targets a visible humanoid within 30 feet, which must make a DC 10 Charisma save or smile for 1 minute. It regains all charges at dawn; spending its last charge has a 1-in-20 chance to turn it into a scowls wand.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Wand of smiles (p. 141) (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the wand can impose a brief facial state; dial: one target, a save, limited charges, and a chance of changing into its counterpart.

rules.statement: A campaign's DM decides which listed spells are available and how characters can learn them; some may be readily available, unavailable, or gated behind a quest or found text. Because clerics, druids, and paladins prepare from their class's full spell list, the DM may restrict additions to story-appropriate choices to avoid overwhelming a player.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Chapter 3: Spells (p. 148) (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the DM controls access and learning; dial: narrative gates and curated choices balance spell options with campaign and player needs.

rules.statement: On a plane without a dawn, the DM chooses a time every 24 hours when dawn-recharged items regain charges; even where dawn occurs, the DM may choose another daily recharge time.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Recharging Without a Dawn (p. 145) (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recharge occurs once per 24 hours; dial: the DM sets a workable local time when the plane has no dawn or a different schedule is desired.

rules.statement: A 6th-level spell can ward an outdoor or underground area from a 30-foot cube up to a 90-foot cube for 24 hours; casting it in the same area daily for a year makes it last until dispelled. The caster can designate immune creatures and a spoken password, and a successful dispelling removes only one ward effect at a time.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Druid Grove, p. 155 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one protected area with separately removable effects; dial: make it permanent after a year of daily casting, paid for by sustained ritual effort.

rules.statement: A grove ward can create heavily obscuring fog that doubles movement cost through it, grasping plants as an entangle effect, up to four animated tree guardians, and one choice of additional wind or growth effects. The guardians fight intruders, follow the caster’s spoken orders in the area, cannot leave it, and return to being rooted trees when the spell ends.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Druid Grove, p. 155 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: guardians and terrain effects remain bounded by the ward; dial: grant active defenders, but they cannot leave and cease functioning when the spell ends.

rules.statement: A summoned greater steed is a spirit given one of six listed mount forms and the celestial, fey, or fiend type; it has its chosen form’s statistics, with Intelligence raised to 6 if lower and the ability to understand one language the caster speaks. The caster controls it in combat, can communicate telepathically within 1 mile, and can share self-only spells while mounted; it reappears restored if dismissed temporarily, reduced to 0 hit points, or summoned again, but only one mount from this spell or find steed can be bonded at once.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Find Greater Steed, p. 157 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one continuing mount bond; dial: gain a loyal, reusable companion, limited to one bond and removable permanently by releasing it.

rules.statement: A creature summoned by infernal calling is an unfriendly devil of challenge rating 6 or lower, controlled by the DM, and remains for up to an hour while the caster concentrates. Verbal orders are obeyed only when they suit the devil, or after a successful contested Charisma check against its Wisdom; failure makes it immune to further orders, and if concentration ends it can act freely for 3d6 minutes before disappearing.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Infernal Calling, p. 159 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the devil retains its own motives; dial: use its true name for advantage on an order check, risking disobedience and temporary loss of control.

rules.statement: Possessing an individual devil’s talisman lets the caster summon that devil if its challenge rating is no more than the spell’s limit plus 1, and it obeys every command without a Charisma check. Casting with a slot above 5th increases the permitted challenge rating by 1 per slot level.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Infernal Calling, p. 159 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ordinary summoning leaves the devil discretionary; dial: a specific talisman grants reliable command, but only over its associated devil and within the challenge-rating limit.

rules.statement: Mass polymorph can transform up to ten visible creatures into beasts they have seen, with each beast’s challenge rating no greater than the target’s or half its level if it has no challenge rating; unwilling targets can resist with a Wisdom save. The target takes the beast’s statistics but keeps its hit points, alignment, and personality, gains temporary hit points equal to the beast’s hit points, and reverts when those temporary hit points run out, it dies, or the spell ends; its gear melds and it cannot use equipment, speak, or cast spells in beast form.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Mass Polymorph, p. 162 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation preserves identity and ordinary hit points; dial: adopt a more capable beast body, at the cost of losing speech, spellcasting, and equipment use.

rules.statement: Invulnerability makes its caster immune to all damage for up to 10 minutes while concentration lasts; casting consumes an adamantine piece worth at least 500 gp. If concentration ends, the immunity ends.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Invulnerability, p. 161 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: damage is blocked only during maintained concentration; dial: obtain total damage immunity, paid for with a costly consumed component and concentration.

rules.statement: Mind spike deals 3d8 psychic damage on a failed Wisdom save or half as much on a success; after a failed save, the caster knows the target’s location for up to an hour while both remain on the same plane. While that knowledge lasts, the target cannot hide from the caster or gain an invisibility benefit against them; higher-level slots add 1d6 damage per level above 2nd.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Mind Spike, p. 163 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: tracking works only across the same plane and requires concentration; dial: pierce hiding and invisibility, but only after the target fails its save.

rules.statement: Earthbind targets one visible creature within 300 feet; a failed Strength save reduces its flying speed to 0 for up to a minute while concentration lasts. An affected airborne creature descends safely at 60 feet per round until it lands or the spell ends.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Earthbind, p. 156 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: flight is suppressed rather than causing a fall; dial: ground a flying target, limited by a save and concentration.

rules.statement: A creature affected by enemies abound loses the ability to distinguish allies from foes and regards all visible creatures as enemies for up to a minute while concentration lasts. When it chooses a target for an attack, spell, or other ability, it must choose randomly from valid visible targets, and it must make an opportunity attack if able; taking damage lets it repeat its save to end the effect.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Enemies Abound, p. 156 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: confusion lasts only while concentration holds; dial: disrupt allegiance and targeting, with damage offering a chance to end the effect.

rules.statement: A creature bound in a mental prison takes 5d10 psychic damage whether it succeeds or fails on its Intelligence save; a failed save also traps it in an illusory danger that it cannot see or hear beyond and restrains it for up to a minute. Moving out, making a melee attack through the illusion, or reaching through it deals 10d10 psychic damage and ends the spell; a creature immune to being charmed succeeds automatically.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Mental Prison, p. 162 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: escape attempts end the trap but inflict greater damage; dial: isolate and restrain a target, limited by its save and charm immunity.

rules.statement: A creature killed by negative energy flood rises as a zombie at the start of the caster’s next turn and pursues the nearest creature it can see. If the target is undead instead, it makes no save and gains temporary hit points equal to half the total rolled on 5d12.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Negative Energy Flood, p. 164 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the created zombie follows its own nearest-target pursuit rather than the caster’s orders; dial: convert a death into an active undead creature, with its behavior uncontrolled.

rules.statement: A spell can capture a dying humanoid’s soul in a small silver cage for up to 8 hours; the soul can be used up to six times for healing, truthful answers, a brief advantage, or sensory observation of a place it knew on the same plane. While captured, the humanoid cannot be revived, and the soul is released when the spell ends, the cage is destroyed, or its sixth use is spent.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Soul Cage, p. 167 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one dying humanoid and at most six uses; dial: 8 hours and a costly cage. The capture prevents revival and confines the soul.

rules.statement: A summoned greater demon acts on its own initiative; the caster can give it a verbal order each turn, but it tests its resolve at the end of every turn and may break free to attack nearby non-demons. A blood-drawn circle can keep it from crossing, harming, or targeting those inside; if concentration ends early, an uncontrolled demon may remain for 1d6 rounds.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Summon Greater Demon, p. 168 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control is provisional and tested every turn; dial: a true name hinders the test and a blood circle offers protection at the cost of consuming its component.

rules.statement: A lesser-demon summoning brings a randomly determined group—two, four, or eight demons, with maximum challenge ratings of 1, 1/2, or 1/4 respectively. The demons are hostile to everyone and attack the nearest non-demons; a blood circle can protect those within it, consuming the blood when the spell ends.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Summon Lesser Demons, p. 168 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the die determines the group and the demons are hostile; dial: a protective circle limits danger but consumes the blood component.

rules.statement: A temple created for 24 hours can bar chosen creature types on a failed Charisma save; those that enter despite this suffer a d4 penalty on attacks, ability checks, and saving throws. It also blocks divination sensors and targeting, prevents ethereal passage and physical entry through its exterior, and adds the caster’s Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) to healing from spells of level 1 or higher; casting it at the same location daily for a year makes it permanent.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Temple of the Gods, pp. 168–169 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the temple lasts 24 hours and its protections are bounded to its interior; dial: repeated daily casting can make the location permanent.

rules.statement: A Tiny nonmagical object that is unattached and not carried can be animated for 8 hours as a controlled creature; it has 10 hit points, and at 0 hit points it becomes the original object with excess damage carrying over. A bonus action issues mental commands within 120 feet, and a spell slot above 3rd level animates two additional objects per slot level above 3rd.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Tiny Servant, pp. 169–170 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each servant lasts 8 hours and is limited by its object and hit points; dial: higher slots increase the number animated.

rules.statement: A water-shaping cantrip affects visible water within 30 feet in a space no larger than a 5-foot cube: it can move or redirect it up to 5 feet without damaging force, shape or animate it, change its color or opacity, or freeze it if no creature is in it. Non-instantaneous changes last 1 hour, and only two such effects can be active from the caster at once; one can be dismissed with an action.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Shape Water, p. 166 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: effects are limited by the small volume, short duration, and two-effect cap; dial: the caster can dismiss a lasting effect with an action.

rules.statement: A rope consumed during a one-minute casting creates a nearly invisible trap lasting 8 hours; a qualifying creature entering its 5-foot-radius area must save or be hoisted and restrained. The captive can escape with a successful Dexterity save at the end of a turn, or the captive or an ally can use an action and succeed on an Arcana check against the caster’s spell save DC; the spell ends when no creature remains restrained.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Snare, p. 166 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the trap is limited by its radius, duration, and creature sizes; dial: escape is possible through either a repeated save or an action and check.

rules.statement: A burst of psychic energy affects creatures in a 20-foot-radius sphere, except creatures with Intelligence 2 or lower; a failed save deals 8d6 psychic damage and imposes a 1-minute penalty of 1d6 to attack rolls, ability checks, and Constitution saves to maintain concentration. The affected creature can end the penalty early by succeeding on an Intelligence save at the end of a turn.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Synaptic Static, p. 168 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect is limited to its area and one minute; dial: a successful repeat save ends the penalty early.

rules.statement: A creature caught by a storm sphere can take 2d6 bludgeoning damage on entering or ending its turn there, and the area is difficult terrain; while concentrating, the caster can use a bonus action each turn to attack a creature within 60 feet of the sphere’s center with lightning. The storm also hinders listening nearby, and casting with a higher-level slot increases the damage of its effects.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Storm Sphere, p. 167 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the field lasts up to 1 minute and requires concentration; dial: higher-level slots increase damage.

rules.statement: A caster can teleport to a visible unoccupied destination within 90 feet and bring carried objects plus one willing creature of the caster’s size or smaller that is within 5 feet; the companion needs an unoccupied space near the destination or is left behind. The departure causes a thunderous burst that deals 3d10 thunder damage within 10 feet, halved on a successful save, and higher-level slots add 1d10 per level above 3rd.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Thunder Step, p. 170 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: destination, companion, and carried-weight limits constrain travel; dial: higher-level slots increase the departure damage.

rules.statement: In a shared campaign, characters gain one checkpoint for each hour an adventure is designed to last, plus one if they complete an adventure designed for a higher tier than their own. They advance by spending four checkpoints at levels 1–4 or eight at level 5 and above, and must level up at the end of a session when they have enough.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Appendix A: Shared Campaigns—Character Advancement, pp. 174–175 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: rewards depend on the adventure’s planned duration rather than play style or actual time; dial: a higher-tier adventure grants one extra checkpoint.

rules.statement: For a Spanish male character, roll d100 and use the name assigned to the result’s range in the table; each listed range covers two consecutive results.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Appendix B: Character Names, Spanish, Male (dnd5e-xanathar#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the roll chooses a name from a fixed table without an additional cost.

rules.statement: For a Spanish female character, roll d100 and use the name assigned to the result’s range in the table; each listed range covers two consecutive results.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Appendix B: Character Names, Spanish, Female (dnd5e-xanathar#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the roll chooses a name from a fixed table without an additional cost.

rules.statement: A warlock’s power comes through a pact with a planar entity; the patron dictates any obligations required in return, which may range from a loose agreement to detailed conditions. The relationship need not be affectionate or mutual, and the passage does not specify a general penalty for breaking the pact.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Warlock — Patron’s Attitude; Special Terms of the Pact, p. 54 (dnd5e-xanathar#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a pact supplies the warlock’s source of power; dial: set the patron’s demands and relationship; cost: the patron may require specific conduct or service.

rules.statement: A Celestial patron adds specified spells to the warlock’s available choices at each listed spell level, and grants the warlock the light and sacred flame cantrips without counting them against the cantrips known limit.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: The Celestial — Expanded Spell List; Bonus Cantrips, p. 55 (dnd5e-xanathar#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these spells are available as warlock options; dial: use this patron’s listed additions; in-world reason: the pact opens access to celestial magic.

rules.statement: A Celestial warlock has a pool of d6s equal to 1 plus warlock level. As a bonus action, the warlock spends up to a number of dice equal to their Charisma modifier (minimum one) to restore their total roll in hit points to one visible creature within 60 feet; all dice return after a long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: The Celestial — Healing Light, p. 55 (dnd5e-xanathar#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: healing consumes dice from a limited pool; dial: set pool size by level; cost: spent dice return only after a long rest.

rules.statement: A Hexblade can curse one visible creature within 30 feet as a bonus action; for 1 minute, attacks against it gain a damage bonus equal to proficiency bonus and score a critical hit on a d20 roll of 19 or 20. If it dies, the warlock regains hit points equal to warlock level plus Charisma modifier (minimum 1); the curse ends early if the target or warlock dies or the warlock is incapacitated, and the feature recharges after a short or long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: The Hexblade — Hexblade’s Curse, p. 56 (dnd5e-xanathar#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one target is cursed at a time; dial: retain the listed duration and recharge; cost: using the curse commits a limited feature use.

rules.statement: A Hexblade can touch a proficient weapon without the two-handed property after a long rest and use Charisma instead of Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls until the next long rest. The warlock also gains proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: The Hexblade — Hex Warrior, p. 56 (dnd5e-xanathar#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the weapon’s attacks use Charisma while the binding lasts; dial: one eligible weapon per long rest; cost: the benefit ends at the next long rest.

rules.statement: After slaying a humanoid, a Hexblade can bind its spirit as a specter, which gains temporary hit points equal to half the warlock’s level, takes its own turns, and obeys verbal commands. It serves until the warlock’s next long rest, then departs; this can be used again after a long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: The Hexblade — Accursed Specter, p. 57 (dnd5e-xanathar#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the slain humanoid’s spirit becomes a temporary servant; dial: preserve the once-per-long-rest limit; cost: a humanoid must be slain and service ends at the next long rest.

rules.statement: A Horizon Walker can use an action to sense the direction and distance of the nearest planar portal within 1 mile; after using this ability, it recharges on a short or long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Horizon Walker — Detect Portal, p. 44 (dnd5e-xanathar#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sensing reveals only the closest portal’s direction and distance; dial: use the 1-mile range; cost: the sense cannot be repeated until a short or long rest.

rules.statement: A Horizon Walker can briefly enter the Ethereal Plane by casting etherealness as a bonus action without a spell slot; the spell ends at the end of the current turn. The feature recharges after a short or long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Horizon Walker — Ethereal Step, p. 44 (dnd5e-xanathar#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the user crosses into the Ethereal Plane briefly; dial: limit the crossing to the current turn; cost: the ability recharges only after a short or long rest.

rules.statement: When taking the Attack action, a Horizon Walker can teleport up to 10 feet to a visible unoccupied space before each attack. If that action targets at least two different creatures, the ranger can make one extra attack against a third creature.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Horizon Walker — Distant Strike, p. 44 (dnd5e-xanathar#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: short teleports occur as part of attacking; dial: cap each move at 10 feet and require a visible open destination; cost: the extra attack requires attacks against two different creatures.

rules.statement: When an attack damages a Horizon Walker, the ranger can use a reaction to gain resistance to all damage from that attack for the current turn.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Horizon Walker — Spectral Defense, p. 44 (dnd5e-xanathar#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resistance applies only to the triggering attack’s damage; dial: retain the reaction cost; cost: it competes with other reactions.

rules.statement: At 2nd level, a War Magic wizard may use a reaction when hit by an attack or failing a saving throw: gain +2 AC against that attack or +4 to that save. Until the end of the wizard’s next turn, they cannot cast spells other than cantrips.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: War Magic — Arcane Deflection, p. 61 (dnd5e-xanathar#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the reaction’s defense against a temporary restriction on spellcasting; it trades immediate protection for reduced magical output.

rules.statement: At 2nd level, the wizard adds their Intelligence modifier to initiative rolls.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: War Magic — Tactical Wit, p. 61 (dnd5e-xanathar#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the initiative bonus by Intelligence; tactical quickness depends on the character’s mental aptitude.

rules.statement: At 6th level, the wizard can hold power surges up to their Intelligence modifier, with a minimum capacity of one. A long rest resets the number to one; successfully ending a spell with dispel magic or counterspell grants one, and ending a short rest with none grants one.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: War Magic — Power Surge, p. 61 (dnd5e-xanathar#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial storage capacity by Intelligence and cap it; the wizard’s stored power is limited rather than inexhaustible.

rules.statement: Once per turn, when a wizard spell deals damage to a creature or object, the wizard can spend one power surge to add force damage equal to half their wizard level to that target.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: War Magic — Power Surge, p. 61 (dnd5e-xanathar#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the damage by wizard level and charge one stored surge; extra force requires previously accumulated power.

rules.statement: At 10th level, while concentrating on a spell, the wizard gains +2 AC and a +2 bonus to all saving throws.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: War Magic — Durable Magic, p. 61 (dnd5e-xanathar#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the defense to active concentration; maintaining a spell is the condition and opportunity cost.

rules.statement: At 14th level, when using Arcane Deflection, the wizard can also deal force damage equal to half their wizard level to as many as three chosen creatures they can see within 60 feet.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: War Magic — Deflecting Shroud, p. 61 (dnd5e-xanathar#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial targets to three and range to 60 feet; the offensive burst is tied to using the defensive reaction.

rules.statement: These backstory tables are optional prompts, not binding rules: the player may choose results, roll, ignore a roll that conflicts with another result, and arrange life events in any order.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: This Is Your Life — Ideas, Not Rules; How and When to Use the Tables, p. 62 (dnd5e-xanathar#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial is player choice; the tables provide inspiration rather than compulsory character facts.

rules.statement: A devil’s temptation life-event result calls for a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, an alignment that is not already evil shifts one step toward evil, and the character starts with an additional 1d20 + 50 gp.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Life Events — Supernatural Events, p. 72 (dnd5e-xanathar#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the saving-throw DC and reward to the stated values; resisting the temptation avoids the alignment shift and extra wealth.

rules.statement: A complex trap remains dangerous over successive rounds after it activates, and may grow more dangerous over time. It is not defeated by one check: each active element must be addressed separately, usually through multiple successes; as a default, three successes or actions disable one element.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Complex Traps; Defeating Complex Traps, pp. 119, 124 (dnd5e-xanathar#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the number and consequences of successes to fit each element; the trap’s continuing operation forces characters to manage danger while dismantling it.

rules.statement: For a complex trap, another character cannot attempt the same check against the same element until the end of the turn after a character succeeds; checks cannot be made by several characters in rapid succession to disable it immediately.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Defeating Complex Traps, p. 124 (dnd5e-xanathar#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the delay to the stated turn boundary; coordinated work is limited so disabling the trap takes time.

rules.statement: A supernatural-event result may have the character briefly visit the Feywild or Shadowfell, or see a portal believed to lead to another plane; these results establish an event, not a travel procedure or portal operation rule.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Life Events — Supernatural Events, p. 72 (dnd5e-xanathar#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial whether the event is selected or randomly rolled; the passage supplies a possible encounter but no mechanics for crossing planes.

rules.statement: After a workweek of carousing, make a Charisma (Persuasion) check: a result of 1–5 creates a hostile contact, 6–10 creates none, 11–15 creates one allied contact, 16–20 creates two, and 21 or higher creates three. Each workweek of carousing carries a 10% chance of a complication.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Carousing, p. 128–129 (dnd5e-xanathar#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial the complication chance or contact results; carousing can create useful allies but also trouble.

rules.statement: An allied contact can help once, but not at risk to their life; a hostile contact obstructs the character without committing a crime or violence. After helping or hindering, the contact requires renewed carousing before doing so again. Unspecified allied contacts are limited to 1 + the character’s Charisma modifier, minimum 1; named contacts do not count against this limit.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Carousing, p. 128–129 (dnd5e-xanathar#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial the reliability and number of contacts; social ties grant limited aid, not permanent service.

rules.statement: A Dark Shard Amulet requires attunement by a warlock. While worn, it can serve as a focus for warlock spells, and once per long rest the wearer can attempt to cast an unknown warlock-list cantrip with a DC 10 Intelligence (Arcana) check; failure wastes the action and the use.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Dark Shard Amulet, p. 138 (dnd5e-xanathar#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial the available cantrip access; the patron-realm shard lends a limited magical capability.

rules.statement: A creature wearing an attuned Charlatan’s Die can choose the result whenever it rolls the six-sided die.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Charlatan’s Die, p. 129 (dnd5e-xanathar#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial whether deliberate outcomes are allowed; the bound item gives control over its own roll.

rules.statement: A creature wearing an attuned Ersatz Eye can see through it as through a normal eye. While embedded in the eye socket, no one other than its owner can remove it.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Ersatz Eye, p. 138 (dnd5e-xanathar#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial removal and replacement rules; the artificial eye restores sight but is physically embedded.

rules.statement: A creature wearing an attuned Hat of Wizardry can use it as a focus for wizard spells and, once per long rest, attempt to cast an unknown wizard-list cantrip with a DC 10 Intelligence (Arcana) check. A failed check wastes the action and the use.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Hat of Wizardry, p. 138 (dnd5e-xanathar#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial the permitted spell list or attempt frequency; the hat provides restricted access to wizard magic.

rules.statement: When a creature makes an attack roll while wearing a Clockwork Amulet, it can take 10 on the d20 instead of rolling; after use, this property is unavailable until the next dawn.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Clockwork Amulet, p. 138 (dnd5e-xanathar#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial the recharge schedule; predictable Mechanus magic trades uncertainty for one-use reliability.

rules.statement: A 7th-level Temple of the Gods takes 1 hour to cast, appears in visible unoccupied space within 120 feet, and lasts 24 hours. It occupies a space up to 120 feet on each side; casting it in the same place daily for a year makes it permanent.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Temple of the Gods, p. 168–169 (dnd5e-xanathar#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial duration or permanence requirement; a costly, repeated ritual can establish lasting sacred space.

rules.statement: The temple bars entry to selected celestials, elementals, fey, fiends, or undead that fail a Charisma save, and hinders those that succeed: they subtract a d4 from attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws inside. Divination sensors cannot appear inside, creatures there cannot be targeted by divination, and magical healing of 1st level or higher restores extra hit points equal to the caster’s Wisdom modifier, minimum 1.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Temple of the Gods, p. 169 (dnd5e-xanathar#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial barred creature types and protective effects; the sacred space selectively excludes and impedes threats.

rules.statement: The temple is opaque magical force; nothing can pass physically through its exterior, and Ethereal travel into its interior is blocked. Dispel Magic and Antimagic Field do not end or suppress it, but Disintegrate destroys it instantly.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Temple of the Gods, p. 169 (dnd5e-xanathar#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial which countermeasures work; the structure resists ordinary magical interference but has a specific destructive counter.

rules.statement: Tenser’s Transformation lasts up to 10 minutes with concentration. It grants 50 temporary hit points, advantage on weapon attacks, an extra 2d12 force damage on weapon hits, listed weapon, armor, and shield proficiencies, Strength and Constitution saving throw proficiency, and two attacks with the Attack action unless another feature already grants Extra Attack; the caster cannot cast spells while it lasts and risks one exhaustion level afterward on a failed DC 15 Constitution save.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Tenser’s Transformation, p. 169 (dnd5e-xanathar#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial duration and exhaustion risk; martial enhancement suspends spellcasting and can exact an aftereffect.

rules.statement: Thunder Step teleports the caster to a visible unoccupied space within 90 feet. Creatures within 10 feet of the departure space make a Constitution save, taking 3d10 thunder damage on a failure or half on a success; the boom can be heard up to 300 feet away.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Thunder Step, p. 169 (dnd5e-xanathar#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial range and audible radius; rapid relocation is bounded by sight and announces the departure.
